senses.meaning_zh: （使）二聚；（使）两个分子或分子亚基结合形成二聚体
senses.meaning_en: To combine, or cause two molecules or molecular subunits to combine, into a dimer.
senses.english_definition: When molecules or molecular subunits dimerize, or something dimerizes them, two of them join to form a single paired unit.
senses.collocation_en: receptors dimerize; dimerize upon ligand binding
senses.collocation_zh: 受体发生二聚；在配体结合后发生二聚
senses.sentence_en: The receptor molecules dimerize when the ligand binds to them.
senses.sentence_zh: 配体与这些受体分子结合后，受体分子发生二聚。

etymology_story.zh: 该词属于以 dimer“二聚体”为基础形成的科学词族；dimer 最终结合了希腊语表示“二”的 di- 和 meros“部分”。其含义由“由两个部分组成的单位”发展为“形成这种双单元结构”。
etymology_story.en: Dimerize belongs to the scientific word family based on dimer, which ultimately combines Greek di-, 'two,' and meros, 'part.' The idea of a unit made of two parts underlies the verb meaning 'to form such a paired structure.'

morphology_enriched.zh: dimer（二聚体）＋ -ize（使成为；形成）→ dimerize，兼作及物和不及物动词。主要词族：dimer、dimeric（二聚体的）、dimerization（二聚作用）、dimerized（二聚化的）、dimerizing（正在二聚的）；相关形式有 homodimer（同源二聚体）、heterodimer（异源二聚体）、homodimerize（同源二聚）、heterodimerize（异源二聚）。英式拼写也可用 dimerise、dimerisation。
morphology_enriched.en: Dimer + -ize ('make or become') forms dimerize, used both transitively and intransitively. The main family includes dimer, dimeric, dimerization, dimerized, and dimerizing. Related forms include homodimer, heterodimer, homodimerize, and heterodimerize. British spelling also permits dimerise and dimerisation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pair up（配成一对）表达通俗，但不说明分子结构；associate（缔合）可指分子通过相互作用结合，不限定数量；oligomerize（寡聚）指形成由少量亚基组成的结构，不限于两个。dimerize 明确限定形成二聚体。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pair up is an informal description that does not specify molecular structure; associate describes molecules joining through interactions without fixing their number; oligomerize means forming a structure with a small number of subunits, not necessarily two. Dimerize specifically means forming a dimer.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: di-＝二，mer＝部分，-ize＝形成：两个单元结合成一对。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Di- means two, mer means part, and -ize means form: two units join as a pair.

pronunciation.note: 重音在 /fiː/，开头 di- 读 /daɪ/。

forms: 物质名称通常不可数；谈不同类型时可见 diphenyls。
family: biphenyl 联苯，常用同义名称。

morphology.text: di-（两个）+ phenyl（苯基）→ diphenyl（两个苯基相连形成的联苯）。

etymology.text: 19世纪英语化学命名使用 di- 与 phenyl 组成此词；di- 经拉丁语追溯至希腊语“二”，phenyl 来自法语 phényle。用“两只苯环牵手”记联苯。

usage_note: 本卡教独立名词“联苯”；带连字符的 diphenyl- 可作化学名称的组合成分。

etymology_story.zh: diphenyl 在19世纪由表示“二”的希腊语源构词成分 di- 与 phenyl“苯基”组成；phenyl 借自法语 phényle。该词既可单独指联苯，也可作为化学名称中的构词成分表示含两个苯基。[词源资料](https://www.etymonline.com/word/phenyl)、[词义资料](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/diphenyl)。
etymology_story.en: Diphenyl was formed in the nineteenth century from Greek-derived di-, meaning two, and phenyl, borrowed from French phényle. It names biphenyl independently and also functions in chemical names to indicate two phenyl groups. [Etymology](https://www.etymonline.com/word/phenyl), [definitions](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/diphenyl).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：di-（二）+ phenyl（苯基，C₆H₅–）。相关命名系列包括 phenyl（苯基）、monophenyl-（单苯基）、diphenyl-（二苯基）和 triphenyl-（三苯基）；常见复合名称包括 diphenyl ether（二苯醚）、diphenylmethane（二苯甲烷）和 diphenylamine（二苯胺）。这些化合物名称不一定表示联苯本身的衍生物；diphenyl- 的修饰作用通常归为构词成分，而非独立形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: di- (two) + phenyl (the C₆H₅– group). The related naming series includes phenyl, monophenyl-, diphenyl-, and triphenyl-; familiar compound names include diphenyl ether, diphenylmethane, and diphenylamine. These names do not necessarily denote derivatives of biphenyl itself; modifying diphenyl- is generally treated as a combining form rather than an independent adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: biphenyl（联苯）是该化合物更通行的名称；phenylbenzene（苯基苯）从“苯上连接一个苯基”的角度命名同一物质。独立名词 diphenyl 与二者同指一种化合物，但构词成分 diphenyl- 仅表示含两个苯基，不要求它们直接相连。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Biphenyl is the more usual name of the compound; phenylbenzene names the same substance as benzene bearing a phenyl group. The independent noun diphenyl denotes that compound, whereas combining diphenyl- indicates two phenyl groups without requiring a direct bond between them.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: di-＝二，phenyl＝苯基：两个苯基直接牵手是联苯，加入其他连接结构则形成二苯基类名称。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Di- means two: two phenyl groups joined directly give biphenyl; other connections produce other diphenyl compounds.

senses.meaning_zh: 所有权，尤指罗马法及相关法律传统中的财产所有权
senses.meaning_en: ownership of property, especially in Roman law and related legal traditions
senses.english_definition: Dominium is the legal right to own property and to control its use or disposal.
senses.collocation_zh: 上级所有权；用益所有权
senses.sentence_en: The historian distinguishes dominium, or ownership, from mere possession.
senses.sentence_zh: 这位历史学家将 dominium，即所有权，与单纯的占有区分开来。

etymology_story.zh: 英语于19世纪借入拉丁语 dominium，原义为“所有权、主人的权力”，与 dominus“主人”相关。它在英语中保留了专门法律用语的性质，核心指对财产的所有及支配权。[词源与词义资料](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/dominium)。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Latin dominium, meaning ownership or a master's authority, in the nineteenth century; it is related to dominus, meaning master. In English it remains a specialist legal term for ownership and control of property. [Etymology and definition](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/dominium).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 dominium 作为整词借用，没有常用的直接派生系列；历史上可分析为拉丁语 domin-（主人）+ -ium（构成名词的后缀）。同源词族包括 domain（领域；领地）、dominion（统治权；领土）、dominate（支配）、dominant（占支配地位的）、dominance（支配地位）、domination（控制）、dominator（支配者）、domineer（专横地支配）和 domineering（专横的）；这些词并非都由英语 dominium 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats dominium as a whole-word borrowing with no common direct derivative series; historically it contains Latin domin- (master) and the noun-forming suffix -ium. Its etymological family includes domain, dominion, dominate, dominant, dominance, domination, dominator, domineer, and domineering; these are not all direct English derivatives of dominium.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ownership（所有权）是最直接、最通用的对应词；title（权原；所有权资格）强调权利的法律依据或归属；possession（占有）强调实际持有或控制，不必然包含所有权。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ownership is the closest general equivalent; title emphasizes the legal basis or recognized entitlement to ownership; possession concerns holding or controlling something and does not necessarily imply ownership.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: dominus＝主人：dominium 就是对财产“作主”的所有权。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Dominus means master: dominium is the right to act as the property's owner.

etymology_story.zh: dreg 源于中古英语，来自古诺尔斯语中表示沉淀物或酵母沉渣的词。它从液体底部的残渣引申为少量残余，又进一步用于贬指最无价值的部分；现代英语尤其常用复数 dregs。[词义与词源资料](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/dreg)。
etymology_story.en: Dreg entered Middle English from an Old Norse word for sediment or yeast deposits. Its meaning extended from material left at the bottom of a liquid to a small remainder and, disparagingly, the least valuable part; modern usage particularly favors plural dregs. [Definitions and etymology](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/dreg).

morphology_enriched.zh: dreg 是不可再作常用现代构词拆分的词根；dreg + -s → dregs（复数，也是多数义项的常用形式）。派生链为 dreg + -y → dreggy（含渣的；浑浊的，双写 g），dreggy + -ness → dregginess（含渣状态；浑浊，y 改为 i）；形容词变化为 dreggier、dreggiest。[派生词资料](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/dreggy)。
morphology_enriched.en: Dreg is a simple lexical base; dreg + -s gives dregs, the usual form for most senses. Its derivative chain is dreg + -y → dreggy (containing sediment or muddy), with doubled g, and dreggy + -ness → dregginess, with y changing to i; adjective comparison gives dreggier and dreggiest. [Derivative forms](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/dreggy).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sediment（沉淀物）中性地指沉降的颗粒；lees（酒脚；酒糟沉淀）尤其指葡萄酒等液体中的沉渣；remnant（残余）泛指剩下的部分，不自带“沉底”或“低劣”的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sediment neutrally denotes particles that settle; lees particularly refers to deposits in wine and similar liquids; remnant means a remaining part without inherently suggesting settled matter or worthlessness.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住杯底：沉下的是渣，剩下的是最后一点，贬义引申为最差的部分。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the bottom of a cup: sediment, the last little remainder, and figuratively the worst part.

etymology_story.zh: drupe 于18世纪由现代拉丁语 drupa“核果”进入英语，后者沿用拉丁语中指熟透、起皱橄榄的名称，并可追溯至希腊语。原本与橄榄有关的词，在植物学中扩展为具有坚硬内果皮这一结构的果实类别。[词源资料](https://www.etymonline.com/word/drupaceous)。
etymology_story.en: Drupe entered English in the eighteenth century from Modern Latin drupa, a botanical term based on the Latin name for an overripe, wrinkled olive and ultimately of Greek origin. A word associated with olives became the name of a fruit category characterized by a hard inner fruit-wall layer. [Etymology](https://www.etymonline.com/word/drupaceous).

morphology_enriched.zh: drupe 在现代英语中作为整词词根使用，复数为 drupes。相关派生词包括 drupe + -aceous → drupaceous（核果的；核果状的；结核果的，去掉末尾 e），drupe + -let → drupelet（小核果，如覆盆子上的单个小果），以及 drupeole（小核果，较少见）；这些词都围绕核果结构构成词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Drupe functions as a whole lexical base in modern English, with plural drupes. Related formations include drupe + -aceous → drupaceous (relating to, resembling, or producing drupes), dropping final e; drupe + -let → drupelet (a small drupe, such as one unit of a raspberry); and the less common drupeole (a small drupe).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: stone fruit（核果）是最接近的日常对应说法，园艺语境中常侧重桃、李、樱桃等；drupelet（小核果）指小型核果，尤其是聚合果的组成单位，并非所有核果的同义词。drupe 是强调果实结构的植物学术语。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Stone fruit is the closest everyday equivalent, often focusing horticulturally on peaches, plums, cherries, and similar fruits; drupelet means a small drupe, especially a unit of an aggregate fruit, rather than any drupe. Drupe is the botanical term emphasizing fruit structure.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从橄榄想到桃子：外层包着硬核，硬核里面才是种子。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think from olive to peach: outer fruit, a hard stone, then the seed inside.

senses.meaning_en: an instrumental piece or movement modeled on a dumka, often contrasting melancholy and lively sections

etymology_story.zh: 英语在19世纪末经捷克语借入 dumka，其源头是乌克兰语 duma“叙事民间诗歌”的指小形式。这个名称后来也用于受该民歌传统启发的器乐曲，尤其常见于悲喜情绪交替的作品。[词源与词义资料](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/dumka)。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed dumka through Czech in the late nineteenth century, ultimately from a Ukrainian diminutive of duma, a narrative folk poem. The name also came to denote instrumental works inspired by that tradition, often contrasting melancholy and gaiety. [Etymology and definitions](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/dumka).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 dumka 作为整词借入，不分析为英语词根加英语后缀；来源语构词可概括为 duma 的词干 dum- + 指小后缀 -ka。英语音乐用语常保留复数 dumky，也可见英语化复数 dumkas；没有常用的英语动词、副词或独立形容词派生形式。[复数形式资料](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/dumka)。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats dumka as a whole-word borrowing, not an English root-plus-suffix formation; its source-language structure can be summarized as dum-, the stem of duma, plus diminutive -ka. Musical English commonly retains plural dumky, while anglicized dumkas also occurs; there are no common derived English verbs, adverbs, or independent adjectives. [Plural form](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/dumka).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ballad（叙事民歌）强调讲述故事；lament（哀歌）强调悲伤或悼念；character piece（性格小品）泛指表达特定情绪的器乐曲。三者都只能部分对应 dumka，不能完整替代其特定文化来源及常见的情绪对比。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ballad emphasizes a song's narrative character; lament emphasizes sorrow or mourning; character piece broadly describes an instrumental work expressing a particular mood. Each overlaps with dumka but does not fully convey its cultural origin and characteristic emotional contrasts.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把“小叙事歌”记成音乐中的小故事：先沉思，再欢舞，情绪可以转折。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember a little musical story: reflection can turn into dancing, with a change of mood.

etymology_story.zh: 此词于19世纪以新西兰的 Dun Mountain（邓山）之名加岩石名称后缀 -ite 构成。该山出露的富含橄榄石的岩石成为这种岩石命名的依据。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in the nineteenth century from Dun Mountain in New Zealand and the rock-naming suffix -ite. The mountain's exposed olivine-rich rock provided the basis for the name.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：Dun（专名词干，来自 Dun Mountain）+ -ite（岩石、矿物名称后缀）→ dunite。主要词族：dunites（复数），dunitic（纯橄岩的；纯橄岩质的）；olivine（橄榄石）是相关矿物名称，并非其派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: Dun, the proper-name base from Dun Mountain, + -ite, a suffix used in rock and mineral names, → dunite. The main family forms are dunites, the plural, and dunitic, meaning relating to or composed of dunite; olivine names the associated mineral and is not a derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: peridotite（橄榄岩）和 ultramafic rock（超镁铁质岩）是范围更广的相关术语：纯橄岩属于橄榄岩，而超镁铁质岩还包括其他富含镁、铁的岩石；两者都不能在精确分类中完全替代 dunite。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Peridotite and ultramafic rock are broader related terms: dunite is a type of peridotite, while ultramafic rock includes additional magnesium- and iron-rich rocks. Neither is an exact substitute for dunite in precise classification.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Dun 山 + 岩石后缀 -ite：把邓山与几乎全是橄榄石的岩石连起来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Dun Mountain + the rock suffix -ite: connect the mountain with rock made almost entirely of olivine.

meaning: 使种群遗传性状退化的

pronunciation.note: 重音在 /dʒɛn/，其中 g 读 /dʒ/。

usage_note: 多见于遗传学史、优生学史讨论；描述旧文献时须区分作者当时的判断和已经证实的事实。

senses.meaning_zh: 被认为不利于后代遗传特征的；所谓使种群遗传素质退化的，尤见于历史上的优生学论述
senses.meaning_en: Considered harmful to the inherited characteristics of future generations, especially in historical eugenic writing.
senses.english_definition: If an influence is described as dysgenic, it is claimed to make the inherited characteristics of later generations less favorable.
senses.collocation_zh: 所谓不利于后代遗传特征的效应；所谓逆向遗传选择
senses.sentence_en: The historian examined claims about the dysgenic effects of social policy.
senses.sentence_zh: 这位历史学家考察了有关社会政策会使后代遗传特征退化的论断。

senses.meaning_zh: 与遗传失调有关的；导致杂交后代不育或其他遗传异常的
senses.meaning_en: Relating to genetic dysfunction, especially abnormalities associated with hybrid dysgenesis.
senses.english_definition: In genetics, a dysgenic cross is a mating that produces offspring with abnormalities such as reduced fertility or increased mutation.
senses.collocation_zh: 引发遗传失调的杂交；遗传失调的杂交后代
senses.sentence_en: The dysgenic cross produced fruit flies with reduced fertility.
senses.sentence_zh: 这次引发遗传失调的杂交产生了生育力降低的果蝇。

etymology_story.zh: 此词由源自希腊语的 dys-（不良、异常）与 -genic（与产生、起源有关的）组成，早期主要用于与 eugenic（优生的）相对的论述。后来它也用于遗传学，描述杂交遗传失调等现象；历史上针对人群的用法带有优生学的价值判断。
etymology_story.en: The word combines Greek-derived dys-, meaning bad or abnormal, with -genic, relating to production or origin, and was used early on in opposition to eugenic. It later also appeared in genetics for phenomena such as hybrid dysgenesis; its historical application to human populations carries eugenic value judgments.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：dys-（不良、异常）+ -genic（与产生或遗传起源有关的）→ dysgenic。主要词族及相关构词：dysgenics（研究或主张所谓遗传退化的学说），dysgenesis（发育不全；遗传失调），dysgenetic（发育异常的；遗传失调的）；eugenic、eugenics 是采用相反前缀 eu- 的对照词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: dys-, meaning bad or abnormal, + -genic, relating to production or genetic origin, → dysgenic. Main family members and related formations include dysgenics, concerning alleged hereditary deterioration; dysgenesis, meaning defective development or genetic dysfunction; and dysgenetic. Eugenic and eugenics are contrasting formations with eu-.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: deleterious（有害的）泛指造成损害，不限定遗传；maladaptive（不利于适应的）强调某种特征在特定环境中降低适应度；dysgenic 则特指被认为不利于后代遗传特征的作用，或具体的遗传失调现象。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Deleterious means harmful without necessarily implying inheritance. Maladaptive describes a trait that reduces fitness in a particular environment. Dysgenic specifically concerns alleged adverse effects on inherited characteristics or particular forms of genetic dysfunction.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: dys- 表示“出了问题”，-genic 联系产生与遗传：记作“遗传或生殖过程出了问题”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Dys- signals something going wrong; -genic connects with production and inheritance: think of a problem affecting genetic or reproductive outcomes.

usage_note: 色谱等实验中使用；eluant 是用于洗脱的液体，eluate 是收集到的流出液。

senses.meaning_zh: 洗脱剂；用于将物质从吸附材料上洗出的流体
senses.meaning_en: A fluid used to wash an adsorbed substance out of a material, especially in chromatography.
senses.english_definition: An eluant is a solvent or other fluid that carries substances off an adsorbent, for example through a chromatography column.
senses.collocation_zh: 洗脱剂组成；洗脱剂流速
senses.sentence_en: The researchers used a mixture of water and methanol as the eluant.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员使用水和甲醇的混合液作为洗脱剂。

etymology_story.zh: eluant 是 eluent 的异体拼写，属于与 elute（洗脱）相关的科学词汇，最终源自拉丁语 eluere，意为“洗出、冲洗干净”。词义保留了用流体将吸附物质带走的基本图景。
etymology_story.en: Eluant is a variant spelling of eluent and belongs to the scientific vocabulary associated with elute, ultimately from Latin eluere, meaning to wash out or wash clean. Its meaning preserves the image of a fluid carrying an adsorbed substance away.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学习可分析为 elu-（见于 elute、elution 的洗脱词干）+ -ant（表示起作用之物的词尾）；elu- 不是独立英语单词。主要词族：eluant／eluent（洗脱剂），eluants／eluents（复数），elute（洗脱），elutes、eluted、eluting（动词变化），elution（洗脱），eluate（洗脱液，即洗脱后收集到的流出液）。
morphology_enriched.en: For modern learning, analyze the word as elu-, the stem shared with elute and elution, + -ant, an ending indicating something that acts; elu- is not an independent English word. Main family forms include eluant/eluent; their plurals eluants/eluents; elute, elutes, eluted, and eluting; elution; and eluate, the liquid collected after elution.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: eluent（洗脱剂）与 eluant 同义，是更常见的拼写；mobile phase（流动相）强调在色谱系统中移动的相，范围更广。注意 eluate（洗脱液）指收集到的流出液，不是加入系统的洗脱剂。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Eluent is an exact synonym and the more usual spelling. Mobile phase emphasizes the phase moving through a chromatographic system and is a broader term. Eluate names the collected liquid leaving the system, rather than the eluant introduced into it.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 elu- 连到 elute“洗出”：eluant 是负责把吸附物带出来的流体。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect elu- with elute, to wash out: the eluant is the fluid that carries the adsorbed material out.

etymology_story.zh: 此词经拉丁语传入英语，源自希腊语 enneas（九个一组），其基础是 ennea（九）。它既可泛指九个组成的集合，也常以首字母大写形式用于古埃及九神组合等专名。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through Latin from Greek enneas, a group of nine, based on ennea, meaning nine. It can describe any set of nine and is often capitalized in names for groups such as an ancient Egyptian company of nine gods.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常视为整体借词；从古典构词看，ennea- 表示“九”，ennead- 是借入的词干，不宜机械地把末尾 -ad 当作自由使用的日常英语后缀。主要词族：enneads（复数），enneadic（九个一组的；与《九章集》有关的）；同数字词根的相关词有 enneagon（九边形）、enneagonal（九边形的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, ennead is normally treated as a borrowed whole word. In classical formation, ennea- means nine and ennead- is the borrowed stem; the ending -ad should not be treated as a freely productive everyday English suffix. Main family forms are enneads and enneadic; related words sharing the numerical base include enneagon and enneagonal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: nonet（九个一组）尤其常指九重奏、九重奏曲或九人乐团；group of nine（九个组成的一组）是中性的日常表达；ennead 更偏学术或文学语体，常见于宗教与哲学语境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nonet also means a group of nine, especially nine musicians or a composition for them. Group of nine is the neutral everyday expression. Ennead is more scholarly or literary and often occurs in religious or philosophical contexts.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ennea- 就是“九”：九位神站成一组，就是一个 ennead。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ennea- means nine: picture nine gods standing together as one ennead.

pronunciation.note: 单音节；元音为 /ɜː/，末尾 /st/ 紧接，不加元音。

forms: 副词，无时态或复数变化。
family: erstwhile 从前的；昔日的。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；erst + while → erstwhile（从前的）。

etymology.text: 源自古英语 ǣrest，原是 ǣr“早”的最高级形式；后来保留为表示“从前”的古雅副词。

usage_note: 古语或诗歌用语；普通交流通常说 formerly 或 once。

senses.meaning_zh: 从前；以前；昔日，属古语或诗歌用语
senses.meaning_en: Formerly or previously; archaic or poetic.
senses.english_definition: If something happened or was true erst, it happened or was true at an earlier time.
senses.collocation_zh: 从前被称为；昔日备受喜爱的
senses.sentence_en: The garden, erst beloved, now lay neglected.
senses.sentence_zh: 这座昔日备受喜爱的花园，如今已荒废无人照料。

etymology_story.zh: erst 源自古英语 ærest，原是表示“较早、以前”的 ær 的最高级形式，具有“最早、首先”的意思。后来它发展出“以前、从前”的用法，如今主要保留在古雅或诗歌语言中。
etymology_story.en: Erst comes from Old English ærest, originally the superlative of ær, meaning earlier or before, and carried the sense earliest or first. It later developed the meaning formerly and now survives mainly in archaic or poetic language.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 erst 是不可再作能产拆分的独立副词，不能把 -st 当作其现代最高级词尾。主要相关复合词为 erstwhile（从前的，形容词；从前，副词），可作 erst + while 的历史构词理解；erst 本身没有常用屈折变化或其他常用派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, erst is an independent adverb without a productive internal breakdown; its -st is not a modern superlative ending. Its main related compound is erstwhile, meaning former as an adjective or formerly as an adverb, historically understood as erst + while. Erst itself has no usual inflected forms or other common derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: formerly（从前）是中性且常用的对应词；previously（以前）强调某个参照时间之前；once（曾经）可表示过去某时的状态。erst 的时间意义相近，但具有明显的古语或诗歌色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Formerly is the neutral, common equivalent. Previously emphasizes a time before a reference point, while once can describe a state at some time in the past. Erst has a similar temporal meaning but a distinctly archaic or poetic tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“更早、最早”连到“从前”：erst 指向过去，erstwhile 也保留这条时间线。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect earlier and earliest with formerly: erst points back into the past, and erstwhile preserves that same time connection.

meaning: 可依法要求支付或履行的

pronunciation.note: 重音在首音节 /ɛk/，g 读 /dʒ/，末尾弱读 /əbəl/。

forms: 形容词，无名词复数或动词时态变化。
family: exigibility 可要求履行性。

morphology.text: exig-（要求、索取）+ -ible（可被……的）→ exigible（可被要求履行的）。

etymology.text: 17世纪从法语 exigible 借入；法语 exiger“要求”上溯拉丁语 exigere。想成一项已经可以向人提出的付款要求。

usage_note: 正式法律或财务文字用语，须结合具体义务和到期条件理解。

senses.meaning_zh: （法律或正式用语）可依法要求支付或履行的；可征收的
senses.meaning_en: (legal or formal) demandable as a legal right; payable or collectible
senses.english_definition: If a payment or obligation is exigible, someone has the legal right to demand that it be paid or fulfilled.
senses.collocation_zh: 可依法追索的债务；可依法征收的税款
senses.sentence_en: The debt becomes exigible on the date specified in the agreement.
senses.sentence_zh: 该债务自协议规定的日期起即可依法要求偿还。

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自法语 exigible，其词源可追溯至拉丁语 exigere，意为“索取、征收、要求”。它在法律和财务语境中表示某项款项或义务已可被依法要求支付或履行。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed exigible from French, ultimately from Latin exigere, meaning 'to demand, collect, or exact.' In legal and financial contexts, it describes a payment or obligation that can rightfully be demanded.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中可分析为受限词干 exig-（要求、索取）+ -ible（可被……的），但并不是由一个常用英语动词 exig 加后缀临时构成的。主要派生词为 exigibility（可依法要求履行或支付的性质）；exigent（紧迫的；苛求的）和 exigency（紧急情况；迫切需要）是同源词，并非由 exigible 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, the word can be analyzed as the bound stem exig- ('demand or exact') + -ible ('capable of being'), although it was borrowed rather than newly formed from an ordinary English verb exig. Its principal derivative is exigibility; exigent and exigency are related words from the same historical source, not direct derivatives of exigible.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: payable（应付的）侧重款项应当支付；due（到期应付的）侧重付款期限已经到来；enforceable（可依法强制执行的）侧重法律执行力。exigible 更专门强调权利人可以提出支付或履行要求。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Payable emphasizes that a sum is to be paid; due emphasizes that the time for payment has arrived; enforceable emphasizes the availability of legal enforcement. Exigible more specifically concerns the right to demand payment or performance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: exig- 表“索取”，-ible 表“可以被”：可以依法向你索取的。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link exig- with 'demand' and -ible with 'can be': something that can rightfully be demanded.

meaning: 扑通一声重重落下（或坐下）

pronunciation.note: 单音节；元音为 /ʌ/，词尾 /mp/ 连读。

forms: flumps；flumped；flumping。
family: flump 也可作名词，表示这类动作或声音。

morphology.text: flop（扑倒）+ plump（重重落下）→ flump（混成词，扑通落下）。

etymology.text: 19世纪初英语出现 flump，词典把它联系到 flop 与 plump 的混成及拟声。念出开头 fl- 和结尾 -ump，可联想重物落下的声音。

usage_note: 非正式用词，常与 down、onto 连用，强调沉重而突然的动作。

senses.meaning_zh: （非正式）扑通落下或坐下；把……重重放下
senses.meaning_en: (informal) to fall or sit down heavily, or put something down heavily
senses.english_definition: If you flump down somewhere, you let yourself fall or sit down heavily, and if you flump something down, you put it down heavily.
senses.collocation_en: flump down on the sofa; flump into a chair
senses.collocation_zh: 扑通坐到沙发上；一屁股坐进椅子里
senses.sentence_en: She flumped down on the sofa after a long day at work.
senses.sentence_zh: 忙碌了一整天后，她扑通一声坐到了沙发上。

senses.meaning_zh: （非正式，较少见）重物落下的闷响；扑通一声的落下
senses.meaning_en: (informal, less frequent) a heavy fall or the dull sound it makes
senses.english_definition: A flump is a heavy fall or the dull sound made when something lands heavily.
senses.collocation_en: with a flump; a soft flump
senses.collocation_zh: 扑通一声；轻轻的一声闷响
senses.sentence_en: The cushion landed on the floor with a soft flump.
senses.sentence_zh: 靠垫落到地板上，发出轻轻的一声闷响。

etymology_story.zh: flump 在19世纪初已有使用记录，通常被视为一个模仿沉重落地声的表现性词语，也常被解释为 flop 与 plump 的混成。其含义从“扑通落下”自然延伸到“重重坐下”或“重重放下”。
etymology_story.en: Flump is recorded from the early nineteenth century and is generally treated as an expressive imitation of a heavy landing, often explained as a blend of flop and plump. Its meaning extends naturally from falling heavily to sitting down heavily or putting something down with a thud.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 flump 是不可再按生产性词缀拆分的基本词；flop + plump 是可能的历史混成解释。动词屈折形式为 flumps、flumped、flumping；名词 flump 与动词同形，复数为 flumps，没有常用的进一步派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, flump is a simple base without productive internal affixes; flop + plump is a possible historical blending analysis. Verb forms are flumps, flumped, and flumping; the corresponding noun has the plural flumps, and there are no widely used further derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: flop（松垮地倒下）强调身体失去支撑或疲惫放松；plump（重重落下或坐下）强调突然下落；thud（砰的一声；发出闷响）强调声音。flump 把沉重动作与低沉落地声结合起来，语气常略带诙谐。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Flop emphasizes a loose or exhausted collapse; plump emphasizes a sudden heavy descent; thud emphasizes the dull impact sound. Flump combines the heavy movement with its sound and often has a mildly humorous tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 flop 的“倒下”和 plump 的“沉重”合起来：flump，就是“扑通”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Combine the collapse of flop with the weight of plump: flump means landing with a heavy 'whump.'

meaning: 加利亚德舞（文艺复兴时期的三拍子舞蹈）

pronunciation.note: 重音在首音节 /ɡæl/；后面接 /j/，末尾弱读 /əd/。

forms: 复数 galliards。
family: galliardise 欢乐、活泼（古语），与 galliard 同源。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；galliard（活泼的，旧时形容词义）+ -ness（性质、状态）→ galliardness（欢乐、活泼，旧用词）。舞蹈名 galliard 可联想轻快活泼的动作。

etymology.text: 源于古法语 gaillard“勇健、活泼”；英语把这股活泼劲用来命名动作轻快的舞蹈。

usage_note: 历史舞蹈术语；本卡教舞蹈义，通常为三拍子，曾流行于16、17世纪。

senses.meaning_zh: 加利亚德舞；这种文艺复兴时期的活泼三拍子舞蹈的配乐
senses.meaning_en: a lively Renaissance dance in triple time, or music for this dance
senses.english_definition: A galliard is a lively dance in triple time that was popular during the Renaissance, or a piece of music written for this dance.
senses.collocation_en: dance a galliard; a pavane and galliard

etymology_story.zh: galliard 经法语 gaillarde 传入英语，与 gaillard“活泼的、强健的”有关，法语舞名也与意大利语 gagliarda 有联系。这一名称体现了舞蹈中富有活力的步伐和跳跃；英语历史上也曾把 galliard 用作表示“活泼的、强健的”的形容词。
etymology_story.en: Galliard entered English through French gaillarde, associated with gaillard, meaning 'lively or vigorous,' and the French dance name is also connected with Italian gagliarda. The name reflects the dance's energetic steps and leaps; English also formerly used galliard as an adjective meaning 'lively or vigorous.'

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 galliard 是完整借入的基本词，不宜拆成 gall + -iard；名词复数为 galliards。历史词族包括形容词 galliard（活泼的、强健的，现已古旧）及其派生名词 galliardness（活泼、欢乐，古旧），现代通常只需掌握舞蹈及舞曲名词义。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, galliard is a borrowed base and should not be divided into gall + -iard; its noun plural is galliards. Its historical family includes the now-archaic adjective galliard ('lively or vigorous') and the derivative galliardness ('liveliness or gaiety'); current use chiefly concerns the dance and its music.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dance（舞蹈）和 dance tune（舞曲）是较宽泛的近义表达；jig（吉格舞或舞曲）同样常有轻快活泼的特点，但属于不同的舞蹈与音乐类型，不能作为 galliard 的严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dance and dance tune are broader near-equivalents. A jig can likewise be lively, but it names a different dance and musical type, so it is not an exact synonym of galliard.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 词源关键词是“活泼”：把 galliard 记成文艺复兴舞会上跳跃的三拍子。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor the word to its historical idea of 'lively': picture Renaissance dancers leaping to a triple beat.

senses.meaning_zh: （苏格兰及英格兰北部方言）抱怨，发牢骚；龇牙咧嘴，做怪相
senses.meaning_en: (Scottish and northern English dialect) to complain or grumble; to grimace or bare the teeth
senses.english_definition: If someone girns, they complain in an irritated way or twist their face into a grimace.
senses.collocation_en: girn about the weather; girn and greet
senses.collocation_zh: 抱怨天气；发牢骚又哭闹（greet 在这里是苏格兰方言中的“哭”）
senses.sentence_en: He's always girning about the weather.
senses.sentence_zh: 他总是在抱怨天气。

senses.meaning_zh: （苏格兰及英格兰北部方言，较少见）怪相；龇牙咧嘴的表情；牢骚
senses.meaning_en: (Scottish and northern English dialect, less frequent) a grimace, a distorted grin, or a complaint
senses.english_definition: A girn is a twisted facial expression or a grumbling complaint.
senses.collocation_en: a girn of displeasure; have a girn
senses.collocation_zh: 不悦的龇牙咧嘴表情；发一通牢骚
senses.sentence_en: He pulled a girn when he tasted the bitter medicine.
senses.sentence_zh: 他尝到苦药时，龇牙咧嘴地做了个怪相。

etymology_story.zh: girn 源于中古英语中与 grin 对应的形式，体现了元音与 r 的位置互换，即音位换位。它在苏格兰及英格兰北部保留下来，含义从“露齿、扭曲面部”发展到表示不满的“抱怨、发牢骚”。
etymology_story.en: Girn descends from a Middle English form corresponding to grin, with the vowel and r changing places through metathesis. It survived in Scots and northern English, developing from baring the teeth or contorting the face to expressing dissatisfaction by grumbling.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 girn 是不可再拆分的基本词，不含可分析的前后缀。动词形式为 girns、girned、girning；girn + -er → girner（发牢骚者），girning 也可表示抱怨这一行为；同形名词的复数为 girns。相关形式 gurn 常用于“做怪相”这一义项。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, girn is a simple base with no internal affixes. Verb forms are girns, girned, and girning; girn + -er gives girner ('someone who grumbles'), and girning can name the activity; the corresponding noun has the plural girns. The related form gurn is commonly associated with making distorted facial expressions.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: grumble（嘟囔着抱怨）强调低声或反复表达不满；whine（哼哼唧唧地抱怨）强调惹人厌烦的腔调；grimace（做痛苦或厌恶的怪相）强调面部动作。girn 在方言中可以连接“嘴上抱怨”与“脸上不满”两层意思。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Grumble suggests low-voiced or repeated dissatisfaction; whine emphasizes an irritating complaining tone; grimace concerns a facial expression of pain or disgust. In dialect use, girn can connect verbal complaint with a visibly displeased face.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: grin 换个音位成 girn：笑脸一扭，变成苦脸和牢骚。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Rearrange the sounds of grin into girn: the grin twists into a grimace, then into a grumble.

pronunciation.note: 重音在首音节 /ɡlɪs/，t 要发音。

forms: glisters；glistered；glistering。
family: glisteringly 闪耀地。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；glister + -ing + -ly → glisteringly（闪耀地）。

etymology.text: 14世纪进入英语，可能来自中古荷兰语 glisteren；它和现代 glitter 意思相近，适合记作古雅的“闪耀”。

usage_note: 古语或文学用词；日常英语更常用 glitter。

senses.meaning_zh: （文学用语或古雅用语）闪耀；闪闪发光
senses.meaning_en: (literary or archaic) to glitter or sparkle
senses.english_definition: If something glisters, it shines with bright flashes of light.
senses.collocation_en: glister in the sunlight; glister with gold
senses.collocation_zh: 在阳光下闪耀；因金饰而闪闪发光
senses.sentence_en: Dew glistered on the grass in the morning sun.
senses.sentence_zh: 露珠在晨光照耀的草地上闪闪发亮。

senses.meaning_zh: （文学用语，较少见）闪光；闪耀的光泽
senses.meaning_en: (literary, less frequent) glittering light or brilliance
senses.english_definition: The glister of something is its bright, sparkling appearance.
senses.collocation_en: the glister of gold; the glister of jewels
senses.collocation_zh: 黄金的闪耀光泽；珠宝的璀璨光芒
senses.sentence_en: The glister of the jewels caught her eye.
senses.sentence_zh: 珠宝闪耀的光芒吸引了她的目光。

etymology_story.zh: glister 可追溯到中古英语 glisteren，通常认为它与中古荷兰语及其他日耳曼语言中表示“闪耀”的相近形式有关，但具体借入路径并不完全确定。它保留了与 glitter 相近的意义，如今主要出现在文学或刻意古雅的表达中。
etymology_story.en: Glister goes back to Middle English glisteren and is generally connected with similar Middle Dutch and other Germanic forms meaning 'to shine,' although its precise route into English is uncertain. It retains a meaning close to glitter and now occurs chiefly in literary or deliberately archaic expression.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 glister 应作为基本词记忆，不宜把 gl-、-ist-、-er 当作可自由组合的词素。动词形式为 glisters、glistered、glistering；glistering 可作分词形容词，表示“闪耀的”；glistering + -ly → glisteringly（闪耀地，罕见）。名词 glister 与动词同形。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, glister should be treated as a base rather than divided into freely productive elements such as gl-, -ist-, and -er. Verb forms are glisters, glistered, and glistering; glistering can function as a participial adjective meaning 'sparkling'; glistering + -ly gives the rare adverb glisteringly. The noun has the same form as the verb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: glitter（闪闪发光）强调许多明亮的小闪光，是较通用的表达；sparkle（闪耀）强调活泼、跳动的小亮点；glisten（泛着亮光）常用于湿润或光滑表面。glister 与 glitter 最接近，但文学和古雅色彩更强。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Glitter emphasizes numerous bright flashes and is the more general expression; sparkle suggests lively points of light; glisten often describes a wet or smooth reflective surface. Glister is closest to glitter but carries a stronger literary or archaic flavor.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 glister 与 glitter 并排记：同样闪耀，glister 带着古典文学的光泽。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pair glister with glitter: the same bright flashes, expressed with an older literary voice.

pronunciation.note: 重音在首音节 /ɡɜː/，开头读 /ɡ/，不读 /ɡw/。

forms: 复数 guerdons；本卡教名词。
family: guerdon 也可作动词“酬报”；guerdoner 给予报酬的人。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；guerdon + -er → guerdoner（给予酬报的人）。

etymology.text: 中古英语从古法语 gueredon 借入，背后有日耳曼语“回报”的词；结尾又受到拉丁语 donum“礼物”的影响。把它记成回赠的奖赏。

usage_note: 诗歌或古雅文学用语，日常通常说 reward。

senses.meaning_zh: （文学或古雅用语）酬报；奖赏
senses.meaning_en: Literary or archaic: a reward or recompense.
senses.english_definition: A guerdon is something that someone receives as a reward for their service or achievement.
senses.chinese_definition: guerdon 指某人因服务或成就而获得的奖赏或酬报。
senses.collocation_en: a rich guerdon; receive a guerdon
senses.collocation_zh: 丰厚的酬报；获得奖赏
senses.sentence_en: The knight sought no guerdon for his service.
senses.sentence_zh: 那位骑士不求为自己的效劳获得任何酬报。

senses.meaning_zh: （文学或古雅用语）酬谢；奖赏
senses.meaning_en: Literary or archaic: to reward someone.
senses.english_definition: To guerdon someone means to give them a reward for something they have done.
senses.chinese_definition: guerdon 某人，意思是因其所做之事而给予奖赏。
senses.collocation_en: guerdon someone with something; richly guerdoned
senses.collocation_zh: 以某物酬谢某人；得到丰厚奖赏
senses.sentence_en: The king guerdoned the messenger with a purse of gold.
senses.sentence_zh: 国王赏给信使一袋金币。

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语从古法语 guerdon、gueredon 借入，通常认为其源头是日耳曼语中表示“回报、报偿”的词，词形又受到拉丁语 donum“礼物”的影响。英语先用它表示奖赏，后来也用作“给予奖赏”的动词。
etymology_story.en: Middle English borrowed the word from Old French guerdon or gueredon, generally traced to a Germanic word for repayment or recompense, with its form influenced by Latin donum, meaning “gift.” English used it for a reward and subsequently also as a verb meaning to reward.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 guerdon 是不可再作有效拆分的借词，可直接兼作名词和动词。词族包括 guerdons（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、guerdoned（过去式及过去分词）、guerdoning（现在分词），以及罕见的 guerdoner（给予奖赏者）；不要把词尾 -don 当作现代英语后缀。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, guerdon is an unanalyzable loanword functioning as both noun and verb. Its family includes guerdons, guerdoned, guerdoning, and the rare agent noun guerdoner, meaning someone who rewards; final -don is not a productive English suffix.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: reward（奖赏）最通用；recompense（酬报、补偿）强调对付出或损失的回报；guerdon 意义接近，但具有鲜明的文学和古雅色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Reward is the ordinary general term; recompense emphasizes a return for effort or compensation for loss. Guerdon has a similar meaning but a distinctly literary or archaic tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“付出之后得到回赠”：名词是酬报，动词是给予酬报。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think “a gift in return for service”: the noun is the reward, and the verb means to give it.

pronunciation.note: 主重音在 hawk；两个部分的元音分别为 /ɔː/ 和 /iː/。

forms: 复数 hawkweeds。
family: Hieracium 山柳菊属。

morphology.text: hawk（鹰）+ weed（草）→ hawkweed（山柳菊）。

etymology.text: 16世纪英语把拉丁语植物名 hieracium 译成 hawkweed；拉丁语名又来自希腊语 hierax“鹰”。看见名字就想到“鹰草”。

usage_note: 植物名称，花形常像蒲公英；相似花形不代表两者是同一属。

senses.meaning_zh: 山柳菊；山柳菊属及若干近缘属的菊科植物
senses.meaning_en: A plant of the genus Hieracium or certain related genera in the daisy family.
senses.english_definition: A hawkweed is a plant in the daisy family that usually has yellow or orange flowers resembling small dandelions.
senses.chinese_definition: hawkweed 指菊科的一类植物，通常开黄色或橙色花，花朵形似小蒲公英。
senses.collocation_zh: 橙花山柳菊；鼠耳山柳菊
senses.sentence_en: Orange hawkweed had spread across the meadow.
senses.sentence_zh: 橙花山柳菊已经蔓延到整片草甸。

etymology_story.zh: 英语在16世纪用 hawk“鹰”和 weed“草”组成这个植物名，对应拉丁语 hieracium；拉丁语名称来自与希腊语 hierax“鹰”有关的植物名。其命名传统与古人认为鹰会利用这种植物增强视力的说法有关。
etymology_story.en: English formed the plant name in the sixteenth century from hawk and weed, corresponding to Latin hieracium, a plant name derived from Greek and associated with hierax, meaning “hawk.” The naming tradition reflects an ancient belief that hawks used the plant to sharpen their sight.

morphology_enriched.zh: hawk（鹰）+ weed（草、野生草本植物）→ hawkweed，是名词加名词的复合词；复数为 hawkweeds。orange hawkweed 和 mouse-ear hawkweed 是植物名称短语，不是后缀派生词；本词没有常用的动词或形容词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Hawk + weed forms the noun–noun compound hawkweed; its plural is hawkweeds. Orange hawkweed and mouse-ear hawkweed are plant-name phrases rather than suffixal derivatives, and the word has no commonly used derived verb or adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Hieracium（山柳菊属）是相关植物的属名，但并不涵盖现代分类中所有称作 hawkweed 的植物；Pilosella（鼠耳山柳菊属）包括若干也称 hawkweed 的植物；dandelion（蒲公英）是外形相似的另一类植物，不是严格近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hieracium is a botanical genus associated with hawkweeds, but it does not include every plant now called hawkweed; Pilosella includes several other plants bearing the name. Dandelion names a similar-looking but different plant, not a true synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hawk“鹰”+ weed“草”：名字里的“鹰草”，实际是开菊状花的山柳菊。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hawk + weed gives “hawk plant”: picture a hawk beside a small, dandelion-like flower.

senses.meaning_zh: （罕见、旧式用语）日光信号器；日光反射信号或电文

senses.chinese_definition: helio 指利用反射日光发送信号的装置，也可指通过这种装置传送的信息。
senses.collocation_en: a helio station; send a helio
senses.collocation_zh: 日光信号站；发送日光信号电文

senses.meaning_zh: （罕见、旧式用语）用日光信号器发送；用反射日光通信
senses.meaning_en: Rare or historical: to signal or communicate by heliograph.
senses.english_definition: If you helio a message, you send it by reflecting sunlight with a heliograph.
senses.chinese_definition: helio 一条信息，意思是使用日光信号器反射阳光，将这条信息发送出去。
senses.collocation_en: helio a message; helio to a station
senses.collocation_zh: 用日光信号器发送信息；向某信号站发送日光信号
senses.sentence_en: The patrol helioed its position to the fort.
senses.sentence_zh: 巡逻队用日光信号器向堡垒报告了自己的位置。

etymology_story.zh: helio 是 heliograph“日光信号器；用日光信号器通信”的缩略形式，其源头是希腊语 hēlios“太阳”。随着日光信号通信的使用，这个简称也可指所发送的信号或信息。
etymology_story.en: Helio is a shortening of heliograph, the name of a sunlight-signalling instrument and the corresponding verb; its ultimate source is Greek hēlios, meaning “sun.” In the context of heliograph communication, the shortened noun could also refer to a transmitted signal or message.

morphology_enriched.zh: 独立词 helio 主要由 heliograph 截短而来，不应解释成一个完整的 helio- 加零后缀构词式。名词复数及动词第三人称单数为 helios，动词形式有 helioed、helioing；相关词包括 heliograph（日光信号器；以日光通信）、heliographic（日光信号的）、heliogram（日光信号电文），以及表示“太阳”的构词成分 helio-，如 heliocentric（以太阳为中心的）。
morphology_enriched.en: The independent word helio is chiefly a clipping of heliograph, rather than a transparent formation consisting of helio- plus a zero suffix. Its plural and third-person singular are helios, with verb forms helioed and helioing; related formations include heliograph, heliographic, heliogram, and words containing the combining form helio-, meaning “sun,” such as heliocentric.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: heliograph 是仪器及通信动作的完整名称；heliogram 专指通过日光信号器发送的电文；signal（信号）范围更广，并不限于反射日光。helio 是具有旧式通信背景的简称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Heliograph is the full term for the instrument and the signalling action; heliogram specifically denotes a message transmitted by heliograph. Signal is much broader and need not involve sunlight, whereas helio is a shortened term associated with historical communication.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: helio- 联想到太阳：把阳光反射出去，就把信息送出去。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect helio- with the sun: reflected sunshine carries the message.

senses.meaning_zh: （工业用语）粗切削机具；木材碎料机
senses.meaning_en: Industrial: a machine or tool that removes material rapidly or reduces wood to smaller pieces.
senses.english_definition: A hogger is a machine or cutting tool used to remove large amounts of material or break wood into smaller pieces.

etymology_story.zh: hogger 由 hog 加 -er 构成；“贪占者”义来自 hog 从“猪”发展出的动词义“贪婪地占用”。铁路中的“机车司机”义与把大型机车称为 hog 的俚语有关，工业义则与 hog 表示“大量粗切削、去除材料”的用法相连。
etymology_story.en: Hogger is formed from hog plus -er; the monopolizer sense comes from the verb hog, whose meaning developed from the animal name to greedy appropriation. The railroad sense is associated with hog as slang for a large locomotive, while industrial uses relate to hog meaning to remove material in large quantities.

morphology_enriched.zh: hog + -er → hogger：短元音后的词尾 g 双写，再加 -er；该后缀既可表示人，也可表示机器或工具。词族包括 hog、hogs、hogged、hogging、hogger、hoggers，以及 hoggish（贪婪自私的）、hoggishly（贪婪自私地）、hoggishness（贪婪自私）。
morphology_enriched.en: Hog + -er forms hogger, with final g doubled after the short vowel; -er can name either a person or a machine or tool. The family includes hog, hogs, hogged, hogging, hogger, hoggers, hoggish, hoggishly, and hoggishness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: monopolizer（独占者）最接近贪占义，较正式；hoarder（囤积者）强调积存而不愿舍弃，不一定抢占共享资源；locomotive engineer（机车司机）是铁路义的中性名称。这些词不能跨义项互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Monopolizer is a more formal equivalent for someone who takes exclusive control; hoarder emphasizes accumulating and keeping possessions rather than necessarily taking shared resources. Locomotive engineer is the neutral equivalent of the railroad sense; these alternatives are not interchangeable across senses.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hog“贪占、猛吃”+ -er：人把资源揽走，机器把材料大量“吃掉”；机车司机义另按铁路俚语记忆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hog + -er: a person takes the available resources, while a machine “eats through” material; remember the locomotive-driver sense as railroad slang.

pronunciation.note: 重音在第二音节 /sɛpt/，其中 c 读 /s/。

forms: incepts；incepted；incepting。
family: inceptor 摄入者或开始者，随专业语境解释。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；incept（摄入）+ -or（表示施事者的名词后缀）→ inceptor（摄入者）。

etymology.text: 19世纪英语取自拉丁语 inceptus，它来自 incipere“开始、着手”，更早由 in- 和 capere“拿取”组成；生物学中可联想把食物拿入体内。

usage_note: 罕见生物学用词，本卡只教摄食义；普通英语通常说 ingest。

senses.meaning_zh: （罕见、正式用语）开始；着手；发起
senses.meaning_en: Rare and formal: to begin or initiate.
senses.english_definition: To incept something means to begin it or bring it into existence.
senses.chinese_definition: incept 某事，意思是开始这件事，或使其产生。
senses.collocation_en: incept a project; incept a scheme
senses.collocation_zh: 启动项目；发起计划
senses.sentence_en: The organization was formed to incept and support new research projects.

senses.meaning_zh: （罕见，生物学用语）摄入；摄取食物
senses.meaning_en: Rare, in biology: to take in food or other material.
senses.english_definition: When an organism incepts food, it takes the food into its body or cell.
senses.chinese_definition: 生物体 incept 食物，意思是把食物摄入体内或细胞内。
senses.collocation_zh: 摄入食物；摄取食物颗粒
senses.sentence_en: The amoeba incepts food particles by surrounding them with pseudopodia.
senses.sentence_zh: 变形虫用伪足包围食物颗粒，将其摄入细胞内。

etymology_story.zh: incept 来自拉丁语 incipere“开始”的词干 incept-；incipere 由 in- 与 capere“拿取”构成。英语保留了“开始”的意义，生物学中的“摄入”则体现了“拿入、取入”的语义联系。
etymology_story.en: Incept comes from incept-, a stem of Latin incipere, meaning “to begin,” formed from in- and capere, meaning “to take.” English retained the sense of beginning, while the biological sense of ingestion reflects the associated idea of taking something in.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜将 incept 视为借入的拉丁词干，而不是由独立英语单词拼成；历史结构可写为 in- + -cept-（与“拿取”有关）。词族包括 incepts、incepted、incepting、inception（开始、创始）、inceptive（表示开始的）、inceptively（表示开始地），以及 inceptor（发起者；历史上亦指获准取得某些大学学位者）；inceptor 不宜直接解释为通常所说的“摄食者”。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, incept is best treated as a borrowed Latin stem, not a combination of independent English words; its historical structure is in- + -cept-, associated with taking. Its family includes incepts, incepted, incepting, inception, inceptive, inceptively, and inceptor, meaning a beginner or initiator and historically someone admitted to certain university degrees; inceptor should not be presented as the ordinary word for an organism that ingests food.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: begin（开始）最普通，可用于广泛语境；initiate（发起、启动）强调使某个过程开始；ingest（摄入）对应生物学义，也是现代科学表述中更通常的选择。incept 本身罕见，两个义项的近义词不能混用。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Begin is the ordinary, broadly applicable term; initiate emphasizes causing a process to start. Ingest corresponds to the biological sense and is the more usual choice in modern scientific writing; incept is rare, and the synonyms for its two senses are not interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 同一条“拿进来”的线索：把事情拿到手上就是着手，把食物拿进体内就是摄入。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use “take in” as the link: taking a task in hand suggests beginning it, while taking food into the body means ingesting it.

senses.pos: v. 动词（indwell 的过去式和过去分词，主要用于宗教或文学语境）
senses.meaning_zh: 居于……之内；内在地存在于
senses.meaning_en: Lived or existed within someone or something, especially as a spiritual presence.
senses.english_definition: If a spirit or power indwelt someone, it lived or was present within that person.
senses.chinese_definition: 如果某种灵或力量居于某人体内，它就在这个人的内在生命中存在。
senses.collocation_en: indwelt by the Holy Spirit; indwelt by God
senses.collocation_zh: 有圣灵内住的；有上帝内住的
senses.sentence_en: They believed that the Holy Spirit indwelt every believer.
senses.sentence_zh: 他们相信圣灵住在每一位信徒里面。

etymology_story.zh: indwell 由表示“在内”的 in- 与本土动词 dwell“居住”组合而成，后来尤其用于描述神灵或精神力量的内在存在。indwelt 沿用了 dwell → dwelt 的不规则过去时变化。
etymology_story.en: Indwell combines in-, meaning 'within', with the native English verb dwell, meaning 'live or reside', and became particularly associated with an inward spiritual presence. Indwelt follows the irregular pattern dwell → dwelt.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：in-（在内）+ dwell（居住）→ indwell；indwelt 是其不规则过去式及过去分词，不应拆成 ind + welt。词族及屈折形式：indwell、indwells、indwelling、indwelt，以及另一过去形式 indwelled；indwelling 也可作形容词，表示“内住的”，或作名词，表示“内住”。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: in- ('within') + dwell ('reside') → indwell; indwelt is its irregular past tense and past participle, not a combination of ind and welt. The family and inflections include indwell, indwells, indwelling, indwelt, and the alternative past form indwelled; indwelling also functions as an adjective meaning 'dwelling within' and a noun meaning 'an inward spiritual presence'.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: inhabited（居住于）强调占据某个居所；resided within（存在或居住于内部）较中性；pervaded（遍及、弥漫于）强调影响充满整体。indwelt 更突出内在的持续存在，且常带宗教意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Inhabited emphasizes occupying a dwelling or place; resided within is a more neutral expression for being located inside; pervaded emphasizes spreading throughout something. Indwelt particularly suggests an abiding inward presence, often with religious meaning.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: in = 在内，dwelt = 曾居住：indwelt 就是“住在里面了”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: In means 'inside' and dwelt means 'lived': indwelt means 'lived within'.

pronunciation.note: 主重音在第三音节 /kɑː/，首音节带次重音。

forms: 通常作文字系统名称，不加复数词尾。
family: kana 假名；hiragana 平假名。

morphology.text: 日语 kata（片、部分）+ kana（假名）→ katakana（片假名），英语整词借入。

etymology.text: 从日语 katakana 借入，由 kata 与 kana 组成；字形取汉字的一部分，可用“片段式的假名”来记。

usage_note: 日语的一套音节文字，常用于外来词等；英语普通名词 katakana 通常小写。

senses.meaning_zh: 片假名（日语的一套表音文字，常用于外来词等）
senses.meaning_en: A Japanese phonetic script commonly used for loanwords and certain other purposes.
senses.english_definition: Katakana is a set of Japanese written characters used especially for foreign words, foreign names, and emphasis.
senses.chinese_definition: 片假名是日语使用的一套文字，尤其用于书写外来词、外国人名以及需要强调的内容。
senses.collocation_zh: 用片假名书写；片假名字符
senses.sentence_en: Foreign names are usually written in katakana in Japanese.

etymology_story.zh: 英语从日语 katakana（片仮名）借入此词，其中 kata 表示“片、部分”，kana 表示“假名”。片假名在日本早期用作注音和阅读辅助，其字形多取自汉字的一部分。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed katakana from Japanese, where kata means 'part or fragment' and kana means 'kana character'. The script developed in Japan as an aid to pronunciation and reading, with its characters largely taken from portions of Chinese characters.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整词借入的独立词项；日语内部结构为 kata（片、部分）+ kana（假名）。英语通常将其用作不可数名词，以 katakana characters 表示单个字符；katakana writing 等结构中的 katakana 是名词作定语，不必另列形容词词性，常用英语派生词较少。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, katakana is a borrowed lexical unit; its Japanese structure is kata ('part or fragment') + kana ('kana character'). It is normally an uncountable noun, with katakana characters referring to individual symbols; in expressions such as katakana writing, it is an attributive noun rather than a separate adjective, and it has few common English derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 此词没有常用的严格同义词。kana（假名）是包含片假名和平假名的上位词；hiragana（平假名）是另一套假名；kanji（汉字）指日语使用的汉字，不能与 katakana 互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym. Kana is the broader term covering both katakana and hiragana; hiragana is the other kana script; kanji refers to the Chinese characters used in Japanese and is not interchangeable with katakana.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: kata“片”+ kana“假名”：取汉字的一片，形成片假名。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Kata means 'fragment': fragments of Chinese characters became katakana.

etymology.text: 15世纪的英语词，词典将它联系到 caggen“固定”；想象先固定一个小锚，再沿锚索把船拉过去。

senses.meaning_en: To move a vessel by hauling on a rope or cable attached to an anchor.
senses.english_definition: If sailors kedge a boat, they move it by placing an anchor some distance away and pulling on the rope or cable attached to it.

etymology_story.zh: kedge 在中古英语晚期已有用作航海动词的记录，后来也用于指这种操作所用的轻锚。其更早来源并不确定，有词源解释将它与表示“固定、系牢”的中古英语 caggen 联系起来。
etymology_story.en: Kedge is recorded as a nautical verb in late Middle English and later also named the light anchor used in the operation. Its earlier origin is uncertain, although some accounts connect it with Middle English caggen, meaning 'fasten or secure'.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 kedge 是不可再作常规词缀分析的词基，可作名词和动词。屈折形式为 kedges、kedged、kedging；加 -ed 或 -ing 时去掉词尾不发音的 e；kedging 也可作名词，表示“用小锚移船的操作”，另有复合词 kedge anchor（小锚）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, kedge is a base without a productive prefix–root–suffix breakdown and functions as both noun and verb. Its inflections are kedges, kedged, and kedging; the final silent e is dropped before -ed or -ing. Kedging can also name the operation, and kedge anchor is an established compound.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: light anchor（轻锚）是名词义的概括性释义；warp（用缆索移船）与动词义接近，但缆索也可固定在岸上；tow（拖带）通常依靠另一艘船或外部动力牵引。kedge 特指利用预先放置的锚来牵移船只。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Light anchor is a broad paraphrase of the noun; warp is close to the verb but can involve a line secured ashore; tow usually involves pulling by another vessel or an external source of power. Kedge specifically involves moving a vessel using an anchor placed ahead of it.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先把小锚送到前面，再拉锚索：锚先走，船跟上。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Send the little anchor ahead, then pull: the anchor leads and the boat follows.

etymology.text: 19世纪英语（1880–1885年）把 lactone 和 amide 缩合命名为 lactam；名称提醒你，它与环状结构和酰胺有关。

usage_note: 化学术语，指环状酰胺；不能把内酰胺与内酯混用。

senses.english_definition: A lactam is a chemical compound in which an amide group forms part of a ring of atoms.

etymology_story.zh: lactam 是十九世纪化学命名中由 lactone（内酯）和 amide（酰胺）的部分形式组合而成的名称，用于指环状酰胺。它在名称上与内酯相联系，但内酰胺含酰胺结构，内酯则含酯结构。
etymology_story.en: Lactam arose in nineteenth-century chemical nomenclature by combining parts of lactone and amide to name cyclic amides. The name links it with lactones, but lactams contain an amide linkage whereas lactones contain an ester linkage.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词来源为 lact(one) + am(ide) → lactam，属于截取混成；现代英语通常将 lactam 作为完整化学词基使用。词族及相关构词包括 lactams（复数）、lactamization（内酰胺化）、β-lactam（β-内酰胺）和 β-lactamase（β-内酰胺酶）；这里不能把 lact- 简单理解为“该物质来自乳汁”。
morphology_enriched.en: The formation is lact(one) + am(ide) → lactam, a clipped blend; modern English generally treats lactam as a complete chemical base. Its family and related formations include lactams, lactamization, β-lactam, and β-lactamase. The element lact- does not imply that the compound comes from milk.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cyclic amide（环状酰胺）是直接同义表达；amide（酰胺）是上位词，既包括环状也包括非环状结构；lactone（内酯）是结构相关的比较词，指环状酯，并非同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cyclic amide is a direct synonym; amide is the broader term and includes both cyclic and acyclic structures; lactone is a related structural comparison meaning 'cyclic ester', not a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: lactone 的“成环”联想，加上 amide 的“酰胺”：环里的酰胺就是 lactam。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Take the ring association of lactone and the amide linkage of amide: a lactam is an amide in a ring.

etymology.text: 19世纪命名，词典将它联系到希腊语 leimon“草地”，可能是对更早德语“草地矿石”名称的翻译。想成潮湿草地中发现的褐色铁矿。

etymology_story.zh: 英语从法语 limonite 借入这一十九世纪的矿物名称，其词源与希腊语 leimōn“草地、湿草地”有关，呼应了湿地中形成的铁矿沉积。现代矿物学通常将褐铁矿视为以针铁矿为主的混合物，而不是具有固定成分的独立矿物种。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the nineteenth-century mineral name from French limonite, ultimately connected with Greek leimōn, meaning 'meadow or wet meadow', in reference to iron deposits associated with wet ground. Modern mineralogy generally treats limonite as a mixture chiefly containing goethite rather than as a distinct mineral species with a fixed composition.

morphology_enriched.zh: 从历史构词看，limon-（与希腊语“草地”有关）+ -ite（矿物名称后缀）构成 limonite；现代英语中它主要是整词借入的专业词，limon- 不是常用的自由词根。词族包括 limonitic（含褐铁矿的；褐铁矿质的）和 limonitization（褐铁矿化作用）。
morphology_enriched.en: Historically, limon- (connected with Greek 'meadow') combines with the mineral-name suffix -ite to form limonite. In modern English it is principally a borrowed technical term, and limon- is not a common free-standing root. Its family includes limonitic ('containing or resembling limonite') and limonitization ('formation of or alteration into limonite').

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: brown iron ore（褐色铁矿石）是传统近义名称；bog iron（沼铁矿）强调湿地中的形成环境，成分不一定与褐铁矿完全相同；goethite（针铁矿）是确定的矿物种，也是褐铁矿的主要成分，不能直接等同于整个混合体。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Brown iron ore is a traditional near-synonym; bog iron emphasizes formation in wetland environments and need not have exactly the same composition; goethite is a defined mineral species and the chief constituent of limonite, not an exact synonym for the mixture.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 湿草地的 meadow 联想，加上矿物后缀 -ite：记住湿地里的黄褐色铁矿。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect 'wet meadow' with the mineral suffix -ite: picture yellow-brown iron deposits in wet ground.

etymology_story.zh: 该词承自古英语 lungenwyrt，由表示“肺”的成分和 wyrt（植物、草本）构成。植物或地衣的外观被认为类似肺组织，因此其名称与旧时治疗肺部疾病的用途产生了联系。
etymology_story.en: The word descends from Old English lungenwyrt, combining an element meaning “lung” with wyrt, meaning “plant” or “herb.” The appearance of the plants or lichens was associated with lung tissue, linking their names with their former use for lung complaints.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：lung（肺）+ wort（草本植物，现主要保留在植物名称中）→ lungwort。词族及屈折形式：lungworts（复数）；没有常用的直接派生动词、形容词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: lung + wort, an element meaning “herb” that now survives chiefly in plant names. The plural is lungworts; there are no common directly derived verbs, adjectives, or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pulmonaria（肺草属植物）对应开花植物义；spotted dog（斑点狗，肺草的民间俗名）强调斑叶外观；tree lungwort（树肺衣）专指地衣义，不能与肺草属植物混同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pulmonaria identifies the flowering-plant group; spotted dog is a folk name referring to the spotted leaves of common lungwort; tree lungwort identifies the lichen and must be distinguished from the flowering plant.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: lung“肺”+ wort“草”：外观让人联想到肺的植物或地衣。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Lung + wort: a plant or lichen whose appearance suggested lungs.

pronunciation.note: 重音在首音节 /meɪ/，末尾弱读 /lə/。

family: malar bone 颧骨；zygomatic 颧骨的。

morphology.text: 拉丁语 mal-（颊、颌）+ -ar（……的）→ malar（颧部的、颊部的）。

etymology.text: 18世纪英语借入新拉丁语 malaris，它来自拉丁语 mala“颊、颌”；把位置记在面颊上。

usage_note: 解剖及医学描述用语，常修饰区域、骨或皮疹等；本卡只考部位意义。

senses.meaning_zh: 颧部的；颊部的；颧骨的

senses.meaning_zh: 颧骨（解剖学用语）
senses.meaning_en: The cheekbone or zygomatic bone

etymology_story.zh: 英语在18世纪借入新拉丁语 malaris，后者源于拉丁语 māla（面颊）。该词先表示与面颊有关的部位，也可作为名词指构成面颊隆起的颧骨。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word in the eighteenth century from New Latin malaris, derived from Latin māla, meaning “cheek.” It describes structures associated with the cheek and also functions as a noun for the cheekbone.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常将 malar 作为完整的解剖学词干；历史结构为拉丁语 māl-（面颊）+ -āris（……的），对应英语形式 -ar。词族及相关构词：malars（名词复数）、submalar（颧下的）、malarplasty（颧骨整形术）；这里的 mal- 不表示“坏”。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats malar as a complete anatomical base; historically it contains Latin māl- “cheek” + -āris “relating to,” represented by English -ar. Family and related formations include malars, submalar, and malarplasty; this mal- does not mean “bad.”

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: zygomatic（颧骨的）更明确指向颧骨及其相关结构；buccal（颊部的）常用于口腔侧的颊部组织；cheekbone（颧骨）是名词义更日常的对应表达。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Zygomatic refers more specifically to the cheekbone and associated structures; buccal often concerns the cheek tissues on the oral side; cheekbone is the everyday equivalent of the noun malar.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 malar 固定在面颊隆起处：形容词指颧部，名词指颧骨。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor malar to the prominence of the cheek: the adjective describes the area, and the noun names its bone.

senses.meaning_zh: 无足鸟；纹章中通常不画脚、形似燕子的鸟形图案
senses.meaning_en: A heraldic bird resembling a swallow and conventionally shown without feet
senses.english_definition: A martlet is a small bird shown on a coat of arms, usually resembling a swallow and represented without feet.
senses.collocation_zh: 纹章无足鸟；三只纹章无足鸟
senses.sentence_en: The shield bears three gold martlets on a blue field.
senses.sentence_zh: 盾形纹章的蓝色底面上绘有三只金色无足鸟。

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自法语 martelet，与 martinet、martin 等燕类鸟名有关，带有“小鸟”的指小意味。英语后来将它专门用于纹章中通常不画脚的鸟形图案。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from French martelet, associated with bird names such as martinet and martin and carrying a diminutive sense. In English it became a specialized term for the conventionally footless bird depicted in heraldry.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常将 martlet 作为整体词处理；词尾外形与指小后缀 -let 相似，但 mart- 不是能独立表示“鸟”的现代英语词根。复数为 martlets；无常用的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats martlet as a lexical whole. Its ending resembles the diminutive suffix -let, but mart- is not an independent modern English root meaning “bird.” The plural is martlets, and there are no common direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: heraldic swallow（纹章燕）是便于理解的近义描述；swallow（燕子）指真实鸟类，不含无足的绘画惯例；martin（燕类鸟）与其名称和形象相关，但并非该纹章图案的严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Heraldic swallow is a useful descriptive near-equivalent; swallow names a real bird without implying the footless convention; martin is related in name and appearance but is not an exact synonym for the heraldic figure.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想到 martin 一类的小燕子，再去掉脚：纹章里的 martlet。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a small martin-like bird, then omit its feet: a heraldic martlet.

etymology.text: 中古英语 mercerie 来自古法语同形词，关联 mercer“经营布料的商人”；想象街边摆满丝绸布匹的店。

senses.meaning_zh: 绸布、服饰等商品，尤指优质织物（历史用语）

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语 mercerie 借自古法语，指商人经营的货物及其买卖，与 mercer（绸布商）属于同一词族，最终可追溯到拉丁语 merx（商品）。英语中的用法逐渐集中于织物，尤其是优质布料及相关商品，并延伸指店铺。
etymology_story.en: Middle English mercerie was borrowed from Old French for merchants' goods or their trade and belongs to the same family as mercer, ultimately from Latin merx, meaning “merchandise.” English usage became especially associated with fine textiles and related goods and also extended to the shop selling them.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 mercer（绸布商）+ -y（表示行业、货物或场所）→ mercery，但整个词历史上由法语借入。核心词族：mercer、mercers（绸布商的复数）、mercery、merceries（店铺义复数）；商品和行业义通常不可数。
morphology_enriched.en: A modern analysis is mercer + -y, with the ending denoting a trade, its goods, or a place, although the whole word was historically borrowed from French. The core family comprises mercer, mercers, mercery, and merceries, the plural for shops; the goods and trade senses are normally uncountable.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: drapery（布匹或布业）与其织物义接近，但各地区用法不同；haberdashery（缝纫用品或男士服饰）与其商品范围部分重叠；textile trade（纺织品贸易）范围更广，且是现代通用表达。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Drapery overlaps with the cloth and cloth-trade senses, though regional usage varies; haberdashery overlaps in sewing goods or clothing accessories; textile trade is broader and is a current general expression.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 mercer“绸布商”出发：他卖的货、做的生意和开的店，都可叫 mercery。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with mercer, a cloth merchant: mercery can name the goods, the business, or the shop.

etymology.text: 17世纪英语从西班牙语 mirador 借入，关联 mirar“看”；继续可追溯到拉丁语 mirari“惊叹”。站到楼台向外看，便能记住。

usage_note: 常用于西班牙语地区的建筑或景观描述，重点是可眺望四周的高处、阳台或楼台。

senses.meaning_zh: 观景台；观景楼、塔或楼台

senses.english_definition: A mirador is a tower, balcony, or other elevated structure from which you can look out over the surrounding area.

etymology_story.zh: 英语在17世纪从西班牙语借入 mirador，该词来自 mirar（看），本义是供人观看远处的地方。Mirar 最终源于拉丁语 mīrārī（惊叹、赞叹），经历了从“惊叹地看”到一般“看”的语义变化。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed mirador from Spanish in the seventeenth century; it comes from mirar, meaning “to look,” and names a place for looking out. Mirar ultimately derives from Latin mīrārī, meaning “to wonder at” or “admire,” reflecting a shift from wondering at something to looking at it.

morphology_enriched.zh: 英语中为整体借词；在西班牙语中可分析为 mir-（看）+ -ador（构成人或器物等名称的后缀），在本词中表示观景处。英语复数通常为 miradors，也可见保留西班牙语形式的 miradores；无常用的英语直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: It is a whole-word borrowing in English. In Spanish, mir- “look” combines with -ador, a suffix forming names of agents or instruments and, here, a place for looking out. English plurals include miradors and the retained Spanish form miradores; there are no common direct English derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: lookout（瞭望处）强调观察周围，常带警戒意味；viewpoint（观景点）不一定有建筑设施；belvedere（观景楼、观景亭）强调为赏景而建的建筑，与 mirador 最接近。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lookout emphasizes observation and may suggest keeping watch; viewpoint need not include any built structure; belvedere emphasizes a structure built to enjoy a view and is the closest architectural equivalent.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: mirar“看”→ mirador“登高向外看的地方”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Mirar means “look”: a mirador is a raised place for looking out.

etymology_story.zh: 英语在19世纪借入德语矿物名 Monazit，其词源与希腊语 monazein（独处）有关。这个名称指向该矿物最初被注意到的零散、孤立晶体。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the German mineral name Monazit in the nineteenth century; its origin is connected with Greek monazein, meaning 'to be alone.' The name refers to the isolated crystals in which the mineral was initially observed.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史构词可分析为 monaz-（源自希腊语，表示独处）+ -ite（矿物名称后缀）；现代英语通常将 monazite 作为完整矿物名使用。相关形式：monazites（复数，指不同种类或样品）、monazitic（独居石的；含独居石的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Historically, the formation is monaz- (from Greek, referring to being alone) + -ite (a mineral-name suffix); modern English generally treats monazite as a complete mineral name. Related forms include monazites, a plural for varieties or specimens, and monazitic, meaning 'of or containing monazite.'

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 无常用精确同义词。rare-earth phosphate（稀土磷酸盐）是更宽泛的类别名称；bastnäsite（氟碳铈矿）和 xenotime（磷钇矿）也是稀土矿物，但成分、晶体结构不同，不能与独居石互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym. Rare-earth phosphate is a broader category; bastnäsite and xenotime are other rare-earth minerals, but their compositions and crystal structures differ, so their names are not interchangeable with monazite.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: monaz- 联想“独处”，-ite 标记矿物：独自出现的晶体 → 独居石。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect monaz- with 'being alone' and -ite with minerals: an isolated crystal points to monazite.

forms: 复数 mondes；单数 monde。
family: monde 社交圈；beau monde 上流社会

morphology.text: monde + -s → mondes（多个社交圈）；这里的 -s 是复数词尾，monde 作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 英语借入法语 monde（世界、社会），上溯拉丁语 mundus（世界）。把不同社交圈想成各自的小世界，便能记住这个文学用词。

usage_note: 罕见的文学用语；本卡采用 monde 的“社交圈”义及其复数。日常可说 social circles。不是把法语“世界”的所有用法都搬入英语。

senses.pos: n. 复数名词（罕见文学用法）
senses.meaning_zh: 社交圈；社会圈层；不同的社会小世界
senses.meaning_en: Social circles or distinct social worlds, in rare literary usage.
senses.english_definition: Mondes are different social circles or social worlds whose members share a particular way of life.
senses.collocation_zh: 时尚社交圈；文学圈（均为罕见文学性组合）
senses.sentence_en: Her memoir moves between the mondes of artists and aristocrats.
senses.sentence_zh: 她的回忆录穿梭于艺术家和贵族各自的社交世界。

etymology_story.zh: mondes 是英语借词 monde 的复数；monde 来自法语，意为“世界；社会”，上溯拉丁语 mundus（世界）。英语中的文学用法把某个社会圈层看作一个独立的“小世界”。
etymology_story.en: Mondes is the plural of the English borrowing monde, from French monde, meaning 'world' or 'society,' ultimately from Latin mundus, 'world.' Its literary social meaning treats a particular circle as a distinct little world.

morphology_enriched.zh: monde（世界；社会圈）+ -s（复数词尾）→ mondes；-s 是屈折词尾，不是派生后缀。相关表达有 beau monde（上流社会）和 demi-monde（历史上指处于体面社会边缘的社交阶层）；这些表达不是 mondes 的直接派生词。此词罕见，没有常用的高频固定搭配。
morphology_enriched.en: Monde ('world; social circle') + -s (plural ending) → mondes; -s is inflectional rather than derivational. Related expressions include beau monde ('fashionable society') and demi-monde (historically, a social group on the fringes of respectable society); these are not direct derivatives of mondes. The word is rare and has no common high-frequency fixed collocations.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: circles（圈子）最普通，强调具有共同关系或兴趣的人群；milieus（社会环境）更强调周围的文化和生活背景；social worlds（社会小世界）突出各圈层各有规范和生活方式，最接近 mondes 的文学意象。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Circles is the ordinary term for groups linked by relationships or interests; milieus emphasizes surrounding social and cultural environments; social worlds highlights groups with their own norms and ways of life, closely matching the literary image in mondes.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一个 monde 是一个“小世界”；加 -s，就是多个各有生活方式的社交世界。
mnemonic_anchor.en: One monde is a little world; add -s to picture several social worlds, each with its own way of life.

morphology.text: morula + -ation → morulation（桑椹胚形成，词尾 a 合并）；morula 作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 英语借入新拉丁语 morula，源于拉丁语 morum（桑椹）与小称词尾 -ula。早期胚胎像一颗细胞紧密聚集的小桑椹。

usage_note: 胚胎学术语，指早期细胞形成的实心团；注意区别于后续具有腔隙的囊胚阶段。

senses.meaning_zh: 桑椹胚；受精卵卵裂后形成的实心细胞团
senses.meaning_en: A solid ball of cells formed during early embryonic cleavage.
senses.english_definition: A morula is an early embryo consisting of a compact ball of cells formed as a fertilized egg divides.
senses.collocation_zh: 桑椹胚期；致密化桑椹胚
senses.sentence_en: The embryo reached the morula stage before developing into a blastocyst.
senses.sentence_zh: 这个胚胎先达到桑椹胚期，随后发育成囊胚。

etymology_story.zh: morula 来自新拉丁语，取自拉丁语 morum（桑椹）的小称形式，字面意思是“小桑椹”。这个名称形容早期胚胎紧密聚集的细胞在外观上像桑椹。
etymology_story.en: Morula comes from New Latin, using a diminutive of Latin morum, 'mulberry,' to mean 'little mulberry.' The name describes the resemblance between a mulberry and the tightly clustered cells of an early embryo.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史构词为 mor-（桑椹）+ -ula（拉丁语小称后缀）；现代英语把 morula 作为完整的专业名词使用。相关形式：morulae 或 morulas（复数）、morular（桑椹胚的；桑椹状的）、morulation（桑椹胚形成）；morular 和 morulation 使用去掉词尾 -a 的词干 morul-。
morphology_enriched.en: The historical formation is mor- ('mulberry') + -ula (a Latin diminutive suffix); modern English treats morula as a complete technical noun. Related forms include morulae or morulas (plurals), morular ('relating to a morula; mulberry-shaped'), and morulation ('formation of a morula'); morular and morulation use the stem morul-, without final -a.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 无常用精确同义词。embryo（胚胎）是上位词；blastula（囊胚）通常指形成内部腔隙的后续阶段；blastocyst（哺乳动物囊胚）指哺乳动物具有囊胚腔和分化细胞群的阶段，均不能直接替换 morula。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym. Embryo is the broader term; blastula generally denotes a later stage with an internal cavity; blastocyst denotes the mammalian stage with a cavity and differentiated cell populations. Neither later-stage term is interchangeable with morula.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “小桑椹”就是外形线索：细胞紧密成团 → 桑椹胚。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The 'little mulberry' supplies the visual clue: tightly packed cells form a morula.

usage_note: 本卡选“起源于肌肉”的义项；描述肌肉形成的相关义不作为本题答案。

etymology_story.zh: myogenic 是科学英语用希腊语来源的 myo-（肌肉，源于 mys）和 -genic（表示产生或起源）组成的词。它既可描述活动起源于肌肉，也可描述肌肉组织的形成和发育。
etymology_story.en: Myogenic was formed in scientific English from Greek-derived myo-, 'muscle,' from mys, and -genic, expressing production or origin. It can describe activity originating in muscle or processes involved in muscle formation and development.

morphology_enriched.zh: myo-（肌肉）+ -genic（起源于……的；与生成有关的）→ myogenic。相关词族包括 myogenically（以肌源性方式）、myogenesis（肌肉发生；肌肉形成）和 myogenetic（与肌肉发生有关的）；这些词共享 myo- 与表示发生、生成的词素。
morphology_enriched.en: Myo- ('muscle') + -genic ('originating in; relating to production') → myogenic. The related family includes myogenically ('in a myogenic manner'), myogenesis ('muscle formation or development'), and myogenetic ('relating to myogenesis'); these share myo- and elements expressing origin or formation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: muscle-derived（来源于肌肉的）强调来源，适合部分肌源性语境；muscle-forming（形成肌肉的）对应生肌、成肌这一义项；myogenetic（肌肉发生的）主要强调肌肉发育过程，通常不用于替代描述血管肌源性反应的 myogenic。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Muscle-derived emphasizes origin and fits some source-related uses; muscle-forming corresponds to the developmental sense; myogenetic chiefly concerns muscle development and is generally unsuitable as a replacement when describing a vascular myogenic response.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: myo- 是“肌肉”，-genic 连接“来源或生成”：来自肌肉，或生成肌肉。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Myo- means 'muscle'; -genic links it to origin or formation: arising from muscle or forming muscle.

etymology.text: 19世纪英语按美国加州的地名 Napa 给这种软皮革命名，随后也写作 nappa。用“地名变成皮革名”来记。

usage_note: 指柔软的皮革，常用于手套或服装；nappa 一般小写，地名 Napa 首字母大写。

etymology_story.zh: nappa 是 napa 的拼写变体，名称源于美国加利福尼亚州的 Napa，当地在19世纪生产了这种柔软皮革。这个地名后来成为皮革名称，使用范围逐渐扩展到多种柔软皮革。
etymology_story.en: Nappa is a spelling variant of napa, named after Napa, California, where this soft leather was produced in the nineteenth century. The place name became a leather term whose use later broadened to various soft leathers.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 nappa 是不可进一步拆分的名词词基，通常作不可数名词；napa 是其拼写变体。常见组合有 nappa leather（纳帕软革）和 nappa-lined（衬有纳帕皮革的）；nappa-like（像纳帕皮革的）是可按需构成的形容词，没有常用的独立派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, nappa is an unanalyzable noun base, normally used as a mass noun; napa is a spelling variant. Common combinations include nappa leather and nappa-lined ('lined with nappa'); nappa-like is a freely formed adjective meaning 'resembling nappa.' There is no common independent family of derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: napa 是相同皮革名称的另一种拼写；soft leather（软皮革）是更宽泛的描述，不限定皮革类别；lambskin（羔羊皮）限定原料来源，而 nappa 也可由其他动物皮制成，因此两者不能完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Napa is an alternative spelling of the same leather name; soft leather is a broader description that does not specify a leather type; lambskin specifies the animal source, whereas nappa can also be made from other hides or skins, so the terms are not fully interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Napa 地名 → nappa 皮革名；把名称与柔软、光滑的皮革触感相连。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Napa the place gives nappa the leather: connect the name with a soft, smooth leather texture.

forms: 岩石材料名词；指种类或岩样时可用复数 norites。
family: noritic 苏长岩的

morphology.text: norite + -ic → noritic（苏长岩的，去 e）；norite 整词作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 英语借入挪威语 norit，由 Norge（挪威）和岩石名称词尾 -it 构成。记住它是以挪威命名的一种岩石。

usage_note: 地质术语，属于辉长岩类，通常含斜长石和斜方辉石；不指沉积形成的砂岩。

senses.meaning_zh: 苏长岩：主要由斜长石和斜方辉石组成的深成火成岩
senses.meaning_en: A plutonic igneous rock composed chiefly of plagioclase and orthopyroxene
senses.english_definition: Norite is a coarse-grained igneous rock that consists mainly of plagioclase feldspar and orthopyroxene.
senses.collocation_zh: 层状苏长岩；苏长岩侵入体
senses.sentence_en: The samples were identified as norite because they contained abundant plagioclase and orthopyroxene.

etymology_story.zh: 该词借自挪威语 noritt，其名称以挪威国名 Norge 为基础，并加上岩石名称中常见的词尾。它以地理名称命名，后来成为一种特定深成岩的地质学名称。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Norwegian noritt, a name based on Norge, meaning Norway, with a suffix used in rock names. A geographical reference thus became the geological name for a particular plutonic rock.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 norite 作为完整词基，不宜拆成普通英语词根与前缀。复数：norites；形容词：norite 去末尾 e 加 -ic → noritic（苏长岩的）。norite intrusion 中的 norite 是名词作定语，不构成独立的常用形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, norite functions as a whole base rather than a transparent combination of ordinary English roots and prefixes. Its plural is norites; dropping final e and adding -ic gives noritic, meaning relating to norite. In norite intrusion, norite is an attributive noun rather than a separate common adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有严格等义的常用词。相关术语：gabbro（辉长岩）通常以单斜辉石为主要辉石；norite（苏长岩）以斜方辉石为主要辉石；gabbronorite（辉长苏长岩）则含显著数量的两类辉石。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym. Related terms differ mineralogically: gabbro typically has clinopyroxene as its principal pyroxene, norite has orthopyroxene, and gabbronorite contains substantial amounts of both.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 挪威命名的岩石：norite → 苏长岩；矿物识别抓住“斜长石＋斜方辉石”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A rock named for Norway: norite. Recognize it by the pairing of plagioclase and orthopyroxene.

meaning: 冰原岛峰；露出冰面的山峰

pronunciation.note: 采用所列词典的一种英语读音；Merriam-Webster 的重拼标音在这里转写为 IPA。

forms: 可数；常见复数 nunataks。
family: nunatak hypothesis 冰原岛峰避难所假说

morphology.text: 格陵兰语历史构词：nuna（土地） + -taq（与之相属的事物） → nunataq（冰原中露出的岩峰）；英语借入后拼作 nunatak。英语中整词作为独立词素记忆，像白色冰海里露出的一小块陆地。

etymology.text: 英语从格陵兰因纽特语 nunataq 借入。想象冰原是一片白海，而露出的岩峰是一座小岛。

usage_note: 四周被冰川冰包围、顶部露出冰面的山峰或山脊；不能把完全埋在冰下的山也叫作 nunatak。

senses.meaning_zh: 冰原岛峰：突出于冰盖或冰川之上、四周被冰包围的裸露山峰或山脊
senses.meaning_en: An exposed rocky peak or ridge surrounded by an ice sheet or glacier
senses.english_definition: A nunatak is a rocky peak or ridge that rises above an ice sheet or glacier and is surrounded by ice.
senses.collocation_zh: 孤立的冰原岛峰；裸露的冰原岛峰
senses.sentence_en: An isolated nunatak rose above the ice sheet.
senses.sentence_zh: 一座孤立的冰原岛峰耸立在冰盖之上。

etymology_story.zh: 该词借自格陵兰语 nunataq，指被冰包围的裸露陆地或岩峰。英语保留了这一冰川地貌含义，用它命名仿佛白色冰海中岛屿一样的山峰。
etymology_story.en: The word was borrowed from Greenlandic nunataq, referring to exposed land or rock surrounded by ice. English retained this glacial-landform meaning for peaks that resemble islands in a sea of ice.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 nunatak 是整体借入的名词，不按英语前后缀继续拆分；常规复数为 nunataks。源语中可辨认出与 nuna（陆地）有关的成分，但不应把源语构词直接当作英语构词；英语中没有常用的派生动词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, nunatak is a borrowed noun treated as a whole base, with the regular plural nunataks. Its source contains material related to Greenlandic nuna, meaning land, but source-language structure should not be presented as productive English morphology. It has no common derived verb or adverb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 近义或相关表达：ice-surrounded peak（被冰包围的山峰）是解释性近义表达；rock outcrop（岩石露头）范围更广，不要求被冰包围；mountain peak（山峰）只说明山体顶部，不说明冰川环境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ice-surrounded peak is a descriptive near-equivalent. Rock outcrop is broader and does not require surrounding ice, while mountain peak identifies a summit without specifying a glacial setting.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 冰海中的陆地小岛：周围全是冰，只有岩峰露在外面。
mnemonic_anchor.en: An island of land in a sea of ice: ice all around, with a rocky summit exposed.

forms: 单数 oblast；复数 oblasts 或 oblasti；本词已经是复数。
family: oblast 州、行政区

morphology.text: oblast（州） + -i（借入的复数形式） → oblasti（多个州）；词干末尾辅音结合后形成 oblasti。

etymology.text: 英语借入俄语 oblast（行政区），并保留俄语来源的复数形式 oblasti。把它当成地图上几块不同的行政区域来记。

usage_note: 用于俄罗斯及一些相关地区的行政区划语境。oblasti 后接复数谓语，不再加 -s。

senses.meaning_zh: 州；行政区：oblast 的一种复数形式，用于俄罗斯等国的行政区划
senses.meaning_en: Administrative regions in Russia and certain other countries; a plural of oblast
senses.english_definition: Oblasti are administrative regions in Russia and certain other countries.
senses.collocation_zh: 俄罗斯的各州；若干州
senses.sentence_en: The report compares population changes across several Russian oblasti.
senses.sentence_zh: 该报告比较了俄罗斯若干州的人口变化。

etymology_story.zh: oblasti 是英语名词 oblast 保留俄语来源特征的一种复数形式；俄语 область 表示地区或行政区，其历史含义与管辖权和统治范围有关。英语还使用按自身规则构成的复数 oblasts。
etymology_story.en: Oblasti is a source-language plural used in English alongside the singular oblast, borrowed from Russian область. The Russian word denotes a region or administrative territory and is historically associated with authority or jurisdiction; English also uses the regular plural oblasts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 词元为 oblast；oblasti 是其借入的复数形式，与英语规则复数 oblasts 并存。可作学习性表示：oblast → oblasti，但 -i 在这里不是可任意套用的英语复数后缀，也不需要额外的辅音变化。该词没有常用的英语派生动词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: The lemma is oblast; oblasti is a borrowed plural that exists alongside the regular English plural oblasts. The relationship can be shown as oblast → oblasti, but -i is not a freely productive English plural suffix, and no additional consonant change is required. There is no common derived English verb or adverb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: oblasts 与 oblasti 是同一名词的不同复数形式，含义相同；regions（地区）范围更宽，也可指非行政区域；provinces（省）是近似的行政区称呼，但在具体国家制度中未必与 oblasti 等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Oblasts and oblasti are alternative plurals with the same meaning. Regions is broader and can include nonadministrative areas; provinces is an approximate administrative equivalent whose institutional meaning depends on the country.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一个 oblast，多个 oblasti 或 oblasts：看地图上的多个州。
mnemonic_anchor.en: One oblast, several oblasti or oblasts: picture several administrative regions on a map.

pronunciation.note: 采用所列词典的一种英语读音；Merriam-Webster 的重拼标音在这里转写为 IPA。

forms: 可数；复数 obols。
family: obolus 同义形式；obolary 仅有小额钱币的（古旧词）

morphology.text: obol-（obol / obolus 的词干） + -ary → obolary（仅有小额钱币的、贫穷的，古旧用词）；obol 整词作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 经拉丁语 obolus 借入，源头是古希腊语 obolos/obelos。古希腊一德拉克马相当于六奥博尔，可用六枚小币换一枚大币的画面记忆。

usage_note: 本卡选古钱币义，不考同名重量单位。历史语境中，一奥博尔等于六分之一德拉克马。
