etymology_story.zh: 来自拉丁语 clamant-，即 clamans 的词干形式；clamans 是 clamare（呼喊）的现在分词。英语保留了“高声呼喊”的意义，并将其引申为需要或问题“迫切要求关注”。
etymology_story.en: Clamant comes from Latin clamant-, the stem of clamans, the present participle of clamare, meaning 'to cry out.' English retained the idea of loud calling and extended it to needs or problems that urgently demand attention.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是带有拉丁分词词干的形容词；历史上可分析为 clam-（呼喊）+ -ant（分词成分），但 clam- 不是现代英语中能自由使用的词根。clamantly（迫切地；喧嚷地）是罕见副词；clamor/clamour（喧嚷）、clamorous（喧闹的）、exclaim（惊呼）、proclaim（宣告）和 declaim（慷慨陈词）属于相关词源词群，并非都由 clamant 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: This adjective preserves a Latin participial stem, historically analyzable as clam- ('cry out') + -ant (a participial element); clam- is not a freely productive modern English root. Clamantly is a rare adverb. Clamor/clamour, clamorous, exclaim, proclaim, and declaim belong to the related etymological family rather than all being derivatives of clamant.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: urgent（紧急的）强调必须立即处理；pressing（紧迫的）强调现实压力；clamorous（喧嚷的）强调声音大或要求强烈。clamant 可把“呼喊般强烈”与“亟须关注”联系起来，但使用频率低得多。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Urgent stresses the need for immediate action; pressing emphasizes practical pressure; clamorous emphasizes loud noise or insistent demands. Clamant can connect the force of a cry with the urgency of a need, but it is much less common.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一个需要仿佛在“大声呼救”，就是 clamant：迫切得让人无法忽视。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a need crying out for help: clamant means urgent enough to demand attention.

etymology_story.zh: 柯勒律治在十九世纪初将这个词引入英语，借自德语 Klerisei（教士阶层），其更早词源与拉丁语 clericus（教士）有关。他将原本指宗教人士的名称扩展为承担教育与文化职责的有学识阶层。
etymology_story.en: Coleridge introduced the word into English in the early nineteenth century from German Klerisei, meaning 'clergy,' with earlier roots connected to Latin clericus. He extended a name for religious personnel to a learned class responsible for education and cultural life.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 clerisy 作为借词整体记忆，不宜机械拆成 cler- + -isy；它通常作为集合名词使用，没有常用的直接派生词。cleric（教士）、clerical（教士的；文书工作的）、clergy（教士群体）和 clerk（办事员）是历史相关词，并非由 clerisy 加后缀生成；anti-clerisy 不是应列为常规词族成员的固定派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat clerisy as a whole borrowed word rather than mechanically dividing it into cler- + -isy. It normally functions as a collective noun and has no common direct derivatives. Cleric, clerical, clergy, and clerk are historically related words, not suffixal derivatives of clerisy; anti-clerisy is not an established standard member of its word family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: intelligentsia（知识分子阶层）常突出社会或政治影响；intellectuals（知识分子）可指一个个从事思想活动的人；literati（文人、文学界人士）主要侧重文学修养。clerisy 更突出作为整体的有学识文化阶层，有时带精英意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Intelligentsia often highlights a class's social or political influence; intellectuals can refer to individual people engaged in intellectual work; literati focuses on literary learning. Clerisy presents learned cultural figures as a collective class and can suggest an elite.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“掌握学问的教士群体”联想到“守护学问的知识阶层”；现代核心义是知识界。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Move mentally from learned clergy to the wider class that preserves learning: the clerisy is the educated cultural class.

morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, cognomen is a whole loanword; its division into an additional-name element and nomen belongs to Latin historical morphology. synonyms_and_nuances.en: Surname usually means an inherited family name in modern usage; byname means an additional identifying name; nickname is generally informal and may be affectionate or teasing. etymology_story.en: Coition comes from Latin coitio, derived from coire, meaning 'to come together' or 'to have intercourse'; coire combines co- ('together') with ire ('to go'). The general idea of coming together became specialized as sexual union.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，coition 是借入的动作名词，不宜把 coi- 当作可以自由构词的英语词根；co- + ire 是历史来源，表面的 -tion 对应拉丁语动作名词形式。直接相关的形容词 coitional（性交的）很少见；coitus（性交）和 coital（性交的）是同源词，不能说成均由 coition 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, coition is a borrowed action noun, and coi- is not a freely productive English root. Co- + ire explains its historical origin, while the visible -tion reflects the Latin action-noun formation. Coitional is a rare related adjective; coitus and coital are cognates rather than direct derivatives of coition.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sexual intercourse（性交）是较通行而明确的表达；coitus（性交）具有医学或技术色彩；copulation（交配、交合）常用于生物学，尤其是动物行为。coition 同样正式，但在现代英语中更少见。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sexual intercourse is the more widely used explicit expression; coitus has a medical or technical tone; copulation is frequent in biological descriptions, especially of animals. Coition is similarly formal but less common in modern English.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: co- 表示“一起”，ire 表示“走”：历史上的“走到一起”在这里专指性结合。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Co- means 'together' and ire means 'go': the historical idea of going together becomes sexual union.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古法语 contumelie 进入中古英语，源自拉丁语 contumelia，意为“侮辱、凌辱”。现代英语保留了这种带有傲慢与轻蔑意味的旧义，主要用于正式或文学语境。
etymology_story.en: The word entered Middle English through Old French contumelie, from Latin contumelia, meaning insult or abuse. Modern English preserves this sense of arrogant, contemptuous mistreatment, chiefly in formal or literary contexts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 contumely 是不可再作实用拆分的借词，词尾不是副词后缀 -ly。同族派生词有 contumelious（傲慢侮辱的）、contumeliously（傲慢侮辱地）和 contumeliousness（傲慢侮辱的性质）；该名词通常不可数，文学用法中也可用复数 contumelies 表示多次侮辱。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, contumely is an unanalyzed borrowing; its ending is not the adverb suffix -ly. Its derivative family includes contumelious, contumeliously, and contumeliousness; the noun is usually uncountable, although literary contumelies can denote individual insults.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: insult 指一般的侮辱性言语或行为；scorn 强调鄙视、轻蔑的态度；abuse 强调辱骂或恶劣对待。contumely 尤其突出居高临下的羞辱，语体也更庄重、古雅。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Insult is a general term for an offensive remark or act; scorn emphasizes contemptuous rejection; abuse emphasizes harsh language or mistreatment. Contumely particularly suggests haughty humiliation and has a more elevated, literary register.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把“轻蔑的态度”变成“羞辱的言行”，就是 contumely；整词记忆，不按 -ly 副词拆解。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Contempt turned into humiliating words or treatment is contumely; remember it as a whole noun, not an -ly adverb.

etymology_story.zh: 该词是数学术语，由表示“共同”的 co- 与 planar（平面的）组成。planar 属于 plane（平面）的词族，其历史根源与拉丁语 planus（平坦的）有关。
etymology_story.en: This mathematical term combines co-, meaning together, with planar, meaning relating to a plane. Planar belongs to the family of plane, whose historical roots lie in Latin planus, meaning flat.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：co-（共同）+ planar（平面的）→ coplanar（共面的）；planar 可按 plane 去掉词尾 e 后加 -ar 理解。核心词族包括 plane（平面）、planar（平面的）、planarity（平面性）、coplanarity（共面性）、noncoplanar（不共面的）和 noncoplanarity（非共面性）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: co- (together) + planar (relating to a plane) → coplanar; planar can be analyzed as plane with final e removed plus -ar. The core family includes plane, planar, planarity, coplanarity, noncoplanar, and noncoplanarity.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: in the same plane 是最准确的释义短语；planar 表示平面的或与平面有关的，不必涉及多个对象共面；collinear 表示共线，条件比共面更严格。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: In the same plane is the exact paraphrase; planar means flat or relating to a plane without necessarily comparing several objects; collinear means lying on one straight line, a stricter condition than being coplanar.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: co- 表示“一起”，planar 表示“平面”：一起落在同一张无限延伸的平面上。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Co- means together and planar points to a plane: imagine all the objects lying together on one infinitely extended flat sheet.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古英语来自古英语 dihtan，意为“安排、规定或准备”，更早借自拉丁语 dictare，意为“口授、规定”。其含义由“安排妥当”发展为“整备、穿戴和装饰”，如今主要见于古文和诗歌。
etymology_story.en: The word comes through Middle English from Old English dihtan, meaning to arrange, prescribe, or prepare, borrowed from Latin dictare, meaning to dictate or prescribe. Its meanings developed from arranging things to preparing, dressing, and adorning them, and it now survives chiefly in historical or poetic language.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 dight 视为不可再作实用拆分的词基。屈折形式包括 dights、dighting，以及过去式和过去分词 dight 或 dighted；分词可作形容词。该词没有常用的现代派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, dight is best treated as an unanalyzed base. Its inflections include dights, dighting, and the past-tense and past-participle forms dight or dighted; the participle can function adjectivally. It has no commonly used modern family of derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: adorn（装饰）强调增添美感；deck（装点）常指用显眼的饰物装饰；array（盛装打扮）强调衣着或排列的仪式感。dight 与它们部分重合，但带有鲜明的古语或诗歌色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Adorn emphasizes added beauty; deck often suggests conspicuous decoration; array suggests elaborate dress or formal arrangement. Dight overlaps with these meanings but has a distinctly archaic or poetic register.

etymology_story.zh: 该词属于以新拉丁语分类名 Dioecia 为背景形成的科学词汇，最终结合了希腊语表示“两”的 di- 和表示“家、住所”的 oikos。其命名意象是雌雄“分住两家”，即生殖功能分布在不同个体上。
etymology_story.en: The word belongs to scientific vocabulary associated with the New Latin classification name Dioecia, ultimately combining Greek di-, meaning two, and oikos, meaning house. The naming image is of the sexes occupying two separate households, with male and female reproductive functions in different individuals.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词分析为 di-（两）+ oec-（家、住所）+ -y（状态），也可将 dioec- 作为科学词干整体识记。相关词族包括 dioecious（雌雄异株或异体的）、dioeciously（以雌雄异株或异体方式）和 dioeciousness（雌雄异株或异体的性质）；dioecism 是较少见的同义名词。
morphology_enriched.en: The combining elements are di- (two), oec- (house), and -y (condition); dioec- can also be learned as a scientific stem. Related forms include dioecious, dioeciously, and dioeciousness; dioecism is a less common synonymous noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dioecism 是较少见的同义词；gonochorism（雌雄异体）通常用于动物；unisexuality（单性性）含义更宽，还可描述单朵花或单个生殖结构，不能单凭它判断植物是否雌雄异株。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dioecism is a less common synonym; gonochorism usually describes separate sexes in animals; unisexuality is broader and can describe an individual flower or reproductive structure without establishing that an entire plant species is dioecious.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: di-＝两，oec-＝家：雌雄各住一家。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Di- means two and oec- means house: male and female live in separate houses.

etymology_story.en: Diploidy was formed from diploid with the state-forming suffix -y; diploid ultimately draws on Greek diploos, meaning double, together with -oid, a suffix indicating form or resemblance. Genetics uses this family for the possession of two complete chromosome sets.

morphology_enriched.zh: 直接构词公式为 diploid（二倍体的；二倍体）+ -y（状态）→ diploidy（二倍性）。主要词族包括 diploid（形容词或名词）、diploids（二倍体，复数）、diploidize／diploidise（使成为二倍体）和 diploidization／diploidisation（二倍化）；动词还可形成 diploidized、diploidizing 等屈折形式。
morphology_enriched.en: The immediate formation is diploid + -y → diploidy. The principal family includes diploid as an adjective or noun, the plural diploids, diploidize or diploidise, and diploidization or diploidisation; the verb also has inflected forms such as diploidized and diploidizing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: diploid state（二倍体状态）和 diploid condition（二倍性状态）是直接的释义性近义表达。euploidy（整倍性）则是上位概念，指染色体数为完整基本染色体组的整数倍，并不限于两套。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Diploid state and diploid condition are direct explanatory equivalents. Euploidy is broader: it describes a chromosome complement consisting of whole multiples of the basic chromosome set and is not restricted to two sets.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Double chromosome sets give diploidy: remember two complete sets, rather than just two chromosomes.

etymology_story.zh: 该词最终来自拉丁语 domine，即 dominus“主人、先生”的呼格形式，原本用于尊称他人。在苏格兰，它成为教师的称呼；美国的牧师义则与荷兰语 dominee 的使用有关。
etymology_story.en: The word ultimately comes from Latin domine, the vocative of dominus, meaning master or lord, and began as a respectful form of address. It became a term for a schoolmaster in Scotland, while the American ministerial sense is associated with Dutch dominee.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 dominie 是借入的完整词基，不宜拆成有独立意义的英语词根和后缀；复数为 dominies。它没有常用的现代派生词族；历史语源上的 dominus 不等于现代英语中的直接构词词基。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, dominie is a borrowed whole-word base rather than a transparent combination of English roots and affixes; its plural is dominies. It has no commonly used modern family of derivatives, and its historical source dominus is not a direct modern English building block.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: schoolmaster 指男教师或学校负责人，最接近其苏格兰义；teacher 是不限性别和地域的普通称呼；minister 对应其牧师义，但不限定荷兰归正会。dominie 本身带有地域和历史色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Schoolmaster is closest to the Scottish sense and refers to a male teacher or school head; teacher is the ordinary term without a gender or regional restriction; minister matches the clerical sense without specifying the Dutch Reformed tradition. Dominie carries regional and historical associations.

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自新拉丁语植物属名 Dracaena，最终源于希腊语 drakaina，意为“雌龙”。属名与某些种类产生的红色“龙血”树脂有关，并非所有龙血树属植物都会产生这种树脂。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from the New Latin genus name Dracaena, ultimately from Greek drakaina, meaning female dragon. The name is associated with the red resin called dragon's blood produced by certain species, rather than by every member of the genus.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 dracaena 是整体借入的植物名称，不作实用的英语词根加词缀拆分；常见复数为 dracaenas。Dracaena 是首字母大写的属名；dracaena-like（像龙血树属植物的）是可自由构成的比较表达，并非固定的常用派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, dracaena is a borrowed plant name without a useful English root-and-affix breakdown; its usual English plural is dracaenas. Capitalized Dracaena is the genus name; dracaena-like is a freely formed comparison rather than an established common derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dragon tree（龙血树）是用于某些种类的俗名，不能在所有语境中替代属名；corn plant（香龙血树）通常特指 Dracaena fragrans；houseplant（室内植物）只是更宽泛的类别词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dragon tree is a common name for certain species and does not always replace the genus name; corn plant usually refers specifically to Dracaena fragrans; houseplant is merely a broader category.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “雌龙”连到“龙血”：某些种类流出红色树脂，因此得名。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect the female dragon with dragon's blood: the red resin of certain species explains the name.

senses.meaning_zh: 麦糟；酿酒糖化后留下的谷物残渣，常用作牲畜饲料

etymology_story.zh: 该词承自中古英语 draf，意为“谷壳、残渣”，与冰岛语和荷兰语中的同源词有关。其较宽泛的“渣滓”义，在现代酿酒行业中特别指糖化并滤出麦汁后剩下的谷物。[词源资料](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/draff)；[行业用法](https://www.edinburghwhiskyacademy.com/blogs/definition/whisky-words-draff)。
etymology_story.en: The word continues Middle English draf, meaning husks or refuse, with cognates in Icelandic and Dutch. Its broader meaning of residue survives especially in brewing and distilling, where it denotes grain remaining after the wort is drained off. [Etymology](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/draff); [industry usage](https://www.edinburghwhiskyacademy.com/blogs/definition/whisky-words-draff).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 draff 是不可再作常规拆分的独立词根，通常用作不可数名词。派生词 draff + -y → draffy，意为“含渣滓的；糟粕般的；无价值的”，属罕见或旧式用语；draffs 是少见的复数形式。没有常用的现代动词或副词派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, draff is a simple base without a productive internal breakdown and is normally uncountable. Draff + -y gives draffy, meaning containing dregs, resembling refuse, or worthless; this adjective is rare or dated. Draffs is an uncommon plural. There are no common modern verb or adverb derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: brewers’ spent grain（啤酒糟）是啤酒生产中最接近的技术名称；residue（残留物）适用范围更广；dregs（沉渣、渣滓）通常强调液体底部的沉积物，而 draff 主要指谷物的固体残余。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Brewers’ spent grain is the closest technical equivalent in beer production; residue is a broader term for anything left behind; dregs usually emphasizes sediment at the bottom of a liquid, whereas draff chiefly denotes solid grain remains.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 麦汁流走，湿谷壳留下：留下喂牲畜的那堆，就是 draff。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The wort drains away; the wet grain stays behind. That leftover animal feed is draff.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 dulse 来自盖尔语海藻名称，与苏格兰盖尔语 duileasg 和爱尔兰语 duileasc 相联系。它在英语中保留了沿海食物名称的具体含义，尤其指传统上采来食用的红藻。[词源资料](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/dulse)。

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 dulse 是整体借词，没有可独立分析的英语前缀或后缀；通常不可数，表示不同种类时可用复数 dulses。历史复合词 dulse + man → dulseman，指“卖食用红藻的人”，复数为 dulsemen，属旧时地域用语；没有常用的现代派生形容词或动词。[历史用例](https://deriv.nls.uk/dcn23/1179/1609/117916097.23.pdf)。
morphology_enriched.en: Dulse is a whole-word borrowing with no separately meaningful English prefix or suffix. It is normally uncountable, although dulses can refer to different kinds. The historical compound dulse + man gives dulseman, a seller of edible seaweed, with plural dulsemen; this is dated regional vocabulary. There are no common modern adjective or verb derivatives. synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dillisk 是 dulse 的地域性别称；red seaweed（红藻）是范围更广的类别名称；edible seaweed（食用海藻）强调用途，也包括许多非红藻品种，不能在所有语境中替换 dulse。

etymology_story.zh: ebonite 是19世纪出现的材料名称，由 ebon 或 ebony“乌木”的词干与材料名称后缀 -ite 构成。名称借用了乌木坚硬、深黑的形象，指这种外观和质地使人联想到乌木的硬橡胶。[词源资料](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/ebonite)。
etymology_story.en: Ebonite arose in the nineteenth century from the stem of ebon or ebony, combined with the material-forming suffix -ite. Its name evokes ebony’s hardness and dark appearance, applying that image to hard rubber. [Etymology](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/ebonite).

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：ebon-（与 ebony“乌木”相联系的词干）+ -ite（材料名称后缀）→ ebonite。相关词族包括 ebony（乌木；乌黑的）、ebon（乌木；乌黑的，文学用语）、ebonize/ebonise（使呈乌木般的黑色）和 ebonization/ebonisation（乌木化；染成乌黑）；后两者主要从 ebony 派生，并非表示制造硬橡胶。ebonite rod 中的 ebonite 是名词作定语。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: ebon-, the stem associated with ebony, + -ite, a material-forming suffix, → ebonite. Related words include ebony, the wood or its black color; literary ebon; ebonize/ebonise, to give something an ebony-like black finish; and ebonization/ebonisation, that finishing process. The latter forms derive from ebony and do not normally mean making hard rubber. In ebonite rod, ebonite is an attributive noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hard rubber（硬橡胶）是最直白的同义名称；vulcanite（硬质硫化橡胶）在材料语境中通常与 ebonite 同义。普通 rubber（橡胶）范围更广，不能体现其坚硬、高度硫化的特点。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hard rubber is the plain descriptive equivalent; vulcanite is generally synonymous with ebonite in materials terminology. Rubber alone is broader and does not specify the hard, extensively vulcanized material.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ebony 乌木 + 材料后缀 -ite：像乌木一样硬的橡胶。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ebony plus material-forming -ite: rubber as hard as ebony.

etymology_story.zh: 这个科学名称由 electro-“电”和 -scope“观察仪器”构成，英语用例可追溯至19世纪初。其更深层的希腊语词源分别涉及“琥珀”和“观察”，名称因此体现了使电荷效应可见的功能。[词源与释义](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/electroscope)。
etymology_story.en: This scientific name combines electro-, referring to electricity, with -scope, an observing instrument, and is recorded in English from the early nineteenth century. Its deeper Greek elements concern amber and observing, matching the instrument’s role in making the effects of electric charge visible. [Etymology and definition](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/electroscope).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词公式：electro-（电）+ -scope（观察或检测仪器）→ electroscope。词族包括 electroscopes（复数）、electroscopic（验电的；验电器的）、electroscopically（通过验电方式，罕见副词）和 electroscopy（验电；利用验电器进行检测，专业名词）。这些派生词不构成 electroscope 本身的额外常用词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: electro-, electricity, + -scope, an observing or detecting instrument, → electroscope. Its family includes plural electroscopes; electroscopic, relating to electroscopes or charge detection; rare electroscopically, by electroscopic means; and technical electroscopy, detection or examination using an electroscope. These derivatives do not give electroscope itself additional common parts of speech.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: electric-charge detector（电荷检测器）是解释性的近义表达；electrometer（静电计）是相关仪器名称，通常更强调定量测量电荷或电势。electroscope 主要强调显示是否带电，不宜与 ammeter（电流表）混用。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Electric-charge detector is a descriptive equivalent; electrometer names a related instrument, usually emphasizing quantitative measurement of charge or electric potential. Electroscope chiefly emphasizes indicating charge and should not be confused with ammeter, which measures electric current.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Electro- means electricity and -scope suggests observing: watch the leaves separate to detect charge.

etymology_story.zh: eluent 的词源是拉丁语 ēluere“洗出”的现在分词 ēluēns，其词干为 ēluent-。这一“洗出东西的”含义进入化学术语后，用来命名使物质被洗脱的介质。[词源资料](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/eluent)。
etymology_story.en: Eluent is based on Latin ēluēns, with stem ēluent-, the present participle of ēluere, meaning to wash out. Chemistry adopted this active idea of washing something out as the name for the medium that effects elution. [Etymology](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/eluent).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 eluent 是学术借词，宜与 elute“洗脱”作为同族词关联记忆；历史上可分析为 ē-/ex-（出）+ lu-（洗）+ -ent-（现在分词词干成分），不能把 -ent 简单泛化为“化学试剂后缀”。词族包括 elute、elutes、eluted、eluting（洗脱及其屈折形式）、elution（洗脱过程）、eluate（洗脱后流出的液体）、elutable（可洗脱的）、coelute（共同洗脱）和 coelution（共同洗脱现象）；eluents 为复数，eluant 为异体拼写。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, eluent is a learned borrowing best connected with its family member elute. Historically it contains ē-/ex-, out, lu-, wash, and the participial stem element -ent-; -ent should not be treated as a general suffix meaning chemical reagent. The family includes elute and its inflections elutes, eluted, and eluting; elution, the process; eluate, the outgoing liquid; elutable, capable of being eluted; coelute, to elute together; and coelution, that occurrence. Eluents is the plural, and eluant is a spelling variant.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: eluting solvent（洗脱溶剂）在液相色谱中是近义表达，但范围限于溶剂；mobile phase（流动相）强调流体在色谱系统中的角色，在洗脱色谱中可与 eluent 对应；eluant 是同词异体拼写。注意 eluent 指进入系统的洗脱介质，eluate 则指洗脱后流出的液体。[IUPAC 定义](https://goldbook.iupac.org/terms/view/E02040)。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Eluting solvent is a close equivalent in liquid chromatography but is limited to solvents; mobile phase emphasizes the fluid’s role in the system and corresponds to eluent in elution chromatography; eluant is a spelling variant. Crucially, eluent denotes the incoming eluting medium, whereas eluate denotes the outgoing fluid after elution. [IUPAC definition](https://goldbook.iupac.org/terms/view/E02040).

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“洗出”：eluent 是进去洗的介质，eluate 是洗完流出的液体。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think wash out: the eluent goes in to do the washing; the eluate comes out afterward.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，ephor 是完整借入的词干，不宜强行拆成可自由使用的英语词缀；历史构词逻辑为“在上＋看”。相关派生词有 ephoral（监察官的）、ephorate（监察官职位、任期或监察官团体）和 ephorship（监察官职位）；复数为 ephors。

etymology_story.en: Middle English eremite came through ecclesiastical Latin eremita from Greek erēmitēs, meaning a person living alone in the wilderness, ultimately from erēmos ('desolate, uninhabited'). Hermit shares this ancestry, while eremite retains a more distinctly religious or literary character.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中以 eremite 为借入的基本词；eremit- 是派生时使用的词干形式：eremit-＋-ic → eremitic（隐修的），另有 eremitical（隐修的）、eremitically（以隐修方式）和 eremitism（隐修生活或制度）。hermit 和 hermitage（隐修处）属于历史同源词，而非直接由 eremite 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats eremite as a borrowed base, with eremit- used in derivation: eremit- + -ic → eremitic ('relating to solitary religious life'). Other derivatives include eremitical, eremitically, and eremitism ('solitary religious life or its practice'). Hermit and hermitage are historically related words rather than direct derivatives of eremite.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hermit（隐士）最接近，使用范围也更广；recluse（离群索居者）不一定有宗教动机；anchorite（定居隐修者）通常更具体地指退居固定修室、专事宗教生活的人。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hermit is the closest and more widely used equivalent; recluse does not necessarily imply a religious motive; anchorite more specifically suggests a religious solitary who withdraws to a fixed cell or dwelling.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “荒野、无人之地”→远离人群、独自修行。
mnemonic_anchor.en: An 'uninhabited wilderness' → someone who withdraws from society for solitary devotion.

etymology_story.en: Eugenol is a scientific name formed from Eugenia, the plant genus in which the clove tree was formerly classified. The ending -ol appears in names of hydroxyl-containing compounds; here the substance is a phenol.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式为 eugen-（取自 Eugenia 的命名词干）＋-ol（化学命名词尾）。相关化学词有 eugenyl（丁香酚基的）、eugenolate（丁香酚盐或丁香酚负离子）、isoeugenol（异丁香酚）、methyleugenol（甲基丁香酚）及 eugenyl acetate（乙酸丁香酚酯）；这些表示相关结构或衍生物，并非可互换的物质名称。
morphology_enriched.en: The structure is eugen- (a naming stem taken from Eugenia) + -ol (a chemical naming suffix). These denote related structures or derivatives and are not interchangeable substance names.

etymology_story.zh: euphotic 是由希腊语来源的 eu-（好、充分）、phōt-（光）和形容词词尾 -ic 构成的现代科学词。它在水生生态学中专指光照足以支持净光合作用的水层，而非一切能检测到光的水层。
etymology_story.en: Euphotic is a modern scientific formation using Greek-derived eu- ('well, sufficiently'), phōt- ('light'), and the adjective suffix -ic. In aquatic ecology, it identifies water with enough light for net photosynthesis, rather than every depth at which light can be detected.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式为 eu-（充分）＋phot-（光）＋-ic（形容词后缀）；也可分析为 eu-＋photic（有光的）。常用词组有 euphotic zone 和 euphotic depth；相关同根术语包括 photic（有光的）、aphotic（无光的）和 dysphotic（弱光的），后三者并非由 euphotic 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: The structure is eu- ('sufficiently') + phot- ('light') + -ic (an adjective suffix), or eu- + photic. Established combinations include euphotic zone and euphotic depth. Related root-sharing terms include photic, aphotic, and dysphotic; these are not direct derivatives of euphotic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sunlit（阳光照到的）是日常描述，不说明光合作用条件；well-lit（光照良好的）更宽泛，也可指人工照明；photic（有光的）在部分文献中与 euphotic 接近，但也可泛指存在光照的水域。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sunlit is an everyday description that does not specify photosynthetic conditions; well-lit is broader and can describe artificial illumination; photic sometimes overlaps with euphotic but can refer more generally to water receiving light.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: eu-＝充分，phot-＝光：光够用，才能净光合。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Eu- means 'sufficiently' and phot- means 'light': enough light for net photosynthesis.

etymology_story.zh: 官衔名词经晚期拉丁语 exarchus 源自希腊语 exarchos（领导者），后来用于帝国总督和教会长官。植物学形容词则是独立的科学构词，其中 ex- 表示“外”，-arch 表示“开始、起源”，指木质部从外侧开始分化。
etymology_story.en: The official title comes through Late Latin exarchus from Greek exarchos ('leader') and developed into imperial and ecclesiastical titles. The botanical adjective is a separate scientific formation in which ex- means 'outside' and -arch means 'beginning or origin', referring to xylem differentiation beginning toward the outside.

morphology_enriched.zh: 官衔名词在现代英语中以 exarch 为整体词干，相关词有 exarchate（总督辖区、督主教辖区或其职位）、exarchy（总督统治或辖区）和 exarchal（总督或督主教的）。植物学形容词可分析为 ex-（外）＋-arch（起始位置）；同系列有 endarch（内始式的）和 mesarch（中始式的），二者不是 exarch 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: The official title functions as the base exarch in modern English, with related forms exarchate ('an exarch’s jurisdiction or office'), exarchy ('an exarch’s government or territory'), and exarchal ('relating to an exarch'). The botanical adjective divides into ex- ('outside') + -arch ('position of origin'); parallel formations include endarch and mesarch, which are not derivatives of exarch.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: governor（总督、地方长官）是历史行政义的宽泛近义词；viceroy（副王）强调代表君主统治，但并非这一拜占庭官衔的严格同义词；legate（使节、代表）接近部分教会用法，强调受委派的代表身份。植物学义没有同样简洁、通用的单词近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Governor is a broad equivalent for the historical administrative sense; viceroy emphasizes ruling for a monarch but is not an exact equivalent of the Byzantine title; legate overlaps with some ecclesiastical uses by emphasizing delegated representation. The botanical sense has no equally concise, widely used single-word synonym.

senses.english_definition: An extern is a student or trainee who spends a limited period in a workplace to learn how a profession is practised.

etymology_story.zh: extern 源于拉丁语 externus，意为“外面的”，与法语 externe“走读生、院外见习生”等用法有关。英语中的人员称谓最初强调不住在所属机构内，后来也用于接受短期职业训练的学生。
etymology_story.en: Extern comes ultimately from Latin externus, meaning 'outside', and is associated with French externe, used for nonresident students and trainees. The English noun originally emphasized living outside an institution and later extended to students gaining short-term professional experience.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 extern 作为完整词基，不宜机械拆成 ex- 和 tern。extern + -ship → externship（见习期、见习项目）；externs 是复数；external（外部的）、externally（在外部）和 externality（外部性）属于同源词，不能都视为由人员名词 extern 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, extern is normally treated as a complete base rather than mechanically divided into ex- and tern. Extern + -ship forms externship, a training placement or period; externs is the plural. External, externally, and externality are historically related words, rather than direct derivatives of the person noun extern.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: intern（实习生）通常承担较持续、较有结构的实际工作；trainee（受训者）泛指正在接受职业训练的人；observer（观摩者）主要旁观，通常不直接参与工作。extern 的具体职责和期限取决于机构，不能仅凭词名判断。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: An intern typically undertakes a more sustained, structured work placement; a trainee is anyone receiving occupational training; an observer mainly watches rather than participates. An extern's actual duties and placement length depend on the institution.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“外”的词源线索：extern 是到机构里学习、传统上住在机构外的见习生。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the historical idea of 'outside': an extern trains inside an institution but traditionally lives outside it.

etymology_story.zh: falchion 经中古英语及盎格鲁法语的相关形式传入，最终与拉丁语 falx“镰刀”有关。名称把刀刃与镰刀联系起来，但历史上的 falchion 并非都具有同样明显的弯曲形状。
etymology_story.en: Falchion entered through Middle English and Anglo-French forms ultimately related to Latin falx, meaning 'sickle'. The name associates the blade with a sickle, although historical falchions varied in how strongly their blades curved.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 falchion 是不可作常规词缀分析的完整词基；falchions 是复数。falchion-shaped（宽刃弯刀形的）是可按需构成的复合形容词，并非常用派生词；该词没有常用的动词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, falchion is a complete base without a productive prefix–suffix breakdown; falchions is its plural. Falchion-shaped is a possible descriptive compound rather than a common established derivative. The word has no commonly used derived verb or adverb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sword（剑、刀）是较宽泛的类别名称；scimitar（弯刀）通常让人联想到中东等地区的弯刃刀；sabre（军刀）通常指较长的单刃军用刀，尤其与骑兵有关。falchion 则特指欧洲历史上的一种宽刃单刃刀。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sword is the broad category; scimitar usually suggests a curved sword associated with regions such as the Middle East; sabre usually denotes a relatively long, single-edged military sword, especially a cavalry weapon. Falchion identifies a particular historical European type with a broad, single-edged blade.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用词源中的“镰刀”记住宽阔的切削刀刃，再把它放进中世纪欧洲的场景。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the cutting blade of a sickle, then place that image in medieval Europe.

etymology_story.zh: feculent 来自拉丁语 faeculentus“充满沉渣的”，其基础 faex 指酒渣或沉淀物。意义由含沉渣扩展到污浊、含废物，在医学语境中也可具体指含粪便。
etymology_story.en: Feculent comes from Latin faeculentus, meaning 'full of dregs', based on faex, 'dregs or sediment'. Its meaning broadened from containing sediment to being filthy or waste-laden, with a specifically faecal meaning in medical contexts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可作词源辅助分析：fec-（沉渣、污物）+ -ulent（充满……的），但它在现代英语中主要是借入的完整形容词，并非自由组合的新词。相关派生词有 feculence（污浊、污物）、feculency（污浊，较少见）和 feculently（污浊地，罕见）；fecal/faecal（粪便的）与其同源。
morphology_enriched.en: For etymological learning, the word can be analysed as fec- 'dregs or filth' + -ulent 'full of', although modern English primarily treats it as a borrowed adjective. Related derivatives include feculence, the less common feculency, and the rare adverb feculently. Fecal/faecal is historically related.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: filthy（肮脏的）是通用词，强调很脏；turbid（浑浊的）强调悬浮颗粒造成的不清澈，不一定含污物；faecal/fecal（粪便的）专指与粪便有关。feculent 强调含沉渣或污物，在医学中可与粪便有关。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Filthy is a general word meaning very dirty; turbid describes cloudiness caused by suspended particles without necessarily implying filth; faecal/fecal specifically concerns faeces. Feculent emphasizes the presence of dregs or foul matter and can have a faecal meaning in medicine.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “充满沉渣”就是核心画面：一杯混着污物的浑水。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep the literal image 'full of dregs': a glass of liquid clouded with foul sediment.

etymology_story.zh: felwort 可追溯到古英语 feldwyrt，由 feld“田野”和 wyrt“植物、草本”组成，字面意思是“田野里的草本植物”。这个古老植物名称后来用于龙胆科的一些植物，而不同地区的具体指称可能不同。
etymology_story.en: Felwort goes back to Old English feldwyrt, combining feld 'field' and wyrt 'plant or herb', literally 'field herb'. The old plant name came to designate certain members of the gentian family, with its precise reference varying by region.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史构词是 field 的古形式 feld + wort（草本植物）；现代词形中的 fel- 不是能自由构词的常用词根。felworts 可表示多株或多种相关植物；没有常用派生词。wort 仍可见于其他植物名称，但这些名称不是 felwort 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Historically, the compound consists of feld, an old form of field, + wort 'herb'. The surviving element fel- is not a commonly productive modern root. Felworts can refer to multiple plants or kinds; there are no common derivatives. Wort also occurs in other plant names, which are not derivatives of felwort.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gentian（龙胆类植物）是较宽泛且较常见的名称；autumn gentian（秋龙胆）通常特指 Gentianella amarella。felwort 是传统俗名，可能指不同的龙胆科植物，因此不能在所有语境中与某一个物种名称完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gentian is a broader and more familiar plant name; autumn gentian usually identifies Gentianella amarella. Felwort is a traditional common name that can refer to different gentian-family plants, so it is not universally interchangeable with any single species name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把古形式还原为 field + wort：“田野里的草”，再联系龙胆科植物。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Restore the old compound to field + wort: 'a field herb', associated with the gentian family.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 fop 加后缀 -ery 构成。fop 早先表示“愚人”，后来转指过分讲究衣着和仪态的男子，foppery 也由愚蠢行为之意发展出浮华打扮和矫饰举止之意。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed from fop and the suffix -ery. Fop originally meant a fool and later came to describe a man excessively concerned with dress and manners; foppery likewise developed from foolish behavior toward fashionable display and affectation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：fop（过分讲究衣着的男子）+ -ery（行为、作风），词尾 p 双写。主要词族：fop、fops（名词单复数）；foppish（浮华矫饰的）；foppishly（浮华矫饰地）；foppishness（浮华矫饰）；foppery（浮华作风），复数 fopperies 可指具体的矫饰行为或装饰。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: fop, a man excessively concerned with dress, + -ery, denoting behavior or practices, with doubling of p. The principal family includes fop, plural fops; foppish, affectedly fashionable; foppishly, in a foppish manner; foppishness, the quality of being foppish; and foppery, with plural fopperies for particular affectations or ornamental excesses.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dandyism（讲究衣着的作风）更侧重精心经营个人风格，未必含贬义；affectation（矫揉造作）不限于衣着；vanity（虚荣）强调渴望获得赞赏的心理。foppery 尤其贬指衣着和仪态上的过度修饰。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dandyism emphasizes cultivated personal style and need not be disapproving; affectation covers artificial behavior beyond clothing; vanity emphasizes the desire for admiration. Foppery particularly criticizes excessive ornament and affected manners.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: fop 是爱炫装的人，-ery 把“人”变成他的“作风”：浮华矫饰。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A fop displays his finery; -ery turns the person into the practice: excessive dress and display.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语进入英语，最终来自拉丁语 fructificare，由 fructus（果实、收获）和表示“制造、使成为”的成分构成。植物“结果”的具体意义后来也用于努力、思想或投资“产生收益、取得成果”。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through French and ultimately comes from Latin fructificare, formed from fructus, meaning fruit or produce, and an element meaning to make. The literal production of fruit also supplied a figurative meaning: producing benefits or successful results.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形态分析：fruct-（果实、成果的拉丁词根）+ -ify（使成为、产生）。动词形式：fructifies、fructified、fructifying；主要派生词为 fructification（结果；成果的产生）。相关拉丁词根词有 fructiferous（结果实的），但它不是由 fructify 直接加后缀构成。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern morphological analysis: fruct-, a Latin root meaning fruit or produce, + -ify, meaning to make or produce. Inflected forms are fructifies, fructified, and fructifying; the principal derivative is fructification, the production of fruit or results. Fructiferous, meaning fruit-bearing, shares the Latin root but is not formed directly by adding a suffix to fructify.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bear fruit（结果；见成效）最接近其不及物用法，也更常用；yield（产出）常直接接具体成果或收益；fertilize（施肥；使受精）强调促成生育或生长的过程，而非最终取得成果。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bear fruit is the closest and more usual equivalent of the intransitive senses; yield commonly takes a specific product or benefit as its object; fertilize emphasizes enabling growth or reproduction rather than the eventual achievement of results.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: fruct- 表示“果”，-ify 表示“使产生”：树结果，努力也结果。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Fruct- means fruit and -ify means make or produce: plants bear fruit, and efforts produce results.

morphology_enriched.zh: 在现代英语中，fugu 是不可再拆分的日语借词，没有常用的英语派生词。指鱼时通常单复数同形，指食物时通常不可数；fugu chef（河豚料理厨师）和 fugu sashimi（河豚刺身）是短语，不是派生词。fuguhiki（河豚切片刀）是另一个日语复合词借词，并非英语中 fugu 的常规派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, fugu is an unanalyzed Japanese loanword with no established common English derivatives. Its fish plural is generally unchanged, and its food use is normally uncountable; fugu chef and fugu sashimi are phrases rather than derivatives. Fuguhiki, a knife for slicing pufferfish, is a separate borrowed Japanese compound rather than a regular English derivative of fugu.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pufferfish（河豚）是较中性的鱼类名称；blowfish（河豚）是强调其鼓胀特征的常用名称；globefish（河豚、球形鱼）也是相关俗名，但较少用。这些名称的具体指称可有重叠和差异，fugu 尤其突出日本料理语境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pufferfish is a relatively neutral name for the fish; blowfish is a common name highlighting its inflation; globefish is another, less usual common name. Their precise applications can overlap or vary, while fugu particularly evokes Japanese cuisine.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the whole word fugu to Japanese pufferfish cuisine: one name covers both the fish and the dish.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由动词短语 gad about（四处闲逛、外出游玩）合成。gad 在中古英语中已有漫游、闲逛之意，整个短语后来被用来称呼经常这样活动的人。
etymology_story.en: The noun was formed from the verb phrase gad about, meaning to roam or go out for pleasure. Gad already meant to wander in Middle English, and the phrase became a name for someone habitually engaged in such outings.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：gad（闲逛、外出游玩）+ about（到处），由动词短语合成为指人的名词。复数：gadabouts。相关形式：gad、gads、gadded、gadding，以及短语 gad about、gad around；没有常用的 gadabout 副词或抽象名词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: gad, meaning to roam for pleasure, + about, meaning from place to place, forming a person-denoting noun from a verb phrase. The plural is gadabouts. Related forms are gad, gads, gadded, and gadding, together with gad about and gad around; there are no common adverbial or abstract-noun derivatives of gadabout.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: social butterfly（交际花、活跃的社交者）突出交往对象多；socialite（社交名流）通常暗示上流或时尚社交圈；wanderer（漫游者）强调到处走动，未必参加社交。gadabout 兼有频繁外出和寻乐社交之意。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Social butterfly emphasizes frequent interaction with many people; socialite usually suggests fashionable or high-society circles; wanderer emphasizes movement without necessarily implying social activity. Gadabout combines habitual outings with pleasure-seeking or social visits.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: gad about＝到处游玩；gadabout＝总在到处游玩的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: To gad about is to go out and about for fun; a gadabout is the person who keeps doing it.

pronunciation.note: 采用美式读音；音标将词典的读音符号转写为 IPA。

etymology.text: 中古英语已有 garfysshe 这个鱼名，后来成为 garfish。把它长长的身体和尖长的嘴连成一个形象来记。

usage_note: 本卡采用北美淡水鱼雀鳝义；在其他地区也可能指颌部细长的海鱼，识别时要看地域和物种。

etymology_story.zh: garfish 的前一成分与古英语 gār（矛）有关，后一成分 fish 表示“鱼”，名称形象地描绘了鱼的细长尖颌。这个名称在不同地区用于不同的长颌鱼类，因此既可指海生颌针鱼，也可在北美指雀鳝。
etymology_story.en: The first element of garfish is connected with Old English gār, meaning spear, while fish supplies the second element; the name evokes the fish's long, pointed jaws. Regional usage applies it to different long-jawed fishes, including marine needlefish and, in North America, gars.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形式可分析为 gar + fish 的复合名词；现代 gar 本身也用作雀鳝的名称，但历史命名意象中的 gar 是“矛”。复数通常为 garfish，也可用 garfishes，尤其在区分种类时。相关词为 gar，复数 gar 或 gars；没有常用的 garfish 派生动词、形容词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern form is analyzable as the compound gar + fish. Gar also independently names a freshwater gar today, but the historical naming image involves a spear. The plural is usually garfish, with garfishes also possible, especially for different kinds. The related noun gar has plurals gar or gars; garfish has no common derived verb, adjective, or adverb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: needlefish（颌针鱼）对应其海鱼义，但范围通常更广；gar（雀鳝）对应其北美用法；alligator gar（鳄雀鳝）仅指雀鳝中的一个特定种。海生颌针鱼与雀鳝属于不同的鱼类科，名称相近不表示它们是同一种鱼。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Needlefish corresponds to the marine sense but generally covers a broader group; gar corresponds to the North American sense; alligator gar names only one particular gar species. Marine needlefish and gars belong to different fish families despite the overlapping common names.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: gar 的历史意象是“矛”：尖颌像矛的鱼；再按海水、淡水语境区分具体所指。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the historical spear image: a fish with spear-like jaws; use the marine or freshwater context to identify the intended fish.

morphology.text: gel（凝胶） + -ation（过程） → gelation（形成凝胶的过程）。

etymology.text: “成胶”这个义项由英语 gel 加 -ation 构成。另一个较早的“冻结”义来自拉丁语 gelatio；本卡记液体逐渐形成凝胶的画面。

usage_note: 用于材料、食品等领域。本卡只教“成胶”，不把它直接当作“结冰”或“蒸发”。

senses.meaning_zh: 胶凝；液体或溶胶形成凝胶的过程
senses.meaning_en: the process of forming a gel
senses.english_definition: Gelation is the process in which a liquid or sol develops a network that makes it become a gel.
senses.collocation_zh: 胶凝时间；胶凝温度
senses.sentence_en: The researchers measured how temperature affected the gelation time.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员测量了温度对胶凝时间的影响。

etymology_story.zh: 英语中较早表示“冻结”的 gelation 源自拉丁语 gelatio，与 gelare（冻结）有关。现代科学中的“胶凝”义则与 gel（凝胶）及表示过程的 -ation 相联系，强调材料形成凝胶，而非必然结冰。
etymology_story.en: An older English sense meaning freezing comes from Latin gelatio, related to gelare, meaning to freeze. The modern scientific sense is associated with gel and the process suffix -ation, referring to gel formation without necessarily involving ice.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 gel（凝胶；形成凝胶）+ -ation（过程）→ gelation（胶凝）。主要相关词包括 gel、gels、gelled、gelling，以及 gelator（成胶剂）；gelatin（明胶）和 gelatinous（胶状的）属于历史相关词，不是由 gelation 直接派生的词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: gel + -ation, a process suffix, → gelation. Principal related forms include gel, gels, gelled, gelling, and gelator, a substance that promotes gel formation; gelatin and gelatinous are historically related words rather than direct derivatives of gelation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gel formation（凝胶形成）是最直接的同义表达；gelling（成胶）常用于较一般的技术或日常描述；solidification（凝固）范围更广，并不一定涉及凝胶网络的形成。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gel formation is the closest equivalent; gelling is common in less formal technical or everyday descriptions; solidification is broader and does not necessarily involve the formation of a gel network.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: gel 是凝胶，-ation 表过程：液体内部“织出网”，就是胶凝。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Gel names the material; -ation names the process: a liquid builds an internal network and becomes a gel.

morphology.text: gelee 作为独立借词、独立词素记忆；gelee + -like（像……的） → gelee-like（胶冻状的）。-like 表示相似，不是原词内部的组成部分。

etymology.text: 借自法语 gelée，意为胶冻、果冻；它可追溯到中古法语。想象餐盘上一小块透明、会轻轻颤动的果冻。

usage_note: 多见于餐饮菜单；也写 gelée。本卡采用无重音符号拼写 gelee，只教食品义，不教化妆品凝胶义。

etymology_story.zh: gelee 是法语 gelée 去掉重音符号后的英语借词形式；法语词原与 geler（冻结）的过去分词有关，可追溯至拉丁语 gelare（冻结）。它从“冻结、凝结”的概念发展出烹饪中的“胶冻”义。
etymology_story.en: Gelee is an English borrowing of French gelée with its accent omitted; the French word is connected with the past participle of geler, to freeze, ultimately from Latin gelare. The idea of freezing or setting developed into the culinary meaning of a jelly.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 gelee 是整体借入的词，通常不拆分为英语词根和词缀；带重音符号的拼写为 gelée。复数为 gelees 或 gelées；没有常用的固定派生词族，gelee-like（胶冻状的）只是临时构成的相似性表达。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, gelee is a whole-word borrowing and is not normally divided into English roots and affixes; gelée is the accented spelling. Its plural is gelees or gelées; it has no common established derivational family, and gelee-like is simply a transparent formation expressing resemblance.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: jelly（果冻；胶冻）是更普通、范围更广的用词；gel（凝胶）侧重物理状态或材料性质，不一定是食品；aspic（肉冻；咸味胶冻）专指咸味凝冻食品，不能泛指甜味 gelee。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Jelly is the more ordinary and broader term; gel describes a physical state or material and need not be edible; aspic specifically refers to a savory jelly and does not cover sweet gelees.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“凝住”的画面：调味液体凝成一块轻颤的胶冻。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture flavored liquid setting into a delicate, wobbling jelly: that is a gelee.

usage_note: 解剖学用语，常见于 glenoid cavity；这里描述骨性关节窝，不能泛指身体的任何空腔。

senses.meaning_zh: 浅窝状的；关节盂的

etymology_story.zh: glenoid 源自希腊语 glēnoeidēs，意为“关节窝状的”，由 glēnē（关节窝，也指眼球）和表示“形似”的成分构成。它先用于描述浅窝状的解剖结构，后来也作为名词指关节盂本身。
etymology_story.en: Glenoid comes from Greek glēnoeidēs, meaning socket-shaped, formed from glēnē, a joint socket or eyeball, and an element meaning resembling. It describes shallow, socket-like anatomical structures and is also used as a noun for the joint socket itself.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代医学构词可分析为 glen-（关节窝）+ -oid（形似……的）→ glenoid。相关词包括 glenoidal（关节盂的）、glenohumeral（盂肱的）、glenolabral（关节盂与盂唇的）、supraglenoid（关节盂上的）和 infraglenoid（关节盂下的）；名词复数为 glenoids。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern medical analysis: glen-, joint socket, + -oid, resembling, → glenoid. Related forms include glenoidal, relating to the glenoid; glenohumeral, involving the glenoid and humerus; glenolabral, involving the glenoid and labrum; supraglenoid, above the glenoid; and infraglenoid, below it. The noun plural is glenoids.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: glenoidal（关节盂的）与形容词 glenoid 意义接近，但使用较少；glenoid cavity（关节盂）明确指解剖结构；socket（窝；承窝）范围更广，可指多种解剖结构或机械承接部位。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Glenoidal is a less common adjective with a closely related meaning; glenoid cavity explicitly names the anatomical structure; socket is broader and can describe various anatomical hollows or mechanical receptacles.

morphology.text: gray（灰色） + beige（米色） → greige（灰米色的）：这是英语中对该颜色词的混成理解，保留两种颜色的部分读音。

etymology.text: 先由法语 grège 借入，法语又承自意大利语 greggio，原指未加工的状态；英语后来把它与 gray 和 beige 联系起来，用于灰米色。

etymology_story.zh: 纺织用语 greige 借自法语 grège，后者来自意大利语 greggio，表示“未经加工的”。后来，灰米色这一颜色义受到 gray（灰色）和 beige（米色）的混成联想影响，因此不能用这两个英语词解释其全部历史。
etymology_story.en: The textile term greige was borrowed from French grège, from Italian greggio, meaning raw or unprocessed. The later color sense was influenced by a blend-like association with gray and beige, so those English words do not explain its entire history.

morphology_enriched.zh: 纺织义中的 greige 是整体借词；颜色义可按 gray（灰色）+ beige（米色）的混成关系理解，没有可独立分出的常用英语词缀。它可直接兼作形容词和颜色名词，没有常用的固定派生词族；greige goods 和 greige fabric 是常见词组。
morphology_enriched.en: In its textile sense, greige is a whole-word borrowing; its color sense can be understood through a blend of gray and beige, without a separately identifiable common English affix. It functions directly as both an adjective and a color noun and has no common established derivational family; greige goods and greige fabric are standard phrases.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 颜色方面，taupe（灰褐色）通常带更明显的褐色调，beige（米色）通常更偏浅黄褐色；纺织方面，unbleached（未漂白的）只说明未经过漂白，不能完整表达 greige 所指的未染整状态。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For color, taupe generally has a more noticeable brown component, while beige is usually more yellowish or light brown; in textiles, unbleached specifies only the absence of bleaching and does not fully express the unfinished state conveyed by greige.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 颜色记 gray + beige；纺织记“坯布还没漂染”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: For color, remember gray + beige; for textiles, picture raw fabric before bleaching and dyeing.

etymology.text: 来自新拉丁语属名 Guaiacum；该名称经西班牙语 guayaco 追溯到泰诺语 guayacan。它把加勒比地区的树木名称带进了英语。

etymology_story.zh: guaiac 经法语等欧洲语言形式传入英语，可追溯到西班牙语 guayaco 以及泰诺语的加勒比树名 guayacán；新拉丁语属名 Guaiacum 与它同源。词义从树木及木材扩展到树脂，再在临床用语中转作动词，表示用这种树脂制成的试剂进行检测。
etymology_story.en: Guaiac entered English through European forms including French and ultimately traces through Spanish guayaco to the Taíno Caribbean tree name guayacán; the New Latin genus name Guaiacum has the same origin. Its meaning extended from the tree and wood to the resin, and clinical usage also converted it into a verb for testing with a reagent made from that resin.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 guaiac 是不可再按英语词缀拆分的借词；动词由名词直接转类而来，仅用于专业临床语境。相关词包括 guaiacum（愈创木或其树脂）、guaiacol（愈创木酚，名称中的 -ol 表示醇类或酚类化合物）和 guaiaconic acid（愈创木脂酸）；这些相关名称不表示 guaiac 本身由相同片段拼合而成。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, guaiac is a borrowing without a productive internal English affix structure; the specialized clinical verb is formed by direct conversion from the noun. Related terms include guaiacum, the tree or its resin; guaiacol, whose -ol ending identifies an alcohol or phenolic compound; and guaiaconic acid. These related names do not imply that guaiac itself is assembled from the same components.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: guaiacum（愈创木；愈创木脂）与名词 guaiac 意义最接近，也可指植物属名；lignum vitae（铁梨木；愈创木材）主要指这种坚硬木材，不指检测试剂；occult blood test（隐血试验）是更广的检测类别，并非都使用愈创木脂。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Guaiacum is the closest noun equivalent and can also name the botanical genus; lignum vitae chiefly names the hard wood and does not mean the testing reagent; occult blood test names a broader category of tests, not all of which use guaiac.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一条材料链：愈创木树 → 木材中的树脂 → 隐血检测试剂 → 用它检测。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the material chain: guaiac tree → resin from its wood → a hidden-blood reagent → testing with that reagent.

usage_note: 动物学和解剖学用语；常修饰 pouch、area、fluttering 等。它表示所在部位，不直接表示疾病。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 gula，意为“喉咙”，加上表示所属关系的形容词后缀。英语主要在动物学和解剖学中使用这个词，描述喉部的位置或结构。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin gula, meaning 'throat,' with an adjective-forming suffix expressing a relationship. In English, it is used chiefly in zoology and anatomy for structures or regions associated with the throat.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代专业词汇可分析为 gul-（喉）+ -ar（与……有关的）。本词没有常用的派生动词或副词；常见术语组合有 gular pouch（喉囊）、gular sac（喉囊）和 gular plate（喉板）。
morphology_enriched.en: In technical vocabulary, the structure is gul- ('throat') + -ar ('relating to'). There are no commonly used derived verbs or adverbs; established combinations include gular pouch, gular sac, and gular plate.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: throat-related 是通俗、宽泛的“与喉部有关的”；pharyngeal 专指咽部；laryngeal 专指喉头。gular 常用于动物喉部及其外部结构，不能与后两者随意互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Throat-related is a broad everyday equivalent; pharyngeal specifically concerns the pharynx; laryngeal specifically concerns the larynx. Gular often describes an animal's throat region and external throat structures, so these terms are not freely interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: gul- 指“喉”：把 gular pouch 想成鸟喉下鼓起的囊。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect gul- with 'throat': picture a bird inflating the pouch beneath its throat.

meaning: 升降索（升降帆或旗的绳索）

forms: 可数名词；复数 halliards。halyard 是同义拼写。
family: halyard 升降索；hale / haul 拉、拖。

morphology.text: 历史结构 hale（用力拉） + -ier（工具） → halier（用于拉起的索） → halliard；现代拼写作为独立词素记忆，不把结尾硬拆成 yard。

etymology.text: 这是 halyard 的异体拼写，可追溯到中古英语 halier。英语后来受 yard 的拼写影响改变了词尾；记住它的工作是把帆或旗拉起来。

usage_note: 航海用语，也用于旗杆。halliard 和 halyard 指同一种索；不要误作普通测量单位 yard。

senses.meaning_zh: 升降索；用于升降帆、旗等的绳索
senses.meaning_en: a rope used to raise or lower a sail, flag, or similar object
senses.english_definition: A halliard is a rope that you use to raise or lower a sail, a flag, or another object on a mast or pole.
senses.collocation_zh: 升旗索；主帆升降索
senses.sentence_en: She pulled the halliard to raise the flag.

etymology_story.zh: halliard 是 halyard 的异体拼写，可追溯到中古英语 halier，与 halen（拉、拖）有关。后来的词尾拼写受到 yard（帆桁）的影响，但不能据此把它的历史来源简单解释为 haul + yard。
etymology_story.en: Halliard is a variant spelling of halyard, traceable to Middle English halier and related to halen, meaning 'to haul or pull.' Its later ending was influenced by yard, the spar supporting a sail, but its historical formation is not simply haul + yard.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜把 halliard 视为整体词干，不作能产的词根加后缀拆分。常见拼写为 halyard；复数分别为 halliards、halyards；flag halliard（升旗索）和 main halliard（主帆升降索）是复合术语。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, halliard is best treated as a whole stem rather than a productive root-and-suffix formation. The usual spelling is halyard; the plurals are halliards and halyards. Flag halliard and main halliard are compound technical terms.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: halyard 是同一个词的通常拼写，意义相同；line 泛指船上各种绳索；sheet 指调节帆角度的帆脚索，功能不同，不能用来替换 halliard。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Halyard is the usual spelling of the same word, with no difference in meaning. Line is a broader nautical term for a rope; sheet means a line used to control a sail's angle and is a functional contrast rather than an interchangeable synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住历史上的“拉”：halliard 是把帆或旗拉上去的索。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the historical idea of pulling: a halliard pulls a sail or flag upward.

senses.meaning_zh: 锚链孔；船首供锚链或锚缆通过的部位
senses.meaning_en: an opening or the part of a ship's bow through which an anchor cable passes
senses.english_definition: A ship's hawse is an opening, or the area at the bow containing such openings, through which its anchor cables pass.
senses.collocation_zh: 锚链孔；锚链管
senses.sentence_en: The anchor chain ran out through the hawse.

senses.meaning_zh: 双锚泊时两根锚缆的相对状态
senses.meaning_en: the relative arrangement of a ship's two anchor cables
senses.english_definition: When a ship is anchored with two anchors, its hawse is the arrangement of the two cables, especially whether they are clear or crossed.
senses.collocation_en: a clear hawse; a foul hawse
senses.collocation_zh: 锚缆互不交缠的状态；锚缆交缠的状态
senses.sentence_en: The ship's turn left her with a foul hawse.
senses.sentence_zh: 船身转动后，两根锚缆交缠在了一起。

etymology_story.zh: 源自中古英语 halse，通常追溯至古诺尔斯语 háls，原义为“颈部”。在航海用语中，这个词转而指船首与锚缆有关的部位，并进一步用于描述双锚缆的排列状态。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Middle English halse, generally traced to Old Norse háls, meaning 'neck.' Nautical usage applied it to the bow region associated with anchor cables and extended it to the arrangement of two such cables.

morphology_enriched.zh: hawse 在现代英语中是不可进一步拆分的词干。词族主要包括复合词 hawsehole（锚链孔）、hawsepipe（锚链管）和 hawsepiece（锚链孔部位的船首构件）；复数为 hawses。hawser（粗缆）不能按 hawse + -r 分析。
morphology_enriched.en: Hawse is an unsegmented stem in modern English. Its family consists chiefly of compounds such as hawsehole, hawsepipe, and hawsepiece; its plural is hawses. Hawser is not formed by adding -r to hawse.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hawsehole 明确指锚链穿过的孔；hawsepipe 指衬护或形成通道的管状结构。hawse 的范围较宽，还可指相关船首部位或双锚缆状态，因此这几个词并非在所有语境中都能互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hawsehole specifically names the opening through which an anchor cable passes; hawsepipe names the tubular structure forming or lining that passage. Hawse has a broader range, including the relevant bow region and the arrangement of two anchor cables.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住“船的颈口”：锚链从这里穿出，再联想到两根锚链是否交缠。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the ship's 'neck opening,' where anchor cables emerge; then picture whether two cables remain clear or become crossed.

morphology.text: be-（加强语气） + hest（命令） → behest（吩咐、命令）；hest 本身作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 中古英语 hest、hes 来自古英语 hǣs，与“命令”有关。它在现代更常见的亲属是 behest，想象古代统治者发出一道命令。

usage_note: 古语或文学语言。现代日常表达通常用 command 或 order；常在历史叙述中见到。

senses.meaning_zh: 命令；吩咐（古语或诗歌用语）
senses.meaning_en: a command or authoritative instruction, in archaic or poetic language
senses.english_definition: A hest is a command that someone gives, especially in old-fashioned or poetic language.
senses.collocation_en: at his hest; obey a hest
senses.collocation_zh: 奉他的命令；遵从命令
senses.sentence_en: At the king's hest, the gates were opened.

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语 hest、heste 承接古英语 hǣs（命令），末尾的 t 是后来增加的。它与古英语表示“命令”的动词属于同一历史词族，现代主要保留在古风文字中，与它相关的 behest 更常见。
etymology_story.en: Middle English hest and heste continue Old English hǣs, meaning 'command,' with a later added final t. The noun belongs to the historical family of an Old English verb meaning 'to command'; today it survives chiefly in archaic writing, while the related behest is more familiar.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 hest 是独立词干，复数为 hests，没有常用的能产派生词。behest（命令、要求）是历史相关词，但不宜把它当作现代英语临时用 be- + hest 构成的词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, hest is an independent stem, with the plural hests and no commonly used productive derivatives. Behest is a historical relative, but it should not be presented as a word newly formed in modern English by adding be- to hest.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: command 强调权威及服从；order 是日常和正式语境中常见的“命令”；behest 带正式或文学色彩，常见于 at someone's behest。hest 的古语、诗歌色彩最强。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Command emphasizes authority and obedience; order is the ordinary term in both everyday and official contexts; behest is formal or literary and often occurs in at someone's behest. Hest has the strongest archaic or poetic coloring.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用熟词 behest 联想：at the king's hest，就是“奉王命”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the related word behest as an anchor: at the king's hest means 'on the king's command.'

meaning: 不便的；狭窄而不舒适的

pronunciation.note: 采用美式读音；音标将词典的读音符号转写为 IPA。

forms: 比较可用 more / most incommodious。
family: commodious 宽敞方便的；incommodiously 不便地；incommodiousness 不便。

morphology.text: in-（不） + commodious（宽敞方便的） → incommodious（不便、不舒适的）。

etymology.text: 英语用否定前缀 in- 与 commodious 构成；commodious 的词根来自拉丁语 commodus，含“合适、方便”之意。给方便加一个否定，就成了难以舒适使用的状态。

usage_note: 较正式或文学化，常形容住处、座位、通道等不便使用或过于狭小。

senses.meaning_zh: 不便使用的；狭窄而不舒适的（正式或旧式用语）
senses.meaning_en: inconvenient or uncomfortable to use, especially because of insufficient space
senses.english_definition: A place or arrangement that is incommodious is inconvenient or uncomfortable, often because it does not provide enough room.
senses.collocation_zh: 狭窄不便的住所；不宽敞舒适的房间
senses.sentence_en: They spent the winter in damp, incommodious lodgings.
senses.sentence_zh: 他们在潮湿、狭窄而不舒适的住所里度过了冬天。

etymology_story.zh: 这个词体现了 in-（不）与 commodious（方便、适用，后常指宽敞舒适）的否定关系，其词源基础可追溯至拉丁语 commodus（合适、方便）。因此，它既可表示“不方便”，也可特别形容住所或空间狭窄难用。
etymology_story.en: The word expresses the negative relationship between in- ('not') and commodious ('convenient or suitable,' later especially 'spacious and comfortable'), ultimately resting on Latin commodus, meaning 'suitable or convenient.' It can therefore describe general inconvenience or, more specifically, cramped and uncomfortable accommodation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词分析为 in-（不）+ commodious（宽敞舒适的、方便的）。直接派生词有 incommodiously（不便地）和 incommodiousness（不便、狭窄不适）；相关词有 commodious、commodiously、commodiousness，以及 incommode（使不便）和较少用的 incommodity（不便）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern analysis is in- ('not') + commodious ('spacious and comfortable; convenient'). Direct derivatives are incommodiously and incommodiousness. Related words include commodious, commodiously, commodiousness, incommode, and the uncommon noun incommodity.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: inconvenient 强调带来麻烦或不便；cramped 强调空间不足、活动受限；uncomfortable 强调身体或心理上的不舒适。incommodious 常把空间不适用与使用不便结合起来，语体较正式、旧式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Inconvenient emphasizes practical difficulty; cramped emphasizes insufficient space and restricted movement; uncomfortable emphasizes a lack of physical or mental comfort. Incommodious often combines unsuitable space with practical inconvenience and sounds formal or old-fashioned.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: commodious 是“宽敞好用”，加 in-：空间挤，使用也不方便。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Commodious means roomy and convenient; add in- and picture a cramped room that is awkward to use.

meaning: 枕外隆凸（头颅后部的骨性凸起）

pronunciation.note: 采用 Cambridge 词条的英美共有读音 /ˈɪn.i.ən/。

forms: 通常用单数；复数 inia 或 inions。
family: inial 枕外隆凸的。

morphology.text: ini-（inion 的派生词干） + -al（……的） → inial（枕外隆凸的）；inion 本身作为独立解剖名词记忆。

etymology.text: 经新拉丁语来自希腊语 inion，原指头后部，与表示筋腱的希腊语词有关。记住头颅背后可以定位的一处骨性凸起。

usage_note: 解剖学定位用语，指头颅后方的特定骨性标志，不指整个后脑或大脑组织。

senses.meaning_zh: 枕外隆凸点；头颅后部枕外隆凸上最突出的测量标志点
senses.meaning_en: The most prominent point of the external occipital protuberance, used as a skull landmark.
senses.english_definition: The inion is the most prominent point on the bony projection at the back of your skull, which is used as a reference point in anatomical measurements.
senses.collocation_zh: 确定枕外隆凸点的位置；鼻根点至枕外隆凸点的距离
senses.sentence_en: The researcher measured the distance from the nasion to the inion.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员测量了鼻根点到枕外隆凸点的距离。

etymology_story.zh: 来自希腊语 inion，意为“后脑、项部”，通常认为与表示“筋、腱”的希腊语 is（属格 inos）有关。进入现代解剖学术语后，其含义缩小为头颅后部的一个特定测量标志点。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Greek inion, meaning the back of the head or nape, generally connected with Greek is, genitive inos, meaning sinew. In modern anatomical terminology, its meaning narrowed to a specific measurement landmark on the back of the skull.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，inion 是借入的完整词，不能按普通英语前后缀拆分。相关形式：复数 inia；形容词 inial（枕外隆凸点的）；派生时可分析为 ini- + -al。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, inion is a borrowed whole word rather than a combination of ordinary English affixes. Related forms are the plural inia and the adjective inial, meaning relating to the inion; the adjective can be analyzed as ini- + -al.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全对应的常用近义词。相关术语 external occipital protuberance（枕外隆凸）指整个骨性隆起，inion 指其最突出的标志点；occiput（枕部、后脑）指更大的头部区域。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday synonym. The related term external occipital protuberance names the whole bony projection, whereas inion identifies its most prominent landmark point; occiput refers to the broader back region of the head.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“后脑”定位到“后脑骨突上的一点”：inion 是测量点。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Move from “back of the head” to “one point on its bony bump”: the inion is a measurement landmark.

pronunciation.note: 采用美式读音；音标将词典的读音符号转写为 IPA。

forms: intreats；过去式、过去分词 intreated；现在分词 intreating。现代通常拼 entreat。
family: entreat 恳求，现代拼写；entreaty 恳求。

morphology.text: 历史结构 en-（加强） + treat（对待、商谈） → entreat（恳求）；intreat 是它的旧拼写，不能把 in- 当成否定。

etymology.text: 这是 entreat 的古拼写；entreat 经中古英语 entreten 来自盎格鲁法语 entreter，最初与商谈、对待有关，后来发展出迫切请求的意思。

usage_note: 古语拼写，多见于旧文学。现代写作使用 entreat；可接某人，再接 to do 表示恳求对方做事。

senses.meaning_zh: 恳求；央求；entreat 的古旧拼写

etymology_story.zh: intreat 是 entreat 的历史拼写变体；entreat 经中古英语和盎格鲁法语传入，词源与 treat 所属的“处理、对待、商谈”词族相连。词义由商谈、交涉等用法逐渐发展出“郑重请求、恳求”。
etymology_story.en: Intreat is a historical spelling variant of entreat, which entered through Middle English and Anglo-French and belongs to the same historical family as treat, involving handling, dealing, or negotiation. Its meanings developed from dealing and negotiation to making an earnest request.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代使用中应把 intreat 视为 entreat 的古旧拼写整体，不把 in- 解释为否定前缀。屈折形式：intreats、intreated、intreating；对应现代词族包括 entreat、entreats、entreated、entreating、entreaty（恳求）、entreaties（复数）和 entreatingly（恳求地）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern use, treat intreat as an archaic spelling of the whole word entreat; in- is not a negative prefix here. Inflected forms are intreats, intreated, and intreating; the corresponding modern family includes entreat, entreats, entreated, entreating, entreaty, its plural entreaties, and entreatingly.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: entreat（恳求）是现代标准拼写，与 intreat 意义相同；implore（苦苦哀求）通常更突出强烈情绪或迫切需要；beseech（恳切央求）带有较鲜明的庄重或文学色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Entreat is the standard modern spelling and has the same meaning as intreat. Implore often emphasizes stronger emotion or urgent need, while beseech has a distinctly solemn or literary tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 古书里的 intreat，就是今天的 entreat：把请求说得格外恳切。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Intreat in an old text is today's entreat: an especially earnest request.

senses.meaning_zh: 虹膜炎

etymology_story.zh: 这是由 iris（虹膜）和表示炎症的医学后缀 -itis 构成的医学词。iris 源自希腊语“彩虹”，后来因眼睛这一部分具有颜色而用来指虹膜。
etymology_story.en: This medical term was formed from iris and the medical suffix -itis, meaning inflammation. Iris comes from the Greek word for rainbow and was later applied to the colored part of the eye.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：ir-（iris 在此词中的词干形式，虹膜）+ -itis（炎症）→ iritis。相关形式：iritic（虹膜炎的）；医学复数 iritides；基础词 iris 的复数为 irises 或 irides；相关复合词 iridocyclitis（虹膜睫状体炎）使用词干 irid-。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: ir-, the stem form of iris used here, + -itis, meaning inflammation, → iritis. Related forms include iritic, meaning relating to iritis, and the medical plural iritides; the base noun iris has the plurals irises and irides. The related compound iridocyclitis, inflammation of the iris and ciliary body, uses the stem irid-.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: inflammation of the iris（虹膜发炎）是直接释义；anterior uveitis（前葡萄膜炎）是范围更广的相关术语；iridocyclitis（虹膜睫状体炎）明确表示炎症同时涉及虹膜和睫状体。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Inflammation of the iris is a direct paraphrase. Anterior uveitis is a broader related term, while iridocyclitis specifically indicates inflammation involving both the iris and the ciliary body.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: iris 是眼中的“彩虹”，-itis 表示发炎：虹膜发炎就是 iritis。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Iris is the eye's “rainbow,” and -itis means inflammation: iritis is inflammation of that colored part.

etymology_story.zh: jeepney 通常被解释为 jeep（吉普车）与 jitney（小型公共载客汽车）的混成词。它得名于第二次世界大战后菲律宾将军用吉普车改装成公共载客车辆的做法，后来也用于当地制造的同类车辆。
etymology_story.en: Jeepney is commonly explained as a blend of jeep and jitney, a small public passenger vehicle. The name arose from the Philippine practice of converting military jeeps into public transport after the Second World War and later extended to locally built vehicles of the same general type.

morphology_enriched.zh: 通常的混成分析：jeep + jitney 的末尾部分 -ney → jeepney；-ney 不是能自由构词的英语后缀。常用屈折形式为复数 jeepneys；jeepney driver（吉普尼司机）、jeepney route（吉普尼线路）属于名词组合，不构成独立形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: The usual blend analysis is jeep + the ending -ney from jitney → jeepney; -ney is not a freely productive English suffix. The regular plural is jeepneys. Expressions such as jeepney driver and jeepney route are noun combinations and do not establish a separate adjective part of speech.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: minibus（小巴）强调车辆较小；shared taxi（合乘出租车）强调多名乘客共享车辆；jitney（小型公共载客汽车）是相关的英语词，但这些词都不必然指菲律宾特有的 jeepney。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Minibus emphasizes a small bus, shared taxi emphasizes passengers sharing a vehicle, and jitney is a related term for a small public passenger vehicle. None necessarily identifies the specifically Philippine vehicle called a jeepney.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: jeep 的车头，jitney 的载客用途：拼成菲律宾 jeepney。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A jeep's front with a jitney's passenger-carrying role: picture a Philippine jeepney.

etymology_story.en: Jujube entered English through French and can be traced through Medieval Latin jujuba and Latin zizyphum to Greek zizyphon, names for the fruit. It also came to name the tree and a confection originally made with or flavored with the fruit.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，jujube 是完整借词，没有可独立分析的常用英语词根和词缀；复数为 jujubes。常见组合有 jujube tree（枣树）、jujube fruit（枣果）和 jujube paste（枣泥）；jujube-like（像枣的）是可按需构成的复合形容词，并非核心固定派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, jujube is a whole borrowed word without a useful breakdown into ordinary English roots and affixes; its plural is jujubes. Common combinations include jujube tree, jujube fruit, and jujube paste. Jujube-like is a possible descriptive compound adjective rather than a core established derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chinese date and red date can name the fruit, with red date especially common for red or dried jujubes. Gumdrop is a near equivalent only for the confectionery sense and cannot refer to the fruit or tree.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 kurta 经印地语和乌尔都语 kurtā 借入，进一步源自波斯语 kurta，意为衬衣或长衫。这个服装名称随着南亚传统衣着进入英语。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed kurta through Hindi and Urdu kurtā, ultimately from Persian kurta, meaning a shirt or tunic. The garment's name entered English along with knowledge of traditional South Asian clothing.

morphology_enriched.zh: kurta 是整体借入的名词，现代英语中不拆作词根加词缀；kurta + 复数词尾 -s → kurtas。相关服装名称 kurti（通常较短的女式长衫）也是南亚语言借词，不是用英语后缀从 kurta 派生出来的词。
morphology_enriched.en: Kurta is a borrowed noun that is not divided into a root and affixes in modern English; kurta + plural -s gives kurtas. The related garment name kurti, usually a shorter women's tunic, is another South Asian loanword rather than an English suffixal derivative of kurta.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tunic（束腰外衣或长上衣）是范围更广的近义词；shirt（衬衣）只说明服装大类；kameez（南亚长上衣）指相关的南亚服装，其剪裁和搭配习惯可能与 kurta 不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tunic is a broader near-synonym; shirt identifies only the general garment category; kameez names a related South Asian garment whose cut and customary combinations may differ from those of a kurta.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 kurta 整体记成“宽松、长身、南亚长衫”的轮廓，不硬拆词。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember kurta as one whole word attached to the silhouette of a loose, long South Asian shirt.

etymology_story.zh: laic 经后期拉丁语 laicus 源自希腊语 laikos，原意为“属于人民的”，其基础是 laos（人民）。在基督教语境中，它逐渐用来区分普通信徒与神职人员，后来也发展出“世俗的”含义。
etymology_story.en: Laic comes through Late Latin laicus from Greek laikos, meaning 'of the people,' based on laos, 'people.' In Christian usage it distinguished ordinary believers from the clergy and later also developed the meaning 'secular.'

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 laic 作为整体词基；历史上的 -ic 对应形容词后缀，但 lai- 不是可独立使用的现代英语词根。词族包括 laical（非神职的）、laically（以世俗方式）、laicity（世俗性质）、laicism（世俗主义）、laicize/laicise（使世俗化；使神职人员恢复平信徒身份）及 laicization/laicisation（世俗化；恢复平信徒身份）；名词复数为 laics。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats laic as a whole base; historically, -ic corresponds to an adjective suffix, but lai- is not an independent modern English root. Its family includes laical, laically, laicity, laicism, laicize/laicise, and laicization/laicisation; laicize can mean either to secularize or to return a cleric to lay status. The noun plural is laics.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: lay（非神职的；平信徒）最适合表示神职身份上的区别；secular（世俗的）强调与宗教事务或宗教控制相分离；nonclerical（非神职的）仅说明不属于神职群体，不必表示没有宗教信仰。laic 较正式，名词用法尤其少见。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lay most directly marks the distinction between clergy and ordinary people; secular emphasizes separation from religious concerns or control; nonclerical merely indicates that someone is outside the clergy and does not imply a lack of religious belief. Laic is formal, especially as a noun.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: laos“人民”→ 普通信众 → 非神职的；进一步联想到世俗事务。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Laos means 'people': ordinary believers lead to 'nonclerical,' then to the broader idea of secular affairs.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 lakh 借自印地语和乌尔都语 lākh，可追溯到梵语表示“十万”的 lakṣa，中间经历了中古印度语言形式的演变。它随南亚计数习惯进入英语，至今广泛用于当地的金额和人口表达。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed lakh from Hindi and Urdu lākh, ultimately from Sanskrit lakṣa, 'one hundred thousand,' through Middle Indo-Aryan forms. It entered English with South Asian counting practices and remains widely used there for money and population figures.

morphology_enriched.zh: lakh 是整体借入的计数词，没有英语词缀可拆。接在具体数词后通常不变形，如 five lakh；独立名词复数可为 lakhs，如 lakhs of people。相关借词 lakhpati 指拥有至少十万卢比财富的人，其中 pati 在来源语言中意为“主人”，不是英语后缀。
morphology_enriched.en: Lakh is a borrowed counting term with no English affixes to separate. It normally remains unchanged after a specific numeral, as in five lakh, but takes the noun plural lakhs in expressions such as lakhs of people. The related loanword lakhpati denotes someone with wealth of at least one hundred thousand rupees; pati means 'master' in the source language and is not an English suffix.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: one hundred thousand（十万）与 one lakh 数值完全相同，是国际英语中更通用的表达；a hundred grand（十万块钱）是非正式金额表达，只适用于金钱，且具体币种依语境而定。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: One hundred thousand is numerically identical to one lakh and is more widely understood internationally; a hundred grand is an informal monetary equivalent, applies only to money, and depends on context for its currency.

mnemonic_anchor.en: One lakh equals 100,000: the South Asian grouping 1,00,000 represents the same number.

etymology_story.en: Latten comes from Middle English forms such as latoun and laton, borrowed from Anglo-French and Old French laton; its earlier origin is uncertain. morphology_enriched.zh: latten 在现代英语中是不可再拆分的材料名，词尾 -en 不是可用于本词分析的现代英语后缀。通常用作不可数名词，没有常用的派生词族；latten plate（拉顿铜合金薄板）等是名词修饰名词的组合。

etymology_story.zh: 英语 lento 借自意大利语 lento，意为“缓慢的”，其源头是拉丁语 lentus，曾表示“柔韧的、迟缓的”。它作为乐谱速度指示进入英语，随后也用于修饰或指称慢速乐段。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed lento from Italian lento, meaning “slow,” ultimately from Latin lentus, which had meanings including “pliant” and “sluggish.” Its use as a musical direction extended to describing and naming slow passages.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 lento 是不可再拆分的意大利语借词；同一形式可作副词、形容词和名词。名词复数为 lentos，也可用意大利语复数 lenti；相关音乐术语有 lentissimo“极缓慢地”，其意大利语构词为 lent- + -issimo，不能分析为保留完整 lento 后直接添加后缀。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, lento is an unanalyzed Italian loanword used as an adverb, adjective, and noun. Its noun plurals are lentos and Italian lenti; the related musical term lentissimo means “very slowly” and has the Italian structure lent- + -issimo, with the final -o of lento replaced.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: slow 表示一般意义上的“缓慢的”；adagio 指从容、舒缓的音乐速度；largo 通常强调宽广、舒展的慢速。lento 直接强调速度缓慢，这些音乐术语的具体速度范围会因作品和演奏传统而重叠。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Slow is the general term; adagio suggests a leisurely, unhurried musical pace; largo emphasizes a broad, spacious slow pace. Lento directly emphasizes slowness, and the practical tempo ranges of these musical terms can overlap.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 看到 lento，就把乐谱中的时间拉长：慢速演奏，也可指慢速乐段。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Let lento stretch musical time: play slowly, or name the slow passage itself.

etymology.text: 来自 letcher 与 lecher 的缩短或变形；lecher 经中古英语来自古法语，早期有贪食、放纵之人的意味，后来用于好色者。

usage_note: 口语贬义词，对人的强烈负面评价，不宜随意用于普通的赞美或恋爱兴趣。

etymology_story.zh: letch 与 lech 是相关的拼写形式，其历史与 lecher 及旧拼写 letcher 的缩短有关。lecher 经中古英语来自古法语 lecheor，早期可指贪食或放纵的人，后来专指好色者。
etymology_story.en: Letch is related to the spelling lech and historically to shortened forms of lecher and its older spelling letcher. Lecher came through Middle English from Old French lecheor, which could describe a gluttonous or self-indulgent person before acquiring its specifically sexual sense.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语把 letch 视为独立词基，名词和动词形式相同；常用屈折形式为 letches、letched、letching。拼写变体为 lech；历史相关词族包括 lecher“好色之徒”、lecherous“好色的”、lecherously“好色地”、lecherousness“好色”和 lechery“淫荡行为”，不能把这些词全部当作由现代 letch 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats letch as an independent base used as both noun and verb; its regular inflections are letches, letched, and letching. Lech is a spelling variant; the historically related family includes lecher, lecherous, lecherously, lecherousness, and lechery, rather than a set of direct modern derivatives of letch.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: lecher 与名词 letch 最接近，但语体较书面；leer 强调色迷迷的眼神，主要对应动词用法；womanizer 强调一个男人不断追逐女性或与女性发生关系，并不专指令人不适的凝视。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lecher is the closest noun synonym but is more literary; leer emphasizes a sexually suggestive look and mainly matches the verb use; womanizer describes a man who repeatedly pursues women or has relationships with them, rather than specifically someone who stares offensively.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 letch 联想到 lecher：名词是“色鬼”，动词是“色迷迷地看”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link letch with lecher: the noun names the person, and the verb names the offensive looking or behavior.

etymology_story.zh: linga 借自梵语 liṅga，基本义为“标志、特征、象征”。英语沿用了它在印度教语境中的专门含义，指代表湿婆的圣物，其宗教意义不限于外形上的生殖象征。
etymology_story.en: Linga was borrowed from Sanskrit liṅga, meaning “mark,” “characteristic,” or “symbol.” English adopted its specialized Hindu sense for an emblem of Shiva, whose religious significance extends beyond its phallic form.

morphology_enriched.zh: linga 在现代英语中是不可再拆分的借词，复数为 lingas；lingam 是相关名称形式。没有常用的英语派生词族；linga-like 可按 linga + -like 临时组成，意为“林伽状的”，但不是必须掌握的固定派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Linga is an unanalyzed loanword in modern English, with the plural lingas; lingam is a related name for the same sacred emblem. It has no established common English derivational family; linga-like can be formed productively as linga + -like, meaning “resembling a linga,” but is not a core lexical derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: lingam 是同一圣物的另一常用名称；Shiva emblem 是较宽泛的解释性说法，也可涵盖其他湿婆象征；phallic symbol 强调阳具象征，范围更广，不能完整表达林伽的宗教意义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lingam is an alternative name for the same sacred object; Shiva emblem is a broader explanatory expression that can include other representations of Shiva; phallic symbol emphasizes sexual symbolism and does not convey the linga's full religious significance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 梵语本义是“标志”：林伽就是指向湿婆的神圣标志。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with the Sanskrit meaning “mark”: a linga is a sacred mark representing Shiva.

etymology_story.en: English borrowed Hindi loṭā in the early nineteenth century as the name of a traditional South Asian water vessel. Its meaning comes directly from the object, with no connection to English lot. [Origin and definition](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/lota)

morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, lota is an unanalyzed borrowed base; its plural is lotas, and lotah is a spelling variant. It has no established common derivative family; lota-like is a possible descriptive formation rather than a standard family member.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Water pot is a broad near-equivalent; an ewer generally has a handle and spout; a jug usually has a handle and pouring lip. Lota specifically names the traditional rounded South Asian vessel, usually without a handle.

morphology.text: ly-（松开、裂解） + -ase（酶） → lyase（裂合酶）；这类酶可通过脱去基团形成双键，或把基团加到双键上。

etymology.text: 现代生物化学术语，词基来自希腊语 lyein（松开、分解），再加酶名称后缀 -ase。把“松开连接”与酶的名称连起来记。

senses.meaning_zh: 裂合酶；催化非水解、非氧化断键，或相应逆向加成反应的一类酶
senses.meaning_en: An enzyme that catalyzes bond cleavage without hydrolysis or oxidation, or the corresponding reverse addition reaction.
senses.english_definition: A lyase is an enzyme that breaks a chemical bond without using hydrolysis or oxidation, often leaving a double bond, or catalyzes the reverse reaction by adding a group across a double bond.
senses.collocation_zh: 果胶酸裂合酶；裂合酶活性

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代生物化学术语，由源自希腊语 lyein（松开、分解）的词基与酶名后缀 -ase 构成，名称突出其催化断键的作用。[词源](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/lyase)
etymology_story.en: This modern biochemical term combines a base associated with Greek lyein, meaning to loosen or dissolve, with the enzyme suffix -ase. Its name highlights its role in catalyzing bond cleavage. [Etymology](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/lyase)

morphology_enriched.zh: 科技词构词分析为 ly-（松开、裂解）＋ -ase（酶）→ lyase；复数为 lyases。同源词有 lyse（裂解）、lysis（裂解作用）、lytic（裂解的）；命名词族包括 photolyase（光裂合酶）、pectate lyase（果胶酸裂合酶）和 ATP-citrate lyase（ATP-柠檬酸裂合酶）。
morphology_enriched.en: The scientific formation is ly- meaning loosen or split + -ase meaning enzyme → lyase; the plural is lyases. Related root-family words include lyse, lysis, and lytic; enzyme names include photolyase, pectate lyase, and ATP-citrate lyase.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有适用于全部裂合酶的常用严格同义词。enzyme（酶）是上位词；bond-cleaving enzyme（断键酶）只是较宽泛的描述；hydrolase（水解酶）是对照类别，通过水解断键，不能与 lyase 互换。[分类区别](https://vitrinelinguistique.oqlf.gouv.qc.ca/fiche-gdt/fiche/26554028/lyase)
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym covering all lyases. Enzyme is the broader category; bond-cleaving enzyme is a less precise description; hydrolase is a contrasting class that cleaves bonds by hydrolysis and is not interchangeable with lyase. [Classification distinction](https://vitrinelinguistique.oqlf.gouv.qc.ca/fiche-gdt/fiche/26554028/lyase)

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ly- 表示“松开”，-ase 表示“酶”：裂合酶常把基团拆下留下双键，也能反向加回。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ly- suggests loosening and -ase signals an enzyme: remove a group to leave a double bond, or add it back in the reverse reaction.

morphology.text: male-（坏） + fact-（做） + -ion（行为） → malefaction（恶行）；fact- 在这里与拉丁语“做”的词干相连。

etymology.text: 来自后期拉丁语 malefactio，关联拉丁语 malefacere（做坏事）。把“坏”与“所做的事”连起来，就是恶行。

usage_note: 正式或文学化的名词，比 everyday wrongdoing 更庄重；可指犯罪，也可指恶劣行为。
