etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 malefactio，与 malefacere（作恶）相连，后者由 male（坏地）和 facere（做）组成；“做坏事”的基本含义保留为英语中的恶行或违法行为。[词源与释义](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/malefaction)
etymology_story.en: It comes from Latin malefactio, associated with malefacere, to do wrong, formed from male meaning badly and facere meaning do. The underlying idea of doing evil survives in its English meaning of wrongdoing or a criminal act. [Origin and definition](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/malefaction)

morphology_enriched.zh: 可按拉丁词素分析为 male-（坏地）＋ fact-（做）＋ -ion（行为或结果）；这是借入词的词素分析，并非由现代英语 male 和 faction 拼成。复数为 malefactions；相关词族有 malefactor（作恶者）、malefic（有害的）、maleficent（作恶的）和 maleficence（恶意、恶行）。
morphology_enriched.en: Its Latinate elements are male- meaning badly + fact- meaning do + -ion marking an action or result; this analyzes a borrowing rather than a compound of modern English male and faction. The plural is malefactions; related family words include malefactor, malefic, maleficent, and maleficence.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: misdeed（不当行为）可指较轻的过错；wrongdoing（不法或不当行为）通常概括行为整体；crime（犯罪）明确涉及法律禁止。malefaction 语体更庄重，强调作恶，但不必专指法律上的犯罪。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Misdeed can refer to a relatively minor wrong; wrongdoing usually describes improper conduct collectively; crime specifically concerns an act prohibited by law. Malefaction is more elevated and emphasizes evil conduct without necessarily establishing a legal offense.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: male- 坏地＋ fact- 做＋ -ion 行为＝“做出的坏事”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Badly + do + action gives the core idea: a bad deed.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 maleficus（作恶的、有害的），由 male（坏地）和与 facere（做、造成）有关的 -ficus 构成；英语保留了“造成坏影响”的含义。[词源](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/malefic)
etymology_story.en: It derives from Latin maleficus, meaning harmful or evildoing, combining male meaning badly with -ficus, related to facere meaning make or do. English preserves the central idea of producing an evil influence. [Etymology](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/malefic)

morphology_enriched.zh: 可按拉丁词素分析为 male-（坏地）＋ -fic（做、造成）；这里的 male- 与表示“男性”的 male 无关。直接派生词为 malefically（有害地、恶意地）；相关词族有 maleficent（有害的）、maleficence（恶意、恶行）、malefaction（恶行）和 malefactor（作恶者）。占星名词由形容词转用，复数为 malefics。
morphology_enriched.en: Its Latinate elements are male- meaning badly + -fic meaning making or doing; male- here is unrelated to male meaning masculine. The direct derivative is malefically; related family words include maleficent, maleficence, malefaction, and malefactor. The astrological noun is a conversion of the adjective, with plural malefics.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: malign（有害的、恶意的）与形容词义接近；malevolent（恶意的）更强调希望别人受害；baleful（凶恶的、不祥的）常带威胁或灾祸色彩。名词义的直接对应表达是 malefic planet（凶星）。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Malign closely matches the harmful-influence sense; malevolent emphasizes wishing harm on others; baleful often suggests menace or impending disaster. The direct equivalent of the noun is malefic planet.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: male- 坏＋ -fic 造成＝造成坏影响；占星术把被认为有这种影响的行星称为凶星。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bad + making means producing harm; astrology applies the same label to planets believed to bring harmful influences.

pronunciation.note: 采用美式读音；音标将词典的读音符号转写为 IPA。

forms: 可数名词；复数 mantelets；也读 /ˌmæntəˈlɛt/。
family: mantle 披风；mantlet 可指军事掩体，是相关拼写。

morphology.text: mantel（旧法语“披风”词基） + -et（小称后缀） → mantelet（小披风；短披肩）。

etymology.text: 中古英语从盎格鲁法语借入，是 mantel（披风）的指小形式。把一件大披风缩成只罩住肩部的小披肩，就容易记住。

usage_note: 服装史用语。本卡只教短披肩义；同词还有古代攻城防护掩体义，需由穿戴或军事语境区分。

senses.meaning_zh: 活动护屏；移动掩体，尤指历史上用于保护攻城者或炮手的屏障，亦拼作 mantlet
senses.meaning_en: A movable protective screen or shelter, especially one used historically by soldiers; also spelled mantlet.
senses.english_definition: A mantelet is a movable barrier that soldiers use for protection from enemy weapons, especially during a siege.
senses.collocation_en: a wooden mantelet; behind a mantelet
senses.collocation_zh: 木制活动护屏；在活动护屏后面

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语借自古法语 mantelet，是 mantel（披风）的指小形式，字面义为“小披风”；英语中的服饰义和军事护屏义都体现了覆盖、遮护的概念。[词源与两项释义](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/mantelet)
etymology_story.en: Middle English borrowed Old French mantelet, a diminutive of mantel meaning cloak, literally a little cloak. Its clothing and military-screen senses both express the idea of covering or sheltering. [Origin and both senses](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/mantelet)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常整体记忆；历史构词为古法语 mantel（披风）＋ -et（小称后缀）。复数为 mantelets，异体拼写为 mantlet；没有常用的直接派生词族。mantle（披风、覆盖物）是同源相关词，其派生或屈折形式 mantled、mantling 不应误列为 mantelet 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats it as a whole borrowed word; historically it is Old French mantel meaning cloak + diminutive -et. The plural is mantelets, and mantlet is a spelling variant; there is no common direct derivative family. Mantle is a related word, but mantled and mantling belong directly to mantle rather than mantelet.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 服饰义中，cape（披肩、斗篷）最接近；cloak（斗篷）通常较长；shawl（披巾）通常是披裹用的布片。军事义中，protective screen（防护屏）是较宽泛的对应表达，强调屏障功能。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For clothing, cape is the closest general equivalent; cloak usually suggests a longer garment; shawl generally denotes a piece of fabric draped around the body. In the military sense, protective screen is a broader equivalent emphasizing its barrier function.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“小披风”记起：披在肩上是短斗篷，挡在兵前是护屏。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with a little cloak: over the shoulders it is a cape; in front of soldiers it is a protective screen.

forms: 形容词，无时态变化；也可读 /ˈmæntrɪk/。
family: mantra 真言；咒语；mantras 为其复数。

morphology.text: mantr-（mantra 的词干，真言） + -ic（……的） → mantric（真言的；咒语的）；加后缀时去掉 mantra 的末尾 a。

etymology.text: 由 mantra 加形容词后缀构成；mantra 借自梵语，原指神圣的言辞、祈请公式，与“思考”的词根相连。

usage_note: 本卡教宗教真言相关义。mantra 在日常英语中也可指反复强调的口号，需区分具体场景。

senses.meaning_en: relating to mantras or their recitation
senses.english_definition: Mantric words or practices involve sacred words or sounds repeated in prayer or meditation.
senses.collocation_zh: 真言吟诵；真言冥想
senses.sentence_en: The ceremony began with mantric chanting.

senses.meaning_zh: 如咒语般反复的；具有反复吟诵效果的
senses.meaning_en: repeated or rhythmical in a way that resembles a mantra
senses.english_definition: If words or music are mantric, their repeated sounds or phrases create an insistent or absorbing effect.
senses.collocation_zh: 咒语般的反复；咒语般循环的节奏

etymology_story.zh: mantric 由 mantra 加形容词后缀构成；mantra 借自梵语 mantra，意为神圣的言辞或祈请公式，与表示“思考”的词根有关。由真言反复持诵的特点，又产生了“咒语般反复的”这一引申义。参见[《美国传统英语词典》](https://ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=mantric)。
etymology_story.en: Mantric is formed from mantra, borrowed from Sanskrit mantra, a sacred utterance or formula associated with a root meaning 'think'. The repeated recitation of mantras also gives the adjective its extended meaning of insistently repetitive; see the [American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=mantric).

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：mantra（真言）去掉词尾 -a，再加 -ic（……的）→ mantric。核心词族：mantra（名词，真言；反复强调的话）、mantras（名词复数）、mantric（形容词，真言的；咒语般反复的）；这里的 mantr- 是 mantra 的构词词干，不是独立英语单词。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: mantra loses its final -a before the adjective suffix -ic, producing mantric. The core family comprises mantra (a sacred formula or repeatedly stated principle), mantras (its plural), and mantric; mantr- is the combining stem of mantra, not an independent English word.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: incantatory（咒语般的）强调吟诵的声音和感染力；ritualistic（仪式性的）强调固定仪式或程式；repetitive（反复的）仅强调重复，未必具有宗教意味或催眠般的效果。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Incantatory emphasizes the sound and evocative power of chanting; ritualistic emphasizes prescribed ceremonies or routines; repetitive simply indicates repetition, without necessarily suggesting religion or an absorbing effect.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: mantra 是“反复念的真言”，mantric 就是“真言的”，也可指“像真言一样反复的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A mantra is a repeated sacred formula; mantric means belonging to it or repeating like it.

meaning: 大理石般冷峻的；冷漠端肃的

pronunciation.note: 采用美式读音；音标将词典的读音符号转写为 IPA。

forms: 形容词；副词 marmoreally；相关形容词 marmorean。
family: marmoreally 冷峻地；marmorean 大理石般的；marble 大理石。

morphology.text: marmoreal（大理石般冷峻的） + -ly（副词后缀） → marmoreally（冷峻地）；marmoreal 的词基与拉丁语 marmor（大理石）相连。

etymology.text: 来自拉丁语 marmoreus（大理石的），其基础是 marmor（大理石）。从冰冷、光滑的雕像联想到人的冷峻神态。

usage_note: 文学性较强；可描述大理石般的外观，也可比喻人冷峻、疏离的神态。本卡重点教后者。

senses.meaning_zh: 大理石制的；具有大理石外观或质感的
senses.meaning_en: made of marble or resembling marble
senses.english_definition: Something marmoreal is made of marble or resembles its pale, smooth, hard surface.

senses.sentence_en: Soft lighting enhanced the hall's marmoreal splendour.

senses.meaning_en: cold, aloof, solemn, or lacking animation
senses.english_definition: Someone or something marmoreal seems cold, still, or emotionally distant, like a marble statue.

etymology_story.zh: 该词以拉丁语 marmoreus（大理石制的）为基础，而 marmoreus 来自 marmor（大理石），英语形式带有后缀 -al。大理石雕像冰冷、静止的形象进一步引出了形容人冷峻或缺乏生气的用法。参见[《牛津高阶英语词典》](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/marmoreal)。
etymology_story.en: The word is based on Latin marmoreus, 'made of marble', from marmor, 'marble', with the English suffix -al. The coldness and stillness of marble statues motivated its figurative application to people and performances; see the [Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/marmoreal).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 marmoreal 作为完整的借源形容词学习；可作词源性分析：marmore-（与大理石有关的词干）+ -al（形容词后缀）。词族：marmoreal（大理石的；冷峻的）、marmoreally（副词，大理石般地；冷峻地）、marmorean（较少见的同义形容词）；marble（大理石）与其历史同源，并非由 marmoreal 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, marmoreal is normally learned as a whole borrowed-base adjective; an etymological analysis is marmore- (a marble-related stem) + -al. Its family includes marmoreal, marmoreally (the corresponding adverb), and marmorean (a less common equivalent adjective); marble is historically related rather than derived from marmoreal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: marble-like（大理石般的）直接描述材质特征或外观；statuesque（雕像般优美庄严的）通常赞美体态或仪表；impassive（不露声色的）强调没有显露情绪，而不涉及大理石般的外貌。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Marble-like directly describes material qualities or appearance; statuesque usually praises an imposing, graceful figure; impassive describes an absence of visible emotion without implying a marble-like appearance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“大理石”想到“冰冷、光滑、静止的雕像”，再想到人的冷峻端肃。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture marble: pale, smooth, cold, and still; transfer those qualities to a person's expression or manner.

meaning: 伙伴间的亲密感；友好随意的气氛

pronunciation.note: 按 Merriam-Webster 的读音标记转写为宽式 IPA。

forms: 不可数名词，指相处时的亲近感。
family: matey 友好随和的；mateyness 同义拼写

morphology.text: matey + -ness → matiness 伙伴间的亲密感；这是 mateyness 的另一拼写，结尾改写为 -iness。

etymology.text: 英语 matey 表示像伙伴一样亲近，加表示状态的 -ness 成为 mateyness；matiness 是它的另一拼写。想象老朋友聊天时的随意亲近。

usage_note: 较少见的英式用语，常见拼写是 mateyness。形容关系或气氛，不表示朋友的数量。

etymology_story.zh: matiness 是 mateyness 的另一拼写，来自 matey（像伙伴一样亲近的）加表示状态或性质的 -ness，进一步的词基是 mate（伙伴）。它既可描述自然的亲切，也可暗示过分或刻意的熟络。
etymology_story.en: Matiness is an alternative spelling of mateyness, formed from matey, 'friendly like a companion', and the state-forming suffix -ness, ultimately based on mate. It can describe easy friendliness or suggest excessive or affected familiarity.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词链：mate（伙伴）+ -y → matey（亲热随意的）；matey + -ness → mateyness，也写作 matiness。相关词包括 mate、mates（伙伴的复数）、matey、maty（matey 的另一拼写）、mateyness、matiness，以及较少见的副词 matily（亲热随意地）；不能把 matiness 误拆为 mat（垫子）+ -iness。读音及用法参见[《柯林斯词典》](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english-spanish/matiness)。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: mate + -y → matey; matey + -ness → mateyness, alternatively spelled matiness. Related forms include mate, mates (its plural), matey, maty (a variant of matey), mateyness, matiness, and the less common adverb matily; matiness is not formed from mat plus -iness. For pronunciation and usage, see [Collins Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english-spanish/matiness).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: friendliness（友善）含义最广，不要求关系熟络；camaraderie（伙伴情谊）强调共同经历或活动形成的情感纽带；familiarity（熟悉；亲昵随便）强调关系或举止上的不拘礼节，有时暗示越界。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Friendliness is broad and does not require closeness; camaraderie emphasizes bonds formed through shared experiences or activities; familiarity emphasizes closeness or informality and can suggest taking liberties.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: mate 是“伙伴”：matiness 就是“像老伙伴一样相处”的那股亲热随意劲儿。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with mate: matiness is the quality of treating people like old companions.

meaning: 欧瑞香（一种开紫花、结红果的灌木）

pronunciation.note: 采用美式读法；词典用参照 mezereon 的省略标音表示词尾 -eum，此处展开转写。

forms: 植物个体可数，复数 mezereums；本课指灌木，不指旧时药用树皮。
family: mezereon 同一种灌木；mezerein 瑞香脂素

morphology.text: mezereum 整词作为独立词素记忆。联记 mezere(um) + -in → mezerein 瑞香脂素：去掉拉丁语词尾 -um 后形成物质名。

usage_note: 植物学用词；普通名 mezereum 小写，学名写 Daphne mezereum。不要把观赏植物当作可食用植物。

etymology_story.zh: mezereum 经拉丁化植物名称传入英语，与中古拉丁语 mezereon、阿拉伯语 māzaryūn 及更早的波斯语植物名称相连。这个名称既用于植物本身，也用于其旧时入药的树皮。参见[《柯林斯英语词典》](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/mezereum)。
etymology_story.en: Mezereum entered English through Latinized plant naming and is connected with Medieval Latin mezereon, Arabic māzaryūn, and an earlier Persian plant name. It names both the shrub and its bark formerly used medicinally; see [Collins English Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/mezereum).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 mezereum 作为完整的借入植物名学习，不能机械拆成具有现代英语意义的词根和后缀；-um 反映其拉丁化形式。相关名称：mezereon（同株植物的另一名称，也可指其树皮）、Daphne mezereum（植物学名）、mezerein（由该植物名称构成的化合物名，指其中的一种二萜化合物）；这些名称不构成普通英语中能自由扩展的派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, mezereum is normally learned as a whole borrowed plant name rather than divided into productive English morphemes; -um reflects its Latinized form. Related names include mezereon (another name for the shrub and sometimes its bark), Daphne mezereum (the botanical name), and mezerein (a diterpene compound named after the plant); these do not form a freely productive everyday English word family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: mezereon（欧瑞香）是植物义的对应名称；February daphne（二月瑞香）是突出早花特征的俗名；daphne（瑞香属植物）范围更广，不能在要求精确物种名称时直接替换。以上植物名称也不都能替换其干燥树皮义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mezereon is an equivalent name for the shrub; February daphne is a common name highlighting its early flowering; daphne is broader and can refer to other members of the genus. These plant names are not all interchangeable with the dried-bark sense.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 mezereum 作为整株植物记住：早春粉紫花、随后红浆果；旧药材义记它的干树皮。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor the whole name to early pink-purple flowers and later red berries; connect the historical medicinal sense with dried bark.

etymology.text: 英语 mile 加表示量的 -age 形成 mileage；milage 是其另一拼写。把它与车上记录英里数的仪表联记。

etymology_story.zh: milage 是 mileage 的另一拼写；mileage 由 mile（英里）与表示数量、计量或费用的 -age 构成。其意义由英里数扩展到燃油经济性、里程费用及抽象的利用价值，现代通常采用 mileage 这一拼写。拼写关系参见[《韦氏词典》](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/milage)，主要义项参见[《剑桥英语词典》](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/mileage)。
etymology_story.en: Milage is a variant spelling of mileage, formed from mile and -age, a suffix used in words for quantities, measurement, or charges. Its meanings extend from distance to fuel economy, travel reimbursement, and figurative usefulness; mileage is the usual modern spelling, as reflected in [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/milage) and the [Cambridge Dictionary](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/mileage).

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：mile（英里）+ -age → mileage；milage 是省去 e 的拼写变体，词性和读音不因此改变。直接相关形式：mile、miles（英里的复数）、mileage、milage；常用复合形式包括 high-mileage（高里程的）、low-mileage（低里程的）、gas mileage（燃油经济性）、mileage allowance（里程补贴）。所列各义的搭配通常都使用 mileage 拼写。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: mile + -age → mileage; milage is a spelling variant without the e, with no resulting change in pronunciation or part of speech. Directly related forms are mile, miles, mileage, and milage; common compounds include high-mileage, low-mileage, gas mileage, and mileage allowance. Collocations in all the senses listed normally use the spelling mileage.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: distance（距离）不限定计量单位，也不专指车辆累计里程；fuel economy（燃油经济性）只对应燃料利用效率义；usefulness（用处）对应比喻义，强调实用程度，而 milage 常强调从某事物中持续获得的效益。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Distance is independent of measurement unit and need not refer to accumulated vehicle travel; fuel economy corresponds only to the fuel-efficiency sense; usefulness matches the figurative sense but emphasizes practical value, while milage often suggests benefit repeatedly obtained from something.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 mile“英里”串联：跑了多少英里、一份油能跑多少英里、每英里补多少钱，再到一件事还能发挥多少价值。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow mile: miles travelled, miles per unit of fuel, payment per mile, then how much further value something can provide.

etymology.text: 经中古英语借自拉丁语 minium，原来是红色颜料名，后来也用于红铅。用古画里鲜明的红色记住它。

senses.meaning_en: Red lead, or lead tetroxide (Pb₃O₄), a red or orange-red pigment.
senses.english_definition: Minium is a red or orange-red substance containing lead that has been used as a pigment.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 minium 借自拉丁语 minium，该词在古代可指朱砂等红色颜料，后来也用于红铅。英语中的现代专门用法主要指四氧化三铅。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed minium from Latin minium, an ancient name applied to red pigments, including cinnabar, and later also to red lead. Its modern technical use in English chiefly denotes lead tetroxide.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 minium 作为完整借词记忆，不拆成 mini-（微小）与词尾。相关词有 miniaceous（铅丹红色的）及较罕见的 miniate（用铅丹涂饰）；它们共享拉丁语颜料名称这一来源，并非现代英语中自由生成的常用派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, minium is an intact loanword, not mini- meaning 'small' plus an ending. Related words include miniaceous, meaning minium-red, and the rare verb miniate, meaning to decorate with minium; these share the Latin pigment name rather than forming a productive modern English family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: red lead（红铅）是常用同义名称；lead tetroxide（四氧化三铅）突出化学组成；minium 则较常见于颜料、艺术史和矿物学语境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Red lead is the usual synonymous name; lead tetroxide emphasizes chemical composition; minium is especially associated with pigments, art history, and mineralogy.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 minium 固定联想为古画中的橙红色铅丹颜料；不要与表示“微小”的 mini- 混淆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor minium to the orange-red lead pigment in an old painting; keep it separate from mini- meaning 'small'.

senses.meaning_zh: 犹太宗教法中因特定禁忌性关系而具有特殊身份的人；不泛指非婚生子女
senses.meaning_en: A person with a particular Jewish legal status arising from certain prohibited sexual unions.
senses.english_definition: In Jewish religious law, a momzer is a person whose status results from certain prohibited sexual unions, rather than simply from having unmarried parents.
senses.collocation_en: the status of a momzer; declared a momzer

senses.meaning_zh: 混蛋；可恶的家伙，有时也戏指狡猾或难对付的人（源自意第绪语的非正式用法）
senses.meaning_en: An objectionable, devious, or formidable person, sometimes described with grudging affection.
senses.english_definition: If someone calls a person a momzer, they mean that the person is unpleasant or cunning, although the word can sometimes express reluctant admiration.
senses.collocation_en: a little momzer; a clever momzer
senses.collocation_zh: 小混蛋；狡猾的家伙
senses.sentence_en: That little momzer had talked his way into the best seat again.
senses.sentence_zh: 那个小滑头又靠一番花言巧语坐上了最好的位子。

etymology_story.zh: momzer 是 mamzer 的一种英语拼写形式，经意第绪语传自希伯来语 mamzēr，原为犹太宗教法中的身份术语。在意第绪语及受其影响的英语口语中，它又发展出骂人或带戏谑色彩的用法。
etymology_story.en: Momzer is an English spelling variant of mamzer, transmitted through Yiddish from Hebrew mamzēr, originally a Jewish legal status term. In Yiddish and English influenced by it, the word also developed insulting and sometimes teasing uses.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 momzer 是不可再分析的借词，常规复数为 momzers；异体拼写 mamzer 的英语复数为 mamzers，希伯来语复数 mamzerim 也见于专门文本。相关希伯来语名词 mamzerut 表示这种身份，其中 -ut 是希伯来语抽象名词后缀，并非英语后缀。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, momzer is an unanalyzed loanword, with the regular plural momzers. The variant mamzer has the English plural mamzers, while Hebrew mamzerim also occurs in specialist texts. The related Hebrew noun mamzerut names the status; its -ut is a Hebrew abstract-noun suffix, not an English suffix.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: mamzer 是同一词的另一种拼写；bastard 在辱骂义上可相近，但其历史上的非婚生含义不能准确替代犹太宗教法概念；scoundrel 指品行恶劣的人，不含宗教法身份意义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mamzer is an alternative spelling of the same word. Bastard can match the insulting use, but its historical reference to birth outside marriage does not accurately reproduce the Jewish legal category. Scoundrel describes a morally objectionable person without any religious legal meaning.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住两层语境：宗教法中的特定身份，口语中的“混蛋或滑头”；不能简单等同于“非婚生”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember two contexts: a specific religious legal status and the conversational 'rogue or rascal'; birth outside marriage alone is not the defining idea.

etymology_story.zh: morbific 来自拉丁语 morbificus，英语借入过程也与法语 morbifique 有关；其组成包含 morbus（疾病）和表示“造成”的成分。这个词保留了“造成疾病”的原义，如今主要见于较旧或专门的文字。
etymology_story.en: Morbific derives from Latin morbificus, with French morbifique also involved in its transmission into English; its elements refer to disease and causing or making. It retains the meaning 'causing disease' and now occurs chiefly in older or specialist writing.

morphology_enriched.zh: morb-（疾病）＋ -ific（造成……的）→ morbific（致病的）。相关拉丁词根词族包括 morbid（病态的；对死亡等有异常兴趣的）、morbidly（病态地）和 morbidity（患病情况；发病率）；它们不是直接由 morbific 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Morb- meaning 'disease' + -ific meaning 'causing or producing' forms morbific. The related Latin-root family includes morbid, morbidly, and morbidity; these are not direct derivatives of morbific.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pathogenic（致病的）是现代科学语境中的常用对应词；disease-causing（引起疾病的）直白易懂、适用面广；morbid（病态的）通常描述病态状态或兴趣，不等于“致病的”。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pathogenic is the usual modern scientific equivalent; disease-causing is transparent and broadly usable. Morbid usually describes a diseased condition or an unhealthy interest, rather than something that causes disease.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: morb- 是“疾病”，-ific 是“造成”：合起来就是“造成疾病”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Morb- supplies 'disease' and -ific supplies 'causing': together, 'causing disease'.

etymology_story.zh: mothy 由英语 moth 加形容词后缀 -y 构成；moth 经中古英语承自古英语 moþþe。其意义从“有蛾的”自然延伸为“受蛾侵扰或遭其幼虫蛀蚀的”。
etymology_story.en: Mothy was formed in English by adding the adjective suffix -y to moth, which descends through Middle English from Old English moþþe. The sense naturally extends from 'having moths' to 'infested with moths or damaged by their larvae'.

morphology_enriched.zh: moth（蛾）＋ -y（具有……特征的）→ mothy。比较级 mothier，最高级 mothiest，相关名词 mothiness（多蛾或虫蛀的状态）；常用相关复合词有 moth-eaten（虫蛀的）和 mothproof（防蛀的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Moth + -y meaning 'having or characterized by' forms mothy. Its comparative is mothier, its superlative is mothiest, and the related noun is mothiness. Common related compounds include moth-eaten and mothproof.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: moth-infested（有蛾虫侵扰的）强调虫害存在；moth-eaten（虫蛀的）强调已经出现的损坏；threadbare（磨得很薄的）强调磨损，不说明存在蛾虫。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Moth-infested emphasizes the presence of an infestation; moth-eaten emphasizes resulting damage; threadbare describes fabric worn thin through use and does not imply moths.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: moth＋-y：衣柜里“有蛾”，衣物就可能“虫蛀”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Moth + -y: moths in the cupboard, possible moth damage in the clothes.

senses.meaning_zh: 氯化物的旧称；仍用于某些商品或传统名称

senses.sentence_zh: 肥料标签将氯化钾标为 muriate of potash。

etymology_story.zh: muriate 借自法语 muriate，属于与 muriatic acid（盐酸）相关的早期化学命名体系，最终可追溯至拉丁语 muria（盐水）。随着现代氯化物命名确立，它通常被 chloride 取代，但保留在 muriate of potash 等名称中。
etymology_story.en: Muriate was borrowed from French muriate within an older chemical naming system associated with muriatic acid, ultimately from Latin muria, meaning brine. Modern chloride terminology largely replaced it, although it survives in names such as muriate of potash.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史构词可理解为 muri-（来自拉丁语 muria，盐水）＋ -ate（盐类名称词尾）；现代英语通常将 muriate 作为完整的旧化学名称记忆。复数为 muriates；相关词 muriatic（盐酸的）主要见于 muriatic acid（盐酸），并非由 muriate 简单添加 -ic 构成。
morphology_enriched.en: Its historical structure can be understood as muri-, from Latin muria meaning 'brine', plus the salt-name ending -ate; modern English usually treats muriate as an intact older chemical term. The plural is muriates. The related adjective muriatic occurs chiefly in muriatic acid and is not formed simply by adding -ic to muriate.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chloride（氯化物）是现代标准对应词；hydrochloride（盐酸盐）在某些历史药物名称中与 muriate 对应，但不能替代所有氯化物名称；salt（盐）范围更广，包含许多并非氯化物的化合物。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chloride is the standard modern equivalent. Hydrochloride corresponds to muriate in some historical pharmaceutical names but cannot replace it for every chloride. Salt is a broader category that includes many compounds other than chlorides.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 沿着“盐水 muria → 旧称盐酸 muriatic acid → 氯化物 muriate”这条命名线索记忆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the naming chain: brine, muria → muriatic acid → its salts, historically called muriates.

senses.meaning_zh: 近视者（医学或正式用语）
senses.meaning_en: A person with nearsightedness; a medical or formal term.
senses.english_definition: A myope is someone who can see nearby objects clearly but has difficulty seeing distant objects clearly.
senses.collocation_en: a high myope; an uncorrected myope
senses.collocation_zh: 高度近视者；未接受视力矫正的近视者

senses.sentence_zh: 未接受视力矫正的近视者可能难以看清远处的路牌。

etymology_story.zh: myope 经法语追溯至拉丁语 myops，最终源于希腊语 myōps，通常分析为表示“闭合”的 myein 与表示“眼睛”的 ōps 相结合。这个名称与近视者为看清远物而眯眼的动作有关。
etymology_story.en: Myope came through French from Latin myops, ultimately from Greek myōps, traditionally analyzed as combining myein, meaning 'to close,' with ōps, meaning 'eye.' The name refers to the squinting associated with trying to see distant objects.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，myope 通常作为完整的名词词基学习，不宜强拆为具有独立现代意义的 my- 和 -ope。相关词族共享 myop-：myopia（近视，亦指目光短浅）、myopic（近视的；目光短浅的）、myopically（近视地；目光短浅地）；myopes 是复数形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, myope is best learned as a whole noun base rather than divided into independently meaningful my- and -ope. Its related family shares myop-: myopia, meaning nearsightedness or figurative shortsightedness; myopic, meaning nearsighted or lacking foresight; and myopically, the corresponding adverb. Myopes is the plural.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: nearsighted person（近视者）是美式英语中的日常表达；short-sighted person（近视者）是英式英语中的常见表达。myope 更简洁，但主要用于医学或正式语境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nearsighted person is the everyday American expression, while short-sighted person is usual in British English. Myope is more compact but belongs mainly to medical or formal contexts.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “闭眼”缩成“眯眼”：眯着眼看远处的人，就是 myope。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect 'closing the eye' with squinting: a myope squints to make distant objects clearer.

senses.english_definition: Napery consists of the cloth items used on a dining table, especially tablecloths and napkins, and can also refer more broadly to household linen.

etymology_story.zh: napery 源自中古英语 naperie，借自盎格鲁法语或古法语中表示家用织物的词。其基础词 nape 意为“桌布”，最终与拉丁语 mappa（布；餐巾）相联系，后来尤其用于餐桌织物。
etymology_story.en: Napery comes from Middle English naperie, borrowed from Anglo-French or Old French for household linen. Its base, nape, meant 'tablecloth' and ultimately connects with Latin mappa, meaning a cloth or napkin; English usage became especially associated with table linen.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史上可分析为 nape（桌布，旧词）+ -ery（表示一类物品的集合）；现代英语中通常把 napery 作为整体词学习。相关词 napkin（餐巾）也来自表示“桌布”的同一法语词基，并含指小后缀 -kin；napery 本身没有常用的现代派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Historically, the word can be analyzed as nape, an obsolete word for a tablecloth, plus collective -ery. Modern English normally treats napery as a whole word. The related word napkin comes from the same French base with the diminutive suffix -kin; napery itself has no productive everyday derivative family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: table linen（餐桌织物）是最直接、最常用的对应表达；household linen（家用织物）范围更广，包括床上用品和毛巾。linen（亚麻布；家用织物）既可指材料，也可统称织物用品，而 napery 尤其让人想到桌布和餐巾。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Table linen is the closest and most usual equivalent. Household linen is broader and includes bedding and towels. Linen can name either a fabric or household textile items, whereas napery particularly suggests tablecloths and napkins.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 napery 和 napkin 联记：一条餐巾，扩展成整桌的布艺用品。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link napery with napkin: picture one napkin expanding into the whole table's collection of cloth items.

senses.meaning_zh: 甘松；尤指根和根茎可用于制香的喜马拉雅植物
senses.meaning_en: Spikenard, especially the Himalayan plant whose roots and rhizomes are used in perfumery.
senses.english_definition: Nard is a plant whose aromatic underground parts are used to make perfume.

senses.meaning_zh: 甘松香膏；甘松香油
senses.meaning_en: An aromatic ointment, perfume, or oil made from spikenard.
senses.english_definition: Nard is also a fragrant preparation made from the plant, especially an expensive perfume or ointment mentioned in ancient texts.
senses.collocation_zh: 纯甘松香膏；甘松香油
senses.sentence_en: The ancient account describes a small jar filled with expensive nard.
senses.sentence_zh: 这段古代记载描述了一个装满昂贵甘松香膏的小罐。

etymology_story.zh: nard 可追溯至古英语中的借词，源于拉丁语 nardus，后者来自希腊语 nardos；更早的来源并不完全确定。这个名称既指芳香植物，也指用它制成的香料和香膏，因此常见于古代贸易、宗教和香料文献。
etymology_story.en: Nard is attested as an Old English borrowing from Latin nardus, which came from Greek nardos; its more distant origin is uncertain. The name was used both for the aromatic plant and for preparations made from it, explaining its association with ancient trade, religious texts, and perfumery.

morphology_enriched.zh: nard 是不可再作实用拆分的词基。相关词有 nardine（甘松的；甘松制的，罕用），可分析为 nard + -ine，以及 spikenard（甘松），可分析为 spike + nard；表示香油或香膏时，nard 通常为不可数名词。
morphology_enriched.en: Nard is an unanalyzable base in practical modern usage. Related forms include the rare adjective nardine, meaning of or made from nard, formed with -ine, and the compound spikenard, formed from spike + nard. Nard is normally uncountable when it denotes perfume, oil, or ointment.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: spikenard（甘松）是植物义的主要对应词，也可指其香料；nard oil（甘松香油）明确限定为油状制品；ointment（软膏；香膏）只说明制品形态，并不表示其中一定含甘松。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Spikenard is the main equivalent for the plant and can also name its perfume. Nard oil specifically denotes the oily preparation. Ointment describes a preparation's form and does not by itself imply that it contains nard.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一株芳香甘松，一罐珍贵香膏：植物名也指它制成的香料。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture an aromatic plant beside a precious perfume jar: nard names both the source and its fragrant product.

etymology.text: 经后古典拉丁语 nosologia，使用古希腊语 nosos（疾病）和 -logia（论述、学问）组成。把各种疾病放进有序分类表来记。

usage_note: 医学和医学史用词，关注疾病如何定义、归类和命名；不是对个别病人的护理。

senses.meaning_zh: 疾病分类学
senses.meaning_en: The branch of medicine concerned with classifying diseases.
senses.english_definition: Nosology is the study of how diseases are named, defined, and organized into groups.
senses.collocation_zh: 精神疾病分类学；医学疾病分类学

senses.sentence_zh: 遗传学的进展改变了研究人员研究疾病分类的方式。

senses.meaning_zh: 疾病分类体系
senses.meaning_en: A system for classifying diseases.
senses.english_definition: A nosology is a particular system that places diseases into categories according to their defining features.
senses.collocation_en: a diagnostic nosology; an evolving nosology
senses.collocation_zh: 诊断分类体系；不断发展的疾病分类体系
senses.sentence_en: The proposed nosology groups these disorders according to their underlying causes.
senses.sentence_zh: 拟议的疾病分类体系按照这些疾病的根本病因对其进行归类。

etymology_story.zh: nosology 属于以希腊语词素构成的医学学术词，并与新拉丁语 nosologia 相联系：nosos 意为“疾病”，-logia 表示“研究或论述”。它的核心含义从对疾病的系统研究，具体落实为疾病的分类及其分类体系。
etymology_story.en: Nosology is a learned medical formation associated with New Latin nosologia and built from Greek nosos, meaning 'disease,' and -logia, meaning study or discourse. Its meaning centers on the systematic classification of diseases and extends to a particular classification system.

morphology_enriched.zh: noso-（疾病）+ -logy（研究学科）→ nosology。词族包括 nosologist（疾病分类学家）、nosological 和 nosologic（疾病分类学的）、nosologically（从疾病分类学角度）；表示多个分类体系时，复数为 nosologies。
morphology_enriched.en: Noso-, meaning disease, + -logy, meaning a field of study, forms nosology. Its family includes nosologist, a specialist in disease classification; nosological and nosologic, the corresponding adjectives; and nosologically, the adverb. Nosologies is the plural when referring to multiple classification systems.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: disease classification（疾病分类）是最直接的通俗表达；disease taxonomy（疾病分类体系）强调分类的结构与层级；diagnostic classification（诊断分类）强调诊断实践使用的类别和标准。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Disease classification is the plain-language equivalent. Disease taxonomy emphasizes the structure and hierarchy of the categories. Diagnostic classification emphasizes the categories and criteria used in making diagnoses.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: noso- 是疾病，-logy 是学问：给疾病分门别类的学问。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Noso- means disease and -logy means study: imagine arranging diseases into clearly labeled groups.

etymology.text: 由英语 nugget 加 -y 形成，先以小而紧实的块状物作比喻，再用来形容人的结实体格。联想小块金属的厚实感。

etymology_story.zh: nuggety 由英语 nugget（小块，尤指天然金块）加形容词后缀 -y 构成。它既可直接描述含有小块金的材料，也把金块小而紧实的形象用于人的体格，后者尤其见于澳大利亚和新西兰英语。
etymology_story.en: Nuggety was formed from English nugget, a small lump especially of native gold, with the adjective suffix -y. It can literally describe material containing nuggets, while the image of a compact, solid lump also underlies its use for a person's physique, especially in Australian and New Zealand English.

morphology_enriched.zh: nugget（小块；天然金块）+ -y（具有……特征的；含有……的）→ nuggety。词族核心包括 nugget、其复数 nuggets，以及形容词 nuggety；nugget 的“有价值的小段信息”义也保留了“小块珍贵之物”的意象。
morphology_enriched.en: Nugget, meaning a small lump or natural gold lump, + -y, meaning characterized by or containing, forms nuggety. The core family consists of nugget, its plural nuggets, and the adjective nuggety. The noun's figurative sense of a valuable piece of information preserves the image of a small, precious unit.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: stocky（矮壮的）是体格义最接近的近义词；sturdy（结实的）强调强健耐用，不一定个子矮；gold-bearing（含金的）与采矿义相关，但不说明金是否呈天然块状。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Stocky is the closest synonym for the physique sense. Sturdy emphasizes strength without necessarily implying shortness. Gold-bearing relates to the mining sense but does not specify whether the gold occurs in nuggets.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: nugget 是紧实的小金块：人像小金块一样敦实，矿石里也可以藏着小金块。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with a compact gold nugget: a person can look solid like one, and ore can contain actual ones.

etymology_story.zh: oleum 源自拉丁语 oleum（油），更早来自希腊语 elaion（橄榄油）；其化学用法与德语 Oleum 的使用有关。这一名称沿用了早期把某些外观油状的液体称为“油”的命名习惯，并不表示发烟硫酸属于油脂。
etymology_story.en: Oleum comes from Latin oleum, meaning oil, ultimately from Greek elaion, meaning olive oil; its chemical use is associated with German Oleum. The name reflects the older practice of calling some oily-looking liquids oils, rather than classifying the substance as a fat or ordinary oil.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 oleum 是整体借入的不可数名词，不宜把 -um 当作可自由添加的英语后缀。同源词族以 ole-、oleo- 表示“油”：oleic（油酸的）、oleate（油酸盐或酯）、olein（油精；油酸甘油酯）、oleaginous（油质的；油滑的）、oleochemical（油脂化学品；油脂化学的）；这些词并非都由现代化学名词 oleum 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, oleum is a borrowed mass noun, and -um is not a freely productive English suffix here. Its historical family uses ole- or oleo- for oil: oleic, relating to oleic acid; oleate, a salt or ester of that acid; olein, an oily glyceride; oleaginous, oily or excessively flattering; and oleochemical, a chemical derived from oils or relating to such chemicals. These are not all direct derivatives of the modern chemical noun oleum.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fuming sulfuric acid（发烟硫酸）是直接同义名称；sulfuric acid（硫酸）范围更广，单独使用时不表示含有额外溶解的三氧化硫；disulfuric acid（焦硫酸，H₂S₂O₇）是相关化合物，不能与各种组成的 oleum 完全等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fuming sulfuric acid is a direct synonym. Sulfuric acid is the broader substance name and does not by itself specify additional dissolved sulfur trioxide. Disulfuric acid, H₂S₂O₇, is a related compound, not an exact synonym for oleum of every composition.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ole- 联想“油”：名字取自油状外观，实际记作“发烟硫酸”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect ole- with oil: the name recalls an oily appearance, while the substance is fuming sulfuric acid.

senses.meaning_en: Deserving disgrace or strong condemnation; shameful.
senses.english_definition: An opprobrious act is one that people consider shameful and deserving of strong criticism.

senses.sentence_en: He regarded the betrayal as an opprobrious act.
senses.sentence_zh: 他认为这次背叛是可耻之举。

etymology_story.zh: opprobrious 可追溯至晚期拉丁语 opprobriosus，来自 opprobrium（耻辱；责骂）；后者包含 ob-（向着；针对）和 probrum（耻辱；责难）。它保留了两个相连的方向：向别人施加羞辱，以及某种行为本身招致羞辱。
etymology_story.en: Opprobrious traces back to Late Latin opprobriosus, from opprobrium, meaning disgrace or reproach; that noun combines ob-, toward or against, with probrum, disgrace or reproach. Its meanings cover both expressing shameful condemnation of someone and deserving condemnation oneself.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族可分析为 opprobri-（与 opprobrium“耻辱；谴责”对应的词干）+ -ous（具有……性质的）→ opprobrious。主要成员：opprobrium（耻辱；强烈谴责）、opprobriously（辱骂地；可耻地）、opprobriousness（侮辱性；可耻性）；历史构词中 ob- 在 p 前同化为 op-。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern family can be analyzed as opprobri-, the stem associated with opprobrium, plus -ous, having the quality of, giving opprobrious. Principal family members are opprobrium, disgrace or strong condemnation; opprobriously, in an abusive or shameful manner; and opprobriousness, the quality of being abusive or shameful. Historically, ob- assimilated to op- before p.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: abusive（辱骂的）强调言语攻击；scurrilous（恶言诽谤的）强调粗鄙、恶毒且常不实的指责；disgraceful（可耻的）对应“应受谴责”义。opprobrious 语体更正式，突出鄙视、羞辱或道德谴责。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Abusive emphasizes verbal aggression. Scurrilous suggests coarse, malicious, often false attacks. Disgraceful matches the sense of deserving condemnation. Opprobrious is more formal and particularly conveys contempt, disgrace, or moral reproach.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 opprobrium“耻辱”：言语把耻辱加给别人，行为把耻辱招到自己身上。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor the word in opprobrium, disgrace: words cast disgrace on others, while conduct can bring disgrace on oneself.

senses.meaning_zh: 帕翁音步；由一个长音节和三个短音节组成的古典音步
senses.meaning_en: A classical metrical foot containing one long syllable and three short syllables.
senses.english_definition: A paeon is a unit of rhythm in classical poetry that consists of four syllables, one long and three short.
senses.collocation_en: a first paeon; a fourth paeon
senses.collocation_zh: 第一帕翁音步（长短短短）；第四帕翁音步（短短短长）

senses.sentence_zh: 在第四帕翁音步中，三个短音节之后接一个长音节。

etymology_story.zh: paeon 经拉丁语 paeon 来自希腊语 paiōn，是古典诗律中的音步名称。它在历史上与 paean 所指的颂神歌传统相关，但现代英语中 paeon 指音步，paean 通常指赞歌或热烈赞颂。
etymology_story.en: Paeon comes through Latin paeon from Greek paiōn, the name of a classical metrical foot. It is historically associated with the hymn tradition reflected in paean, but modern English distinguishes paeon, the metrical foot, from paean, a song or expression of praise.

morphology_enriched.zh: paeon 在现代英语中作为整体词根使用：paeon + -ic → paeonic（帕翁音步的）；规则复数为 paeons。按长音节所在位置分为第一、第二、第三和第四帕翁音步；paean（赞歌）是历史相关词，不是 paeon 的复数或派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Paeon functions as an unanalyzed base in modern English: paeon + -ic gives paeonic, relating to this metrical foot; its regular plural is paeons. The first, second, third, and fourth paeons are distinguished by the position of the long syllable. Paean, a hymn of praise, is historically related but is neither a plural nor a derivative of paeon.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: paeonic foot（帕翁音步）是同义表达；cretic（克里特音步）为“长—短—长”，只有三个音节；choriamb（扬抑抑扬格音步）为“长—短—短—长”，虽也有四个音节，却包含两个长音节。后两者是用于辨析的相关术语，并非同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Paeonic foot is an equivalent expression. A cretic has three syllables arranged long–short–long. A choriamb has four arranged long–short–short–long, including two long syllables. The latter two are contrasting metrical terms, not synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 四个位置，一长三短；长音落在哪一位，就是第几帕翁音步。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Four positions, one long and three short: the long syllable's position gives the paeon's number.

pronunciation.note: 由词典中的单数 pallium 读音及拉丁式复数 -ia 转写，重音保留在第一音节。

etymology_story.zh: pallia 是拉丁语 pallium（披袍；覆盖物）的中性复数形式，英语借入单数时也保留了这一复数。其“覆盖”的形象后来扩展到教会肩带、软体动物外套膜和脑部覆盖性结构等名称。
etymology_story.en: Pallia is the Latin neuter plural of pallium, meaning a cloak or covering, retained alongside the borrowed English singular. The image of a covering extended to an ecclesiastical vestment, the mantle of a mollusk, and structures of the forebrain.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是屈折变化，不是新词派生：pallium 的词干 palli- + 拉丁语中性复数词尾 -a → pallia；英语中也见规则复数 palliums。同族包括 pallial（外套膜的；脑披的）、palliate（减轻；掩饰）、palliation（缓解；掩饰）、palliative（缓解的；缓解剂）、palliatively（以缓解方式）；后几词经拉丁语“用披袍覆盖”的动词发展而来，并非由复数 pallia 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: This is inflection rather than derivation: the stem palli- of pallium takes the Latin neuter plural ending -a to form pallia; the regular English plural palliums also occurs. Related words include pallial, relating to a mantle or the brain's pallium; palliate, to relieve or disguise; palliation, relief or concealment; palliative, relieving or a relieving treatment; and palliatively, in a relieving manner. The latter group developed through a Latin verb meaning to cover with a cloak, rather than directly from the plural pallia.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cloaks（披风）是服装义的宽泛近义词；mantles（披袍；外套膜）可对应服装义和软体动物解剖义；cortices（皮质）在哺乳动物脑解剖语境中与脑披有关，但不能概括所有脊椎动物的 pallia。教会义通常直接使用 pallia，不能任意替换为普通披风。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cloaks is a broad equivalent for the clothing sense. Mantles can match both the garment and molluscan anatomical senses. Cortices is related in mammalian brain anatomy but does not cover all vertebrate pallia. The ecclesiastical sense normally retains the specific term pallia rather than substituting an ordinary clothing word.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一件 pallium，多件 pallia；从“披在外面的覆盖层”串起披袍、肩带、外套膜和脑披。
mnemonic_anchor.en: One pallium, several pallia: a covering worn or spread over something connects the cloak, vestment, mantle, and brain senses.

senses.collocation_zh: 自行车挂包；柳条驮篮
senses.sentence_en: The mule carried a panier on each side.
senses.sentence_zh: 这头骡子的两侧各驮着一个篮子。

senses.meaning_zh: 裙撑；使裙子向两侧扩展的支架（通常用复数）
senses.meaning_en: A framework worn under a skirt to extend it sideways, usually referred to in the plural.
senses.english_definition: Paniers are supports worn under a skirt to make it project out at the sides, especially in eighteenth-century dress.
senses.collocation_zh: 十八世纪裙撑；宽大的裙撑
senses.sentence_en: The gown's paniers made it difficult to pass through the narrow doorway.
senses.sentence_zh: 这件礼服的裙撑让穿着者很难通过狭窄的门口。

etymology_story.zh: panier 与更常见的 pannier 同源，经中古英语和法语 panier（篮子）追溯至拉丁语 panarium（面包篮），后者来自 panis（面包）。词义从装面包的篮子扩展到驮载用的侧篮，又因外形相似而用于向两侧撑开的裙撑。
etymology_story.en: Panier and the more usual pannier trace through Middle English and French panier, basket, to Latin panarium, bread basket, from panis, bread. The meaning broadened from a bread basket to side-mounted carrying baskets and, by resemblance, supports that spread a skirt sideways.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 panier 是整体借词，复数为 paniers；较常见拼写为 pannier，复数 panniers。相关形式有 panniered（装有驮篮的；带裙撑的）和 pannier + -ful → pannierful（一驮篮的量），复数 pannierfuls；词源上的 pan- 与“面包”有关，不是表示“全部”的希腊语前缀 pan-。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, panier is a borrowed base with the plural paniers; the more usual spelling is pannier, plural panniers. Related forms include panniered, equipped with panniers or skirt supports, and pannier + -ful, giving pannierful, the amount one pannier holds, plural pannierfuls. The historical pan- element relates to bread and is unrelated to the Greek prefix pan-, meaning all.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: basket（篮子）只说明容器类型，不说明侧挂或成对使用；saddlebag（鞍囊）通常指挂在鞍具或车辆两侧的软质袋；side hoop（侧裙撑）对应历史服装义，强调把裙子向侧面撑开的支架。panier 的现代英语常用拼写是 pannier。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Basket names the container without specifying side mounting or use in pairs. Saddlebag usually suggests a flexible bag carried beside a saddle or vehicle. Side hoop matches the historical clothing sense and emphasizes the framework extending a skirt sideways. Pannier is the usual modern English spelling.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“面包篮”记起：挂在两侧是驮篮，撑在裙子两侧是裙撑。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with a bread basket: carried at the sides, it is a pannier; shaping a skirt at the sides, it becomes a skirt support.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自葡萄牙语 pataca，这个名称早先用于银币，后来成为澳门货币单位的名称。英语保留了它作为货币名称的名词用法。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Portuguese pataca, a name formerly used for silver coins that later became the name of Macao's monetary unit. English retained its use as a currency noun.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，pataca 是不可进一步拆分的借入词，不含能产的英语前缀或后缀。复数为 patacas；无常用派生词。pataca-denominated（以澳门元计价的）由 pataca 与 denominated 构成复合形容词，不属于后缀派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, pataca is an unanalyzed loanword with no productive English prefix or suffix. Its plural is patacas, and it has no common derivatives. Pataca-denominated is a compound adjective meaning expressed in patacas, rather than a suffix-derived form.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Macanese pataca（澳门元）和 Macao pataca（澳门元）是明确地域的同指名称；currency（货币）是上位词，不能专指澳门元。MOP 是货币代码，不是另一个货币名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Macanese pataca and Macao pataca explicitly identify the same currency; currency is a broader term that does not specifically mean the pataca. MOP is its currency code, rather than a separate currency name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把澳门价签上的 MOP 与 pataca 绑定：看到 MOP，就想到澳门元。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link pataca with MOP on a Macao price tag: MOP points to the pataca.

etymology.text: 借自日语 箪笥，读作 tansu，指传统的储物柜。把带抽屉、可搬动的日本木柜与这个声音联记。

senses.meaning_en: a traditional Japanese storage chest or cabinet, especially one with drawers
senses.english_definition: A tansu is a traditional Japanese chest or cabinet used for storing clothes and other belongings.
senses.collocation_zh: 古董日式储物柜；日式抽屉柜
senses.sentence_en: She keeps her folded clothes in an antique tansu.
senses.sentence_zh: 她把叠好的衣服放在一只古董日式抽屉柜里。

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自日语 tansu（箪笥），意为柜橱或抽屉柜。进入英语后，它主要用于指日本传统储物家具，常见木制柜体、抽屉和金属配件。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Japanese tansu, written 箪笥, meaning a cabinet or chest of drawers. In English, it chiefly denotes traditional Japanese storage furniture, often featuring wooden construction, drawers, and metal fittings.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，tansu 是整体借入的名词，不能拆成英语词根和词缀；复数通常仍为 tansu，也可见 tansus。无常用派生词；tansu-style（日式储物柜风格的）是复合修饰语。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, tansu is a borrowed noun that cannot be divided into English roots and affixes. The plural is usually tansu, though tansus also occurs. It has no common derivatives; tansu-style is a compound modifier.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chest（储物箱、柜）强调容纳物品的家具；chest of drawers（抽屉柜）明确指有多层抽屉的家具；cabinet（柜橱）范围更广，可带柜门。三者均不自带 tansu 的日本传统家具含义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chest emphasizes a piece of storage furniture; chest of drawers specifically identifies furniture with several drawers; cabinet is broader and may have doors. None inherently carries tansu's association with traditional Japanese furniture.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 tansu 与日语“箪笥”及带金属拉手的木抽屉柜绑定，整词记忆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor tansu to Japanese 箪笥 and a wooden drawer chest with metal handles; remember it as a whole word.

morphology.text: tinea 整词作为独立词素记忆；tinea + pedis（拉丁语：足的） → tinea pedis 足癣，是医学复合病名。

etymology.text: 来自拉丁语 tinea，原意是蛾或书虫，后来进入医学用语指皮肤病。可用像被虫蚀过的皮肤外观联想，但实际是感染名称。

senses.meaning_zh: 癣；皮肤、毛发或指甲的皮肤癣菌感染
senses.meaning_en: a dermatophyte fungal infection of the skin, hair, or nails
senses.english_definition: Tinea is an infection caused by fungi that affect your skin, hair, or nails.
senses.collocation_zh: 足癣；体癣
senses.sentence_en: The doctor diagnosed the rash as tinea corporis.
senses.sentence_zh: 医生诊断这片皮疹为体癣。

etymology_story.zh: 来自拉丁语 tinea，原指蛾或蛀虫，后来被用于某些皮肤病的名称。现代医学中的 tinea 指真菌感染，词源中的虫类意象并不表示病因是虫。
etymology_story.en: Tinea comes from Latin tinea, meaning a moth or gnawing worm, and was later applied to certain skin diseases. In modern medicine, it denotes fungal infection; the insect imagery in its history does not identify its cause.

morphology_enriched.zh: tinea 是整体借入的医学名词，不宜按英语词缀拆分；拉丁式复数为 tineae，表示病类时通常作不可数名词。少用形容词 tineal 意为“癣的”。相关医学名称包括 tinea pedis（足癣）、tinea corporis（体癣）和 tinea capitis（头癣）；其中 pedis、corporis、capitis 分别是拉丁语“足、身体、头”的属格形式，并非英语后缀。
morphology_enriched.en: Tinea is a borrowed medical noun, rather than a form built from English affixes. Its Latin plural is tineae, though it is usually uncountable when naming the condition. The uncommon adjective tineal means relating to tinea. Related medical terms include tinea pedis, tinea corporis, and tinea capitis: pedis, corporis, and capitis are Latin genitives meaning of the foot, body, and head, rather than English suffixes.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ringworm（癣）是常用名称，并不表示存在寄生虫；dermatophytosis（皮肤癣菌病）更明确地指出致病真菌类别；fungal infection（真菌感染）范围更广，还包括多种非癣类感染。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ringworm is the everyday name and does not imply a parasitic worm; dermatophytosis more explicitly identifies the fungal group responsible; fungal infection is broader and includes many infections other than tinea.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用“虫蚀般的表面变化”连接古义与皮肤病名称，同时牢记：癣的病因是真菌。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect the old image of a gnawed surface with the skin-disease name, while remembering that tinea is caused by fungi.

senses.meaning_zh: 帽子
senses.meaning_en: a hat, in British rhyming slang
senses.english_definition: A titfer is a hat, especially when referred to in Cockney rhyming slang.
senses.collocation_en: wear a titfer; tip your titfer
senses.collocation_zh: 戴帽子；轻抬帽檐致意
senses.sentence_en: He tipped his titfer and gave her a cheerful smile.
senses.sentence_zh: 他轻抬帽檐向她致意，并愉快地笑了笑。

etymology_story.zh: 来自伦敦考克尼押韵俚语 tit for tat，其中 tat 与 hat 押韵，因此整个短语可代指帽子。省略押韵部分 tat 后，剩下的 tit for 被连写为 titfer。
etymology_story.en: Titfer comes from Cockney rhyming slang tit for tat, in which tat rhymes with hat, allowing the phrase to stand for a hat. The rhyming element tat was dropped, and the remaining tit for became titfer.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词路径是 hat → 押韵替代表达 tit for tat → 截短 tit for → 连写 titfer；这是押韵俚语的截短与词汇化，并非普通词根加词缀。现代英语中作整体名词，复数为 titfers，无常用派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: The formation is hat → the rhyming substitute tit for tat → the shortened tit for → the fused spelling titfer. This involves rhyming-slang clipping and lexicalization, rather than ordinary root-and-affix formation. It functions as a whole noun, has the plural titfers, and has no common derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hat（帽子）是中性通用词；headgear（头部穿戴物）范围更广，包括头盔等，通常为不可数名词；cap（便帽、鸭舌帽）指特定类型的帽子。titfer 的区别主要在于其地域性俚语色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hat is the neutral general term; headgear is broader, includes items such as helmets, and is normally uncountable; cap denotes particular kinds of hat. Titfer differs chiefly in its regional slang register.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hat 与 tat 押韵：tit for tat 去掉 tat，留下 titfer＝帽子。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hat rhymes with tat: remove tat from tit for tat, leaving titfer, meaning hat.

senses.meaning_zh: 小圆厚牛里脊肉片；用这种肉片制作的菜
senses.meaning_en: a small, thick, round steak cut from beef tenderloin, or a dish made with it
senses.english_definition: A tournedos is a small, thick, round piece of beef cut from the tenderloin, which can be cooked and served as an individual steak.
senses.collocation_zh: 牛里脊小圆厚肉片；罗西尼式牛里脊肉片

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自法语 tournedos，该词由 tourne（与 tourner“转动”有关）和 dos（背）组成，字面涉及“转背”。这一名称为何用于牛肉切片存在不同解释，不宜把某个转身故事或烹调动作当作确定词源。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed French tournedos, formed from tourne, related to tourner meaning to turn, and dos meaning back. Explanations of how this expression became the name of a beef cut vary, so a particular turning story or cooking action should not be treated as established history.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，tournedos 是整体借入的名词，不含能产的英语词缀；历史上的 tourne + dos 属于法语内部构词。单复数同形，均为 tournedos，词尾 s 不是英语复数标记；无常用派生词。tournedos Rossini 是菜名，不是派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, tournedos is an unanalyzed borrowed noun without productive English affixes; its historical tourne + dos structure belongs to French. Both singular and plural are tournedos, so the final s is not an English plural marker. It has no common derivatives. Tournedos Rossini is a dish name, rather than a derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fillet steak（牛里脊牛排）范围较广，不必具有小圆厚的形状；filet mignon（菲力牛排）与 tournedos 含义重叠，但具体切割和命名习惯因地区而异；beef medallion（圆形小牛肉片）强调外形，未必取自里脊。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fillet steak is broader and need not have a small, thick, round shape; filet mignon overlaps with tournedos, though cutting and naming conventions vary by region; beef medallion emphasizes shape and does not necessarily specify tenderloin.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整词绑定“盘中的小圆厚牛里脊”；法语“转＋背”只作拼写线索，不当作烹调说明。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor the whole word to a small, thick, round tenderloin steak on a plate; use French turn + back only as a spelling cue.

etymology.text: 由英语 God’s wounds 的委婉缩合而来，原来提到基督受难的伤口，后来成为表示惊讶、愤怒的旧式感叹。可联想戏剧人物大吃一惊。

usage_note: 现在主要带旧式或戏剧化色彩，可读 /zaʊndz/ 或 /zuːndz/；感叹词单独使用时常接叹号。

senses.meaning_zh: （旧式，现多用于戏谑）天哪；岂有此理；哎呀
senses.meaning_en: An old-fashioned exclamation of surprise, anger, or indignation, now often used humorously.
senses.english_definition: People say 'zounds' in old-fashioned or humorous speech when they are surprised, angry, or shocked.
senses.collocation_zh: 天哪，先生！；哎呀，老兄！
senses.sentence_en: “Zounds!” cried the actor. “Who has stolen my crown?”
senses.sentence_zh: “岂有此理！”演员喊道，“谁偷走了我的王冠？”

etymology_story.zh: 源自 God's wounds（上帝的伤口）的委婉缩合，原指基督受难时的伤口，用来替代直接的宗教誓语。后来成为表达惊讶或愤怒的感叹词，如今主要带有古风、戏剧或戏谑色彩。
etymology_story.en: Zounds developed as a euphemistic contraction of God's wounds, referring to Christ's wounds during the Crucifixion and softening a religious oath. It became an exclamation of surprise or anger and now chiefly suggests historical drama or humorous imitation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可再作常规词缀分析的固定感叹词；God's wounds → zounds 展示的是历史上的缩合，而不是现代构词公式。无常用屈折形式或派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, zounds is a fixed interjection without a productive root-and-affix analysis; God's wounds → zounds describes historical contraction rather than modern word formation. It has no common inflected forms or derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gadzooks（天哪）同样古旧且常带戏谑意味；good heavens（天哪）较温和，主要表示惊讶；damn（该死）更直接地表达愤怒，语气也更粗。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gadzooks is similarly archaic and often humorous; good heavens is milder and chiefly expresses surprise; damn conveys anger more directly and is more offensive.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: God's wounds 缩成 zounds：古装人物一惊，高喊“天哪！”
mnemonic_anchor.en: God's wounds contracts into zounds: picture a startled character in a historical play crying out.

morphology.text: zym-（发酵） + -urgy（工艺） → zymurgy 发酵工艺学。

etymology.text: 英语仿照 metallurgy 等学科名，用源自希腊语的 zym-（发酵）和 -urgy（工艺）组成。把发酵罐与工艺研究联记。

usage_note: 较专门的应用化学名称，常用于啤酒、葡萄酒等发酵过程；不等于单纯品酒。

senses.meaning_zh: 发酵工艺学，尤指酿酒中的发酵技术
senses.meaning_en: The science and practical application of fermentation, especially in brewing and winemaking.
senses.english_definition: Zymurgy is the scientific study and practical use of fermentation, especially to make beer and wine.
senses.collocation_en: the study of zymurgy; the art of zymurgy
senses.collocation_zh: 发酵工艺学研究；发酵酿造技艺
senses.sentence_en: Her interest in home brewing led her to study zymurgy.
senses.sentence_zh: 她对家庭酿酒的兴趣促使她学习发酵工艺学。

etymology_story.zh: 由源自希腊语 zymē（酵、发酵剂）的 zym- 和表示工艺的 -urgy 构成，构词模式与 metallurgy（冶金学）相似。它用来指发酵的科学与实际应用，尤其是酿酒技术。
etymology_story.en: Zymurgy combines zym-, from Greek zymē meaning leaven or ferment, with -urgy, denoting a form of work or technical practice, on a pattern comparable to metallurgy. It names the science and application of fermentation, especially in making alcoholic drinks.

morphology_enriched.zh: 学术构词成分 zym-（发酵）+ -urgy（工艺、技术）→ zymurgy。派生词有 zymurgist（发酵工艺专家）、zymurgic 和 zymurgical（发酵工艺的）；相关同源词有 zymology（发酵学）、zymologist（发酵学家），它们不是直接由 zymurgy 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Learned combining elements zym- 'fermentation' + -urgy 'technical work or practice' form zymurgy. Derivatives include zymurgist, a fermentation specialist, and the adjectives zymurgic and zymurgical; related formations include zymology and zymologist, which are not direct derivatives of zymurgy.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: zymology（发酵学）强调发酵的科学研究；brewing（酿造，尤指啤酒酿造）强调具体生产过程；fermentation technology（发酵技术）范围更广，还可涉及食品、药品等工业应用。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Zymology emphasizes the scientific study of fermentation; brewing emphasizes the production process, particularly for beer; fermentation technology is broader and can include industrial applications in food and pharmaceuticals.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: zym- 是发酵，-urgy 是工艺：研究怎样让发酵罐酿出酒。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Zym- means fermentation and -urgy means technical practice: think of the science behind a brewing vat.

morphology.text: alcoholic（截短为 alk-） + -y → alky 酒瘾者；另一拼写 alkie 使用 -ie。

etymology.text: 英语 alcoholic 被截短，再加口语称人后缀 -ie 或 -y，形成 alkie、alky。记住这是人物口语称呼，不是饮料名称。

usage_note: 非正式称呼，可能带贬意。讨论健康或与当事人交谈时，a person with alcohol dependence 更尊重人。

senses.meaning_zh: （俚语，常含贬义或冒犯意味）酒瘾者；酒鬼
senses.meaning_en: An informal, often insulting term for a person addicted to alcohol.
senses.english_definition: If someone calls a person an alky, they mean that the person is addicted to alcohol, usually in an insulting or dismissive way.
senses.collocation_en: call someone an alky; an old alky
senses.collocation_zh: 称某人为酒鬼；老酒鬼
senses.sentence_en: He disliked being called an alky while he was trying to stop drinking.
senses.sentence_zh: 他正在努力戒酒，不喜欢别人叫他酒鬼。

etymology_story.zh: 是 alcoholic（酒瘾者）的俚语缩略形式，通过截短、拼写调整以及添加口语后缀 -y 形成，也拼作 alkie。这个称呼常带轻蔑意味，并非中性的医学用语。
etymology_story.en: Alky is a slang shortening of alcoholic, formed through clipping, spelling adjustment, and the familiar ending -y; alkie is an alternative spelling. The label often carries contempt and is not a neutral medical term.

morphology_enriched.zh: alcoholic（酒瘾者）→ 截短并调整拼写的 alk- + 口语后缀 -y → alky；异体拼写为 alkie，复数为 alkies。相关词族包括 alcohol（酒精；酒）、alcoholic（酒精的；酒瘾者）、alcoholism（酒精依赖）和 nonalcoholic（不含酒精的），这些词并非都由 alky 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Alcoholic is clipped and respelled as alk-, then combined with the familiar ending -y to form alky; the alternative spelling is alkie, and the plural is alkies. Related family members include alcohol, alcoholic, alcoholism, and nonalcoholic, although these are not all derivatives of alky.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: alcoholic（酒瘾者）比 alky 更标准，但用于给人贴标签时仍可能带污名；drunkard（酒鬼）强调惯常醉酒，常带谴责；heavy drinker（大量饮酒者）只说明饮酒量大，不一定表示已经形成依赖。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Alcoholic is more standard than alky but can still stigmatize when used as a label; drunkard emphasizes habitual drunkenness and often conveys disapproval; heavy drinker describes high consumption without necessarily implying dependence.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: alcoholic 缩成 alky：词形变短，口气也变得随便、可能冒犯。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Alcoholic shrinks to alky: the shorter form signals casual, potentially insulting speech.

meaning: 戏剧情节中的真相发现；人物顿悟

pronunciation.note: 采用词典所列的一种读音。

morphology.text: ana-（再、重新） + gnōrizein（希腊语：认出） → anagnōrisis → anagnorisis 真相发现；这是希腊语来源的构词线索。

etymology.text: 学术借自古希腊语 anagnōrisis，来自动词 anagnōrizein（认出、发现）。可联想主角突然认出某人的真实身份。

usage_note: 文学和戏剧术语，强调人物意识到真实身份或处境；单纯的情节转折不一定是 anagnorisis。

senses.meaning_zh: （文学、戏剧）人物认出真实身份或发现关键真相的时刻；发现
senses.meaning_en: A character's discovery of a true identity or crucial truth in a literary work, especially a tragedy.
senses.english_definition: Anagnorisis is the moment in a story or play when a character discovers an important truth about themselves, another person, or their situation.
senses.collocation_en: a moment of anagnorisis; anagnorisis and peripeteia
senses.collocation_zh: 发现关键真相的时刻；发现与突转
senses.sentence_en: The hero's anagnorisis comes when he realizes that the stranger is his brother.
senses.sentence_zh: 当主人公意识到那个陌生人就是自己的兄弟时，剧情便迎来了他认出真相的时刻。

etymology_story.zh: 借自古希腊语 anagnōrisis（认出、发现），与 anagnōrizein（认出）有关。亚里士多德在戏剧理论中用它描述人物从不知到知的转变，后来成为文学批评中的术语。
etymology_story.en: Anagnorisis was borrowed from Greek anagnōrisis, meaning recognition or discovery, related to anagnōrizein, 'to recognize.' Aristotle used it in dramatic theory for a change from ignorance to knowledge, and it became an established term in literary criticism.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将它作为完整的希腊语借词使用，不宜硬拆成能自由造词的英语词缀；历史线索为 ana-（再、回）与表示认知的 gnōr- 成分及希腊语名词构形。复数为 anagnorises；罕见形容词 anagnoristic 表示“与认出真相有关的”。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats anagnorisis as a whole Greek loanword rather than a freely productive English prefix-and-suffix construction; its historical components include ana- 'again, back,' a recognition-related gnōr- element, and Greek nominal morphology. The plural is anagnorises; the rare adjective anagnoristic means relating to such recognition.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: recognition（认出、认识到）最接近其核心，但适用范围更广；discovery（发现）强调获知原先未知的事实，不一定涉及身份；epiphany（顿悟）强调突然领悟意义，不一定构成剧情中的关键认知转折。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Recognition is closest to the core meaning but has much broader uses; discovery emphasizes learning a previously unknown fact without necessarily identifying someone; epiphany emphasizes sudden insight without necessarily marking a crucial dramatic recognition.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“不知道”到“认出来”：主角突然明白“原来是你！”
mnemonic_anchor.en: Move from not knowing to recognizing: the character suddenly realizes, 'So it was you!'

pronunciation.note: 按 Merriam-Webster 的读音标记转写为宽式 IPA。

forms: 可数名词，复数 apatosaurs；apatosaurus 是另一形式。

morphology.text: apato-（希腊语：迷惑、欺骗） + -saur（蜥蜴） → apatosaur 迷惑龙。

etymology.text: 来自现代科学拉丁语属名 Apatosaurus，以希腊语表示迷惑的成分和 sauros（蜥蜴）组成。把“令人迷惑的蜥蜴”当作名称线索。

usage_note: 指一种长颈、长尾的植食性蜥脚类恐龙。普通名 apatosaur 小写；拉丁语属名 Apatosaurus 首字母大写。

etymology_story.zh: 由科学属名 Apatosaurus 转成英语普通名词，属名结合了希腊语中表示“欺骗、迷惑”的成分和 sauros（蜥蜴）。这个名称通常解释为“具有迷惑性的蜥蜴”，说的是命名时的解剖学印象，并非这种动物会欺骗人。
etymology_story.en: Apatosaur is an English common-noun form of the scientific genus name Apatosaurus, which combines Greek elements meaning deception and lizard. The name is conventionally interpreted as 'deceptive lizard,' reflecting an anatomical impression associated with its naming rather than deceptive behavior.

morphology_enriched.zh: 直接构词关系为 Apatosaurus（科学属名）→ apatosaur（英语普通名词），去掉科学名称末尾的 -us；历史上可分析为 apato-（迷惑）+ -saur（蜥蜴）。复数为 apatosaurs；相关形式包括 apatosaurus（另一普通名词形式）及专业用语 apatosaurine（迷惑龙亚科的；迷惑龙亚科成员）。
morphology_enriched.en: The immediate formation is Apatosaurus, the scientific genus name, → apatosaur, an English common noun, with the scientific ending -us removed; historically, the name contains apato- 'deception' + -saur 'lizard.' The plural is apatosaurs; related forms include apatosaurus as an alternative common noun and the technical term apatosaurine, referring to a member of, or something belonging to, Apatosaurinae.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: apatosaurus（迷惑龙）是对应的另一名称形式；sauropod（蜥脚类恐龙）是涵盖迷惑龙等恐龙的上位词；diplodocid（梁龙科恐龙）是更具体的分类称呼，但也不只指迷惑龙。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Apatosaurus is an alternative name form for the same animal; sauropod is a broader category that includes apatosaurs; diplodocid is a more specific family-level label but still includes dinosaurs other than apatosaurs.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: apato-（迷惑）+ -saur（蜥蜴）：“迷惑的蜥蜴”就是迷惑龙的名称线索。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Apato- 'deception' + -saur 'lizard': 'deceptive lizard' anchors the dinosaur's name.

morphology.text: capell-（意大利语：头发的词干） + -ini（指小、复数） → capellini 像细发丝的意大利面。

etymology_story.zh: 借自意大利语 capellini，是 capello（头发）的指小复数形式，字面意思是“小头发”。这种面因形状细长、像发丝而得名。
etymology_story.en: Borrowed from Italian capellini, a diminutive plural of capello, meaning 'hair'; its literal meaning is 'little hairs.' The name describes the pasta's thin, hairlike strands.

morphology_enriched.zh: 意大利语内部结构为 capell-（头发词干）+ -in-（指小成分）+ -i（阳性复数词尾）；在现代英语中通常作为完整的借词使用，常按不可数食物名词处理，无常用英语派生词。相关意大利语形式有 capello（单数：头发）、capelli（复数：头发）和 capellino（指小单数）。
morphology_enriched.en: The Italian structure is capell- (hair stem) + -in- (diminutive element) + -i (masculine plural ending). Modern English generally treats it as an intact loanword and a mass noun for food, with no common English derivatives. Related Italian forms are capello (singular), capelli (plural), and capellino (diminutive singular).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: angel hair（天使发丝面）是非常接近的名称，但在区分规格时往往比 capellini 更细；thin spaghetti（细意大利面）是较宽泛的描述；vermicelli（细条面）指另一类细长面，其具体粗细因地区而异。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Angel hair is a close alternative but is often finer when the varieties are distinguished; thin spaghetti is a broader description; vermicelli denotes another thin pasta whose thickness varies by regional convention.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 名字就是“小头发”：像发丝一样细的长面。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The name means 'little hairs': picture long pasta as thin as strands of hair.

pronunciation.note: 按 Merriam-Webster 的读音标记转写为宽式 IPA。

forms: 可数或不可数；表示多次操作时用 cardioversions。
family: cardiovert 进行心律转复；cardioverter 心脏复律器

morphology.text: cardio-（心脏） + -version（转变） → cardioversion 心律转复。

etymology.text: 这是现代英语医学合成词，cardio- 来自希腊语 kardia（心脏），-version 追到拉丁语表示转变的词族。用“把心律转回正常”联记。

usage_note: 医学名词，指用药物或受控电流恢复心律。它与 defibrillation 相关，但不是在所有医学语境下都可以互换的名称。

senses.meaning_zh: 心律转复；通过电击或药物使异常心律恢复正常
senses.meaning_en: restoration of a normal heart rhythm using an electrical shock or medication
senses.english_definition: Cardioversion is a medical procedure or treatment that restores a normal heart rhythm using an electrical shock or medication.
senses.collocation_zh: 电复律；接受心律转复治疗
senses.sentence_en: The patient underwent electrical cardioversion to restore a normal heart rhythm.
senses.sentence_zh: 患者接受了电复律治疗，以恢复正常心律。

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代医学术语，由 cardio-（心脏，源自希腊语 kardia）和表示转变的 version 构成，后者最终源自拉丁语 vertere（转动）。名称表达的是让异常心律转回正常心律。
etymology_story.en: This modern medical term combines cardio-, from Greek kardia meaning 'heart,' with version, ultimately from Latin vertere meaning 'to turn.' It names the conversion of an abnormal heart rhythm back to a normal one.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代结构为 cardio-（心脏）+ version（转变）。同族形式包括 cardiovert（动词：使心律转复）、cardioverts（第三人称单数）、cardioverted（过去式及过去分词）、cardioverting（现在分词）和 cardioversions（名词复数）；cardioverter 指实施电复律的装置。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern structure is cardio- (heart) + version (turning or conversion). The family includes cardiovert (verb), cardioverts, cardioverted, cardioverting, and cardioversions (plural noun); a cardioverter is a device that delivers electrical cardioversion.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: rhythm conversion（心律转复）是较直白的近义表达；electrical cardioversion（电复律）特指用电击实现的转复；defibrillation（除颤）是相关但不能随意互换的术语，通常指针对特定危险心律实施的非同步电击，而电复律通常与心搏同步。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Rhythm conversion is a plain-language near-equivalent; electrical cardioversion specifies conversion by an electrical shock; defibrillation is related but not interchangeable, usually referring to an unsynchronized shock for particular dangerous rhythms, whereas electrical cardioversion is usually synchronized.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cardio- 是“心脏”，version 是“转变”：把心律转回正常。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Cardio- means 'heart' and version suggests turning: turn the heart's rhythm back to normal.

pronunciation.note: 采用词典所列的一种读音。

family: chide 责备；unchid 未受责备的

morphology.text: chid 整词记，是 chide 的不规则过去式；联记 un-（没有） + chid → unchid 未受责备的。

etymology.text: 来自英语 chide 的旧式不规则变形；chide 经中古英语 chiden 追到古英语 cīdan（责备、争辩）。用旧小说里的责备场景记住它。

usage_note: chid 多见于文学或较旧的用法；本课按过去式学习，现代常用 chided。它也能作过去分词。

senses.pos: v. 动词（chide 的不规则过去式，亦可作过去分词；现多见于文学或旧式用法）
senses.meaning_zh: 责备了；斥责了；受到责备的
senses.meaning_en: expressed disapproval of someone; a past-tense and past-participle form of chide
senses.english_definition: If someone chid another person, they spoke to that person critically because they disapproved of something the person had done.
senses.collocation_en: chid him gently; chid herself for
senses.collocation_zh: 温和地责备了他；因……责备自己
senses.sentence_en: She chid herself for having spoken so harshly.
senses.sentence_zh: 她责备自己刚才说话太严厉。

etymology_story.zh: chid 是 chide 的历史性不规则屈折形式；chide 经中古英语 chiden 追溯至古英语 cīdan，意为“争吵、责备”。现代英语更常用规则形式 chided，而 chid 多保留在文学或旧式表达中。
etymology_story.en: Chid is a historical irregular inflection of chide, which comes through Middle English chiden from Old English cīdan, meaning 'to quarrel or rebuke.' Modern English more often uses the regular form chided, while chid survives chiefly in literary or older usage.

morphology_enriched.zh: chid 不是由词根加后缀构成的独立派生词，而是 chide 通过内部元音变化形成的屈折形式。词族包括 chide（原形）、chides（第三人称单数）、chiding（现在分词，也可作形容词或名词）、chided（常用过去式及过去分词）、chid（不规则过去式及过去分词）、chidden（另一过去分词）和 chidingly（副词：责备地）。
morphology_enriched.en: Chid is an inflected form of chide involving an internal vowel change, rather than a separately derived word with a suffix. The family includes chide, chides, chiding (also adjectival or nominal), chided (the usual past tense and past participle), chid (an irregular past tense and past participle), chidden (another past participle), and chidingly (adverb).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: scolded（责骂了）通常更带怒气；rebuked（斥责了）强调明确而严肃的否定；reprimanded（训诫了）常涉及上级或权威的正式批评。chid 往往带文学色彩，责备程度可以较轻。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Scolded usually suggests greater irritation; rebuked emphasizes firm, explicit disapproval; reprimanded often implies formal criticism from someone in authority. Chid has a literary flavor and can describe relatively mild criticism.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: chide 变 chid：元音缩短，责备已发生；它是旧式过去形式。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Chide becomes chid: the vowel shortens, and the scolding is already in the past.

senses.meaning_zh: 钴胺素；具有维生素 B12 活性的含钴化合物
senses.meaning_en: a cobalt-containing compound with vitamin B12 activity
senses.english_definition: Cobalamin is a name for vitamin B12 or for one of the related cobalt-containing compounds that have its vitamin activity.
senses.collocation_zh: 钴胺素缺乏；钴胺素的吸收
senses.sentence_en: Reduced cobalamin absorption can lead to vitamin B12 deficiency.
senses.sentence_zh: 钴胺素吸收减少可导致维生素 B12 缺乏。

etymology_story.zh: 这个名称形成于20世纪中叶，结合了 cobalt（钴）的词干和呼应 vitamin（维生素）的词尾。命名突出这类维生素分子的结构中含有钴。
etymology_story.en: The name was formed in the mid-twentieth century from the stem of cobalt and an ending echoing vitamin. It highlights the cobalt atom present in these vitamin molecules.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可识别的命名结构为 cobal(t)-（钴）+ -amin（呼应 vitamin 的命名成分），不宜把它理解为两个完整单词的直接相加。常见同族名称包括 cobalamins（钴胺素类）、cyanocobalamin（氰钴胺）、hydroxocobalamin（羟钴胺）、methylcobalamin（甲钴胺）和 adenosylcobalamin（腺苷钴胺）。
morphology_enriched.en: The recognizable naming structure is cobal(t)- (cobalt) + -amin (a naming element echoing vitamin), rather than two complete words simply joined together. Common family members include cobalamins, cyanocobalamin, hydroxocobalamin, methylcobalamin, and adenosylcobalamin.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: vitamin B12（维生素 B12）是日常与营养学语境中的通用对应名称；cyanocobalamin（氰钴胺）是补充剂中常见的一种具体形式；methylcobalamin（甲钴胺）是具有辅酶作用的一种形式。后两者是钴胺素的具体成员，不能在所有语境中替代总称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Vitamin B12 is the usual equivalent in everyday and nutritional contexts; cyanocobalamin is a particular form commonly used in supplements; methylcobalamin is a form that functions as a coenzyme. The latter two name specific members of the cobalamin group rather than interchangeable general synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 看到 cobal- 想到 cobalt：B12 的分子中心含有钴。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Let cobal- cue cobalt: vitamin B12 contains a cobalt atom at its center.

etymology_story.zh: 英语通过西班牙语 cocobolo 借入这个树木和木材名称，更早的来源常被追溯至美洲原住民语言。该词在英语中既指树，也指这种树所产的装饰性硬木。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed this tree and timber name through Spanish cocobolo, with its earlier origin commonly traced to an Indigenous American language. In English, it denotes both the tree and its decorative hardwood.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 cocobolo 视为不可再分析的借词，不拆成 coco 和 bolo。作木材名时通常不可数；作树名时可数，复数为 cocobolos。没有常用的单词派生形式；cocobolo wood（可可波罗木木材）、cocobolo handle（可可波罗木手柄）中的 cocobolo 是名词作定语，不构成独立的常用形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats cocobolo as an unanalyzed loanword, not as coco plus bolo. It is usually uncountable as a timber name and countable as a tree name, with the plural cocobolos. It has no common single-word derivatives; in cocobolo wood and cocobolo handle, it functions as a noun modifier rather than a separate common adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cocobolo wood（可可波罗木木材）明确指木材；rosewood（黄檀木、玫瑰木）是范围更广的木材名称，cocobolo 属于其中一类；Dalbergia retusa（微凹黄檀）是主要来源树种的学名，不能在所有木材贸易语境中与 cocobolo 完全等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cocobolo wood explicitly denotes the timber; rosewood is a broader timber category that includes cocobolo; Dalbergia retusa is the scientific name of a principal source species and is not an exact substitute in every timber-trade context.

senses.meaning_zh: 有绉状细褶的；尤指皮肤薄而松皱的
senses.meaning_en: finely wrinkled like crepe fabric or paper, especially of thin skin
senses.english_definition: Something that is crepey has many small wrinkles, like the surface of crepe fabric or paper.
senses.chinese_definition: 某物若呈绉状，就是表面像绉织物或皱纹纸一样，有许多细小的皱褶。

etymology_story.zh: crepey 由 crepe（绉织物、皱纹纸）加形容词后缀 -y 构成；crepe 借自法语 crêpe，最终可追溯至拉丁语 crispus（卷曲的、有皱褶的）。绉织物的细褶外观也用于描述皮肤等表面的细密皱纹。
etymology_story.en: Crepey combines crepe with the adjective-forming suffix -y; crepe comes through French crêpe ultimately from Latin crispus, meaning curled or wrinkled. The finely crinkled appearance of the material also describes wrinkles on skin and other surfaces. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/crepey), [Etymonline](https://www.etymonline.com/word/crepe).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：crepe（绉织物、皱纹纸）+ -y（具有……特征的）→ crepey。相关形式：crepy（异体拼写）、crepiness（绉状质地；皮肤细皱状态）；比较通常可用 more crepey、most crepey。crepe 也写作 crêpe；crape 是相关的历史拼写，常用于丧服绉纱。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: crepe, meaning crinkled fabric or paper, + -y, meaning having the characteristics of, → crepey. Related forms include crepy, an alternative spelling, and crepiness, the quality of being crepey; comparison can use more crepey and most crepey. Crepe also appears as crêpe; the historically related spelling crape is especially associated with mourning fabric.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: wrinkled（有皱纹的）是宽泛用语，可指深浅不一的皱纹；crinkly（有细碎褶皱的）强调密集的小褶；papery（薄而似纸的）强调薄度和质感。crepey 将细密皱褶与绉纸般的外观结合起来，描述皮肤时常兼有薄、松的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Wrinkled broadly describes wrinkles of different sizes; crinkly emphasizes numerous small folds; papery emphasizes thinness and a paperlike texture. Crepey combines fine wrinkling with a crepe-paper appearance and, when describing skin, often suggests thinness and looseness.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: crepe 是皱纹纸；crepey 就是表面像皱纹纸一样起细褶。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture crepe paper: crepey describes a surface covered with similarly fine wrinkles.

etymology_story.zh: 该词源自美国费城枪匠 Henry Deringer 的姓氏，他以制造袖珍手枪闻名。增加一个 r 的 derringer 拼写后来成为通称，用于指这类小型短管手枪。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from the surname of Philadelphia gunsmith Henry Deringer, who became known for pocket pistols. The spelling derringer, with an additional r, became a generic name for this type of small, short-barreled pistol. [Autry Museum](https://collections.theautry.org/mwebcgi/mweb.exe?request=record%3Bid%3DM555916%3Btype%3D101).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可进一步按常用词缀拆分的人名来源名词，词尾 -er 不是表示施事者的后缀。复数为 derringers；相关拼写有 deringer，原始姓氏拼写为 Deringer；derringer-style（德林杰式的）是临时复合形容词，没有常用的派生动词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, this is an eponymous noun without a productive internal affix structure; its final -er is not an agent suffix. The plural is derringers; deringer is a related spelling, and Deringer is the original surname. Derringer-style is a compound adjective; there are no common derived verbs or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pocket pistol（袖珍手枪）是最接近的上位表达，范围更广；pistol（手枪）不限定体积；handgun（手持短枪）还包括左轮手枪等类型。derringer 特指一种体积极小、枪管很短的袖珍手枪。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pocket pistol is the closest broader expression; pistol does not specify size; handgun is broader still and includes revolvers. Derringer identifies a particular type of very small, short-barreled pocket pistol.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Deringer 是枪匠姓氏；多一个 r 的 derringer 成了袖珍手枪的通称。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Deringer named the gunsmith; derringer, with an extra r, names the pocket pistol.

etymology_story.zh: 表示“污暗”的 dinge 是十九世纪从 dingy（污暗的）逆构而来的词，“使污暗”的动词义与这一组意义相连。表示“凹痕、使凹陷”的另一组名词和动词义来源不明，不能直接断言源自古英语 dengan。
etymology_story.en: Dinge meaning dinginess arose in the nineteenth century by back-formation from dingy; the verb meaning to make dingy belongs to this semantic group. The separate dent-related noun and verb have an uncertain origin and should not be confidently derived from Old English dengan. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/dinge), [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/dinge), [Vocabulary.com](https://www.vocabulary.com/dictionary/dinge).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中按 dinge 整词处理，需区分“凹痕”和“污暗”两组意义。可数名词复数及动词第三人称单数为 dinges，过去式和过去分词为 dinged；现在分词可见 dingeing 或 dinging。污暗义相关词族有 dingy（污暗的）、dingier、dingiest、dingily（污暗地）、dinginess（污暗状态）。dinged-up（磕碰损坏的）通常分析为 ding 的过去分词加 up，不宜当作 dinge 专有的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat dinge as a whole modern base, distinguishing its dent-related and dinginess-related meanings. The count-noun plural and third-person singular verb are dinges; the past tense and past participle are dinged, and present-participle spellings include dingeing and dinging. The dinginess family includes dingy, dingier, dingiest, dingily, and dinginess. Dinged-up is normally analyzed through the verb ding plus up, rather than as a derivative specific to dinge.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dent（凹痕；使凹陷）对应撞击义，是现代英语中更常用的表达；dinginess（污暗状态）对应污暗义，侧重整体外观；grime（积垢）更强调附着的污物。dinge 的这两组意义不可混为一谈。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dent matches the impact-related meanings and is much more usual in modern English; dinginess matches the dirty, dull appearance; grime emphasizes accumulated dirt itself. These two meaning groups of dinge should be kept distinct.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 分两条记：凹痕义联想 dent；污暗义联想 dingy。这是意义联想，不是共同词源。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use two hooks: dent for the damage meanings, dingy for the dirty appearance. These are meaning associations, not a claim of shared origin.

etymology_story.zh: dishabille 借自法语 déshabillé，即 déshabiller（脱衣）的过去分词作名词使用；其中 dés- 表示解除，habiller 表示穿衣。英语保留了未穿戴齐整或衣着随便的意义，也曾用它指这种状态下穿的便服。
etymology_story.en: Dishabille was borrowed from French déshabillé, the past participle of déshabiller, meaning to undress, used as a noun; dés- expresses reversal and habiller means to dress. English retained the sense of incomplete or informal dress and also historically used it for clothing worn in that state. [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/dishabille).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整体借入的名词，不应按英语 dis- 加一个独立词 habille 来分析。历史法语结构为 dés-（解除）+ habiller（穿衣）→ déshabiller（脱衣）→ déshabillé（已脱衣的；便服状态）。英语异体为 deshabille；通常作不可数名词，罕见可数用法的复数为 dishabilles；没有常用的派生动词、形容词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, this is a borrowed noun, not a productive combination of English dis- with an independent word habille. Its historical French structure is dés-, reversal, + habiller, to dress, → déshabiller, to undress, → déshabillé, undressed or informal dress. Deshabille is an English spelling variant. The noun is usually uncountable; rare count uses have the plural dishabilles. There are no common derived English verbs, adjectives, or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: undress（未穿戴齐整的状态）最接近，常见于 in a state of undress；informal dress（非正式衣着）不一定不整齐或穿得不全；disarray（凌乱）范围更广，可形容衣着、物品或组织。dishabille 带文学色彩，常描写私人生活中尚未整理衣装的状态。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Undress is closest, especially in a state of undress; informal dress need not be untidy or incomplete; disarray describes disorder more broadly. Dishabille has a literary flavor and often evokes an unprepared, privately dressed appearance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 借法语逻辑记：解除穿衣 → 尚未穿戴齐整。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the French logic: undo the dressing → appear before being fully dressed.
