etymology_story.zh: 该词仿照 epizootic（动物疫病的）构成，以表示“在……之内”的 en- 与表示“动物”的希腊语词根相结合。它强调疾病在当地动物种群中的持续存在，与 epizootic 常指的集中暴发形成区别。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed on the model of epizootic, combining en-, meaning within, with a Greek-derived element meaning animal. It describes a disease's continuing presence in a local animal population, in contrast to the outbreak commonly described by epizootic.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：en-（在……之内）+ zo-（动物）+ -otic（形容词词尾，仿照 epizootic）→ enzootic；形容词也可转用为名词。词族包括 enzootically（以地方性动物病的方式，副词）、enzooticity（动物疾病的地方性存在状态，名词）和 enzootics（名词复数）；epizootic（动物疫病的；动物疫病）是相关对照词。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: en- (within) + zo- (animal) + -otic (an adjective ending modeled on epizootic) → enzootic; the adjective also functions as a noun. Family members include enzootically, the adverb; enzooticity, the noun for the condition of being enzootic; and enzootics, the plural noun. Epizootic is a related contrasting term.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: endemic（地方性的）最接近本词，但适用范围不限于动物疾病；endemic animal disease（地方性动物病）是名词义的直接释义；epizootic（动物疫病的）强调动物群体中的异常增多或暴发，是对照词而非同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Endemic is the closest equivalent but is not restricted to animal diseases; endemic animal disease directly paraphrases the noun; epizootic emphasizes an unusual increase or outbreak in an animal population and is a contrast rather than a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: en- 是“在内”，zo- 是“动物”：疾病长期存在于当地动物群体之内。
mnemonic_anchor.en: En- means within and zo- means animal: the disease stays within the local animal population.

etymology_story.zh: Estrone 是现代激素命名词，将与 estrus（发情期）相关的 estr- 与表示酮的后缀 -one 结合起来。Estr- 的远源是希腊语 oistros，原指“牛虻”，也指“狂躁或强烈冲动”，后来进入生殖生理学术语。
etymology_story.en: Estrone is a modern hormone name combining estr-, associated with estrus, with -one, the suffix indicating a ketone. Estr- ultimately traces to Greek oistros, meaning a gadfly and also frenzy or strong impulse, which later entered reproductive terminology.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代命名结构：estr-（雌激素及相关甾体名称中的词干）+ -one（酮类后缀）→ estrone。异体拼写为 oestrone；相关命名词族包括 estradiol（雌二醇）、estriol（雌三醇）、estrogen／oestrogen（雌激素）、estrogenic／oestrogenic（雌激素的；有雌激素作用的）及 estrane（雌甾烷，相关甾体母体结构）。这些相关名称并非都由 estrone 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern naming structure: estr- (a stem in estrogen and related steroid names) + -one (ketone suffix) → estrone. Oestrone is a spelling variant; the related naming family includes estradiol, estriol, estrogen/oestrogen, estrogenic/oestrogenic, and estrane, a related parent steroid structure. synonyms_and_nuances.en: Oestrone is the traditional British spelling of the same substance; E1 is its standard abbreviated designation; estrogen names the broader hormone class, which includes estrone and other hormones, so it is not an exact substitute.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由表示“毛囊”的 follicul- 与表示“炎症”的医学后缀 -itis 构成。Follicul- 来自拉丁语 folliculus“小袋”，是 follis“袋”的指小形式，后来用于命名毛囊等小囊状结构。

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：follicul-（毛囊；小囊）+ -itis（炎症）→ folliculitis。相关词族包括 follicle（毛囊；滤泡；卵泡）、follicular（毛囊的；滤泡的；卵泡的）和 follicularly（以滤泡或毛囊方式，较少见副词）。复合词包括 perifolliculitis（毛囊周围炎）和 pseudofolliculitis（假性毛囊炎）；后者是独立的相关病名。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: follicul- (follicle or small sac) + -itis (inflammation) → folliculitis. Related family members include follicle, follicular, and the uncommon adverb follicularly. synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hair-follicle inflammation is an accurate plain-language equivalent; follicular inflammation can mean the same in dermatology but is broader without that context; hair-follicle infection applies only to infectious cases because folliculitis can also have noninfectious causes.

etymology_story.zh: 这是由 grease（油脂）和 wood（木；木本植物）组成的美式英语植物名，十九世纪已有使用。这个名称与植物被认为具有的油腻外观、树脂性或易燃特点有关，后来成为几种不同灌木的俗名。
etymology_story.en: This American English plant name combines grease and wood and was in use by the nineteenth century. It alludes to a greasy appearance, resinous character, or ready burning associated with the plants and has been applied to several different shrubs.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：grease（油脂）+ wood（木本植物）→ greasewood（油木），属于复合名词。通常作植物名称或集合用语；表示多种或多株时可用 greasewoods。相关名称有 black greasewood（黑油木）和 greasewood scrub（油木灌丛）；没有常用的派生动词或形容词。

It commonly functions as a plant name or collective term; greasewoods can refer to different kinds or individual shrubs. Related expressions include black greasewood and greasewood scrub; there are no common derived verbs or adjectives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: black greasewood（黑油木）明确指 Sarcobatus vermiculatus；chamise（加州腺口灌木）和 shadscale（鳞苞滨藜）也可在某些地区被称为 greasewood，但它们是不同的植物，不能在严格的植物学语境中互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Black greasewood specifically identifies Sarcobatus vermiculatus. Chamise and shadscale may also be called greasewood regionally, but they are different plants and are not interchangeable botanical names.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: grease + wood：把名字想成“带油脂感的木本灌木”，再联系北美干旱盐碱地。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Grease + wood: picture an oily-looking woody shrub, then place the main species in a dry, salty North American landscape.

etymology_story.zh: hafnium 得名于 Hafnia，即哥本哈根的拉丁名称，并加上金属元素名称中常见的后缀 -ium。这个名称纪念了该元素于 1923 年在哥本哈根被发现。
etymology_story.en: Hafnium was named after Hafnia, the Latin name for Copenhagen, with the ending -ium commonly used in metallic element names. The name commemorates the element's discovery in Copenhagen in 1923.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代科学命名分析：Hafn-（取自 Hafnia，哥本哈根）+ -ium（金属元素命名后缀）→ hafnium（铪）；Hafn- 是专名词干，并非一般英语自由词根。相关词族和术语包括 hafnia（二氧化铪，HfO₂）、hafnate（铪酸盐）、hafnium oxide（氧化铪）和 hafnium carbide（碳化铪）；元素名称通常不可数。
morphology_enriched.en: Scientific naming structure: Hafn-, from Hafnia, Copenhagen, + -ium, a metallic-element naming suffix, → hafnium. Hafn- is a proper-name stem rather than an ordinary independent English root. Related forms and terms include hafnia, hafnium dioxide, HfO₂; hafnate; hafnium oxide; and hafnium carbide. The element name is normally uncountable.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有常用的严格近义词。Hf 是铪的化学符号；hafnia 指二氧化铪而非金属铪；zirconium（锆）是化学性质相近、常与铪共存的另一种元素。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There are no common exact synonyms. Hf is the chemical symbol for hafnium; hafnia means hafnium dioxide rather than the metal; zirconium is a separate, chemically similar element often found alongside hafnium.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Hafnia（哥本哈根）+ -ium（金属名）：记住“以发现城市命名的铪”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hafnia, Copenhagen, + -ium, a metal-name ending: remember hafnium as the metal named after its city of discovery.

senses.meaning_zh: 咯血；从下呼吸道咳出血液或血性痰
senses.meaning_en: The coughing up of blood or blood-stained sputum from the lower respiratory tract.
senses.english_definition: Hemoptysis is the coughing up of blood that comes from the lungs or lower airways.
senses.collocation_zh: 大咯血；反复咯血

etymology_story.zh: 英语通过医学拉丁语吸收了这个词，其源头是希腊语中表示“血”的 haima 和表示“吐出”的 ptysis。现代医学把它专门用于来自肺或下呼吸道的咳血。
etymology_story.en: English acquired the word through medical Latin from Greek elements meaning blood, haima, and spitting, ptysis. In modern medicine, it specifically denotes blood coughed up from the lungs or lower respiratory tract.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代医学构词：hem(o)-（血）+ -ptysis（吐出、咳出）→ hemoptysis（咯血）。英式拼写为 haemoptysis；规则性医学复数为 hemoptyses／haemoptyses，但通常作不可数症状名称。相关形容词为 hemoptytic／haemoptytic（咯血的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern medical structure: hem(o)-, blood, + -ptysis, spitting or coughing up, → hemoptysis. The British spelling is haemoptysis. The medical plurals are hemoptyses and haemoptyses, although the symptom name is usually uncountable. Related adjectives are hemoptytic and haemoptytic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: coughing up blood（咳出血）是最自然的通俗对应表达；blood-stained sputum（血性痰）描述带血的痰液，是咯血的一种表现；hematemesis（呕血）指呕出消化道来源的血，不是咯血的近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Coughing up blood is the closest plain-language equivalent. Blood-stained sputum describes bloody mucus and can be a manifestation of hemoptysis. Hematemesis means vomiting blood from the digestive tract and is a contrasting term, not a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hemo-＝血，-ptysis＝咳出：血从呼吸道被咳出来，就是咯血。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hemo- means blood and -ptysis means spitting out: blood coughed out of the airways is hemoptysis.

etymology_story.zh: 这个词由 hollow（中空的）和 ware（器物、制品）组合而成，用来统称具有内部容积的器皿。在餐具和银器行业中，它逐渐成为茶壶、碗、罐等容器类制品的分类名称。
etymology_story.en: The word combines hollow with ware, meaning manufactured articles, to name vessels with an interior space. In the tableware and silver trades, it became a category covering containers such as teapots, bowls, and jugs.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：hollow（中空的）+ ware（器物总称）→ hollowware；holloware 是合写时简化重复字母 w 的拼写变体，另有 hollow-ware。通常作不可数集合名词；没有常用的派生动词或形容词。相关分类词有 flatware（刀叉匙等扁平餐具）和 tableware（餐具）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: hollow + ware → hollowware. Holloware is a spelling variant that reduces the doubled w at the compound boundary; hollow-ware also occurs. It is normally an uncountable collective noun and has no common derived verbs or adjectives. Related category words include flatware and tableware.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hollowware 是同词异拼，意义相同；tableware（餐具）范围更广，包括各种就餐和上菜用具；silverware（银器、银制餐具）按材质或行业惯例分类，可包括中空器皿和刀叉匙。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hollowware is an alternative spelling with the same meaning. Tableware is broader and covers articles used for eating and serving. Silverware classifies objects by material or trade usage and can include both hollow vessels and cutlery.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hollow＝里面空，ware＝器皿：想到能装茶、汤或糖的壶、碗和罐。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hollow means empty inside and ware means articles: picture pots, bowls, and jugs with room to hold something.

etymology_story.en: Hydrazine belongs to nineteenth-century international chemical nomenclature, combining elements referring to hydrogen and azote, an older name for nitrogen, with the chemical ending -ine. The name was subsequently extended to a class of compounds derived from the parent substance.

morphology_enriched.zh: 科学命名分析：hydr-（取自 hydrogen，氢）+ az-（取自 azote，氮）+ -ine（化学名称后缀）→ hydrazine（肼）。母体物质名称通常不可数；表示肼类衍生物时可数，复数为 hydrazines。主要词族包括 hydrazinium（肼鎓）、hydrazino-（肼基）、hydrazide（酰肼）、hydrazone（腙）、methylhydrazine（甲基肼）和 phenylhydrazine（苯肼）。
morphology_enriched.en: Chemical naming structure: hydr-, from hydrogen, + az-, from azote, nitrogen, + -ine, a chemical naming suffix, → hydrazine. The parent substance is normally uncountable; a derivative is countable, with the plural hydrazines. Principal family members include hydrazinium, hydrazino-, hydrazide, hydrazone, methylhydrazine, and phenylhydrazine.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: diazane（二氮烷）是母体 N₂H₄ 的系统名称；hydrazine hydrate（水合肼）指其水合形式或相应商品水溶液，不能等同于无水肼；methylhydrazine（甲基肼）是取代衍生物，也不是母体肼的同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Diazane is a systematic name for the parent compound N₂H₄. Hydrazine hydrate denotes its hydrated form or corresponding commercial aqueous preparation and is not identical to anhydrous hydrazine. Methylhydrazine is a substituted derivative rather than a synonym for the parent compound.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hydr- 想到氢，az- 想到氮：两个氮连在一起，各带两个氢，即 H₂N—NH₂。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Let hydr- suggest hydrogen and az- suggest nitrogen: two linked nitrogen atoms, each carrying two hydrogens, give H₂N—NH₂.

senses.sentence_zh: 血气检查显示，该患者存在高碳酸血症。

etymology_story.zh: 这是由希腊语来源的医学构词成分组成的术语：hyper- 表示“超过正常水平”，kapnos 原指“烟”，-ia 表示状态。表示“烟”的词根在这里用于二氧化碳，整个词指血液中二氧化碳过多的状态。
etymology_story.en: This medical term combines elements of Greek origin: hyper- means above normal, kapnos means smoke, and -ia marks a condition. The smoke-related root is used here for carbon dioxide, giving the meaning of excessive carbon dioxide in the blood.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代医学构词：hyper-（过高）+ capn-（在此指二氧化碳）+ -ia（状态）。词族及相关构词：hypercapnic（高碳酸血症的）；hypocapnia、hypocapnic（低碳酸血症、低碳酸血症的）；normocapnia、normocapnic（血中二氧化碳水平正常、血中二氧化碳水平正常的）。后两组是共享 capn- 的相关术语，并非由 hypercapnia 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern medical formation: hyper- (excessive) + capn- (carbon dioxide here) + -ia (condition). The word family includes hypercapnic. Related formations sharing capn- include hypocapnia and hypocapnic for abnormally low blood carbon dioxide, and normocapnia and normocapnic for normal blood carbon dioxide; these are related terms rather than direct derivatives of hypercapnia.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hypercarbia（高碳酸血症）基本同义；elevated blood carbon dioxide（血中二氧化碳升高）是直白的描述性表达；carbon dioxide retention（二氧化碳潴留）侧重二氧化碳未被充分排出的过程，常与高碳酸血症相关，但含义不完全相同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hypercarbia is essentially synonymous. Elevated blood carbon dioxide is a plain descriptive equivalent. Carbon dioxide retention emphasizes inadequate removal of carbon dioxide and is often associated with hypercapnia, but is not identical in meaning.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hyper- 是“过多”，capn- 在这里指二氧化碳：血里的二氧化碳超标。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hyper- means too much; capn- points to carbon dioxide: too much carbon dioxide in the blood.

morphology.text: hyper-（过高）+ cholesterol（胆固醇）+ -emia（血液状态，连接时合并词尾）→ hypercholesterolemia（高胆固醇血症）。

etymology.text: 这是进入英语的新拉丁语医学组合词：过高、胆固醇、血液状态三部分连在一起，几乎把病名的中文解释排成了一行。

usage_note: 医学术语，指血中胆固醇过高；不是高血糖。美式词尾 -emia，英式也写 -aemia。

senses.meaning_en: An abnormally high level of cholesterol in the blood.

senses.sentence_zh: 这个家族的几名成员被诊断患有家族性高胆固醇血症。

etymology_story.zh: 这个现代医学术语由 hyper-（过高）、cholesterol（胆固醇）和源自希腊语 haima“血”的 -emia 组成。cholesterol 的名称最终包含表示“胆汁”和“固体”的希腊语成分，反映了这种物质早期从胆结石中被分离出来的历史。
etymology_story.en: This modern medical term combines hyper- (excessive), cholesterol, and -emia, ultimately from Greek haima, meaning blood. The name cholesterol contains Greek elements meaning bile and solid, reflecting the substance's early isolation from gallstones.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：hyper-（过高）+ cholesterol（胆固醇）+ -emia（血液状态）。英式拼写为 hypercholesterolaemia；对应形容词为 hypercholesterolemic、英式 hypercholesterolaemic。相关词族有 cholesterol（胆固醇）、cholesterolemia／cholesterolaemia（血中胆固醇的存在或水平）和 hypocholesterolemia／hypocholesterolaemia（低胆固醇血症）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: hyper- (excessive) + cholesterol + -emia (a blood condition). The British spelling is hypercholesterolaemia; the corresponding adjectives are hypercholesterolemic and British hypercholesterolaemic. Related family members include cholesterol, cholesterolemia/cholesterolaemia (the presence or level of cholesterol in the blood), and hypocholesterolemia/hypocholesterolaemia (abnormally low blood cholesterol).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: high blood cholesterol（高血胆固醇）是常用的通俗对应表达；hyperlipidemia（高脂血症）范围更广，可涉及胆固醇或甘油三酯等血脂升高；dyslipidemia（血脂异常）还可包括某些血脂指标过低，因此后两者并非严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: High blood cholesterol is the usual plain-language equivalent. Hyperlipidemia is broader and can involve elevated cholesterol or triglycerides. Dyslipidemia covers abnormal lipid patterns, including some levels that are too low, so the latter two terms are not exact synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hyper- 过高 + cholesterol 胆固醇 + -emia 血液：胆固醇在血里过高。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hyper- means high, cholesterol names the substance, and -emia locates the condition in the blood.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 hypoglossal 建立在新拉丁语解剖术语 hypoglossus 的基础上，最终来自希腊语 hypo-（在……下）和 glōssa（舌）。它先表示“舌下的”，并用于舌下神经的名称；名词用法是 hypoglossal nerve 的省略。
etymology_story.en: English hypoglossal is based on the New Latin anatomical term hypoglossus, ultimately combining Greek hypo- (under) and glōssa (tongue). Its positional meaning became part of the name of the hypoglossal nerve, and the noun use is a shortening of hypoglossal nerve.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：hypo-（在……下）+ gloss-（舌）+ -al（……的）。名词通过省略 nerve 形成，复数为 hypoglossals；相关词有 hypoglossus（舌下神经的拉丁语名称）和共享 gloss- 的 glossal（舌的）。这里的 hypo- 表示位置，不表示数量不足。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: hypo- (under) + gloss- (tongue) + -al (relating to). The noun arises through omission of nerve and has the plural hypoglossals. Related forms include hypoglossus, the Latin anatomical name, and glossal, meaning relating to the tongue. Here hypo- expresses position rather than deficiency.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 名词义中，hypoglossal nerve（舌下神经）、twelfth cranial nerve（第十二脑神经）和 cranial nerve XII（第 XII 脑神经）指同一种神经，区别主要在命名方式；单独用 hypoglossal 作名词更依赖解剖学语境。形容词的“舌下”位置义可与 sublingual 接近，但 sublingual 不专指舌下神经。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the noun, hypoglossal nerve, twelfth cranial nerve, and cranial nerve XII identify the same nerve through different naming conventions; hypoglossal alone depends more heavily on anatomical context. For the positional adjective, sublingual has a similar meaning, but does not specifically identify this nerve.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hypo- 在下 + gloss- 舌：从“舌下”记住舌下神经。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hypo- means under and gloss- means tongue: under the tongue points to the hypoglossal nerve.

senses.meaning_zh: 原住民；某地原有居民，尤用于正式或学术语境

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语 indigène 进入英语，源自拉丁语 indigena，意为“本地出生者”。拉丁语形式结合了表示“在内”的成分和与“出生、产生”有关的词根，英语保留了“某地原有居民”的核心含义。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through French indigène, from Latin indigena, meaning a native-born inhabitant. The Latin formation combines an element meaning within with a root associated with birth or production, and English preserves the central idea of an original inhabitant.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，indigene 通常作为整体借词处理，复数为 indigenes；不宜按现代英语拆成 in- + digene。相关词族共享 indigen-：indigenous（本土的、原住民的）、indigenously（本土地）、indigenousness／indigeneity（本土性、原住民身份或特质）、indigenize／indigenise（使本土化）、indigenization／indigenisation（本土化）、indigenism（原住民主义）和 indigenist（原住民主义者；原住民主义的）；这些形式并非都由 indigene 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, indigene is normally treated as a borrowed whole, with the plural indigenes, rather than divided into productive English elements in- and digene. Related forms sharing indigen- include indigenous, indigenously, indigenousness, indigeneity, indigenize/indigenise, indigenization/indigenisation, indigenism, and indigenist. They express native origin, Indigenous identity, localization, or associated movements, and are not all direct derivatives of indigene.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: indigenous person（原住民）是较明确的现代对应表达；native（本地人、原住民）含义更宽，也可仅指在某地出生的人；autochthon（土著、原住民）是更罕见的学术或文学用词。indigene 本身较正式，日常表达中不常见。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Indigenous person is an explicit modern equivalent. Native is broader and can simply mean someone born in a place. Autochthon is a rarer scholarly or literary term for an original inhabitant. Indigene itself is formal and uncommon in everyday speech.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 与 indigenous 连记：indigenous 是“本土的”，indigene 是“本土原有居民”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the pair: indigenous describes native origin; an indigene is an original inhabitant.

senses.meaning_zh: 菠萝蜜；菠萝蜜果实或其可食部分

etymology_story.zh: jackfruit 中的 jack 经葡萄牙语 jaca 源自马拉雅拉姆语 cakka，都是这种水果的名称；英语随后加上 fruit。这里的 jack 与男子名 Jack 无关，词形记录了南亚水果名称经葡萄牙语传入英语的过程。
etymology_story.en: The jack in jackfruit comes through Portuguese jaca from Malayalam cakka, names for the fruit, with English fruit added afterward. This jack is unrelated to the personal name Jack and records the passage of a South Asian fruit name into English through Portuguese.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：jack（借入的水果名称）+ fruit（果实），属于复合名词。复数 jackfruits 可指多个果实或多棵树；表示果肉、食材或泛指这种水果时，常用不可数形式 jackfruit。常见组合有 jackfruit tree（菠萝蜜树）和 jackfruit seed（菠萝蜜种子），没有常用的独立派生动词或形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: jack (a borrowed fruit name) + fruit, forming a compound noun. The plural jackfruits can refer to individual fruits or trees; jackfruit is commonly uncountable when referring to flesh, an ingredient, or the fruit generally. Common combinations include jackfruit tree and jackfruit seed, and there are no established everyday derived verbs or adjectives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: jakfruit 是拼写变体；jack 和 jak 可在地区性或植物学用法中指菠萝蜜或菠萝蜜树，但单独使用更依赖语境。它们属于同一名称的变体或简称，日常英语中没有同样通行的独立近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Jakfruit is a spelling variant. Jack and jak can name the fruit or tree in regional or botanical usage, but need more context when used alone. These are variants or shortened names; everyday English has no equally established independent synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 借来的果名 jack + 熟悉的 fruit：热带大果菠萝蜜。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A borrowed name, jack, plus familiar fruit: picture the enormous tropical jackfruit.

morphology.text: kefir + -like → kefir-like（类似开菲尔的），如 kefir-like beverages。kefir 本身作为独立词素记忆。

senses.meaning_zh: 开菲尔；由细菌和酵母共同发酵制成的乳饮品
senses.meaning_en: a fermented milk drink made using bacteria and yeasts
senses.english_definition: Kefir is a slightly sour drink made by fermenting milk with a mixture of bacteria and yeasts.
senses.collocation_zh: 乳开菲尔；开菲尔粒（用于发酵的菌种团块）
senses.sentence_en: She adds plain kefir to her breakfast smoothie.

etymology_story.zh: 英语经俄语 kefir 借入这个与高加索地区发酵乳传统相关的名称。其更早的词源尚不确定，不宜把某种流行解释当作定论。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed kefir through Russian as the name of a fermented milk drink associated with the Caucasus. Its earlier origin is uncertain, so popular explanations should not be treated as established facts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，kefir 是不可进一步分析的借词，没有可独立解释的英语词根和词缀。常见组合有 milk kefir（乳开菲尔）、water kefir（水开菲尔，另一类发酵饮品）和 kefir grains（开菲尔粒）；kefir-like（类似开菲尔的）是临时性的形容词构词，并无庞大的固定派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, kefir is an unanalyzable loanword with no separate English root and affixes. Common combinations include milk kefir, water kefir, a different fermented drink, and kefir grains; kefir-like is a transparent occasional adjective, and there is no extensive established derivative family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全对应的常用近义词。fermented milk（发酵乳）是上位名称；yogurt（酸奶）通常由细菌发酵，质地也往往更稠；buttermilk（酪乳）指另一类乳饮品，不能与 kefir 互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday synonym. Fermented milk is a broader category; yogurt is usually fermented with bacteria and is often thicker; buttermilk is a different milk product and is not interchangeable with kefir.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整词记忆：kefir＝细菌和酵母一起发酵出的酸香乳饮。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the whole word: kefir is tangy milk fermented by bacteria and yeasts together.

meaning: 角化病；角质过度增生形成的皮肤病变

forms: 复数 keratoses；相关形容词 keratotic。
family: keratotic 角化病的；keratin 角蛋白

morphology.text: kerat-（角质）+ -osis（病理状态）→ keratosis（角化病）。

etymology.text: 英语借自德语 Keratose；德语名称以希腊语 keras“角”和病理状态后缀构成。把“角”联想到坚硬角质，就容易理解名称。

usage_note: 医学名词；具体类型由其他修饰词说明，如 actinic keratosis（日光性角化病）。

senses.meaning_zh: 角化病；角质增生形成的皮肤病变
senses.meaning_en: a skin condition or growth involving an overgrowth of keratin
senses.english_definition: Keratosis is a skin condition in which a thickened or rough growth forms because too much keratin develops.
senses.collocation_zh: 日光性角化病；脂溢性角化病
senses.sentence_en: The dermatologist identified the growth as a seborrheic keratosis.
senses.sentence_zh: 皮肤科医生确认该增生物是一处脂溢性角化病皮损。

etymology_story.zh: 这个医学名称建立在希腊语 keras（属格 keratos，“角”）及表示过程或状态的 -osis 之上。“角”所代表的坚硬物质被用于描述皮肤角质的形成及其异常增生。
etymology_story.en: This medical term is built on Greek keras, with the stem kerat-, meaning “horn,” and -osis, denoting a process or condition. The idea of hard, hornlike material was applied to the formation and abnormal accumulation of keratin in skin.

morphology_enriched.zh: kerat-（角；角质）＋-osis（过程或状态）→ keratosis（角化病）；复数为 keratoses，形容词为 keratotic（角化的）。同根相关词有 keratin（角蛋白）、keratinization（角化）和 hyperkeratosis（角化过度）；这些相关词并非全部由 keratosis 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: kerat- (horn or keratin) + -osis (process or condition) → keratosis; the plural is keratoses, and the adjective is keratotic. Related root-family words include keratin, keratinization, and hyperkeratosis; these are not all direct derivatives of keratosis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 以下是相关术语，并非完全同义词：hyperkeratosis（角化过度）强调皮肤角质层增厚；keratinization（角化）指形成角质的过程，可为正常过程；callus（胼胝、老茧）通常指摩擦或压力引起的局部皮肤增厚。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: These are related terms rather than exact synonyms: hyperkeratosis emphasizes thickening of the skin's outer keratin layer; keratinization is the process of forming keratin and can be normal; a callus is localized skin thickening usually caused by friction or pressure.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: kerat-＝角质，-osis＝状态：皮肤出现角质增生的状态。
mnemonic_anchor.en: kerat- means hornlike material and -osis means a condition: think of a keratin buildup in the skin.

meaning: 盗贼统治的；统治者以权谋私的

pronunciation.note: 本卡列出一种读法；IPA 为所列词典发音的转写。

forms: 形容词；比较通常用 more / most kleptocratic。
family: kleptocracy 盗贼统治；kleptocrat 以权谋私的统治者

morphology.text: kleptocrat（以权谋私的统治者）+ -ic → kleptocratic（盗贼统治的）；klepto- 表示偷窃，-crat 表示掌权者。

etymology.text: 现代英语用希腊语来源的 klepto- 和表示统治的 -cracy 构成 kleptocracy，再形成 kleptocratic。可把它记成“把公共权力当提款机”的统治方式。

usage_note: 强烈贬义，常用于政治评论；不只表示政府低效，还强调统治者攫取私人利益。

senses.meaning_zh: 盗贼统治的；统治者利用权力侵吞公共财富的
senses.meaning_en: characterized by rulers using political power to steal public wealth
senses.english_definition: A kleptocratic government is one whose rulers use their power to take public money and resources for themselves.
senses.collocation_en: a kleptocratic regime; a kleptocratic elite
senses.collocation_zh: 实行盗贼统治的政权；利用权力侵吞公共财富的精英集团

senses.sentence_zh: 该报告描述了一个将公共资金转入私人账户的盗贼统治政权。

etymology_story.zh: kleptocratic 属于围绕 kleptocracy（盗贼统治）形成的现代英语词族，其成分源于希腊语 kleptēs（窃贼）和 kratos（权力、统治）。原本表示“窃贼掌权”的构词意象发展为对统治者系统性侵吞公共财富的描述。
etymology_story.en: Kleptocratic belongs to the modern English family centered on kleptocracy, using elements from Greek kleptēs, “thief,” and kratos, “power” or “rule.” The underlying image of rule by thieves became a description of rulers systematically appropriating public wealth.

morphology_enriched.zh: klepto-（偷窃）＋-cratic（具有某种统治性质的）→ kleptocratic。核心词族包括 kleptocracy（盗贼统治）、kleptocrat（侵吞公共财富的掌权者）、kleptocratic（盗贼统治的）及副词 kleptocratically（以盗贼统治的方式，较少见）；kleptocracies 和 kleptocrats 分别是两个名词的复数。
morphology_enriched.en: klepto- (stealing) + -cratic (relating to a form of rule) → kleptocratic. The core family includes kleptocracy, kleptocrat, kleptocratic, and the less common adverb kleptocratically; kleptocracies and kleptocrats are the corresponding noun plurals.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: corrupt（腐败的）范围最广，可指受贿及其他滥权行为；predatory（掠夺性的）强调剥削和攫取资源；venal（贪赃的、可被收买的）强调为金钱出卖职权或原则。kleptocratic 特指掌权者以统治体系侵吞公共财富。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Corrupt broadly covers bribery and other abuses of power; predatory emphasizes exploitation and extraction; venal emphasizes willingness to sell influence or principles for money. Kleptocratic specifically describes rulers using a governing system to appropriate public wealth.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: klepto-＝偷，-cratic＝统治：把国库当成私人钱包。
mnemonic_anchor.en: klepto- means stealing and -cratic means ruling: picture rulers treating the treasury as their own wallet.

etymology_story.zh: limeade 是英语以 lime（青柠）和饮料后缀 -ade 构成的词，构词模式与 lemonade 相同。-ade 在这类词中逐渐成为表示加水、通常加糖的水果饮料的构词成分。
etymology_story.en: English formed limeade from lime and the beverage suffix -ade, following the pattern of lemonade. In such formations, -ade became an element naming fruit drinks diluted with water and usually sweetened.

morphology_enriched.zh: lime（青柠）＋-ade（水果饮料）→ limeade；limeades 可表示多杯或多种青柠汁饮料。limeade 没有常用的固定派生词族；lemonade（柠檬汁饮料）和 orangeade（橙汁饮料）是共享后缀的平行构词，并非它的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: lime (the citrus fruit) + -ade (fruit drink) → limeade; limeades can refer to multiple servings or varieties. Limeade has no common established derivative family; lemonade and orangeade are parallel formations sharing its suffix, not derivatives of limeade.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全对应的常用单词近义词。lime drink（青柠饮料）范围更广；lime juice（青柠汁）指果汁本身，不一定经过稀释或加糖；lemonade（柠檬汁饮料）通常使用黄柠檬而非青柠。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact common single-word synonym. Lime drink is broader; lime juice is the juice itself and need not be diluted or sweetened; lemonade usually uses lemons rather than limes.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: lime＋-ade：把 lemonade 里的 lemon 换成 lime，就是青柠饮料。
mnemonic_anchor.en: lime + -ade: replace the lemon in lemonade with lime to remember the drink.

etymology_story.zh: 英语经新拉丁语借入希腊语 lordōsis，其相关形容词 lordos 有“向后弯的”之意，描述身体后仰、腰背凹入的形态。现代解剖学用 lordosis 表示颈椎或腰椎的前凸曲线，临床语境中也常用来指这种曲线过度增大。
etymology_story.en: English received lordosis through New Latin from Greek lordōsis, related to lordos, meaning “bent backward,” describing a backward-bent, hollow-backed posture. Modern anatomy uses lordosis for the cervical or lumbar inward curve, while clinical usage also applies it to an excessive curve.

morphology_enriched.zh: lord-（弯曲，见于医学词汇）＋-osis（状态）→ lordosis；这里的 lord- 与英语 lord（领主）无关。词族包括复数 lordoses、形容词 lordotic（脊柱前凸的）、hyperlordosis（脊柱前凸过度）和 hypolordosis（脊柱前凸减小）。
morphology_enriched.en: lord- (bending, in medical vocabulary) + -osis (condition) → lordosis; this lord- is unrelated to English lord. The family includes the plural lordoses, the adjective lordotic, hyperlordosis for excessive lordosis, and hypolordosis for reduced lordosis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: lumbar curvature（腰椎曲度）是更宽泛的描述，不一定表示异常；hyperlordosis（脊柱前凸过度）明确表示曲度过大；swayback（凹背、塌腰）是描述明显腰背凹曲的通俗词，精确程度低于医学术语。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lumbar curvature is a broader description and does not necessarily indicate an abnormality; hyperlordosis explicitly means an excessive curve; swayback is an informal description of a pronounced hollow in the lower back and is less precise than the medical terminology.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 侧看腰背：背面向内凹，腰椎向前凸；曲度过大就是前凸过度。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the lower back from the side: the back hollows inward as the lumbar spine curves forward; an exaggerated curve is hyperlordosis.

morphology.text: malleol-（malleolus 去掉 -us 后的词干）+ -ar（……的）→ malleolar（踝的）。看到 malleolar fracture，就可联系踝部骨突的骨折。

etymology.text: 来自拉丁语 malleolus，是 malleus“锤”的指小形式。把踝旁凸起想成一把小锤，可帮助记忆外形。

usage_note: 常见 medial malleolus（内踝）和 lateral malleolus（外踝）；本词指骨性部位，不泛指整只脚。

senses.meaning_en: A bony projection at the ankle.
senses.english_definition: A malleolus is one of the bony projections at the lower end of the tibia or fibula, around the ankle joint.
senses.collocation_zh: 内踝；外踝
senses.sentence_en: The X-ray showed a fracture of the lateral malleolus.
senses.sentence_zh: X 光片显示外踝骨折。

etymology_story.zh: 来自拉丁语 malleolus，意为“小锤”，是 malleus“锤”的指小形式。解剖学用这个名称指踝部形似小锤的骨性突起。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin malleolus, meaning “little hammer,” a diminutive of malleus, “hammer.” Anatomists applied the name to the hammer-like bony projections at the ankle.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常作为完整的解剖学词项学习；构词词干为 malleol-，派生形容词时以 -ar 替换词尾 -us：malleolar（踝的）。复数为 malleoli；相关派生词包括 unimalleolar（单踝的）、bimalleolar（双踝的）、trimalleolar（三踝的）和 supramalleolar（踝上的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, malleolus is normally learned as a whole anatomical term. Its combining stem is malleol-; replacing the ending -us with -ar gives malleolar, “relating to a malleolus.” The plural is malleoli. Related derivatives include unimalleolar, bimalleolar, trimalleolar, and supramalleolar.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ankle bone（踝骨）是较通俗但不够精确的说法；bony prominence（骨性突起）是范围更广的描述。malleolus 特指胫骨或腓骨下端的踝部骨突，并不表示整个踝关节。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ankle bone is a familiar but less precise expression; bony prominence is a broader descriptive term. Malleolus specifically identifies an ankle projection of the tibia or fibula, rather than the entire ankle joint.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: malleolus＝“小锤”：把踝旁突出的骨头想成小锤头。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Malleolus means “little hammer”: picture the ankle's projecting bone as a small hammerhead.

morphology.text: match（慢燃火绳）+ lock（枪机）→ matchlock（火绳枪或其点火装置）；本课教整支枪的意思。

etymology.text: 英语把表示火绳的 match 和表示枪机的 lock 合成，17世纪已有记录。记住“用火绳点火的枪”即可。

usage_note: 历史用语，也能指火绳点火机构；这里的 match 不是比赛，lock 不是门锁。

senses.meaning_zh: 火绳枪
senses.meaning_en: An early firearm fired using a burning match cord.
senses.english_definition: A matchlock is an early type of gun that uses a slowly burning cord to ignite the gunpowder.
senses.collocation_zh: 火绳滑膛枪；火绳钩铳

senses.sentence_zh: 那名士兵携带着一支火绳枪和一段燃烧的火绳。

senses.meaning_zh: 火绳点火枪机
senses.meaning_en: A firearm mechanism that brings a burning cord into contact with priming powder.
senses.english_definition: A matchlock is a gun mechanism that lowers a burning cord onto a small charge of gunpowder to fire the weapon.
senses.collocation_zh: 火绳枪机；火绳点火

senses.sentence_zh: 火绳枪机将灼燃的火绳降入火药池。

etymology_story.zh: 由 match“慢燃火绳”和 lock“枪机”复合而成；这里的 match 不是现代常见的火柴。该名称既指用火绳引燃火药的枪机，也由此指装有这种枪机的整支枪。
etymology_story.en: Matchlock combines match, meaning a slow-burning ignition cord, with lock, meaning a firearm's firing mechanism. The name denotes both the mechanism itself and, by extension, a gun fitted with it.

morphology_enriched.zh: match（慢燃火绳）+ lock（枪机）→ matchlock；复数为 matchlocks。没有常用的词缀派生词；matchlock musket 等表达中的 matchlock 是名词作定语，不构成独立的常用形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Match, “slow-burning cord,” + lock, “firing mechanism,” forms matchlock; its plural is matchlocks. There are no common affix-derived forms. In expressions such as matchlock musket, matchlock functions as a noun modifier rather than a separate common adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: musket（滑膛长枪）和 arquebus（早期长管火枪，常译“钩铳”）是相关枪械名称，但并非严格同义词：matchlock 强调点火方式，musket 和 arquebus 主要区分枪械类型。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Musket and arquebus are related firearm terms rather than exact synonyms. Matchlock identifies the ignition system, whereas musket and arquebus primarily identify types of firearm.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 火绳 match + 枪机 lock＝靠火绳点火的枪机或枪。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A match cord meets a gun's lock: the mechanism, or gun, fires by burning cord.

senses.meaning_zh: 无酵饼；尤指犹太逾越节食用的无酵薄饼
senses.meaning_en: Unleavened bread eaten especially during the Jewish festival of Passover.
senses.english_definition: Matzah is a flat bread made without yeast that Jewish people eat especially during Passover.
senses.collocation_zh: 吃无酵饼；无酵饼粉
senses.sentence_en: During Passover, the family eats matzah instead of ordinary bread.
senses.sentence_zh: 逾越节期间，这家人吃无酵饼来代替普通面包。

etymology_story.zh: 借自希伯来语 maṣṣāh，意为“无酵饼”。英语保留了它与犹太逾越节的联系；按照《出埃及记》的叙述，无酵饼使人想起以色列人匆忙离开埃及时来不及发酵的面团。
etymology_story.en: Matzah comes from Hebrew maṣṣāh, meaning “unleavened bread.” English preserves its association with Passover and the biblical account of the Israelites leaving Egypt before their dough had time to rise.

morphology_enriched.zh: matzah 是借入的完整词项，现代英语中不再拆分为词根和词缀。常见拼写变体包括 matza、matzo 和 matzoh；复数可用 matzahs、matzot 或 matzoth，matzo 的常见英语复数为 matzos。matzah meal（无酵饼粉）和 matzah ball（无酵饼粉丸子）是常见复合表达。
morphology_enriched.en: Matzah is a borrowed lexical base with no productive internal root-and-affix division in English. Common spelling variants include matza, matzo, and matzoh. Plurals include matzahs, matzot, and matzoth; matzos is a common English plural of matzo. Frequent compounds include matzah meal and matzah ball.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: matzo 是同一词的常见拼写变体，意义相同；unleavened bread（无酵饼）是更宽泛的类别名称，不一定具有犹太逾越节的文化背景。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Matzo is a common spelling variant with the same meaning. Unleavened bread names the broader category and does not necessarily carry the Jewish or Passover association.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 matzah 固定在逾越节餐桌上：不发酵的薄饼。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Place matzah on the Passover table: flat bread made without leavening.

senses.meaning_zh: 大型综合设施；尤指大型多厅电影院
senses.meaning_en: A very large complex, especially a cinema with many separate screens.
senses.english_definition: A megaplex is a very large building or group of buildings, especially a cinema containing many separate screening rooms.
senses.collocation_zh: 大型多厅电影院；郊区大型多厅电影院
senses.sentence_en: We watched the film at a megaplex on the edge of town.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们在城郊的一家大型多厅电影院看了这部电影。

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代英语参照 multiplex“多厅电影院”等词形成的名称，将 mega-“巨大”与 -plex 结合。它把“多个影厅”的概念进一步扩展为规模特别大的影院综合体，也可用于其他巨型综合设施。
etymology_story.en: Megaplex is a modern English formation combining mega-, “very large,” with -plex on the model of multiplex. It extends the idea of multiple screening rooms to an especially large cinema complex and can also describe other enormous complexes.

morphology_enriched.zh: mega-（巨大）+ -plex（表示多单元综合设施的构词成分）→ megaplex；复数为 megaplexes。没有常见的词缀派生词；multiplex（多厅电影院）和 cineplex（多厅影院）是相关构词形式，并非由 megaplex 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Mega-, “very large,” + -plex, a formative used for multi-unit complexes, gives megaplex; the plural is megaplexes. There are no common affix-derived forms. Multiplex and cineplex are related formations, not derivatives of megaplex.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: multiplex（多厅电影院）强调有多个影厅；cineplex（多厅影院）意义相近；cinema complex（影院综合体）是较中性的描述。megaplex 进一步强调规模很大，但这些词之间没有普遍适用的严格影厅数量界线。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Multiplex emphasizes several screening rooms; cineplex has a similar meaning; cinema complex is a neutral descriptive expression. Megaplex adds an emphasis on very large scale, without a universally fixed screen-count boundary.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: mega＝巨大；-plex＝多单元综合体：许多影厅组成的巨型影院。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Mega means huge; -plex suggests a complex: picture a giant cinema packed with screening rooms.

senses.meaning_zh: 超材料；通过人工设计结构获得特殊性质的材料
senses.meaning_en: An engineered material whose designed structure produces unusual physical properties.
senses.english_definition: A metamaterial is a material whose specially designed internal structure gives it properties that its constituent substances do not normally have on their own.
senses.collocation_zh: 电磁超材料；声学超材料
senses.sentence_en: The researchers designed an acoustic metamaterial that blocks sound within a specific frequency range.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员设计了一种能够阻挡特定频率范围内声音的声学超材料。

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代科学英语将希腊语来源的 meta-“超越”与 material“材料”结合形成的术语。名称体现了这样的思路：通过设计材料的内部结构，使其呈现普通组成物质单独使用时不具备的性质。
etymology_story.en: Metamaterial is a modern scientific term combining the Greek-derived prefix meta-, “beyond,” with material. The name reflects the idea of engineering internal structures to obtain properties beyond those normally supplied by the constituent substances alone.

morphology_enriched.zh: meta-（超越）+ material（材料）→ metamaterial；复数为 metamaterials。常见相关表达包括 metamaterial-based（基于超材料的）和 metamaterial-inspired（受超材料启发的）。metasurface（超表面）是相关技术术语，通常指具有相应结构设计原理的薄层或表面，并非 metamaterial 的词缀派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Meta-, “beyond,” + material forms metamaterial; its plural is metamaterials. Common related formations include metamaterial-based and metamaterial-inspired. Metasurface is a related technical term for a thin layer or surface using corresponding structural design principles, rather than an affix-derived form of metamaterial.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: engineered material（工程设计材料）是更宽泛的名称；composite material（复合材料）强调由多种组分构成，也不必然是超材料。metamaterial 特别强调人工设计的结构如何产生特殊的整体物理响应。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Engineered material is a broader category. Composite material emphasizes multiple constituents and does not necessarily describe a metamaterial. Metamaterial specifically emphasizes how designed structure produces an unusual overall physical response.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: meta＝超越：靠结构设计，让材料表现超出组成物质本身。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Meta means beyond: designed structure takes a material's behavior beyond that of its ingredients alone.

etymology_story.zh: microbus 是20世纪出现的英语复合词，由表示“小型”的 micro- 和 bus“公共汽车”构成。micro- 源自希腊语 mikros“小”，而 bus 是 omnibus 的缩略形式；omnibus 原为拉丁语，意为“供所有人使用”。
etymology_story.en: Microbus is a twentieth-century English formation combining micro-, meaning 'small', with bus. Micro- comes from Greek mikros, 'small', while bus is shortened from omnibus, a Latin form meaning 'for everyone'.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：micro-（小型）+ bus（客车）→ microbus（小型客车）。复数为 microbuses，属于屈折变化；本词没有常用的直接派生词。相关复合词有 minibus（小型公共汽车）和 microvan（微型厢式车），但它们不是 microbus 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: micro- ('small') + bus → microbus. The plural microbuses is an inflected form; the word has no established common direct derivatives. Related compounds include minibus and microvan, but neither is derived from microbus.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: minibus（小型公共汽车）是最接近的近义词，通常强调小型集体客运车辆；passenger van（客运厢式车）强调厢式车的乘客配置；shuttle bus（接驳车）强调固定地点之间的接送用途，不限定车辆大小。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Minibus is the closest synonym and usually denotes a small vehicle for group transport; passenger van emphasizes a van equipped for passengers; shuttle bus describes transport between particular places, regardless of vehicle size.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: micro- 表示“小”：把 bus 缩小，就是 microbus。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Micro- means 'small': picture a bus scaled down into a microbus.

senses.meaning_zh: 传教学；研究基督教传教使命、历史及实践的学科

etymology_story.zh: missiology 形成于19世纪，由拉丁语 missio“派遣；使命”的词干形式 missi- 与表示“研究学科”的 -ology 结合而成。拉丁语 missio 源自动词 mittere“派遣”，该词在这里专指对基督教传教使命和活动的系统研究。
etymology_story.en: Missiology arose in the nineteenth century from missi-, based on Latin missio, 'a sending' or 'mission', and -ology, denoting a field of study. Missio derives from mittere, 'to send', and the English term specifically developed as the name for the systematic study of Christian mission.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词可分析为 missi-（传教使命）+ -ology（研究学科）→ missiology；不宜简单理解为把英语 mission 的词尾任意删去。主要词族：missiologist（传教学研究者）、missiological（传教学的）、missiologically（从传教学角度）；相关词有 mission（使命；传教）和 missionary（传教士；传教的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: missi- ('mission') + -ology ('field of study') → missiology; this is not simply an arbitrary shortening of the English word mission. The principal derivatives are missiologist, missiological, and missiologically. Related words include mission and missionary.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: mission studies（传教研究）是最接近的对应表达；theology（神学）涵盖对宗教信仰和教义的更广泛研究；evangelism（福音传播）指传播基督教信仰的活动本身，通常不指研究该活动的学科。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mission studies is the closest equivalent; theology covers the broader study of religious belief and doctrine; evangelism normally means the activity of spreading the Christian faith rather than the academic study of that activity.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: missi- 是“派出去传教”，-ology 是“研究”：研究传教的学问。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect missi- with being sent on a mission and -ology with study: the study of Christian mission.

senses.meaning_zh: 黏液纤毛的；涉及黏液与纤毛共同作用的
senses.meaning_en: relating to mucus and cilia acting together, especially in the airways
senses.english_definition: A mucociliary process involves mucus and tiny moving hairs called cilia working together, especially to remove material from the airways.
senses.collocation_zh: 黏液纤毛清除；黏液纤毛转运
senses.sentence_en: The researchers measured mucociliary clearance in the participants.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员测量了参与者的黏液纤毛清除功能。

etymology_story.zh: mucociliary 是现代医学构词，由源自拉丁语 mucus“黏液”的 muco- 与 ciliary“纤毛的”结合而成。ciliary 所联系的拉丁语 cilium 原指“眼睑”，后与“睫毛”联系起来，并在科学术语中用于指细胞表面的毛状结构。
etymology_story.en: Mucociliary is a modern medical formation combining muco-, from Latin mucus, with ciliary. The Latin source cilium originally meant 'eyelid', became associated with an eyelash, and was adopted in scientific terminology for a hairlike cellular structure.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：muco-（黏液）+ ciliary（纤毛的）→ mucociliary；ciliary 可进一步分析为 cili-（纤毛）+ -ary（……的）。本词没有常用的直接派生词。相关词族包括 mucus（黏液）、mucous（黏液的）、mucoid（黏液样的），以及 cilium（单根纤毛）、cilia（纤毛的复数）、ciliary（纤毛的）和 ciliated（有纤毛的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: muco- ('mucus') + ciliary → mucociliary; ciliary can be further analyzed as cili- ('cilium') + -ary ('relating to'). There are no common established direct derivatives. Related families include mucus, mucous, and mucoid, and cilium, its plural cilia, ciliary, and ciliated.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 本词没有可普遍替换的常用单词近义词。相关表达中，ciliary（纤毛的）只涉及纤毛，mucous（黏液的）只涉及黏液；mucus-and-cilia-related（与黏液及纤毛有关的）可作解释性改写，但不是常用专业术语。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common single-word synonym that is generally interchangeable with mucociliary. Ciliary concerns cilia alone, while mucous concerns mucus; mucus-and-cilia-related is an explanatory paraphrase rather than an established technical equivalent.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 黏液黏住颗粒，纤毛推动黏液：两者合作就是 mucociliary。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Mucus traps particles; cilia move the mucus: their teamwork is mucociliary.

etymology_story.zh: multihospital 是现代英语将 multi-“多个”与 hospital“医院”组合而成的形容词，用于描述由多家医院构成的体系或共同参与的活动。multi- 源自拉丁语 multus“多”，hospital 则经法语追溯至中世纪拉丁语 hospitale，原指接待宾客、旅人或有需要者的场所。
etymology_story.en: Multihospital is a modern English formation combining multi-, 'many', with hospital to describe systems or activities involving several hospitals. Multi- comes from Latin multus, while hospital came through French from medieval Latin hospitale, a place receiving guests, travelers, or people in need.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：multi-（多个）+ hospital（医院）→ multihospital；也写作 multi-hospital。该形容词通常用于名词前，没有常用的直接派生名词或副词。hospital 的相关词族包括 hospitalize／hospitalise（使住院）和 hospitalization／hospitalisation（住院；收治入院），这些词并非由 multihospital 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: multi- ('many') + hospital → multihospital, also written multi-hospital. It is normally used before a noun and has no common established directly derived noun or adverb. The hospital family includes hospitalize/hospitalise and hospitalization/hospitalisation; these are not derivatives of multihospital.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: interhospital（医院间的）强调医院之间的联系、转运或比较；multisite（多地点的）强调多个地点，不保证涉及不同医院；multi-institutional（多机构的）强调多个机构参与，范围不限于医院。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Interhospital emphasizes relationships, transfers, or comparisons between hospitals; multisite emphasizes multiple locations, which may belong to one hospital; multi-institutional involves several institutions, which need not all be hospitals.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: multi- 是“多个”：把多家 hospital 放进同一体系或活动。

etymology_story.en: Multilane combines Latin-derived multi-, 'many', with English lane to describe the number of traffic lanes on a road. Lane comes from Old English lanu, 'a narrow passage', and later came to denote a marked channel for vehicles.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：multi-（多个）+ lane（车道）→ multilane；也写作 multi-lane。本词没有常用的直接派生名词或副词。相关构词包括 single-lane（单车道的）、two-lane（双车道的）和 three-lane（三车道的）；这些是使用 lane 构成的平行复合词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: multi- ('many') + lane → multilane, also written multi-lane. There are no common established directly derived nouns or adverbs. Related formations include single-lane, two-lane, and three-lane; these are parallel compounds built with lane.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: multiple-lane（多车道的）与 multilane 基本同义；wide（宽阔的）描述道路宽度，并不说明车道数量；divided（分隔式的）强调相反行驶方向之间有中央隔离设施，与是否多车道是不同属性。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Multiple-lane is essentially equivalent to multilane; wide describes road width without specifying lane count; divided describes a road with a median or barrier separating opposing traffic, a different property from having multiple lanes.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 nano- 与 science 组合而成：nano- 最终源于希腊语 nanos，意为“侏儒”，作为国际单位制前缀表示十亿分之一。随着纳米尺度研究的发展，这一组合成为相关科学领域的名称。
etymology_story.en: The word combines nano- with science: nano- ultimately comes from Greek nanos, meaning 'dwarf,' and denotes one billionth as an SI prefix. As research at the nanoscale developed, the combination became the name of the scientific field.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：nano-（纳米尺度）+ science（科学）。本词通常为不可数名词，没有常用的独立派生形式；相关词族包括 nanoscientist（纳米科学家）、nanoscientific（纳米科学的）。nanoscale（纳米尺度）和 nanotechnology（纳米技术）是共享 nano- 的相关构词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: nano- ('at the nanoscale') + science. The noun is normally uncountable and has no widely used direct derivatives; related family members include nanoscientist and nanoscientific. Nanoscale and nanotechnology are related formations sharing nano-.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全对应的常用近义词。nanotechnology（纳米技术）侧重实际应用；nanoscale science（纳米尺度科学）是接近同义的描述；nanophysics（纳米物理学）仅指其中的物理学分支。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday synonym. Nanotechnology emphasizes practical applications; nanoscale science is a near-equivalent description; nanophysics refers specifically to the physics branch of the field.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: nano- 表示“十亿分之一”：把科学的观察尺度缩到纳米。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Nano- means 'one billionth': shrink the scale of scientific observation to nanometers.

etymology_story.zh: 该词属于以希腊语词素构成的现代医学词汇：nephros 意为“肾”，而 -ectomy 源于表示“切除”的希腊语 ektomē。其名称直接说明了接受切除手术的器官。
etymology_story.en: The term belongs to modern medical vocabulary formed from Greek elements: nephros means 'kidney,' and -ectomy comes from Greek ektomē, meaning 'excision.' The name directly identifies the organ involved in the removal procedure.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：nephr-（肾）+ -ectomy（手术切除）；结合形式 nephr/o 的连接元音 o 在元音开头的后缀前省略。复数为 nephrectomies；派生形式包括 nephrectomize（施行肾切除术）、nephrectomized（已接受肾切除术的）、nephrectomization（肾切除）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: nephr- ('kidney') + -ectomy ('surgical removal'); the linking vowel o in nephr/o is omitted before the vowel-initial suffix. The plural is nephrectomies; derivatives include nephrectomize, nephrectomized, and nephrectomization.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: kidney removal（肾切除）是通俗说法；renal excision（肾切除）是描述性医学表达；nephrotomy（肾切开术）仅表示切开肾脏，并非切除，不能作同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Kidney removal is the plain-language equivalent; renal excision is a descriptive medical expression; nephrotomy means making an incision into a kidney, so it is not a synonym for removal.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: nephr- 锁定“肾”，-ectomy 锁定“切除”：合起来就是肾切除术。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Nephr- identifies the kidney; -ectomy identifies surgical removal: together, kidney-removal surgery.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：net（网络）+ etiquette（礼仪）→ netiquette，属于截短拼合，不是词根加后缀。通常为不可数名词，没有常用的标准派生词；词族联系包括 net、network、etiquette，释义性表达为 online etiquette（网络礼仪）。

It is normally uncountable and has no common standard derivatives; family connections include net, network, and etiquette, with online etiquette as an explanatory equivalent.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 neuro- 与 behavioral 组合而成；neuro- 最终源于希腊语 neuron，原指“筋腱；神经”。随着神经科学和行为研究的发展，这一组合被用于描述神经功能与行为之间的联系。

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：neuro-（神经）+ behavior（行为）+ -al（……的）→ neurobehavioral；英式拼写为 neurobehavioural。直接派生副词为 neurobehaviorally／neurobehaviourally；相关词族包括 behavior／behaviour、behavioral／behavioural、behaviorally／behaviourally。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: neuro- ('neural') + behavior + -al ('relating to') → neurobehavioral; the British spelling is neurobehavioural. synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact common adjectival synonym. etymology_story.zh: 英语 nitrile 来自19世纪的德语化学名称 Nitril，其命名与表示氮的 nitr- 词干有关。后来，该词也成为 nitrile rubber（丁腈橡胶）的简称，并常见于手套等产品名称中。
etymology_story.en: English nitrile comes from the nineteenth-century German chemical name Nitril, formed using the nitrogen-related stem nitr-. The word later also became a shortened form of nitrile rubber and is common in product names such as those for gloves.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜将 nitrile 作为整体化学名称学习，可辨认出与氮有关的 nitr-，但不宜把 -ile 当作可自由套用的现代构词后缀。化合物义的复数为 nitriles，材料义通常不可数；相关化学名称包括 acetonitrile（乙腈）、acrylonitrile（丙烯腈）、benzonitrile（苯甲腈），材料名称为 nitrile rubber（丁腈橡胶）。nitrile gloves 中的 nitrile 是名词作定语。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, nitrile is best learned as a whole chemical name: the nitrogen-related stem nitr- is recognizable, but -ile should not be treated as a freely productive modern suffix. The compound sense has the plural nitriles, while the material sense is normally uncountable; related chemical names include acetonitrile, acrylonitrile, and benzonitrile, alongside the material name nitrile rubber. In nitrile gloves, nitrile is an attributive noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有适用于全部义项的同义词。organic cyanide（有机氰化物）在特定命名语境中可指腈，但 cyanide（氰化物）本身范围更广，不能直接替换；nitrile rubber（丁腈橡胶）对应材料义；NBR（丁腈橡胶的常用缩写）指通常由丙烯腈与丁二烯共聚形成的橡胶。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no synonym covering every sense. Organic cyanide can denote a nitrile in particular naming contexts, but cyanide alone is broader and is not interchangeable; nitrile rubber corresponds to the material sense; NBR is the common abbreviation for the rubber typically made by copolymerizing acrylonitrile and butadiene.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 认准 C≡N 这根“三键”：它锁定腈的结构；丁腈手套则连接到橡胶材料义。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the C≡N triple bond to identify the chemical class; connect nitrile gloves with the rubber-material sense.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 nopal 经墨西哥西班牙语借自纳瓦特尔语 nopalli，原指当地的掌状仙人掌。英语保留了植物名称，也用它指作为蔬菜食用的嫩茎片。[词源资料](https://www.etymonline.com/word/nopal)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed nopal through Mexican Spanish from Nahuatl nopalli, a name for a prickly pear cactus. The borrowed plant name is also used for its edible young pads. [Etymology reference](https://www.etymonline.com/word/nopal)

morphology_enriched.zh: nopal 是整体借入的词，现代英语中不宜进一步拆成词根与词缀。词形及相关形式包括 nopals／nopales（复数）、nopalito／nopalitos（借自西班牙语，指食用嫩茎片）；罕见派生词 nopalry = nopal + -ry，指培育仙人掌以饲养胭脂虫的种植园。
morphology_enriched.en: Nopal is a borrowed base without a productive internal root-and-affix division in modern English. Forms and related borrowings include the plurals nopals and nopales, and nopalito/nopalitos, referring to edible young pads; the rare derivative nopalry consists of nopal + -ry and denotes a cactus plantation maintained for cochineal insects.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: prickly pear（掌状仙人掌）是更通行的名称，也可指其果实；cactus pad（仙人掌茎片）明确指扁平茎片，但未必可食用；nopalito（食用嫩茎片）尤其突出幼嫩、适合烹饪的部位。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Prickly pear is the more familiar plant name and can also denote its fruit; cactus pad specifically identifies a flattened stem without necessarily implying edibility; nopalito particularly suggests a tender young pad used in cooking.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a Mexican cactus: the whole plant in the field, its young pads on the plate.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 octopod 源自新拉丁语分类名称 Octopoda，最终可追溯到希腊语 oktō“八”和 pous（词干 pod-）“足”。原本的“八足”含义在现代动物学中对应这类动物的八条腕。[词源与词性资料](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/octopod)
etymology_story.en: Octopod comes from the New Latin taxonomic name Octopoda, ultimately based on Greek oktō, meaning eight, and pous, with the stem pod-, meaning foot. Its literal eight-footed description corresponds to the eight arms recognized in modern zoology. [Etymology and word classes](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/octopod)

morphology_enriched.zh: octo-（八）+ -pod（足、肢体）→ octopod；复数为 octopods。相关词族包括 octopodan（八腕目的；八腕目动物）、octopodous（八足的；八腕的）和分类名称 Octopoda（八腕目）；octopus（章鱼）是同源相关词。
morphology_enriched.en: Octo- meaning eight + -pod meaning foot or limb forms octopod; its plural is octopods. Related family members include octopodan, an adjective or noun referring to Octopoda, octopodous, meaning eight-footed or eight-armed, and the taxonomic name Octopoda; octopus is a related formation from the same Greek elements.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: octopus（章鱼）是日常用语，octopod 更强调动物分类；cephalopod（头足类动物）范围更广，还包括鱿鱼和乌贼；octopodan（八腕目的；八腕目动物）与 octopod 在分类学语境中近义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Octopus is the everyday term, whereas octopod emphasizes zoological classification; cephalopod is broader and also includes squid and cuttlefish; octopodan is a close taxonomic alternative to octopod as either an adjective or a noun.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: octo- 八 + -pod 足：古人叫“八足”，动物学称“八腕”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Octo- gives eight and -pod gives feet: remember the historical eight feet as the animal's eight arms.

etymology.text: 由希腊语来源的 odynē“疼痛”和表示进食、吞咽的 -phagia 构成医学名称。把“痛”与“吞咽”连起来即可记住。

etymology_story.zh: odynophagia 是由希腊语来源的医学构词成分组成的术语：odynē 表示“疼痛”，phagein 表示“吃”。这一组合在医学中专指吞咽时的疼痛。[医学词源资料](https://www.academie-medecine.fr/le-dictionnaire/index.php?q=odynophagie)
etymology_story.en: Odynophagia is a medical formation using elements derived from Greek odynē, meaning pain, and phagein, meaning to eat. The combination specifically denotes pain during swallowing. [Medical etymology reference](https://www.academie-medecine.fr/le-dictionnaire/index.php?q=odynophagie)

morphology_enriched.zh: odyno-（疼痛）+ -phagia（进食、吞咽）→ odynophagia（吞咽痛）；更细可分析为 odyn- + 连接元音 -o- + phag- + 名词后缀 -ia。相关派生形容词为 odynophagic（吞咽痛的）；通常没有日常使用的动词或副词形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Odyno- meaning pain + -phagia meaning eating or swallowing forms odynophagia; a finer analysis is odyn- + linking -o- + phag- + the noun suffix -ia. The related adjective is odynophagic, meaning involving painful swallowing; there are no everyday verb or adverb forms.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: painful swallowing（吞咽疼痛）是最自然的普通表达；painful deglutition（吞咽疼痛）含义相同，但更正式、更专业。dysphagia（吞咽困难）是相关症状，强调吞咽不畅，不能与吞咽痛等同。[术语辨析资料](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/symptoms/odynophagia-painful-swallowing)
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Painful swallowing is the clearest everyday equivalent; painful deglutition has the same meaning in a more formal medical register. Dysphagia is a related symptom involving difficulty swallowing and is not an interchangeable synonym. [Terminology distinction](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/symptoms/odynophagia-painful-swallowing)

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 疼痛 odyno- + 吞咽 -phagia：一吞就痛。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pain plus swallowing: it hurts to swallow.

etymology_story.zh: orthomolecular 由莱纳斯·鲍林于20世纪60年代创用，将希腊语来源、表示“正确、适当”的 ortho- 与 molecular“分子的”结合起来。名称表达了他通过调节体内已有物质的浓度来提供适当分子环境的构想。[词源资料](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/orthomolecular)
etymology_story.en: Linus Pauling coined orthomolecular in the 1960s by combining Greek-derived ortho-, meaning correct or appropriate, with molecular. The name expressed his proposal to provide an appropriate molecular environment by adjusting concentrations of substances already present in the body. [Etymology reference](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/orthomolecular)

morphology_enriched.zh: ortho-（正确、适当）+ molecular（分子的）→ orthomolecular；molecular 属于 molecule（分子）的形容词词族。相关形式包括 molecule（分子）、molecular（分子的）、molecularly（在分子层面上）及较少见的 orthomolecularly（按正分子医学方式）；orthomolecular medicine 和 orthomolecular therapy 是常见术语组合。
morphology_enriched.en: Ortho- meaning correct or appropriate + molecular forms orthomolecular; molecular belongs to the adjective family of molecule. Related forms include molecule, molecular, molecularly, and the less frequent orthomolecularly, meaning in an orthomolecular manner; orthomolecular medicine and orthomolecular therapy are established combinations.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全对应的常用单词近义词。nutritional（营养的）范围更广；megavitamin（大剂量维生素的）强调维生素用量，是部分正分子实践的特点；biochemical（生物化学的）涉及生物体内化学过程，本身不表示认同正分子疗法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday single-word synonym. Nutritional is broader; megavitamin emphasizes large vitamin doses, a feature of some orthomolecular practices; biochemical concerns chemical processes in living organisms and does not itself imply an orthomolecular approach.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ortho- 适当 + molecular 分子的：记住“调到所主张的适当分子水平”这一理念。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Appropriate plus molecular: remember the proposed aim of adjusting the body's molecular levels.

etymology_story.zh: osteoclastic 是在 osteoclast“破骨细胞”上加形容词后缀 -ic 构成的；其词源成分来自希腊语 osteon“骨”和表示“打碎”的词根。字面的“破骨”在现代生物学中指细胞分解并吸收骨组织的作用。[词源资料](https://dicciomed.usal.es/palabra/osteoclasto)
etymology_story.en: Osteoclastic is formed by adding the adjective suffix -ic to osteoclast, whose elements derive from Greek osteon, meaning bone, and a root meaning to break. The literal bone-breaking description refers in modern biology to cellular breakdown and resorption of bone tissue. [Etymology reference](https://dicciomed.usal.es/palabra/osteoclasto)

morphology_enriched.zh: osteoclast（破骨细胞）+ -ic（……的）→ osteoclastic；内部结构为 osteo-（骨）+ -clast（破坏者）。主要相关词族包括 osteoclasts（复数）、preosteoclast（破骨细胞前体）、osteoclastogenesis（破骨细胞生成）、osteoclastogenic（促进破骨细胞生成的）和 osteoclastoma（骨巨细胞瘤的传统名称）；osteoclasis／osteoclasia（外科折骨术）属于相关构词词族，不能等同于细胞性骨吸收。
morphology_enriched.en: Osteoclast + the adjective suffix -ic forms osteoclastic; internally, osteoclast contains osteo- meaning bone and -clast meaning breaker. Principal related forms include osteoclasts, preosteoclast for a precursor cell, osteoclastogenesis for osteoclast formation, osteoclastogenic for promoting that formation, and osteoclastoma, a traditional name for a giant cell tumor of bone; osteoclasis/osteoclasia refers to surgical breaking of bone rather than cellular bone resorption.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bone-resorbing（吸收骨组织的）强调功能，最接近常见生物学含义；bone-resorptive（骨吸收的）强调骨吸收过程或性质；osteolytic（骨溶解性的）强调骨组织被破坏或丢失，范围更广，不必明确指出破骨细胞。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bone-resorbing emphasizes function and is closest to the usual biological meaning; bone-resorptive emphasizes the process or property of bone resorption; osteolytic more broadly describes bone destruction or loss without necessarily identifying osteoclasts.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: osteo- 骨 + -clast 拆解者 + -ic 的：负责“拆旧骨”的细胞及其活动。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bone plus breaker plus -ic: think of the cells that dismantle old bone and the activity they perform.

etymology_story.zh: 由希腊语来源的 oto-（耳）和 -scope（观察器械）组合而成，字面意思是“观察耳部的器械”。这个名称体现了医学仪器按所检查部位命名的传统。
etymology_story.en: The word combines Greek-derived oto-, meaning 'ear,' with -scope, meaning 'an instrument for viewing.' Its literal meaning, 'an instrument for viewing the ear,' reflects the medical practice of naming instruments after the body parts they examine.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：oto-（耳）+ -scope（观察器械）→ otoscope（耳镜）。相关词族：otoscopes（复数）、otoscopy（耳镜检查法）、otoscopic（耳镜检查的）、otoscopically（通过耳镜检查）。这些词通过 -scope、-scopy 和 -scopic 等构词形式相互联系。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: oto- ('ear') + -scope ('viewing instrument') → otoscope. Related forms include otoscopes (plural), otoscopy (examination with an otoscope), otoscopic (relating to such examination), and otoscopically (by means of such examination), using the related combining forms -scope, -scopy, and -scopic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: auriscope（耳镜）是同义名称；ear scope（耳部观察镜）较通俗；ear speculum（耳窥器）通常指撑开耳道入口的漏斗状部件或器械，不一定包含耳镜的照明和放大装置。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Auriscope is an alternative name for the same instrument; ear scope is a less technical expression. An ear speculum usually refers to the funnel-shaped component or instrument used to open the ear canal entrance and does not necessarily include illumination or magnification.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Oto- means 'ear' and -scope means 'viewer': an otoscope lets you look inside an ear.

etymology_story.zh: 来自拉丁语 pānicula，意为“簇、花簇”，是 pānus 的指小形式。英语将其用于植物学，指主轴多次分枝形成的花序；名称虽译作“圆锥花序”，实际外形不一定严格呈圆锥形。
etymology_story.en: Panicle comes from Latin pānicula, meaning 'a tuft or flower cluster,' a diminutive of pānus. English adopted it as a botanical term for a branching inflorescence, whose overall shape need not be strictly conical.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 panicle 视为完整词干，不拆成 pan + -icle。相关词族：panicles（复数）、panicled（具圆锥花序的；在词尾 e 后加 -d）、paniculate（圆锥花序状的；使用词干 panicul-）、paniculately（呈圆锥花序状地）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, panicle is normally treated as a whole stem, rather than as pan + -icle. Related forms include panicles (plural), panicled ('bearing panicles,' formed by adding -d after the final e), paniculate ('arranged in panicles,' using the stem panicul-), and paniculately ('in a paniculate arrangement').

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: inflorescence（花序）是上位词，涵盖各种花的排列结构；raceme（总状花序）的有梗花直接着生于不分枝的主轴；spike（穗状花序）的花通常无梗，因此后二者不是 panicle 的严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Inflorescence is the broader term for a flower-bearing arrangement. A raceme has stalked flowers on an unbranched main axis, while a spike generally has stalkless flowers; neither is an exact synonym of panicle.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：Pan（潘神）+ pipe（管乐器）→ panpipe。相关形式：panpipes（复数，也是整件乐器的常用名称）、panpiper（排箫演奏者）；panpipe music（排箫音乐）中的 panpipe 是名词作定语，不必另列为形容词。

senses.meaning_zh: 对白人的贬称，尤指被视为贫穷、无知或粗俗的美国南部乡村白人；具有冒犯性
senses.meaning_en: an offensive term for a white person, especially one stereotyped as poor, ignorant, or rural
senses.english_definition: Peckerwood is an insulting word for a white person, especially someone the speaker regards as poor, ignorant, or unsophisticated.
senses.collocation_en: call someone a peckerwood; a backwoods peckerwood
senses.collocation_zh: 用 peckerwood 辱骂某人；偏僻乡下的粗俗白人（侮辱性说法）
senses.sentence_en: He objected when another character called him a peckerwood.
senses.sentence_zh: 另一个人物用 peckerwood 这个侮辱性称呼骂他时，他表示了反对。

etymology_story.zh: 最初是美国方言中将 woodpecker 的组成部分倒置形成的鸟名。后来发展出对白人的贬称；这一称呼也被部分白人监狱群体或白人至上主义群体用作自称，因此现代语境中的含义可能超出普通乡村绰号。
etymology_story.en: Peckerwood began as an American dialectal reversal of the elements in woodpecker. It later became a derogatory term for white people and has also been adopted as a self-designation by some white prison groups or white supremacist groups, giving it additional associations in modern contexts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：peck（啄）+ -er（动作执行者）→ pecker（啄者）；pecker + wood（木头）→ peckerwood，其组成顺序与 woodpecker 相反。复数为 peckerwoods；相关词有 peck、pecker 和 woodpecker，没有常用的专属派生动词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: peck + -er ('one that performs an action') → pecker; pecker + wood → peckerwood, reversing the order found in woodpecker. The plural is peckerwoods. Related words include peck, pecker, and woodpecker; there is no commonly used dedicated derivative verb or adverb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 鸟义对应中性的 woodpecker（啄木鸟）。人物义与 redneck（常贬指美国乡村白人，亦可自称）和 hillbilly（常带刻板印象地指山区乡民）有交集，但 peckerwood 更明确涉及白人身份，并可能带有监狱或白人至上主义关联。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the bird sense, woodpecker is the neutral equivalent. The personal insult overlaps with redneck, often targeting rural white people and sometimes used as a self-description, and hillbilly, which evokes mountain communities; peckerwood more explicitly concerns white identity and may carry prison or white supremacist associations.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 woodpecker 倒过来记鸟义；指人时则记住它是带冒犯性和身份色彩的称呼。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Reverse woodpecker to remember the bird sense; when it refers to a person, remember its offensive and identity-related associations.

senses.meaning_zh: 对虾科动物；对虾科的一种虾
senses.meaning_en: a shrimp belonging to the family Penaeidae
senses.english_definition: A penaeid is a shrimp belonging to the family Penaeidae, which includes many species caught or farmed for food.
senses.collocation_zh: 对虾科幼体；海生对虾科动物
senses.sentence_en: The researchers collected larval penaeids near the coast.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员在近岸采集了对虾科幼体。

senses.meaning_zh: 对虾科的；属于或涉及对虾科的
senses.meaning_en: belonging or relating to the shrimp family Penaeidae
senses.english_definition: Penaeid shrimp belong to the family Penaeidae, and penaeid characteristics or processes are those associated with this family.
senses.collocation_zh: 对虾科虾类；对虾科虾类养殖
senses.sentence_en: Several penaeid species are widely farmed in tropical coastal regions.
senses.sentence_zh: 几种对虾科虾类在热带沿海地区被广泛养殖。

etymology_story.zh: 来自新拉丁语科名 Penaeidae，该名称以属名 Penaeus（对虾属）为基础。英语用 penaeid 表示这一科的成员，也用作形容词描述该科动物及其相关特征。
etymology_story.en: Penaeid comes from the New Latin family name Penaeidae, which is based on the genus name Penaeus. English uses penaeid both for a member of this family and as an adjective describing the family or its associated features.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代分类学构词：Penae-（来自 Penaeus 的词干）+ -id（某科成员的；某科成员）→ penaeid；Penae- + -idae（动物分类中的科名后缀）→ Penaeidae（对虾科）。名词复数为 penaeids；形容词形式不变。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern taxonomic formation: Penae- (the stem associated with Penaeus) + -id ('a member of a family' or 'belonging to that family') → penaeid; Penae- + -idae (the zoological family suffix) → Penaeidae. The noun plural is penaeids; the adjective does not change form.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: penaeid shrimp（对虾科虾类）是更明确的同义表达；shrimp（虾）范围更广，不能单独确定科属；prawn（虾、对虾）在日常和商业用语中的范围随地区变化，也不严格等同于对虾科成员。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Penaeid shrimp is an explicit equivalent. Shrimp is broader and does not identify a family, while prawn varies in everyday and commercial use across regions and is not a precise taxonomic equivalent of penaeid.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 Penaeidae 看作“对虾家族名”，penaeid 就是这个家族的成员，或“这个家族的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of Penaeidae as the shrimp family's name: a penaeid is a family member, and penaeid also means 'belonging to that family.'

aliases: 水下物体表面的附着生物群落

family: periphytic 附着生长的

morphology.text: peri-（周围）+ -phyton（植物、生长物）→ periphyton（附着在水下表面的一群生物）；如今不限于植物。

etymology.text: 英语借自俄语 perifiton；词形中的 peri- 和 phyton 带有希腊语“周围”和“生长”的线索。可想象水下石头外面附着的一层生命。

usage_note: 生态学用语，可包括藻类和微生物等。关键是附着在水下表面，与随水漂浮的 plankton 区分。

translation: 团队从溪底岩石上刮取了附着生物群落。
scenario: 野外调查人员采集溪底岩石表面的生物。

control periphyton on aquarium surfaces 控制水族箱表面的附着生物
context_hint: Notice where the organisms are attached.
hint: Notice where the organisms are attached.

senses.meaning_zh: 附着生物群落；附着在水下物体表面的藻类、微生物及小型动物等
senses.meaning_en: A community of algae, microorganisms, and small animals attached to submerged surfaces.
senses.english_definition: Periphyton is a community of organisms that grows attached to rocks, plants, or other surfaces under water.
senses.collocation_zh: 附着生物生物量；附着生物的生长
senses.sentence_en: The researchers scraped periphyton from submerged stones to measure its biomass.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员从水下石块上刮取附着生物，以测量其生物量。

etymology_story.zh: 这是一个以希腊语来源成分 peri-（周围）和 phyton（植物、生长物）构成的现代科学术语；名称中的植物意象并不限制其现代含义，它也包括附着生活的其他生物。[词源与释义](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/periphyton)
etymology_story.en: This modern scientific term combines Greek-derived peri-, meaning 'around,' and phyton, meaning 'plant' or 'growth'; despite the plant element, its modern meaning also includes other attached organisms. [Etymology and definition](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/periphyton)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词分析：peri-（周围）+ -phyton（植物、生长物）；属于科学组合词。主要派生词：periphytic（附着生物的；附着生长的）；相关组合词：phytoperiphyton（附着植物群落）。periphyton 通常作不可数集合名词，没有常用动词或副词形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: peri- ('around') + -phyton ('plant' or 'growth'), a scientific combining-form construction. Main derivative: periphytic ('relating to periphyton' or 'growing attached to surfaces'); related compound: phytoperiphyton ('the plant component of periphyton'). Periphyton is normally an uncountable collective noun and has no common verb or adverb forms.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: aufwuchs（附着生物群落）是近义专业词；biofilm（生物膜）的范围更广，也可存在于非水生表面；benthic algae（底栖藻类）只指藻类，不能涵盖群落中的细菌和小型动物。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Aufwuchs is a close technical equivalent; biofilm is broader and can occur on surfaces outside aquatic environments; benthic algae refers only to algae and excludes the bacteria and small animals within the community.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: peri-＝周围：水下石头周围附着着一层生命。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Peri- means 'around': picture a living coating growing around an underwater stone.

senses.meaning_zh: 凡士林；矿脂；从石油中制得的半固体烃类混合物
senses.meaning_en: Petroleum jelly, a semisolid mixture of hydrocarbons obtained from petroleum.
senses.english_definition: Petrolatum is a thick, greasy substance made from petroleum that is used in ointments, skin-care products, and lubricants.

senses.sentence_en: The ointment contains white petrolatum as its main ingredient.

etymology_story.zh: 该词是十九世纪形成的新拉丁语式名称，由 petroleum（石油）的词干与拉丁语式结尾 -atum 构成，后来用作这种石油来源半固体物质的正式名称。[词源与释义](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/petrolatum)
etymology_story.en: This nineteenth-century New Latin formation combines the stem of petroleum with the Latin-style ending -atum and became a formal name for the semisolid petroleum product. [Etymology and definition](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/petrolatum)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词分析：petrol-（来自 petroleum，石油）+ -atum（拉丁语式名词结尾）；-atum 在这里不是现代英语中可自由套用的高产后缀。petrolatum 没有常用的简单派生词；常见复合形式有 petrolatum-based（以凡士林为基质的）。相关词 petroleum（石油）和 petrol（汽油，英式英语）不是 petrolatum 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: petrol- (from petroleum) + -atum (a Latin-style noun ending); -atum is not a freely productive modern English suffix here. Petrolatum has no common simple derivatives; a frequent compound form is petrolatum-based. Related words petroleum and petrol ('gasoline' in British English) are not derivatives of petrolatum.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: petroleum jelly（凡士林）是最常见的通用同义名称；soft paraffin（软石蜡）常见于英式药学用语；Vaseline（凡士林品牌）本为商标名称，不能在所有正式语境中与通用成分名等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Petroleum jelly is the usual general synonym; soft paraffin is common in British pharmaceutical terminology; Vaseline is a trademark and is not interchangeable with the generic ingredient name in every formal context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: petrol- 联想到石油：石油制成的半固体油膏。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect petrol- with petroleum: petroleum turned into a semisolid jelly.

meaning: 生药学（研究天然药物的学科）
aliases: 生药学（研究天然药物的学科）

pronunciation.note: 采用所列英语词典的一种读法；省略音节分隔点。

forms: 学科名通常不可数；不用普通名词复数来表示这门学科。
family: pharmacognosist 生药学家；pharmacognostic 生药学的

morphology.text: pharmaco-（药物）+ -gnosy（知识、认识）→ pharmacognosy（认识和研究天然药物的学科）。

etymology.text: 用希腊语来源的 pharmaco-（药物）和 -gnosy（认识、知识）组成的学科名称；把它记成“认识天然药物”。

usage_note: 研究天然来源的药用物质及其鉴别，不能仅理解成开处方或经营药店。

senses.meaning_zh: 生药学；研究天然药物及其来源、鉴定、成分和性质的学科
senses.meaning_en: The scientific study of natural medicinal substances, including their sources, identification, constituents, and properties.
senses.english_definition: Pharmacognosy is the scientific study of medicinal substances obtained from natural sources such as plants, animals, and microorganisms.
senses.collocation_en: pharmacognosy research; a professor of pharmacognosy
senses.collocation_zh: 生药学研究；生药学教授
senses.sentence_en: She studied pharmacognosy to learn how medicinal plants are identified and analyzed.
senses.sentence_zh: 她学习生药学，以了解如何鉴定和分析药用植物。

etymology_story.zh: 该学科名称以希腊语 pharmakon（药物）和 gnosis（知识、认识）为基础，字面意思是“关于药物的知识”。它在十九世纪初的欧洲药学中确立，后来发展为研究天然药物及其成分的学科。[学科名称的历史](https://pharmacognosy.us/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/the-american-society-of-pharmacognosy-50-years-of-progress-in-natural-products-research-chapter-5.pdf)
etymology_story.en: The name draws on Greek pharmakon ('drug') and gnosis ('knowledge'), literally 'knowledge of drugs.' Established in early nineteenth-century European pharmacy, it developed into the study of natural medicinal substances and their constituents. [History of the discipline's name](https://pharmacognosy.us/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/the-american-society-of-pharmacognosy-50-years-of-progress-in-natural-products-research-chapter-5.pdf)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词分析：pharmaco-（药物）+ -gnosy（知识、认识）。主要词族：pharmacognosist、pharmacognost（生药学家）；pharmacognostic、pharmacognostical（生药学的）；pharmacognostically（从生药学角度）；pharmacognosis（较少见的同义名词）。pharmacology（药理学）共享 pharmaco-，但不是本词的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: pharmaco- ('drug') + -gnosy ('knowledge'). Main family: pharmacognosist and pharmacognost ('a specialist in pharmacognosy'); pharmacognostic and pharmacognostical ('relating to pharmacognosy'); pharmacognostically ('from a pharmacognostic perspective'); pharmacognosis (a less common synonymous noun). Pharmacology shares pharmaco- but is not derived from pharmacognosy.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pharmacognosis（生药学）是较少见的近义名称；materia medica（药物学；药物资料体系）是历史上更宽泛的概念；phytochemistry（植物化学）侧重植物化学成分，既不涵盖所有天然药物，也不专以药用价值为研究对象。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pharmacognosis is a less common equivalent; materia medica is a historically broader body of knowledge about medicinal substances; phytochemistry focuses on plant chemicals, neither covering all natural drug sources nor restricting itself to medicinal value.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: pharmaco-＝药，-gnosy＝认识：认识天然药物。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pharmaco- means 'drug' and -gnosy means 'knowledge': knowing natural medicines.

senses.meaning_zh: 多分相关的；根据有序分类数据估计潜在连续变量相关性的
senses.meaning_en: Relating to correlations between latent continuous variables estimated from observed ordinal data.

etymology_story.zh: 音乐义由 poly-（多）与 choric（合唱队的）构成，后者追溯至希腊语 choros（合唱队）；统计义中的 chor- 则与表示区域的希腊语词有关，几何义与表示空间的词有关。相同拼写承载了不同的专业构词来源。[词源与各义项](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/polychoric)
etymology_story.en: The musical sense combines poly- ('many') with choric, ultimately from Greek choros ('chorus'); the statistical sense instead draws on a Greek word for a region, while the geometric sense draws on a word for space. The same spelling therefore represents distinct specialist formations. [Etymologies and senses](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/polychoric)

morphology_enriched.zh: 音乐义：poly-（多）+ choric（合唱队的）；统计义：poly-（多）+ chor-（区域）+ -ic（形容词后缀）；几何义与 polychoron（四维多胞体）对应。名词 polychoric 由 polychoric correlation 省略中心词形成，复数为 polychorics；音乐相关词有 polychoral（多合唱队的）和 polychorally（以多合唱队方式）。tetrachoric（四分相关的）是相关统计术语，不是本词的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Musical formation: poly- ('many') + choric ('choral'); statistical formation: poly- ('many') + chor- ('region') + -ic (adjective suffix); the geometric sense corresponds to polychoron ('a four-dimensional polytope'). The noun polychoric is an elliptical form of polychoric correlation, with plural polychorics. Musical relatives include polychoral and polychorally. Tetrachoric is a related statistical term, not a derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 音乐义中，polychoral（多合唱队的）是更常见的同义词，antiphonal（交替应答的）强调应答方式，并不必然要求多个合唱队；统计义中，tetrachoric（四分相关的）专指两个二分类变量对应的特例，而 polychoric 可处理具有更多有序类别的变量。[统计术语说明](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/polycor/polycor.pdf)
synonyms_and_nuances.en: In music, polychoral is the more usual equivalent, while antiphonal emphasizes alternating responses and does not necessarily require multiple choirs; in statistics, tetrachoric describes the special case with two binary variables, whereas polychoric accommodates additional ordered categories. [Statistical terminology](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/polycor/polycor.pdf)

mnemonic_anchor.zh: poly-＝多：音乐想“多个合唱队”，统计想“多个有序格子”，几何想“四维空间中的多个胞”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Poly- means 'many': picture several choirs in music, several ordered cells in statistics, and multiple cells in four-dimensional geometry.

aliases: 多种文化相互交流融合的

morphology.text: poly-（多）+ culture（文化；去-e）+ -al（形容词后缀）→ polycultural（多种文化互动的）。

etymology.text: 英语用希腊语来源的 poly-（多）与 culture 及形容词后缀 -al 组成。记住它关心文化之间的相互影响。

senses.meaning_zh: 多种文化相互联系、交流并彼此影响的
senses.meaning_en: Involving the connections, exchanges, and mutual influences among multiple cultures.
senses.english_definition: A polycultural view recognizes that different cultures develop through continuing contact and influence one another.

senses.meaning_zh: 多种作物混作的；多品种混养的
senses.meaning_en: Involving the cultivation or rearing of multiple species together.
senses.english_definition: A polycultural farming system grows several crop species together or raises several species within the same production system.
senses.collocation_zh: 多作物混作农业；混作或混养系统
senses.sentence_en: The farm uses a polycultural system in which beans grow between rows of fruit trees.
