etymology_story.zh: 源自新拉丁语 chalcopyrites，由希腊语 chalkos（铜）与拉丁语 pyrites（黄铁矿）组合而成，名称将这种矿物与铜及黄铁矿般的外观联系起来。[韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/chalcopyrite)
etymology_story.en: The word comes from New Latin chalcopyrites, combining Greek chalkos, meaning copper, with Latin pyrites, meaning pyrite; the name connects the mineral with copper and its pyrite-like appearance. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/chalcopyrite)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：chalco-（铜，科学构词成分）+ pyrite（黄铁矿）→ chalcopyrite（黄铜矿）。词族：chalcopyritic（含黄铜矿的；与黄铜矿有关的）；复数 chalcopyrites 用于指不同样品或种类。pyrite（黄铁矿）和 pyritic（黄铁矿的）属于相关基础词族；chalcopyrite 在 chalcopyrite crystals 等结构中作名词定语，不必另立形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: chalco- (a scientific combining form meaning copper) + pyrite → chalcopyrite. The family includes chalcopyritic (containing or relating to chalcopyrite); the plural chalcopyrites can refer to distinct specimens or varieties. Pyrite and pyritic belong to the related base-word family. In expressions such as chalcopyrite crystals, chalcopyrite is an attributive noun rather than a separate adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: copper pyrites（黄铜矿）是传统同义名称；copper iron sulfide（铜铁硫化物）描述其化学组成，但脱离矿物学语境时不一定专指黄铜矿；pyrite（黄铁矿，FeS₂）只是易混淆的相关矿物，并非同义词。[柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/chalcopyrite)
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Copper pyrites is a traditional synonym; copper iron sulfide describes its composition but does not necessarily identify this mineral outside a mineralogical context. Pyrite, FeS₂, is a related mineral that can be confused with chalcopyrite, not a synonym. [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/chalcopyrite)

mnemonic_anchor.zh: chalco- 提示“铜”：外观像黄铁矿，却是提铜的重要矿物。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Let chalco- signal copper: it resembles pyrite but is an important source of copper.

senses.collocation_zh: 海洋刺胞动物；刺胞动物与海绵动物
senses.sentence_en: A hydra is a freshwater cnidarian.

senses.meaning_zh: 刺胞动物的；属于刺胞动物门的
senses.meaning_en: Belonging to or relating to the phylum Cnidaria

etymology_story.zh: 由新拉丁语门名 Cnidaria 加后缀 -an 构成，名称最终源自希腊语 knīdē（荨麻；海荨麻），借植物与这些动物共有的刺痛特征命名。它的名词和形容词用法具有相同的词源与读音。[韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/cnidarian)
etymology_story.en: Cnidarian was formed from the New Latin phylum name Cnidaria plus -an; the name ultimately derives from Greek knīdē, meaning nettle or sea nettle, referring to their stinging properties. Its noun and adjective uses share the same origin and pronunciation. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/cnidarian)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：Cnidaria 去掉末尾 -a，再加 -an → cnidarian，既表示该门的成员，也表示与该门有关。词族：Cnidaria（刺胞动物门，分类名称首字母大写）、cnidarian（刺胞动物；刺胞动物的）、cnidarians（名词复数）；共享词根的相关术语有 cnida（刺胞器，复数 cnidae）与 cnidocyte（刺细胞）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: remove the final -a from Cnidaria and add -an → cnidarian, meaning either a member of the phylum or relating to it. The family includes Cnidaria (the capitalized taxonomic name), cnidarian (noun and adjective), and cnidarians (plural). Related terms sharing the root include cnida (a stinging organelle; plural cnidae) and cnidocyte (a stinging cell).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: coelenterate（腔肠动物）是传统近义词，但旧分类中的范围可能比现代 Cnidaria 更广；jellyfish（水母）和 coral（珊瑚）分别指其中的部分成员，不能替代整个门的名称。形容词 coelenterate 也可见于旧式分类表述。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Coelenterate is a traditional near-synonym, but older classifications may give it a broader scope than modern Cnidaria. Jellyfish and coral name particular members or groups within the phylum and cannot replace its general name. Adjectival coelenterate also occurs in older taxonomic descriptions.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cnid- 联想“荨麻的刺痛”：水母、珊瑚、海葵，共同线索是刺细胞。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect cnid- with a nettle's sting: jellyfish, corals, and anemones share the clue of stinging cells.

etymology_story.zh: 这是二十世纪中叶形成的英语药物俚语：将商标名 Dexedrine 截短为 dex-，再加口语词尾 -y；另一拼写为 dexie。它把药品名称转成了日常俚语中的药片名称。[柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/dexie)
etymology_story.en: This drug slang developed in the mid-twentieth century by shortening the trademark Dexedrine to dex- and adding the informal ending -y; dexie is an alternative spelling. The formation turned a medicine's brand name into a colloquial name for a tablet. [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/dexie)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：dex-（Dexedrine 的截短形式）+ -y（口语名词后缀）→ dexy。词形：dexie（异体拼写）、dexies（通常使用的复数），另见复数 dexys；Dexedrine 是来源商标，dextroamphetamine（右旋安非他明）是相关通用药名，二者不是由 dexy 派生而来。没有常用的规则动词、形容词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: dex- (a clipping of Dexedrine) + -y (an informal noun suffix) → dexy. Forms include dexie (alternative spelling), dexies (the usual plural), and the alternative plural dexys. Dexedrine is the source trademark and dextroamphetamine the related generic drug name; neither is derived from dexy. There are no common regular verb, adjective, or adverb derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dexie 与 dexy 仅拼写不同；Dexedrine 是商标名，语体较正式且所指更具体；upper（兴奋剂，俚语）范围更广，可指多种兴奋性药物，并非都含右旋安非他明。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dexie differs from dexy only in spelling; Dexedrine is a trademark with a more formal register and a more specific reference. Upper is broader slang for a stimulant drug and does not necessarily refer to dextroamphetamine.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Dexedrine 缩成 dex，再加口语小尾巴 -y：品牌名变成药片俚称。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Shorten Dexedrine to dex and add informal -y: a brand name becomes pill slang.

senses.meaning_en: An animal that obtains most of its body heat from external sources
senses.english_definition: An ectotherm is an animal whose body temperature depends mainly on heat obtained from its surroundings rather than heat produced within its body.
senses.collocation_zh: 水生外温动物；陆生外温动物
senses.sentence_en: As an ectotherm, the lizard warms itself by basking in the sun.
senses.sentence_zh: 作为外温动物，这只蜥蜴通过晒太阳使身体暖和起来。

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代科学英语利用希腊语来源的 ecto-（外部）与 therm-（热）组合而成的术语，韦氏词典将其最早已知用例列于 1940 年。其命名强调身体热量主要来自外部，而不是说这种动物的身体始终冰冷。[韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/ectotherm)
etymology_story.en: This modern scientific term combines the Greek-derived elements ecto-, meaning outside, and therm-, meaning heat; Merriam-Webster dates its earliest known use to 1940. Its name emphasizes an external source of body heat rather than a body that is always cold. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/ectotherm)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：ecto-（外部）+ -therm（以某种方式获得或维持体热的生物）→ ectotherm。主要词族：ectotherms（复数）、ectothermic（外温性的）、ectothermically（以外温方式）、ectothermy（外温性；外温生理特征）；也有形容词 ectothermal。endotherm（内温动物）与 endothermy（内温性）是共享 therm- 的对照词，不是 ectotherm 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: ecto- (outside) + -therm (an organism characterized by a particular source or pattern of body heat) → ectotherm. The main family includes ectotherms, ectothermic (adjective), ectothermically (adverb), ectothermy (noun), and the alternative adjective ectothermal. Endotherm and endothermy are contrasting formations sharing therm-, not derivatives of ectotherm.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cold-blooded animal（俗称“冷血动物”）通俗但容易造成体温始终很低的误解；poikilotherm（变温动物）强调体温变化，ectotherm 强调热量来源，二者并不严格等同；endotherm（内温动物）是对照词，强调体热主要来自体内代谢。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cold-blooded animal is a familiar expression but can misleadingly suggest a consistently low body temperature. Poikilotherm emphasizes variable body temperature, whereas ectotherm emphasizes the source of heat, so they are not exact equivalents. Endotherm is a contrasting term for an animal whose body heat comes mainly from internal metabolism.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ecto- 外面 + therm 热：蜥蜴向外界“借热”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ecto- means outside and therm means heat: picture a lizard borrowing warmth from its surroundings.

etymology_story.zh: 体育义取自 National Hockey League（国家冰球联盟）三个单词的首字母，逐个字母读出。[韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/NHL) 医学义则独立取自 non-Hodgkin lymphoma（非霍奇金淋巴瘤）的首字母，与冰球组织没有词源关系。[美国国家癌症研究所](https://www.cancer.gov/publications/dictionaries/cancer-terms/def/nhl)
etymology_story.en: The sporting sense takes the initial letters of National Hockey League and is pronounced letter by letter. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/NHL) The medical sense independently abbreviates non-Hodgkin lymphoma and has no etymological connection with the hockey organization. [National Cancer Institute](https://www.cancer.gov/publications/dictionaries/cancer-terms/def/nhl)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词方式为首字母缩写，而非词根加词缀：体育义 N(ational) + H(ockey) + L(eague)；医学义 N(on-) + H(odgkin) + L(ymphoma)。体育相关派生词 NHLer 指“国家冰球联盟球员”，复数为 NHLers；NHL 本身在 NHL player 等结构中作名词定语，不因此另立形容词词性。医学文本中的 NHLs 可指不同的非霍奇金淋巴瘤类型。
morphology_enriched.en: The formation is initialism rather than root-and-affix derivation: sporting N(ational) + H(ockey) + L(eague), and medical N(on-) + H(odgkin) + L(ymphoma). The sporting derivative NHLer means an NHL player, with plural NHLers. NHL itself functions as an attributive noun in NHL player, without requiring a separate adjective entry. In medical writing, NHLs can refer to different non-Hodgkin lymphoma types.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: National Hockey League 是体育义的完整名称，与 NHL 指同一组织；the league（该联盟）只有在上下文明确时才能代指它。non-Hodgkin lymphoma 是医学义的完整形式；lymphoma（淋巴瘤）范围更广，还包括霍奇金淋巴瘤。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: National Hockey League is the full name of the sporting organization and has the same reference as NHL; the league identifies it only when the context is clear. Non-Hodgkin lymphoma is the full medical expression, while lymphoma is broader and also includes Hodgkin lymphoma.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 看语境展开字母：冰球新闻中是 National Hockey League；医学报告中是 non-Hodgkin lymphoma。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Expand the letters through context: National Hockey League in hockey news, non-Hodgkin lymphoma in a medical report.

etymology_story.zh: PBX 是 private branch exchange 的字母缩写，其中 X 取自 exchange，逐个字母读音。这个名称原指机构内部的专用电话交换设备，后来也用于软件化的同类系统。[《韦氏词典》](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/PBX)
etymology_story.en: PBX abbreviates private branch exchange, taking X from exchange, and is pronounced letter by letter. Originally referring to an organization's private telephone switching equipment, the name also applies to software-based systems serving that function. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/PBX)

morphology_enriched.zh: 缩写结构：P(rivate，专用的) + B(ranch，分支) + (e)X(change，交换系统)。复数为 PBXs；相关技术名称有 IP PBX（基于互联网协议的专用电话交换系统）、hosted PBX（托管式专用电话交换系统）和 PABX（专用自动电话交换机），这些属于复合名称或相关缩写。PBX system 中的 PBX 是名词作定语。
morphology_enriched.en: Abbreviation structure: P(rivate) + B(ranch) + (e)X(change). The plural is PBXs; related technical expressions include IP PBX, hosted PBX, and PABX, meaning private automatic branch exchange. These are compound expressions or related abbreviations; PBX functions as a noun modifier in PBX system.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: private branch exchange（专用电话交换系统）是完整名称，与 PBX 等义；telephone switchboard（电话交换台）更突出接线或操作设备；PABX（专用自动电话交换机）明确强调自动交换功能。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Private branch exchange is the full expression and means exactly the same thing; telephone switchboard emphasizes the switching or operating equipment; PABX explicitly specifies automatic switching.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一家公司内部的电话，也有自己的“交换中心”：private + branch + exchange。
mnemonic_anchor.en: An organization has its own telephone exchange: private + branch + exchange.

etymology_story.zh: rainbird 由 rain（雨）与 bird（鸟）直接复合，至少在十六世纪已有记录。这个名称源于人们把某些鸟类、尤其是杜鹃科鸟类的鸣叫与降雨联系起来的民间认识，并不专指一个物种。[《韦氏词典》](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/rainbird)
etymology_story.en: Rainbird combines rain and bird and is recorded from the sixteenth century. The name reflects a traditional association between approaching rain and the calls of various birds, especially cuckoos, rather than identifying one particular species. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/rainbird)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：rain（雨，名词）+ bird（鸟，名词）→ rainbird（报雨鸟），属于名词复合词；复数为 rainbirds。没有常用的直接派生动词、形容词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: rain, a noun, + bird, a noun, → rainbird, a compound noun. The plural is rainbirds; there are no common directly derived verbs, adjectives, or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Rain crow is a folk name for certain cuckoos and generally has a narrower reference; cuckoo names a kind of bird, some of which are called rainbirds, so the terms are not universally interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: rain + bird：人们听见它叫，就想到雨要来了。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Rain + bird: its call makes people think rain is coming.

etymology_story.zh: amative 在十七世纪进入英语，源于中古拉丁语 amātīvus，其词干来自拉丁语 amāre（爱）。它既可形容容易产生爱恋或情欲的人，也可表示与爱情有关的事物；现代用法较少见。[《韦氏词典》](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/amative)
etymology_story.en: Amative entered English in the seventeenth century from Medieval Latin amātīvus, built on a stem of Latin amāre, meaning 'to love.' It describes either a disposition toward love or something associated with love, and is uncommon in modern usage. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/amative)

morphology_enriched.zh: 词源构形可分析为 amat-（爱，拉丁语词干）+ -ive（形容词后缀）；现代英语通常把 amative 作为借入的完整词使用。直接派生词为 amatively（多情地；表达爱恋地，副词）和 amativeness（多情；情欲倾向，名词）；amatory（爱情的）、amorous（多情的）和 amateur（业余爱好者）是同源词。
morphology_enriched.en: The historical structure is amat-, a Latin stem meaning 'love,' + the adjective suffix -ive; modern English generally treats amative as an established borrowed word. Direct derivatives are amatively, an adverb, and amativeness, a noun; amatory, amorous, and amateur are etymological relatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: amorous（多情的；爱恋的）最接近且更常用；amatory（有关爱情的）更侧重题材或活动；affectionate（亲昵的；充满关爱的）强调温情，不必涉及恋爱或情欲。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Amorous is the closest and more usual alternative; amatory more often describes a subject or activity involving love; affectionate emphasizes tenderness and need not imply romantic or sexual attraction.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: amat- 表示“爱”：amative 就是性情或表现上“带着爱恋的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Amat- means 'love': amative describes a loving inclination or expression.

etymology_story.zh: argle 是 argue（争辩）的方言变体，部分词典将其标为过时用语；argles 是这个动词加上第三人称单数词尾 -s 的形式。其意义仍是“争辩、争执”。[《韦氏词典》](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/argle)、[《柯林斯词典》](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/argle)
etymology_story.en: Argle is a dialectal variant of argue, also labelled obsolete in some dictionaries; argles adds the regular third-person singular ending -s. Its meaning remains 'argues' or 'disputes.' [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/argle), [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/argle)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代屈折：argle（争辩）+ -s（第三人称单数词尾，读 /z/）→ argles。动词形式为 argle、argles、argled（过去式及过去分词）、argling（现在分词及动名词，去掉词尾不发音的 e 再加 -ing）；相关表达 argle-bargle 表示争吵或无谓争论。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern inflection: argle + third-person singular -s, pronounced /z/, → argles. The verb forms are argle, argles, argled for the past tense and past participle, and argling for the present participle and gerund, formed by dropping silent final e before -ing; the related expression argle-bargle refers to quarrelling or pointless argument.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: argues（争辩）是最普通的现代对应词；quarrels（争吵）更突出人际冲突和情绪；wrangles（争执不休）强调反复、拖延或难以解决的争论。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Argues is the ordinary modern equivalent; quarrels emphasizes interpersonal conflict and emotion; wrangles suggests prolonged, repetitive, or difficult disagreement.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 argle 看作 argue 的方言亲戚：he argles，就像 he argues。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Treat argle as a dialect cousin of argue: he argles works like he argues.

senses.phonetic: 英式 BrE /ˈbɜːlɪŋ/；美式 AmE /ˈbɝlɪŋ/；苏格兰变体 Scottish variant /ˈbɪrlɪŋ/

etymology_story.zh: 运动名称 birling 由表示“旋转、使浮木滚转”的 birl 加 -ing 构成，而这个 birl 的更早来源不确定，可能带有拟声性质。另一个表示“饮酒作乐”的同形动词 birl 经中古英语追溯至古英语 byrelian（斟酒、侍酒），属于不同词源。[《柯林斯词典》](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/birling)、[《韦氏词典》](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/birl)
etymology_story.en: The sport name birling adds -ing to birl, meaning to spin or roll a floating log; the earlier origin of this verb is uncertain and possibly imitative. A separate birl meaning to carouse comes through Middle English from Old English byrelian, meaning to serve drink. [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/birling), [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/birl)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：birl（旋转；滚转浮木）+ -ing → birling，可作活动名词，也可作动词的现在分词或动名词。词族包括 birl、birls（第三人称单数）、birled（过去式及过去分词）、birling 和 birler（滚木竞技者；使物体旋转的人），birler 的复数为 birlers；表示“饮酒作乐”的同形动词具有相同的规则屈折。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: birl + -ing → birling, functioning as an activity noun, present participle, or gerund. The family includes birl, birls, birled, birling, and birler, meaning a logroller or someone who makes something spin, with plural birlers; the separate drinking verb follows the same regular inflection.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: logrolling（滚木竞技）对应运动义，但也可表示政治上的互投赞成票；spinning（旋转）对应一般转动义，不限定浮木；carousing（饮酒作乐）只对应另一个苏格兰方言动词的饮酒义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Logrolling names the sport but can also mean exchanging political favours; spinning covers general rotation without specifying a log; carousing corresponds only to the separate Scottish drinking sense.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 脚下浮木 birl（转），脚上选手保持平衡：这项活动就是 birling。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The log birls beneath your feet while you balance: the activity is birling.

morphology.text: catechet-（教理问答相关词干）+ -ic（……的）→ catechetic（问答式教理教学的）。

etymology.text: 借自新拉丁语 catecheticus，与晚期拉丁语 catechesis（教理讲授）相连。想象老师提问、学生逐条回答的教理课。

usage_note: 较书面，多见于宗教教育；catechetical 更常见。本课只教教理问答教学义，不自动等同于所有互动教学。

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自新拉丁语 catecheticus，与晚期拉丁语 catechesis（口头教理讲授）相关，最终可追溯到希腊语中表示“使回响、口头教导”的词。其含义既涉及基督教教理教育，也涉及与这种教育密切相关的问答教学方式。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word from New Latin catecheticus, related to Late Latin catechesis, meaning oral religious instruction, and ultimately to Greek words for resounding and instructing orally. Its meanings cover both Christian doctrinal instruction and the question-and-answer method associated with it.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学习分析：catechet-（教理讲授相关的黏着词干）+ -ic（……的）；catechetic + -al → catechetical（更常用的形容词形式），catechetical + -ly → catechetically（以教理问答方式）。相关词族包括 catechesis（教理讲授）、catechetics（教理教学法）、catechism（教理问答书）、catechist（教理教师）、catechize/catechise（进行教理讲授；盘问）、catechization/catechisation（教理讲授；盘问过程）、catechizer/catechiser（讲授者；盘问者）、catechumen（慕道者）和 catechumenate（慕道期；慕道培育制度）；这些相关词并非全部由 catechetic 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: A useful modern analysis is catechet- (a bound stem associated with religious instruction) + -ic (relating to). Catechetic + -al gives catechetical, the more usual adjective, and catechetical + -ly gives catechetically. Related family members include catechesis (religious instruction), catechetics (its methods), catechism (a doctrinal question-and-answer text), catechist (an instructor), catechize/catechise (instruct or question), catechization/catechisation (the process), catechizer/catechiser (the person), catechumen (a person receiving instruction before baptism), and catechumenate (the period or system of that instruction); these are not all direct derivatives of catechetic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: catechetical（教理讲授的；问答教学的）是更常见的同义形式；Socratic（苏格拉底式的）强调通过追问引导独立推理，不一定要求固定答案；doctrinal（教义的）强调所讲授的教义内容，不限定教学方式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Catechetical is the more usual equivalent. Socratic emphasizes questions that lead learners to reason independently, rather than necessarily reproduce set answers. Doctrinal concerns the beliefs being taught and does not specify a teaching method.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 口头讲授 → 一问一答 → 教理问答；记住 catechetic 与更常见的 catechetical 同义。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Oral instruction → questions and answers → teaching a catechism; connect catechetic with the more familiar catechetical.

etymology_story.zh: chrysalid 与 chrysalis 同源，最终来自希腊语 chrysallis（蝶蛹），其词干为 chry sallid-，其中与 chrysos（金）相关的部分指向某些蛹的金色光泽。英语名词可能经法语 chrysalide 传入，后来也用作表示“蛹的”的形容词。
etymology_story.en: Chrysalid shares its origin with chrysalis, ultimately from Greek chrysallis, meaning a butterfly pupa, with the stem chrysallid- and a connection to chrysos, meaning gold, reflecting the golden appearance of some pupae. The English noun may have entered through French chrysalide and also developed adjectival use.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜将 chrysalid 作为整体词干，不拆为 chrysa + lid；名词复数为 chrysalid + -s → chrysalids。相关形式包括 chrysalis（蛹；复数 chrysalises 或 chrysalides）、chrysalidal（蛹的）和 chrysalid 的形容词用法；pupa、pupal 是语义相关词，不属于同一词根家族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, treat chrysalid as a whole stem rather than splitting it into chrysa + lid; its regular noun plural is chrysalid + -s → chrysalids. Related forms include chrysalis (plural chrysalises or chrysalides), chrysalidal (relating to a chrysalis), and adjectival chrysalid. Pupa and pupal are semantically related but belong to a different word family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chrysalis（蝶蛹）是名词更常见的对应词；pupa（蛹）适用于更多类完全变态昆虫，范围更广；pupal（蛹的；蛹期的）是形容词更常用的近义词。cocoon（茧）指蛹外的保护结构，不能与“蛹”直接等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chrysalis is the more usual noun equivalent. Pupa is broader and applies to the corresponding stage in many insects with complete metamorphosis. Pupal is the more usual related adjective. A cocoon is a protective structure surrounding a pupa, rather than the pupa itself.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 金色光泽的蛹 → chrysalid；记“蛹本身”，并联想到蛹期。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a gold-flecked pupa: chrysalid names the pupa and can also describe its developmental stage.

senses.meaning_zh: 裙撑；撑大裙摆的带箍衬裙
senses.meaning_en: a historical skirt support or hooped underskirt
senses.english_definition: A farthingale is a frame, hoop, or stiff support worn under a skirt, especially in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, to make the skirt stand out.
senses.collocation_zh: 西班牙式裙撑；法国式裙撑
senses.sentence_en: The costume maker fitted a farthingale beneath the queen's gown.
senses.sentence_zh: 服装师在王后的长裙下面装上了裙撑。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语 verdugale 借自西班牙语 verdugado，后者与 verdugo（枝条；细杆）相关。名称源于早期用枝条或类似材料制成的撑裙结构，后来用于指这种裙撑及相关的带箍衬裙。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through French verdugale from Spanish verdugado, related to verdugo, meaning a rod or young shoot. Its name refers to the rods used in early skirt supports and came to denote the support or associated hooped underskirt.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中为不可再作有意义拆分的借词词干 farthingale；farthingale + -s → farthingales（复数）。没有常用的前后缀派生词；farthingale chair（裙撑椅，适合穿宽大裙装者坐的椅子）是复合名词，farthingale 在其中作名词定语。不能按 farthing（旧英国小额硬币）+ ale（麦芽啤酒）解释。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, farthingale is a borrowed stem without a useful internal English breakdown; farthingale + -s gives the plural farthingales. It has no common affixal derivatives. Farthingale chair, a chair accommodating wide skirts, is a compound with farthingale as a noun modifier. The word is not formed from farthing, an old British coin, and ale.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hoop skirt（带箍裙；裙撑）是较宽泛的描述词；crinoline（克里诺林裙撑）通常使人联想到十九世纪的笼式裙撑，也可指硬衬料；pannier（侧裙撑）主要向身体两侧撑开。farthingale 特指较早的历史服饰结构，不能完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hoop skirt is a broader descriptive term. Crinoline often suggests a nineteenth-century cage support and can also name a stiff fabric. A pannier chiefly extends a skirt sideways. Farthingale refers to an earlier historical support, so these terms are not fully interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 细枝做圆箍，圆箍撑大裙：farthingale＝历史服饰中的裙撑。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Young rods become hoops; hoops spread the skirt: a farthingale is a historical skirt support.

meaning: 执意的；不顾一切地决心做某事的
aliases: 执意的；不顾一切地决心做某事的

pronunciation.note: 主重音在 hell /hɛl/，bent 带次重音；结尾 /nt/ 两个辅音要连贯读出。

usage_note: 常用 be hellbent on doing，语气比 determined 强，往往带不听劝或冒险的意味。

senses.meaning_zh: 执意的；不顾后果地决心要做某事的
senses.meaning_en: determined to do something regardless of risks or consequences
senses.english_definition: If someone is hellbent on doing something, they are determined to do it even if it is dangerous or unwise.
senses.collocation_en: hellbent on revenge; hellbent on winning
senses.collocation_zh: 一心要报复；执意要赢

senses.meaning_zh: 不顾一切地；拼命地；飞快地
senses.meaning_en: with reckless determination or at great speed
senses.english_definition: If someone moves or acts hellbent, they do so with fierce determination, often very quickly and without considering danger.
senses.collocation_zh: 拼命策马疾驰；不顾一切地飞奔
senses.sentence_en: The rider galloped hellbent toward the village to fetch help.

etymology_story.zh: 该词形成于十九世纪的美国英语，由加强语气的 hell 与表示“心意已定、倾向于某事”的 bent 组成。其核心含义是不顾后果的决心，也发展出描述拼命行动或急速前进的用法。
etymology_story.en: The word arose in nineteenth-century American English from emphatic hell and bent in the sense of being firmly inclined or determined. Its central idea of reckless determination also developed into uses describing headlong action or rapid movement.

morphology_enriched.zh: hell（加强语气）+ bent（决意的）→ hellbent；常见拼写变体为 hell-bent。bent 在历史上是 bend（弯曲；使转向）的过去分词，此处表示心意朝某目标倾斜；hellbent 本身没有常用的屈折形式或后缀派生词，形容词可用 more/most 构成比较级和最高级，副词通常也直接使用 hellbent。
morphology_enriched.en: Hell (an intensifier) + bent (determined) forms hellbent, also commonly written hell-bent. Bent is historically the past participle of bend and here suggests directing one's will toward a goal. Hellbent has no common inflected or suffixed derivatives; its adjective can take more or most, and its adverb normally has the same form.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: determined（坚定的）通常中性，不必带有鲁莽意味；dead set（铁了心的）强调决心难以改变，语气口语化；headlong（莽撞的；莽撞地）突出急速行动及缺乏考虑。hellbent 常同时包含强烈决心与不顾后果的意味，副词用法比形容词少见。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Determined is generally neutral and need not imply recklessness. Dead set is informal and emphasizes an unchangeable decision. Headlong, as an adjective or adverb, emphasizes haste and insufficient thought. Hellbent often combines intense resolve with disregard for consequences; its adverbial use is less common than its adjective.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: bent＝心意已朝目标倾斜；hell 加强语气：铁了心，拼命冲。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bent directs the will toward a goal; hell intensifies it: fiercely resolved, charging ahead.

etymology_story.zh: 英语从墨西哥西班牙语 huarache 借入，源头是普雷佩查语 kwarachi，意为“凉鞋”。食品义因玉米面饼的长圆形外观像凉鞋鞋底而得名。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed huarache from Mexican Spanish, ultimately from Purépecha kwarachi, meaning sandal. The food takes the same name because its oblong corn-dough base resembles the sole of a sandal.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中为整体借词 huarache，无可直接分析的英语前后缀；huarache + -s → huaraches（复数，适用于凉鞋和食品两义）。huarache sandal（墨西哥编织凉鞋）是复合表达，其中 huarache 作名词定语；没有常用的英语后缀派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, huarache is an unanalyzed borrowing with no productive internal English prefix or suffix. Huarache + -s gives huaraches, the plural for both sandals and the food. Huarache sandal is a compound expression in which huarache is a noun modifier; there are no common English suffixed derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 凉鞋义：sandal（凉鞋）是上位词，不限定产地或编织鞋面。食品义没有完全等同的常用近义词；sope（索佩饼）通常较小、较圆且边缘捏起，tostada（脆玉米饼）通常底薄而脆，均与长圆形、较厚实的 huarache 有别。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For footwear, sandal is the broader term and does not specify Mexican origin or a woven upper. The food has no exact common synonym: a sope is usually smaller and rounder with a raised edge, while a tostada usually has a thin, crisp base; both differ from the oblong, more substantial huarache.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先记编织凉鞋，再记鞋底形玉米饼：同一个名字，两种鞋底轮廓。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with the woven sandal, then picture a sandal-shaped corn cake: one name, two matching outlines.

senses.meaning_en: a Chinese green tea made with twisted leaves
senses.english_definition: Hyson is a type of Chinese green tea whose leaves are twisted during processing.

etymology_story.zh: hyson 借自汉语“熙春”的粤语读音，名称通常解释为“明媚的春天”。英语沿用这个名称，指一种中国绿茶。
etymology_story.en: Hyson comes from the Cantonese pronunciation of the Chinese name 熙春, usually interpreted as 'flourishing spring.' English adopted the name for a variety of Chinese green tea.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可再作有效拆分的借词，没有常用的前后缀派生词。相关复合名称有 young hyson（用嫩叶制成的熙春茶）、old hyson（用较成熟叶片制成的熙春茶）和 hyson skin（加工筛分时分出的较低等级茶叶）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, hyson is an unanalyzed loanword with no established common affixal derivatives. Related compound names include young hyson, made from younger leaves; old hyson, made from more mature leaves; and hyson skin, a lower-grade tea separated during processing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: green tea（绿茶）是上位词；young hyson（嫩叶熙春茶）是更具体的品种名称；gunpowder tea（珠茶）是相关但不同的绿茶，叶片通常揉成小颗粒，而不是较长的卷曲形状。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Green tea is the broader category; young hyson names a more specific variety made from younger leaves; gunpowder tea is a related but distinct green tea whose leaves are generally rolled into small pellets rather than longer twisted shapes.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 熙春＝明媚春光：把春天的绿意连到杯中的卷叶绿茶。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'flourishing spring': spring greenery becomes twisted green tea leaves in your cup.

etymology_story.zh: kasbah 经法语借自阿拉伯语 qaṣba，意为“城塞”。这一名称后来也用于城塞周围的城区，或某些北非城市的历史街区。
etymology_story.en: Kasbah entered English through French from Arabic qaṣba, meaning 'citadel.' The name also came to denote districts surrounding a citadel or historic quarters in certain North African cities.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可再作有效拆分的借词；复数为 kasbahs。casbah 是异体拼写，复数为 casbahs；kasbah-like（像北非城堡的）是可按需构成的复合形容词，没有常用的前后缀派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, kasbah is an unanalyzed loanword; its plural is kasbahs. Casbah is an alternative spelling, with the plural casbahs; kasbah-like is a freely formed compound adjective, and there is no established common family of affixal derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: citadel（城塞）强调城市中的防御核心；fortress（堡垒）泛指坚固的军事据点；medina（麦地那；北非旧城）指传统旧城区，其范围与 kasbah 可能重叠，但不必以城塞为核心。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Citadel emphasizes a city's defensive stronghold; fortress is a general term for a heavily fortified place; medina denotes a traditional old urban district, which may overlap with a kasbah but need not center on a citadel.

etymology_story.zh: pandit 经印地语 paṇḍit 借自梵语 paṇḍita，意为“博学的”或“学者”。它在英语中保留了印度传统学者及尊称的用法；同源形式 pundit 则进一步发展出“专家、时事评论员”的含义。
etymology_story.en: Pandit comes through Hindi paṇḍit from Sanskrit paṇḍita, meaning 'learned' or 'a learned person.' It retains its Indian scholarly and honorific uses in English, while the related form pundit developed the broader meaning of an expert or commentator.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 pandit 是不可再作有效拆分的借词，复数为 pandits，作姓名前的尊称时通常大写为 Pandit。同源形式 pundit 可派生 punditry（专家评论；评论界）；punditry 不宜直接解释为现代 pandit 的常规派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, pandit is an unanalyzed loanword, with the plural pandits; it is normally capitalized as Pandit when used before a name. The related form pundit produces punditry, meaning expert commentary or the activity of commentators; punditry is not a regular direct derivative of modern pandit.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: scholar（学者）泛指从事深入学术研究的人；pundit（专家；评论员）在现代英语中常指公开发表评论的专家；guru（导师；大师）强调指导者身份，不必具有 pandit 所指的经典学问背景。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Scholar broadly denotes someone with advanced academic learning; pundit commonly means an expert who comments publicly; guru emphasizes spiritual guidance or recognized expertise and does not necessarily imply a pandit's knowledge of traditional texts.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心是“博学之人”：精通经典可称 pandit，受尊敬的大师可冠以 Pandit。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to 'a learned person': expertise in traditional texts gives pandit, and public respect gives the title Pandit.

etymology.text: 英语借自法语 transhumance，其动词经西班牙语 trashumar 追溯到拉丁语 trans- 和 humus（土地）。可想象羊群随季节跨越不同牧场。

senses.meaning_zh: 季节性转场放牧；牲畜在不同季节牧场之间的定期迁移
senses.meaning_en: the seasonal movement of livestock between different grazing areas
senses.english_definition: Transhumance is the practice of moving livestock between different grazing areas with the seasons, often between lowland winter pastures and upland summer pastures.
senses.collocation_en: seasonal transhumance; the practice of transhumance

etymology_story.zh: transhumance 借自法语，其相关动词经西班牙语 trashumar 追溯到拉丁语 trans（跨越）和 humus（土地）。这个名称体现了牧群随季节在不同土地和牧场之间迁移的做法。
etymology_story.en: Transhumance was borrowed from French; its associated verb traces through Spanish trashumar to Latin trans, 'across,' and humus, 'ground.' The name reflects the seasonal movement of livestock across different lands and pastures.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中以 transhumance 为借入的专业词整体使用；可作历史构词分析 trans-（跨越）+ hum-（土地）+ -ance（活动或状态名词结尾），但 hum- 不是现代英语中的自由词根。常见同族词 transhumant 可作形容词，意为“实行季节性转场放牧的”，也可作名词，指“转场牧民”；另有较少见的动词 transhume（进行季节性转场）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English uses transhumance as a borrowed technical term. Its historical structure can be represented as trans- 'across' + hum- 'ground' + -ance, an activity or state ending, although hum- is not a free-standing modern English root. The main related word is transhumant, an adjective meaning 'practicing seasonal livestock migration' and a noun meaning a person who does so; the verb transhume is less common.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: seasonal livestock migration（牲畜季节性迁移）是直接的解释性近义表达；pastoral nomadism（游牧）通常涉及牧民家庭或群体更广泛的迁徙；pastoralism（畜牧生计方式）范围更广，不一定包含季节性迁移。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Seasonal livestock migration is a close explanatory equivalent; pastoral nomadism generally involves broader movements of pastoral households or communities; pastoralism is the wider livestock-based way of life and does not necessarily involve seasonal migration.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: trans＝跨越，hum＝土地：羊群随季节跨牧场，夏上山、冬下山。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Trans means 'across' and hum refers to ground: picture herds crossing pastures with the seasons, uphill in summer and downhill in winter.

meaning: 安色尔字体的；圆体大写字母的
aliases: 安色尔字体的；圆体大写字母的

pronunciation.note: 重音在首音节 /ʌn/；后面的 cial 合读 /ʃəl/，不要逐个字母拆读。

family: uncially 以安色尔字体。

morphology.text: uncial + -ly → uncially（以安色尔字体）；uncial 整词作为独立词素记忆，不拆成 un- 否定前缀。

etymology.text: 经晚期拉丁语 unciales litterae 传入，uncialis 原指“一盎司重的”，与 uncia（十二分之一；盎司）有关。后来这个名称用于圆润的大写书体。

usage_note: 本课为字体形容词；常修饰 letters、script、hand。它不是 unusual 的近义词，也不能按 un- 解释为否定。

senses.meaning_zh: 安色尔字体的；古代圆体大写书体的
senses.meaning_en: relating to an ancient style of rounded capital lettering
senses.english_definition: Uncial letters are written in an ancient style of rounded capital lettering used especially in Greek and Latin manuscripts.

senses.pos: n. 可数及不可数名词
senses.meaning_zh: 安色尔体字母；安色尔书体
senses.meaning_en: a rounded capital letter of an ancient script, or the script itself
senses.english_definition: An uncial is a letter in an ancient rounded capital script, and uncial is also the name of that style of writing.
senses.collocation_zh: 用安色尔体字母书写；拉丁安色尔书体
senses.sentence_en: The heading was written in uncials.
senses.sentence_zh: 标题用安色尔体字母写成。

senses.meaning_zh: 用安色尔书体写成的古代手稿，尤指希腊文《圣经》抄本
senses.meaning_en: an ancient manuscript written in uncial letters, especially a Greek biblical manuscript
senses.english_definition: An uncial is an ancient manuscript written in uncial letters, especially a Greek manuscript of the Bible.
senses.collocation_en: a Greek uncial; early biblical uncials
senses.collocation_zh: 希腊文安色尔体抄本；早期安色尔体《圣经》抄本
senses.sentence_en: The scholar compared the reading with those found in several early uncials.
senses.sentence_zh: 这位学者将这一文本异文与几份早期安色尔体抄本中的异文作了比较。

etymology_story.zh: uncial 源自晚期拉丁语 uncialis，与 uncia（十二分之一；盎司；英寸）有关；unciales litterae 常被解释为“英寸高的字母”，但这一历史表述的确切含义仍有争议。该名称后来专指某类古代圆体大写书体，并进一步指其字母和抄本。
etymology_story.en: Uncial derives from Late Latin uncialis, related to uncia, 'a twelfth part, an ounce, or an inch'; unciales litterae is often interpreted as 'inch-high letters,' though the exact historical meaning is disputed. The name later became associated with a particular ancient rounded capital script and, by extension, its letters and manuscripts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 uncial 作为整体词干使用，不能拆成否定前缀 un- 加其他成分。名词复数为 uncials；罕见副词 uncially 表示“以安色尔书体”；相关术语有 half-uncial 和 semi-uncial（半安色尔书体，或该书体的），指相关但不同的书写传统。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats uncial as a whole stem; its beginning is not the negative prefix un-. The countable noun has the plural uncials; the rare adverb uncially means 'in uncial lettering.' Related terms include half-uncial and semi-uncial, used as nouns or adjectives for related but distinct writing traditions.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: majuscule（大写字母；大写书体）范围更广，uncial 是其中一种；capital letter（大写字母）是日常通称，不限定历史书体；half-uncial（半安色尔书体）是相关但不同的书体，并非 uncial 的完全同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Majuscule is the broader term for capital lettering or a capital script, of which uncial is one variety; capital letter is the everyday term and specifies no historical style; half-uncial names a related but distinct script rather than an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 借“英寸高的字母”这一传统解释，想象一排大而圆的古抄本字母；同一个词还能指这些字母写成的抄本。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the traditional 'inch-high letters' interpretation to picture large, rounded manuscript letters; the same word can also name a manuscript written in them.

senses.english_definition: Whitsunday is the Christian festival held seven weeks after Easter to remember the coming of the Holy Spirit to Jesus's disciples.

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自古英语 hwīta sunnandæg，字面意思是“白色星期日”。这一名称通常被认为与新受洗者穿白袍的习俗有关，但具体命名缘由并非完全确定。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Old English hwīta sunnandæg, literally 'white Sunday'. The name is usually associated with the white clothes worn by newly baptized people, although its precise motivation is not entirely certain.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为固定节日名称整体使用；历史构成为 white（白色）+ Sunday（星期日），其中 white 保留为 Whit-。相关形式有 Whit Sunday（分写形式）、Whitsun（缩略形式）、Whitsuntide（圣灵降临节期间）和 Whit Monday（圣灵降临节后的星期一）；这些形式不代表 Whit- 是现代英语中可自由使用的前缀。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Whitsunday functions as a fixed festival name; historically, it combines white and Sunday, with white preserved as Whit-. Related forms include Whit Sunday, the shortened Whitsun, Whitsuntide for the festival period, and Whit Monday for the following Monday; Whit- is not a freely productive modern prefix.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Pentecost（五旬节、圣灵降临节）是更通行的教会名称；Whit Sunday 与 Whitsunday 同义，只是分写；Whitsun 尤见于英国英语，也可泛指相关节期。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pentecost is the more widely used ecclesiastical name; Whit Sunday is an alternative spacing with the same meaning; Whitsun is especially British and can also refer more broadly to the festival period.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Whit- 联系 white：想象白袍受洗者在星期日参加圣灵降临节礼拜。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect Whit- with white: picture newly baptized people in white at a Pentecost Sunday service.

fields.wrong_reason: 同一 zillah 下有多个村庄，因此指行政区而不是某个村庄。

senses.meaning_zh: 南亚的行政区、县区，尤见于有关印度的历史文献
senses.meaning_en: an administrative district in South Asia, especially in historical accounts of India
senses.english_definition: A zillah is an administrative district in parts of South Asia, especially one described in historical writing about India.
senses.collocation_en: a zillah court; the collector of a zillah
senses.collocation_zh: 县区法院；县区行政长官
senses.sentence_en: The old report lists the villages within each zillah.

etymology_story.zh: 英语经印地语、乌尔都语中的 zilā 一类形式借入该词，最终源于阿拉伯语 ḍilʿ，意为“肋骨、侧面或部分”。其行政含义体现了把较大区域划分为若干部分的概念。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word through Hindi and Urdu forms such as zilā, ultimately from Arabic ḍilʿ, meaning 'rib, side, or part'. Its administrative meaning reflects the idea of a territorial subdivision.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可进一步拆分的借词：zillah；复数为 zillahs。相关拼写有 zila、zilla；历史行政用语 zilladar 或 zillahdar 指地区官员，其中 -dar 是表示持有者或掌管者的波斯语来源成分，并非普通英语后缀。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, zillah is an unanalyzed loanword, with the plural zillahs. Related spellings include zila and zilla; the historical administrative terms zilladar and zillahdar denote a district official and contain Persian-derived -dar, meaning a holder or person in charge, rather than an ordinary English suffix.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: district（地区、行政区）是最接近的通用对应词；administrative division（行政区划单位）范围更广，不限定层级；county（县、郡）只能作为便于理解的类比，不能保证行政制度或级别相同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: District is the closest general equivalent; administrative division is broader and does not specify a particular tier; county offers a useful comparison but does not imply an identical administrative system or rank.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“一个部分”联想到“国土划出的一部分”，即县区。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'one part of a larger territory': an administrative district.

aliases: 鹰属猛禽；短翼长尾的林栖鹰

etymology.text: 英语从新拉丁语借入，追溯到拉丁语 accipiter，意思是“鹰”。记住林间敏捷飞行的鹰即可，不必按现代英语硬拆。

senses.meaning_zh: 短翼长尾、善于在林间捕猎的鹰类
senses.meaning_en: a short-winged, long-tailed hawk adapted for hunting among trees
senses.english_definition: An accipiter is a hawk whose short, rounded wings and long tail help it turn quickly while hunting among trees.
senses.collocation_zh: 林栖鹰类；短翼长尾鹰类的辨识

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自拉丁语 accipiter，意思是“鹰”，并通过鸟类学的拉丁命名传统进入英语专业词汇。它在英语中用于描述以短翼、长尾和灵活林间飞行为特点的鹰类。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin accipiter, meaning 'hawk', and entered specialist English through the Latin naming tradition of ornithology. In English, it describes hawks associated with short wings, long tails, and agile flight among trees.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中应整体识记 accipiter，不宜硬拆成英语前缀和词根；复数为 accipiters。拉丁语斜格词干 accipitr- 加形容词后缀 -ine 构成 accipitrine（鹰类的、似鹰的）；大写斜体形式 Accipiter 用作动物属名。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat accipiter as a whole borrowed base in modern English, rather than forcing an English prefix-and-root analysis; its plural is accipiters. The Latin oblique stem accipitr- combines with -ine in accipitrine, meaning relating to or resembling hawks; capitalized, italicized Accipiter is used as a zoological genus name.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hawk（鹰）是较宽泛的对应词；goshawk（苍鹰）和 sparrowhawk（雀鹰）是相关鹰类的具体名称，而非所有 accipiter 都可互换使用的同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hawk is a broader equivalent; goshawk and sparrowhawk name particular related kinds of hawk and are not interchangeable synonyms for every accipiter.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住形态组合：短翼便于转弯，长尾帮助掌舵——林间敏捷的鹰。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the shape: short wings for turning, a long tail for steering—a hawk built for woodland agility.

senses.meaning_zh: 大学礼官；在典礼中执杖、引导队伍等的校方官员
senses.meaning_en: a university official with ceremonial duties, such as carrying a mace or leading processions
senses.english_definition: A bedel is an official at some universities who performs ceremonial duties, such as carrying a mace and leading an academic procession.
senses.collocation_en: a university bedel; the office of bedel

etymology_story.zh: 该词延续了中古英语 bedel 一类形式，与 beadle 有共同的历史渊源，更早属于表示宣告或传唤的日耳曼语词族。由传令、召集人员的职务，发展出大学礼仪官员这一专门含义。
etymology_story.en: The word continues Middle English forms such as bedel and shares its history with beadle, ultimately belonging to a Germanic word family associated with announcing or summoning. The role of a messenger or summoning officer developed into the specialized university ceremonial office.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 bedel 是整体词干，不拆为 bed + -el；复数为 bedels。相关拼写为 bedell，历史相关词为 beadle；bedel + -ship 可构成 bedelship（礼官的职位或任职身份），但该派生词较少见。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, bedel is a whole lexical base, not bed plus -el; its plural is bedels. Bedell is a related spelling, and beadle is historically related; bedel plus -ship forms the uncommon bedelship, meaning the office or status of a bedel.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: beadle（礼官、教区或机构职员）历史相关，但适用机构更广；mace-bearer（执杖官）强调携带仪仗权杖的职责；ceremonial officer（礼仪官）是范围更广的职务描述。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Beadle is historically related but applies to a wider range of institutions; mace-bearer emphasizes the duty of carrying a ceremonial mace; ceremonial officer is a broader description of the role.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“传唤、引导众人”联想到“带领大学典礼队伍的礼官”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect summoning and guiding people with the official who leads a university procession.

pronunciation.note: 采用保留法语鼻化元音的读法 /blɑ̃ˈkɛt/；重音在后面的音节。

forms: 表示菜肴时可作不可数名词；指一份或一种做法时可数，复数 blanquettes。
family: blanc 法语“白色的”；blanquette de veau 白汁炖小牛肉。

morphology.text: 历史奥克语 blanc（白）+ -et（小称后缀）→ blanquet（略白的）；其阴性名词形式经法语传入，成为 blanquette（白汁炖菜）。

etymology.text: 英语借自法语，法语又借自普罗旺斯奥克语 blanqueto，词根与“白色”有关。用浅色肉配白酱的画面来记。

usage_note: 法国菜名，常见 blanquette of veal；重点是白汁炖制，不是任意肉汤。音标采用英语常见读法，法语借词有鼻化等发音差异。

etymology_story.zh: 英语从法语借入 blanquette，这个名称与表示“白色”的 blanc 词族有关。烹饪义对应菜肴和酱汁的浅白色；同一名称也用于法国利穆一带的白起泡酒。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed blanquette from French, where the name belongs to the word family of blanc, meaning 'white'. The culinary use reflects the pale dish and sauce; the same name is also used for a sparkling white wine from the Limoux area of France.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 blanquette 是整体借词，复数为 blanquettes，没有常用的英语动词或形容词派生形式。从法语构词角度，可联系 blanc（白色）和小称后缀 -ette；这不是现代英语中可自由套用的构词公式。相关固定名称有 blanquette de veau（白汁炖小牛肉）和 Blanquette de Limoux（利穆布朗凯特起泡酒）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, blanquette is a whole loanword, with the plural blanquettes and no common English verb or adjective derivatives. Its French formation connects blanc, meaning 'white', with the diminutive suffix -ette; this is not a freely productive English construction. Related fixed names include blanquette de veau for the veal dish and Blanquette de Limoux for the sparkling wine.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: white stew（白汁炖菜）是烹饪义的描述性近义表达；fricassee（白汁烩肉）是相近菜式，但具体烹调方法不一定相同；sparkling white wine（白起泡酒）是酒类义的上位词，不能单独限定为利穆产酒。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: White stew is a descriptive near-equivalent for the dish; fricassee names a related preparation whose cooking method may differ; sparkling white wine is the broader category for the wine sense and does not specifically identify a wine from Limoux.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 联系法语 blanc“白”：白汁炖菜，一杯白起泡酒。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link it to French blanc, 'white': a white-sauce stew and a glass of sparkling white wine.

pronunciation.note: 这是单音节词；中间元音读长音 /iː/，词尾 e 不另成音节。

morphology.text: brede 整词作为独立词素记忆，是 braid 的古旧变体；相关词派生 braid + -ed → braided（编织的）。

etymology.text: 它是英语 braid 的历史变体；braid 经中古英语 breyden 追溯到古英语 bregdan，早有编织、交错之意。可用交错针线联想刺绣。

usage_note: 古旧或文学用词，本课为刺绣装饰；它与 breed 同音，但词义不同，现代写作一般用 embroidery。

etymology_story.zh: brede 是 braid 的历史变体，最终与古英语 bregdan 有关，该动词曾表示迅速移动、扭转和编结等动作。其名词意义由交织的带饰延伸到刺绣及其他交错排列的装饰。
etymology_story.en: Brede is a historical variant of braid, ultimately associated with Old English bregdan, a verb with meanings including moving quickly, twisting, and weaving. The noun developed from interwoven ornament into embroidery and other decorative interlacings.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中视为不可再拆的词干 brede；可数用法的复数为 bredes。它没有常用的独立派生词族；历史相关词族包括 braid（编结；辫子）、braided（编成辫状的）、braiding（编结；编结饰带）和 braider（编结者），这些并非由 brede 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, brede is an unanalyzed stem; its countable plural is bredes. It has no commonly used independent derivative family. Historically related forms include braid, braided, braiding, and braider, but these are not direct derivatives of brede.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: embroidery（刺绣）强调针线绣制的工艺或成品；braid（编带、辫状饰带）强调条状交织结构；interlacing（交织纹样）强调相互穿插的图案。brede 是带有古雅或诗歌色彩的概括性称呼。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Embroidery emphasizes decoration made with stitches; braid emphasizes a narrow woven or plaited structure; interlacing emphasizes a pattern of crossing strands. Brede is an archaic or poetic term that can cover such intertwined ornament.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 brede 与历史相关的 braid 相连：线交织成带，带又成为绣饰。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect brede with its historical relative braid: interwoven threads become a band, then an ornament.

etymology_story.en: The singular carpus entered English through anatomical Latin from Greek karpos, meaning 'wrist.' Carpi preserves the Latin second-declension plural ending -i.

morphology_enriched.zh: carpus → carpi：将拉丁式单数词尾 -us 换为复数词尾 -i，并非在整个单数后直接加后缀。相关词族和构词成分包括 carp-／carpo-（腕）、carpal（腕的；腕骨）、metacarpus（掌部骨骼整体）、metacarpal（掌骨的；掌骨）和 carpometacarpal（腕掌的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Carpus → carpi replaces the Latin singular ending -us with plural -i; it does not simply append a suffix to the complete singular. Related forms and combining elements include carp-/carpo- ('wrist'), carpal, metacarpus, metacarpal, and carpometacarpal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: wrists（手腕）是日常对应词，通常指整个腕部；carpal bones（腕骨）明确指构成腕部的骨头；wrist joints（腕关节）强调关节结构。carpi 是专业复数，可指多个腕部或其腕骨整体，并非单块腕骨的普通复数。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Wrists is the everyday equivalent and usually refers to the whole regions; carpal bones specifies the bones within them; wrist joints emphasizes the articulations. Carpi is a technical plural for multiple wrists or their bony groups, rather than the ordinary plural for individual wrist bones.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: carp- 锁定“腕”，-i 提醒“复数”：把左右两个腕部一起看。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Carp- points to the wrist; -i signals more than one: picture both wrists together.

etymology_story.zh: 表示马的 cayuse 来自族名 Cayuse，反映了该族与北美西部马匹文化的联系。英语将族名转用于相关的小型马，后来也可泛指西部瘦小或粗劣的马。
etymology_story.en: The horse term cayuse comes from the name of the Cayuse people, reflecting their association with horse culture in western North America. English transferred the people's name to small horses associated with them and later used it more broadly, sometimes disparagingly.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 cayuse 是不可再拆的借入词干，没有可辨认的英语前后缀。马义复数为 cayuses；族人义通常用 Cayuse 或 Cayuses；语言名 Cayuse 不作普通可数名词使用。没有常用的直接派生词族；Cayuse horse、Cayuse people 和 Cayuse language 是相关名词短语。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, cayuse is an unanalyzed borrowed stem with no identifiable English affixes. The horse plural is cayuses; the plural for people is Cayuse or Cayuses; the language name Cayuse is not ordinarily countable. There is no commonly used direct derivative family; Cayuse horse, Cayuse people, and Cayuse language are related noun phrases.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 马义近义词包括 pony（小马，主要强调体型）、mustang（北美野化马，强调自由生存的背景）和 bronco（未驯服或尚未充分驯服的马，强调驯化状态）。它们与 cayuse 的所指可能重叠，但并不等同；族名和语言名没有可直接替换的近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the horse sense, pony emphasizes small size, mustang identifies a free-ranging horse of North America, and bronco emphasizes an unbroken or insufficiently trained horse. These categories can overlap with cayuse but are not equivalent; the people's name and language name have no interchangeable synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先记大写 Cayuse 是族名，再记小写 cayuse 是由族名转来的西部小马名。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with capitalized Cayuse, the people's name; lowercase cayuse transfers that name to a western horse.

meaning: 支序分类学；分支分类学
aliases: 支序分类学；分支分类学
按演化亲缘关系分类的方法

pronunciation.note: 重音在第二音节 /dɪs/；开头 cla 弱读 /klə/，末尾 /tɪks/ 不要漏掉 /k/。

forms: 以 -s 结尾但学科名按单数使用，如 cladistics is。
family: cladistic 支序分类的；cladist 支序分类学研究者；cladism 支序分类方法。

morphology.text: clad-（演化支，来自 clade）+ -ist（研究者）+ -ics（学科）→ cladistics（支序分类学）。

etymology.text: 这是现代生物学术语，由 clade 及表示方法、学科的后缀形成；clade 的希腊语源头 klados 意为“树枝”。把亲缘关系画成分叉树来记。

usage_note: 强调依据共有衍生特征推断共同祖先和演化分支，不是只看外表相似。学科名虽有 -s，谓语通常为单数。

senses.pos: n. 名词（不可数，通常接单数谓语）
senses.meaning_zh: 支序分类学；依据共有衍征识别共同祖先及其后代关系的分类方法
senses.meaning_en: A method of biological classification that identifies evolutionary groups through shared derived characteristics.
senses.english_definition: Cladistics is a method of classifying organisms by using shared derived characteristics to identify groups descended from a common ancestor.
senses.collocation_en: use cladistics; the principles of cladistics
senses.collocation_zh: 采用支序分类法；支序分类学的原理
senses.sentence_en: Researchers used cladistics to investigate the evolutionary relationships among the fossils.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员采用支序分类法，研究这些化石所代表生物之间的演化关系。

etymology_story.zh: cladistics 属于现代演化生物学术语词族，其基础 clade 最终源自希腊语 klados，意为“树枝”。树枝的形象被用于表示共同祖先及其后代构成的演化分支，进而形成相关分类方法的名称。
etymology_story.en: Cladistics belongs to a modern evolutionary vocabulary based on clade, ultimately from Greek klados, meaning 'branch.' The branching image came to represent a common ancestor and its descendants and underlies the name of this classification method.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可分析为 clad-（与 clade“演化支”对应的词干）+ -istic（形容词构形成分）+ -s（学科或方法名称中的词尾）；也可直接记作 cladistic + -s。相关词族包括 clade（演化支）、cladistic（支序分类的）、cladistically（按支序分类法）、cladist（支序分类学者）、cladogram（支序图）和 cladogenesis（分支演化）。
morphology_enriched.en: A useful analysis is clad- (the stem associated with clade) + -istic (an adjective-forming element) + -s (an ending used in names of disciplines or methods), or simply cladistic + -s. Related forms include clade, cladistic, cladistically, cladist, cladogram, and cladogenesis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cladistic analysis（支序分析）强调具体分析过程；phylogenetic systematics（系统发育系统学）强调依据共同祖先关系建立分类体系，与 cladistics 密切相关；phylogenetics（系统发育学）范围更广，还包括其他重建和研究演化关系的方法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cladistic analysis emphasizes the analytical procedure; phylogenetic systematics emphasizes classification by common ancestry and is closely associated with cladistics; phylogenetics is broader and includes other approaches to reconstructing and studying evolutionary relationships.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: clad- 是“枝”：用共有的新特征，找出生物在演化树上属于哪一枝。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Clad- means 'branch': shared derived traits help locate organisms on the same evolutionary branch.

etymology_story.zh: coteau 借自法语，在北美地理语境中尤其与加拿大法语的使用有关；其历史形式可追溯到古法语 costel，与表示“侧面、坡面”的 coste 有关，最终源自拉丁语 costa“肋骨、侧面”。coteaux 保留了法语的复数拼写。
etymology_story.en: Coteau was borrowed from French, with Canadian French especially relevant to its North American geographical use; it goes back to Old French costel, related to coste, 'side' or 'slope,' ultimately from Latin costa, 'rib' or 'side.' Coteaux preserves the French plural spelling.

morphology_enriched.zh: coteau → coteaux：在法语借词的单数形式后加 -x，构成保留法语拼写的复数；英语也使用规则复数 coteaus。其法语内部虽有历史构词关系，现代英语中不宜把 coteau 强拆成英语词根和后缀；没有常用的英语直接派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Coteau → coteaux adds -x to form a plural retaining French spelling; English also uses the regular plural coteaus. Although the French word has an internal historical formation, coteau is not usefully divided into English roots and affixes. It has no commonly used direct English derivative family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: uplands（高地）强调相对于周边地区较高的位置；hillsides（山坡）强调山丘的坡面；escarpments（陡坡、陡崖）强调明显而陡峭的高差。coteaux 是带有地域和地理专业色彩的名称，所指地形不一定陡峭。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Uplands emphasizes ground elevated above its surroundings; hillsides identifies the sloping sides of hills; escarpments emphasizes a steep, distinct change in elevation. Coteaux is a regional geographical term and does not necessarily imply steep terrain.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“侧面”联想到高地的坡面；词尾 -x 提醒这是多个 coteau。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Move from 'side' to the sloping side of higher ground; final -x marks more than one coteau.

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代国际科学词汇，由 deoxy-（脱氧的）和 ribose（核糖）组成，名称标示它与核糖之间的氧原子数量差异。[韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/deoxyribose)将其英语首见用例记为 1938 年。
etymology_story.en: This modern international scientific term combines deoxy-, indicating the loss of oxygen, with ribose, naming the corresponding sugar with one fewer oxygen atom. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/deoxyribose) dates its first known English use to 1938.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：deoxy-（脱氧的）+ ribose（核糖）→ deoxyribose（脱氧核糖）；这里的 ribose 是完整糖名，不宜机械拆分。相关形式：deoxyribosyl（脱氧核糖基）；共享生化词干的相关词包括 deoxyribonucleoside（脱氧核糖核苷）、deoxyribonucleotide（脱氧核糖核苷酸）和 deoxyribonucleic acid（脱氧核糖核酸，DNA），它们不是简单在完整词后添加后缀形成的。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: deoxy- (having less oxygen) + ribose (the sugar name) → deoxyribose. Related forms include deoxyribosyl, denoting a group derived from the sugar; deoxyribonucleoside, deoxyribonucleotide, and deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) share the biochemical stem rather than being simple suffix derivatives of the complete word.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 2-deoxyribose（2-脱氧核糖）是通常所指物质的更明确名称，标明缺氧位置；desoxyribose 是较旧的同义名称。ribose（核糖）是相关但不同的糖，不能作为同义词替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: 2-deoxyribose is the more explicit name for the substance normally intended, specifying the position of oxygen loss; desoxyribose is an older synonym. Ribose is a related but chemically different sugar, not an interchangeable synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: deoxy- 提醒“少一个氧”：核糖少一个氧，就是 DNA 中的脱氧核糖。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Deoxy- signals one fewer oxygen: ribose minus one oxygen gives the sugar in DNA.

senses.meaning_zh: 内温动物；主要依靠体内代谢产热的动物

senses.collocation_zh: 鸟类和哺乳动物属于内温动物；小型内温动物

senses.sentence_zh: 小鼠属于内温动物，会利用食物提供的能量来帮助维持体温。

etymology_story.zh: 这是由希腊语来源的构词成分 endo-（内部）和 therm-（热）组成的现代动物学术语，用内部产热这一特征命名动物。[韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/endotherm)将其英语首见用例记为 1940 年。
etymology_story.en: This modern zoological term combines Greek-derived endo- (within) and therm- (heat), naming an animal by its internal production of heat. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/endotherm) dates its first known English use to 1940.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：endo-（内部）+ -therm（与热有关的生物）→ endotherm；复数为 endotherms。相关词族：endothermy（内温性）、endothermic（内温的；在化学中也指吸热的）、endothermically（以内温方式；以吸热方式）；endothermic 的具体意义取决于学科语境。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: endo- (within) + -therm (an organism characterized by a source of heat) → endotherm; plural: endotherms. Related forms are endothermy, endothermic, and endothermically; endothermic concerns internal heat production in biology but heat absorption in chemistry.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: warm-blooded animal（温血动物）是日常近义表达，但科学精度较低；homeotherm（恒温动物）是相关概念，强调体温相对稳定，而 endotherm 强调热量来源，因此二者不能完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Warm-blooded animal is the everyday near-equivalent but is less precise scientifically. Homeotherm is a related term emphasizing relatively stable body temperature, whereas endotherm identifies the source of heat; the two are not exact synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: endo- 在内，therm- 是热：身体内部自己产热。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Endo- means inside and therm- means heat: the animal makes its heat within.

pronunciation.note: 这是单音节词；aa 在这里读双元音 /eɪ/，不要把两个 a 分成两个音节。

etymology.text: 中古英语已有 greal、graal，来自中古法语的器皿名称，更早追溯到中世纪拉丁语 gradalis。后来这个容器名进入骑士寻找圣杯的传说。

etymology_story.zh: Graal 保留了古法语 graal 的拼写，该词原指大浅盘或容器，通常追溯到中世纪拉丁语 gradalis；这种器皿后来成为亚瑟王传奇中的神圣宝物。[词源说明](https://www.etymonline.com/word/grail)；[柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/graal)将 Graal 列为 Grail 的古旧拼写。
etymology_story.en: Graal preserves the spelling of Old French graal, originally a large shallow dish or vessel, usually traced to Medieval Latin gradalis; the vessel became a sacred object in Arthurian legend. See the [etymological account](https://www.etymonline.com/word/grail) and [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/graal), which identifies Graal as an archaic spelling of Grail.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中视为不可再分析的借入词，没有可独立切分的英语前缀或后缀。Grail 是现代常用拼写，Holy Graal 和 Holy Grail 是对应复合名称；没有常用的 Graal 派生词族，Grail 的现代比喻用法不应自动视为 Graal 的常用义。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Graal is an unanalyzed borrowing without separable English prefixes or suffixes. Grail is the usual modern spelling, and Holy Graal and Holy Grail are corresponding compound names; Graal has no common productive derivative family, and modern figurative uses of Grail should not automatically be treated as common senses of Graal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Grail（圣杯）是现代标准拼写；Holy Grail（圣杯）是完整名称，更明确地突出其神圣性质。chalice（圣餐杯）指一种宗教用杯，并不专指传说中的这件圣物。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Grail is the standard modern spelling; Holy Grail is the fuller name and explicitly emphasizes sacredness. Chalice names a type of ceremonial cup and does not specifically identify this legendary object.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Graal is Grail in medieval dress: picture a knight searching for the sacred vessel.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由表示衣片或垂片的 lap 与小称后缀 -et 构成，核心形象是“小片、小瓣”；历史上也用于身体的瓣状部分。[柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/lappet)记录了衣饰、动物身体结构和纺织方面的用法。
etymology_story.en: The word combines lap, meaning a flap or hanging piece, with the diminutive suffix -et, giving the central image of a small flap or lobe; it has also historically described bodily lobes. [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/lappet) records clothing, anatomical, and textile uses.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：lap（衣片、垂片）+ -et（小称后缀，词干末尾 p 双写）→ lappet。复数 lappets；派生形容词 lappeted（有垂片或垂瓣的）；常见复合形式包括 lappet moth（枯叶蛾）、lappet-faced vulture（肉垂秃鹫）、lappet weaving（绞绣织造）和 lappet loom（绞绣织机）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: lap (a flap) + diminutive -et, with the final p doubled → lappet. Forms include plural lappets and adjective lappeted (having lappets); established compounds include lappet moth, lappet-faced vulture, lappet weaving, and lappet loom.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: flap（垂片、片状物）最宽泛；tab（小襻、小片）常带有固定、拉取或标识用途；lobe（瓣、叶状部分）多指身体或器官的圆钝部分。lappet 特别强调小型垂片或瓣状结构，这些近义词不适用于其纺织设备和织物义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Flap is the broadest term for a loose projecting piece; tab often suggests a small piece used for fastening, pulling, or identification; lobe usually denotes a rounded bodily or anatomical division. Lappet emphasizes a small hanging flap or lobe, and these near-synonyms do not cover its textile machinery and fabric senses.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: lap 是垂片，-et 表示小：帽边一小片，动物身上一小瓣。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Lap means flap and -et makes it small: a little flap on a cap or a little lobe on an animal.

etymology_story.en: Mangel is a shortening of mangel-wurzel, borrowed from German Mangelwurzel, an alteration of Mangoldwurzel, combining Mangold, meaning beet, and Wurzel, meaning root. The shortened English name retained the meaning of a beet grown for animal feed. [Etymological source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/mangel-wurzel)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 mangel 视为不可再分析的借入词基，没有常用的英语前后缀拆分。屈折形式：mangel → mangels（复数）；相关全称和异体包括 mangel-wurzel、mangelwurzel、mangold-wurzel 和 mangold，均指饲用甜菜，没有常用的动词、形容词或副词派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, mangel functions as an unanalyzed borrowed base, without a productive English prefix–suffix breakdown. Its plural is mangels; related full forms and variants include mangel-wurzel, mangelwurzel, mangold-wurzel, and mangold, all referring to the fodder beet. It has no established common verb, adjective, or adverb derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: mangel-wurzel（饲用甜菜）是同义全称；fodder beet（饲用甜菜）突出饲料用途；sugar beet（糖用甜菜）则主要用于制糖，是相关作物名称，并非严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mangel-wurzel is the synonymous full form; fodder beet emphasizes agricultural use as animal feed. Sugar beet names a related crop grown primarily for sugar production and is not an exact synonym.

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自拉丁语 multiparus，由 multi-（多）和与 parere（生育、产生）有关的 -parus 构成。英语早期用于表示一胎多仔，后来也用于描述既往分娩经历及植物花序的多个侧轴。[词源与义项来源：Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/multiparous)、[Dictionary.com](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/multiparous)
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin multiparus, combining multi-, meaning many, with -parus, connected with parere, meaning to give birth or produce. Early English use concerned several young at one birth; additional uses concern previous childbirths and multiple lateral axes in flower clusters. [Sources: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/multiparous), [Dictionary.com](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/multiparous)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：multi-（多）+ -parous（生育的、产生的）→ multiparous。核心词族：multiparity（多产；多次分娩的状态）、multipara（经产妇，复数 multiparas 或 multiparae）；相关对比词包括 primiparous（初产的）、nulliparous（未产的）、uniparous（一胎一仔的）和 multigravida（多次妊娠妇女，强调妊娠次数，不等同于多次分娩）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: multi- (many) + -parous (bearing or producing) → multiparous. Its core family includes multiparity (the condition of bearing multiple offspring or having multiple deliveries) and multipara (a woman who has given birth more than once; plural multiparas or multiparae). Related contrasts include primiparous, nulliparous, uniparous, and multigravida, which concerns repeated pregnancies rather than repeated deliveries.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 动物学中的 polytocous（一胎多仔的）最接近该义；产科学中的 parous（经产的）范围较广，只说明有过分娩经历；multigravid（多次妊娠的）强调怀孕次数，不能据此判断分娩次数。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Polytocous closely matches the zoological meaning of producing several young at one birth. Parous is broader in obstetrics, indicating previous childbirth; multigravid concerns multiple pregnancies and does not establish the number of deliveries.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: multi-＝多，-parous＝生：动物看一胎生几个，产科看分娩经历。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Multi- means many and -parous means bearing: count offspring per birth in zoology and childbirth history in obstetrics.

etymology.text: 经晚期拉丁语 pharisaicus，追溯到希腊语中表示法利赛人的名称。英语后来发展出批评自命正义、言行不一的比喻用法。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经教会拉丁语 pharisaicus 追溯至希腊语 pharisaikos，原指与法利赛派有关。其贬义来自基督教文本中对法利赛人的论争性描写，后来扩展为批评伪善或自命正义，并非对这一历史群体的中性概括。[词源来源：Etymonline](https://www.etymonline.com/word/pharisaic)、[义项来源：Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/pharisaic)
etymology_story.en: The word comes through ecclesiastical Latin pharisaicus from Greek pharisaikos and originally referred to the Pharisees. Its disparaging meaning developed from polemical Christian portrayals of that group and broadened to hypocrisy or self-righteousness, rather than providing a neutral historical description. [Etymological source: Etymonline](https://www.etymonline.com/word/pharisaic), [sense source: Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/pharisaic)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族分析：Pharisee（法利赛人）对应的词干 pharisai- + -ic（……的）→ pharisaic；pharisaic + -al → pharisaical（同义形容词）。相关形式包括 pharisaically（伪善地、自命清高地）、pharisaicalness（伪善、自命清高）和 Pharisaism／pharisaism（法利赛派教义；拘守形式或伪善）；Pharisees 是 Pharisee 的复数。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern word-family analysis: the stem pharisai-, corresponding to Pharisee, + -ic → pharisaic; adding -al gives the synonymous adjective pharisaical. Related forms include pharisaically, pharisaicalness, and Pharisaism/pharisaism, referring respectively to Pharisaic doctrine or, figuratively, formalism and hypocrisy. Pharisees is the plural of Pharisee.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sanctimonious（假装圣洁的）突出装出虔诚或高尚的样子；self-righteous（自以为正义的）强调确信自己道德优越，但未必言行不一；hypocritical（虚伪的）强调宣称的原则与实际行为不一致。pharisaic 常兼有道德优越感和拘守表面形式的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sanctimonious emphasizes an affected display of holiness or virtue; self-righteous emphasizes certainty of one's moral superiority without necessarily implying inconsistent conduct; hypocritical emphasizes a mismatch between professed principles and behavior. Pharisaic often combines moral superiority with outward formalism.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记比喻义的核心画面：把道德规则展示给别人，却忽略规则背后的善意；历史义则直接对应法利赛派。
mnemonic_anchor.en: For the figurative sense, picture someone displaying moral rules while overlooking their humane purpose; the historical sense simply refers to the Pharisees.

morphology.text: Adar 整词作为独立词素记忆；复合名称 Adar + Sheni（希伯来语“第二”）→ Adar Sheni（第二阿达尔月）。

etymology.text: 中古英语已从希伯来语 Ădhār 借入这个月名。记住它属于犹太历，而不是公历中的固定一个月。

etymology_story.zh: 英语在中古英语时期从希伯来语 Ădhār 借入这一月名。它一直保留犹太历月份的含义，与公历月份之间只有大致对应关系。[词源来源：Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/Adar)、[历法说明：Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/adar)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the month name from Hebrew Ădhār during the Middle English period. It has retained its Jewish calendar meaning and corresponds only approximately to Gregorian months. [Etymological source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/Adar), [calendar details: Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/adar)

morphology_enriched.zh: Adar 是完整借入的专有名词，在现代英语中不拆为 ad- 和 -ar，也没有常用派生词族。相关复合名称：Adar + Rishon（第一）→ Adar Rishon／Adar I（第一阿达尔月）；Adar + Sheni（第二）→ Adar Sheni／Adar II（第二阿达尔月）。
morphology_enriched.en: Adar is a borrowed proper noun, not a modern English combination of ad- and -ar, and it has no common derivational family. Related compound names are Adar + Rishon (first) → Adar Rishon/Adar I, and Adar + Sheni (second) → Adar Sheni/Adar II.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Adar 没有通常意义上的近义词。相关名称 Adar I／Adar Rishon 指闰年中的第一阿达尔月，Adar II／Adar Sheni 指第二阿达尔月；February（二月）和 March（三月）只是大致重叠的公历月份，并非同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Adar has no ordinary lexical synonyms. The related names Adar I/Adar Rishon identify the first Adar in a leap year, while Adar II/Adar Sheni identify the second; February and March merely overlap approximately and are not synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 Adar 放在尼散月之前：平年一个阿达尔月，闰年两个。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Place Adar before Nisan: one Adar in an ordinary year, two in a leap year.

etymology.text: 英语借自希伯来语 ădhōnāy，意思是“我的主”。这一称呼用于祷告或诵读中代读神名，保留着庄重的宗教语体。

usage_note: 称呼必须大写 A，用于相应宗教诵读语境；不要当作对老师、雇主等普通人的称呼。

senses.meaning_zh: 主；犹太教祷告及经文诵读中对上帝的尊称
senses.meaning_en: a reverential Hebrew title for God, meaning Lord
senses.english_definition: Adonai is a Hebrew title meaning Lord that Jewish worshippers use for God, including when reading the divine name YHWH aloud.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自希伯来语 ădhōnāy，通常译为“我的主”，与表示“主人、主”的 adon 有关。它在犹太教传统中成为对上帝的庄重称呼，并用于诵读时替代四字神名 YHWH。[词源与用法来源：Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/adonai)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Hebrew ădhōnāy, conventionally translated as my Lord and related to adon, meaning lord or master. In Jewish tradition it became a reverential title for God and a spoken substitute for the four-letter divine name YHWH. [Etymological and usage source: Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/adonai)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，Adonai 是整体借入的专有名词，没有可自由组合的英语词根与词缀，也没有常用的英语派生词族。希伯来语词基 adon 表示“主、主人”；相关转写形式有 Adonay 和体现某些诵读传统的 Adonoy，它们不是新增词性。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Adonai is a borrowed proper noun without freely combinable English roots and affixes or a common English derivational family. Its Hebrew base adon means lord or master; related transliterations include Adonay and Adonoy, the latter reflecting certain pronunciation traditions rather than a separate part of speech.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Lord（主）是最接近的英语译称；God（上帝）是更一般的称呼；HaShem（字面义“那名字”）也是犹太教对上帝的称呼，常用于日常谈论，而 Adonai 尤其用于祷告和礼仪诵读。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lord is the closest English rendering; God is a more general designation. HaShem, literally the Name, is another Jewish designation commonly used in ordinary discussion, whereas Adonai is particularly associated with prayer and liturgical reading.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: adon＝主：把 Adonai 记成诵经时使用的庄重称呼“我的主”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Adon means lord: remember Adonai as the reverent my Lord used in sacred reading.

meaning: 不伤害生命的原则；非暴力
aliases: 不伤害生命的原则；非暴力

pronunciation.note: 主重音在中间的 /hɪm/；开头 a 弱读 /ə/，末尾 sa 读 /sɑː/。

forms: 不可数抽象名词，通常不用复数。
family: himsa 伤害、暴力；nonviolence 非暴力。

morphology.text: 梵语 a-（不）+ himsa（伤害）→ ahimsa（不伤害）；英语整体借入。

etymology.text: 英语借自梵语 ahiṃsā，原意是“不伤害”。可用“连微小生命也尽量不伤害”的画面帮助记住这一伦理原则。

usage_note: 见于印度宗教和伦理思想，如印度教、佛教、耆那教；重点是不伤害生命，不只是保持沉默或避免争论。

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自梵语 ahiṃsā，由表示否定的 a- 与表示“伤害”的 hiṃsā 构成，字面意思是“不伤害”。这一概念植根于印度宗教伦理，后来也用于讨论非暴力的社会与政治实践。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Sanskrit ahiṃsā, formed from the negative prefix a- and hiṃsā, meaning “injury,” literally expressing non-injury. Rooted in Indian religious ethics, the concept also came to inform discussions of nonviolent social and political action.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 ahimsa 作为完整借词使用，不宜把其中的梵语成分当作英语中可自由组合的词素。它通常不可数；相关形容词 ahimsic 表示“非暴力的；遵循不害原则的”，但较少见。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats ahimsa as a complete loanword; its Sanskrit components are not freely productive English morphemes. It is normally uncountable; the related adjective ahimsic, meaning nonviolent or observing ahimsa, is uncommon.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: nonviolence（非暴力）侧重不使用暴力的原则或实践；non-injury（不伤害）最接近字面含义；pacifism（和平主义）主要指反对战争或暴力。ahimsa 尤其强调对生命的不伤害，具有鲜明的印度宗教伦理背景。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nonviolence emphasizes avoiding violence in principle or practice; non-injury most closely expresses the literal meaning; pacifism chiefly concerns opposition to war or violence. Ahimsa particularly emphasizes avoiding harm to living beings and carries a distinct Indian religious and ethical background.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 梵语 a- 表示“不”，hiṃsā 表示“伤害”：把“不伤害”扩展到一切生命。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sanskrit a- means “not,” and hiṃsā means “injury”: extend “do no harm” to living beings.

morphology.text: athel-（高贵、贵族）+ -ing（属于某一族的人）→ atheling（王族或贵族成员）。

etymology.text: 中古英语延续古英语 ætheling，与古英语 æthelu（高贵、贵族身份）有关。把它放回盎格鲁撒克逊王族的历史场景中记忆。

etymology_story.zh: 该词源自古英语 æþeling，由表示“高贵的”的 æþele 和表示所属或出身的 -ing 构成。它早期可指贵族男子，后来尤其用于王族男子，并作为历史称谓保留至今。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Old English æþeling, formed from æþele, meaning “noble,” and -ing, indicating affiliation or descent. It could originally denote a nobleman, but became especially associated with male royalty and survives as a historical designation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常将 atheling 作为完整的历史名词使用；athel- + -ing 是历史构词分析，并非现代英语中常用的造词模式。常规复数为 athelings；历史拼写变体包括 ætheling 和 etheling，没有常用的现代派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats atheling as a complete historical noun; athel- + -ing describes its historical formation rather than a common modern word-building pattern. The regular plural is athelings; historical spelling variants include ætheling and etheling, and there are no common modern derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: prince（王子；亲王）是更广泛的王族称谓；royal heir（王位继承人）强调继承身份；nobleman（贵族男子）不一定属于王族。atheling 特指盎格鲁撒克逊历史语境中的王族男子，也不必然指已确定的下一任国王。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Prince is a broader royal designation; royal heir emphasizes succession; nobleman does not necessarily imply royal birth. Atheling belongs specifically to an Anglo-Saxon historical context and does not necessarily identify a designated next king.

senses.meaning_zh: 〔亦作 baldric〕斜跨肩胸、用于悬挂佩剑或号角等物的背带
senses.meaning_en: A belt worn diagonally across the body to carry a sword, horn, or similar object; a variant of baldric.

etymology_story.zh: baldrick 是 baldric 的拼写变体，属于中古英语时期已有的词形系列，与古法语 baldrei 等形式有关。其更早来源并不完全确定，核心含义一直是用于悬挂武器等物的肩带。
etymology_story.en: Baldrick is a spelling variant of baldric, belonging to a group of forms found in Middle English and associated with Old French baldrei and related forms. Its deeper origin is uncertain, while its central meaning has remained a shoulder belt for carrying weapons or similar objects.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 baldrick 是不可再作透明分析的单纯词，不能拆成 bald 与其他部分来解释。常规复数为 baldricks；baldric 是常见异体，baldricked 是罕见形容词，表示“佩着斜肩带的”。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, baldrick is a morphologically opaque simple word and should not be interpreted as bald plus another element. Its regular plural is baldricks; baldric is a common alternative spelling, and baldricked is a rare adjective meaning equipped with a baldrick.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: baldric 与 baldrick 同义，仅拼写不同；shoulder belt（肩带）范围更广，不限于携带武器；sword belt（佩剑带）强调用途，也可以是围在腰间的带子。baldrick 的识别特征是斜跨身体的佩戴方式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Baldric has the same meaning and differs only in spelling; shoulder belt is broader and need not carry a weapon; sword belt identifies the purpose but may refer to a belt worn around the waist. A baldrick is distinguished by its diagonal position across the body.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住一条斜线：肩头连到对侧腰间，佩剑挂在下端。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember one diagonal line: shoulder to opposite hip, with a sword hanging below.

usage_note: bowyers 是造弓的人，不等于使用弓的 archers；此处 bow 的发音是 /boʊ/，不是鞠躬的 /baʊ/。

etymology_story.en: The singular bowyer continues Middle English bowyere, formed from bow with an occupational ending. Bowyers is its regular plural and preserves the traditional name for people who make archery bows.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式为 bow（弓）+ -yer（从业者）→ bowyer（制弓匠），再加复数 -s → bowyers。相关词包括 bow、bows、bowmaker（制弓者）和 bowmaking（制弓）；bowyer’s 是单数所有格，bowyers’ 是复数所有格。
morphology_enriched.en: The formation is bow + occupational -yer → bowyer, followed by plural -s → bowyers. Related forms include bow, bows, bowmaker, and bowmaking; bowyer’s is the singular possessive, while bowyers’ is the plural possessive.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bowmakers（制弓者）最接近原义，但脱离语境时也可能指制作弦乐器弓的人；craftspeople（手艺人）是更宽泛的职业类别；fletchers（制箭匠）制作箭，属于相关职业，并非同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bowmakers is the closest equivalent, although without context it may also refer to makers of bows for stringed instruments; craftspeople is a broader occupational category. Fletchers make arrows and belong to a related trade rather than being synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: bow 是弓，-yer 表示做这门手艺的人，-s 表示不止一人：一群制弓匠。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bow names the object, -yer names the worker, and -s makes a group: people who make bows.

meaning: 苏格兰冲泡麦粉食物；热液冲麦粉糊
aliases: 苏格兰冲泡麦粉食物；热液冲麦粉糊
热液冲麦粉制成的食物

pronunciation.note: 这是单音节词；元音读 /oʊ/，词尾 s 读浊辅音 /z/，末尾 e 不发音。

forms: 食物义通常不可数。
family: Atholl brose 阿瑟尔混合威士忌饮品，是带地名的另一个固定名称。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；实际复合名称 Atholl（苏格兰地名）+ brose → Atholl brose（一种混合威士忌饮品），不等同于本课麦粉食物。

etymology.text: 英语中的这个苏格兰词可能由 Scots bruis（肉汤）变来，经中古英语 brewes 可上溯到盎格鲁法语的汤、糊状食物名称。由热汤或热水冲麦粉来记。

usage_note: 通常把滚烫液体倒入麦粉拌成，不必长时间煮成粥；不要与名称中含 brose 的威士忌饮品混为一谈。

senses.meaning_zh: 〔苏格兰英语〕用热水、肉汤等冲拌燕麦粉制成的食物
senses.meaning_en: A Scottish food made by mixing oatmeal with hot water, stock, or another liquid.
senses.english_definition: Brose is a Scottish food made by stirring hot water, stock, or another liquid into oatmeal, usually without boiling the mixture like porridge.
senses.collocation_en: oatmeal brose; a bowl of brose
senses.collocation_zh: 燕麦粉糊；一碗燕麦粉糊
senses.sentence_en: She made brose by stirring hot stock into a bowl of oatmeal.
senses.sentence_zh: 她把热肉汤拌入一碗燕麦粉中，做成了苏格兰燕麦粉糊。

etymology_story.zh: brose 是苏格兰词，通常被认为与较早的 brois、bruis 等表示肉汤或汤食的形式有关，其词源也与中古英语及法语中的相关汤食名称相联系。词义后来集中到用热液冲拌燕麦粉的苏格兰食物上，具体传承路径存在不确定性。
etymology_story.en: Brose is a Scots word generally associated with earlier forms such as brois and bruis referring to broth or broth-based food, with connections to related Middle English and French food terms. Its meaning became associated particularly with the Scottish preparation of oatmeal mixed with hot liquid, although the precise historical route is uncertain.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 brose 是单纯词，通常不可数，词尾 -s 不是复数标记，也不应反推出单数 bro。常见组合有 oatmeal brose；固定名称 Atholl brose 指一种传统苏格兰饮品，不能直接等同于这里的燕麦粉食物；没有常用的现代派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, brose is a simple word and normally a mass noun; its final -s is not a plural ending, and no singular bro should be inferred. Combinations include oatmeal brose; the established name Atholl brose denotes a traditional Scottish drink rather than simply the oatmeal food defined here. There are no common modern derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: porridge（燕麦粥等谷物粥）通常经煮制；gruel（稀粥）强调稀薄的质地；oatmeal（燕麦粉；燕麦粥）可指原料，也可在某些英语变体中指成品。brose 的特点是将热液直接冲拌进燕麦粉，通常不再像粥那样熬煮。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Porridge is normally cooked by boiling or simmering; gruel emphasizes a thin consistency; oatmeal can name the ingredient or, in some varieties of English, a prepared cereal dish. Brose is distinguished by mixing hot liquid directly into oatmeal, usually without further cooking as porridge.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住制作动作：热汤冲进燕麦粉，拌一拌就是 brose。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the preparation: pour hot broth into oatmeal and stir to make brose.

meaning: 平民男子；乡下男子（古语）
aliases: 平民男子；乡下男子（古语）

pronunciation.note: 这是单音节词；元音读 /ɑː/，末尾 e 不另成音节，结尾保留 /l/。

family: carl 同义拼写；carlish 粗鲁的。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；同义拼写 carl + -ish → carlish（粗鲁的）。

etymology.text: 中古英语从古诺尔斯语 karl（男子、平民）借入。放在古老乡村故事里，记成没有贵族头衔的普通男子。

usage_note: 古旧或方言用词，本课取平民男子义；另有粗鄙者的贬义，不能见到 carle 就一律理解为辱骂。

senses.meaning_en: A man or country fellow, sometimes regarded as rough or low-born.
senses.english_definition: In old or regional language, a carle is a man, especially an ordinary countryman who may be considered rough.
