etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 cruralis“腿的”，由 crus“腿、小腿”的词干 crur- 构成。英语主要将它保留为解剖学形容词；具体指整个腿部还是小腿，需结合专业术语判断。
etymology_story.en: It derives from Latin cruralis, “of the leg,” formed from crur-, the stem of crus, “leg or lower leg.” English retained it mainly as an anatomical adjective, with the precise reference depending on the technical expression.

morphology_enriched.zh: 结构为 crur-（腿；小腿）＋-al（……的）。相关解剖学名词为 crus（腿状结构；脚），复数 crura；crural 本身没有常用的进一步派生词，常见组合有 crural fascia（小腿筋膜）和 crural region（小腿区）。
morphology_enriched.en: The structure is crur- (“leg; lower leg”) + -al (“relating to”). The related anatomical noun is crus, meaning a leg or leglike structure, with the plural crura; crural has no common further derivatives, and established combinations include crural fascia and crural region.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: leg-related（与腿有关的）是宽泛的普通表达；tibial（胫骨的）特指胫骨或相关结构；femoral（股部的；股骨的）指大腿、股骨或相关结构。后两者只在特定解剖语境中与 crural 接近，不能普遍互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Leg-related is a broad everyday equivalent; tibial specifically concerns the tibia or associated structures; femoral concerns the thigh, femur, or associated structures. The latter two overlap with crural only in particular anatomical contexts and are not generally interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: crur-＝腿，-al＝……的：合起来就是“腿部的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Crur- means “leg” and -al means “relating to”: together, “relating to the leg.”

etymology_story.zh: cullender 是 colander 的历史拼写变体，同属中古英语 colander、colyndore 等形式的演变系列。其词源最终可追溯到拉丁语 colare“过滤”，与 colum“筛子、滤器”有关。
etymology_story.en: Cullender is a historical spelling variant of colander, belonging to the same line of development as Middle English forms such as colander and colyndore. Its ultimate source is Latin colare, “to strain,” related to colum, “a sieve or strainer.”

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中应整体识记，不能分析成 cull＋-er；这里的 cull 不是“挑选、剔除”的动词。复数为 cullenders，没有常用的直接派生词；colander 是同一词的现代通行拼写，而非其派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, treat this as a whole word, not as cull + -er; it is unrelated in formation to the verb cull, “select or remove.” The plural is cullenders, there are no common direct derivatives, and colander is the usual modern spelling of the same word rather than a derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: colander（滤水盆）是现代标准表达；strainer（滤器）范围更广，可指多种过滤工具；sieve（筛子）通常具有较细的网孔，也可用于筛粉。cullender 的主要差异在于拼写陈旧或罕见。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Colander is the standard modern term; strainer covers a wider range of filtering utensils; sieve usually suggests a finer mesh and may also be used for sifting flour. Cullender differs chiefly in being an old-fashioned or rare spelling.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 联结 colare“过滤”：有孔的盆让水流走，把食物留下；现代通常写作 colander。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect it with colare, “to strain”: holes let the water escape while the food stays behind; today, usually spell it colander.

etymology_story.zh: cupric 由表示铜的拉丁语词干 cupr- 加上 -ic 构成；其源词 cuprum 可追溯到意为“塞浦路斯的金属”的拉丁语表达。在传统化学命名中，cupric 表示铜的较高常见氧化态，即 +2。
etymology_story.en: Cupric was formed from the Latin copper stem cupr- and -ic; its source, cuprum, ultimately comes from a Latin expression meaning 'metal of Cyprus.' In traditional chemical nomenclature, cupric denotes copper's higher common oxidation state, +2.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代科技构词：cupr-（铜）+ -ic（化学形容词后缀）→ cupric。相关词族包括 copper（铜）、cuprous（铜(I)的）、cuprate（铜酸盐等）、cuprite（赤铜矿）和 cupriferous（含铜的）；这些词共享词源或词干，并非都由 cupric 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern scientific formation: cupr- 'copper' + -ic, a chemical adjective suffix → cupric. Related family members include copper, cuprous 'copper(I),' cuprate, cuprite, and cupriferous 'copper-bearing'; these share an origin or stem rather than all being direct derivatives of cupric.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: copper(II)（铜(II)的）是对应的现代命名表达；divalent copper（二价铜）直接强调价态；copper-containing（含铜的）范围更广，不限定铜的氧化态。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Copper(II) is the corresponding modern nomenclatural expression; divalent copper explicitly emphasizes valency; copper-containing is broader and does not specify copper's oxidation state.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 铜的传统命名配对：cuprous 对应 +1，cupric 对应 +2。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the traditional copper pair: cuprous is +1; cupric is +2.

etymology_story.zh: Cymric 以威尔士语 Cymry“威尔士人”为基础，加英语后缀 -ic 构成，用来表示威尔士的民族、语言和文化。后来它也被用作长毛马恩岛猫的品种名称；这个名称本身不证明该品种起源于威尔士。
etymology_story.en: Cymric was formed from Welsh Cymry 'the Welsh people' with the English suffix -ic to describe Welsh people, language, and culture. It was later adopted as a name for the longhaired Manx cat; the name itself does not establish a Welsh origin for the breed.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：Cymr-（取自 Cymry 的词干）+ -ic（……的）→ Cymric；形容词也可转作语言名词和猫品种名词。猫的可数名词复数为 Cymrics，语言名称通常不可数；相关词 Cymru 意为“威尔士”，Cymry 意为“威尔士人”，二者是威尔士语相关形式，并非英语派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: Cymr-, the stem taken from Cymry, + -ic 'relating to' → Cymric; the adjective also functions as a language name and a cat-breed noun. The countable cat noun has the plural Cymrics, while the language name is normally uncountable; related Welsh forms are Cymru 'Wales' and Cymry 'the Welsh people,' rather than English derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Welsh（威尔士的；威尔士语）是通常使用的对应词；Cambrian（威尔士的）也可用于文学语境，但另有“寒武纪的”这一地质学义；longhaired Manx（长毛马恩岛猫）只对应猫品种义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Welsh is the usual equivalent for the regional adjective and language name; Cambrian can also mean Welsh in literary contexts but has a separate geological meaning; longhaired Manx corresponds only to the cat-breed sense.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Cymry 是“威尔士人”，加 -ic 就是“威尔士的”；猫名义另记为“长毛马恩岛猫”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Cymry means 'the Welsh people'; adding -ic gives 'Welsh.' Remember the cat sense separately as 'longhaired Manx.'

etymology_story.zh: dalasi 是从曼丁卡语借入的货币名称。1971年，冈比亚采用十进制货币体系，达拉西取代冈比亚镑，成为该国的货币单位。

morphology_enriched.zh: 在现代英语中，dalasi 是不可再作英语词根加词缀分析的借词；常用复数为 dalasis。它没有常见的英语派生词；ten-dalasi 等形式是作定语的货币金额组合，并非派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, dalasi is a borrowed word without a productive English root-and-affix breakdown; its usual plural is dalasis. It has no common English derivatives; forms such as ten-dalasi are attributive monetary combinations rather than derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Gambian dalasi（冈比亚达拉西）是更明确的全称；GMD 是货币代码，并非普通词汇近义词；Gambian currency（冈比亚货币）泛指该国货币，不专指一个单位。dalasi 没有通常意义上的词汇近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gambian dalasi is the more explicit full name; GMD is its currency code rather than a lexical synonym; Gambian currency refers broadly to the country's money rather than specifically to one unit. Dalasi has no ordinary lexical synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整体绑定：冈比亚 → dalasi → 100 bututs，不强拆词根。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the whole word: The Gambia → dalasi → 100 bututs; do not force a root breakdown.

senses.meaning_zh: 少女；年轻未婚女子，古雅或诗歌用语
senses.meaning_en: A young unmarried woman, in archaic or poetic usage.
senses.english_definition: A damozel is a young unmarried woman, especially in old-fashioned poetry or stories.
senses.collocation_en: the blessed damozel; a fair damozel
senses.collocation_zh: 蒙福的少女；美丽的少女
senses.sentence_en: The poet describes a damozel looking down from heaven.
senses.sentence_zh: 诗人描写了一位从天堂俯视人间的少女。

etymology_story.zh: damozel 是 damsel 的古雅变体，经古法语 damoisele 等形式，最终可追溯到拉丁语 domina“女主人”的指小形式。它保留了“年轻女子”的含义，并因罗塞蒂的诗作《蒙福的少女》而广为文学读者所知。
etymology_story.en: Damozel is an archaic variant of damsel, descending through Old French forms such as damoisele from a diminutive of Latin domina 'lady or mistress.' It retained the meaning 'young woman' and became familiar to literary readers through Rossetti's poem The Blessed Damozel.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中应将 damozel 作为完整词记忆，不宜拆成有生产力的英语词根和后缀；复数为 damozels。相关形式包括 damsel（少女）、damoisel（古拼写变体）和 demoiselle（同源的法语借词），它们并非都由 damozel 派生；damozel 本身没有常见派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, damozel should be learned as a whole word rather than divided into productive English roots and suffixes; its plural is damozels. Related forms include damsel, the archaic spelling damoisel, and the cognate French borrowing demoiselle; these are not all derivatives of damozel, which has no common derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: damsel（少女）同样带有古雅或骑士传奇色彩，但拼写更常见；maiden（少女；未婚女子）也属文学用语，并可能强调未婚或贞洁；young woman（年轻女子）是中性现代说法，不限定婚姻状况。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Damsel has a similarly archaic or chivalric tone but is the more familiar spelling; maiden is also literary and may emphasize unmarried status or virginity; young woman is neutral modern English and does not specify marital status.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 damozel 看作披着古诗外衣的 damsel：都是“少女”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture damozel as damsel dressed in the language of an old poem: a young woman.

etymology_story.zh: decurion 来自拉丁语 decurio，其词干见于 decurion-，与 decuria“十人组”和 decem“十”有关。该称谓既用于骑兵军官，也用于城市议事会成员；实际军事编制随时代变化，因此不能把所有 decurion 都理解为只指挥十人。
etymology_story.en: Decurion comes from Latin decurio, with the stem decurion-, related to decuria 'a group of ten' and decem 'ten.' The title was used both for cavalry officers and for municipal councillors; military organization changed over time, so a decurion did not invariably command only ten men.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，decurion 是整体借入的历史名词，不是由现代英语动词加 -ion 构成；复数为 decurions。历史分析可联系拉丁语 decuria“十人组”和 decurion- 词干；相关词包括 decury（十人组）、decurial（十人组的；市议员的）和 decurionate（市议员职位或议员团）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, decurion is a borrowed historical noun, not a modern English verb plus -ion; its plural is decurions. Historical analysis connects it with Latin decuria 'a group of ten' and the stem decurion-; related words include decury 'a group of ten,' decurial 'relating to a decury or decurions,' and decurionate 'the office or body of decurions.'

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cavalry officer（骑兵军官）可概括军事义，但不保留古罗马的特定军职；municipal councillor（市议员）对应民政义；alderman（市政官员或市议员）只能作某些语境中的类比，并非完全对应的罗马官称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cavalry officer captures the military sense without specifying the Roman rank; municipal councillor corresponds to the civic sense; alderman offers a contextual analogy but is not an exact equivalent of the Roman title.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 decem“十”联想到“十人组的负责人”，再分别记住骑兵军官和城市议员两种历史身份。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with decem 'ten' and the leader of a group of ten, then remember the two historical roles: cavalry officer and town councillor.

senses.meaning_zh: 使脱氢；从化合物中除去氢
senses.meaning_en: to remove hydrogen from a compound
senses.english_definition: To dehydrogenate a compound means to remove hydrogen atoms from it through a chemical reaction.
senses.collocation_zh: 使烷烃脱氢；通过催化作用使脱氢
senses.sentence_en: The catalyst can dehydrogenate ethane to produce ethene.
senses.sentence_zh: 这种催化剂能使乙烷脱氢，生成乙烯。

etymology_story.zh: 该词由表示去除的 de- 加 hydrogenate“使氢化”构成，产生于近代化学术语体系。hydrogen 最终源于表示“水”和“生成”的希腊语成分，指氢燃烧后能生成水。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in modern chemical terminology by adding the removal prefix de- to hydrogenate. Hydrogen ultimately combines Greek elements meaning 'water' and 'producing', referring to the formation of water when hydrogen burns.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：de-（去除）+ hydrogen（氢）+ -ate（使发生某种作用）。屈折形式：dehydrogenates、dehydrogenated、dehydrogenating；主要词族：dehydrogenation（脱氢）、dehydrogenase（脱氢酶）；相关词：hydrogenate（使氢化）、hydrogenation（氢化）、hydrogen（氢）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: de- ('remove') + hydrogen + -ate (a verb-forming suffix). Inflections: dehydrogenates, dehydrogenated, dehydrogenating. Principal family members: dehydrogenation and dehydrogenase, an enzyme that catalyzes hydrogen removal. Related words include hydrogenate, hydrogenation, and hydrogen.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: remove hydrogen（除去氢）是直接释义；oxidize（使氧化）的范围更广，在许多反应中包括脱氢；dehydrate（使脱水）指除去水，与除去氢并不相同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Remove hydrogen is a direct paraphrase. Oxidize is broader and includes hydrogen removal in many reactions. Dehydrate means to remove water and must be distinguished from removing hydrogen.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: de- 表示去除，hydrogen 表示氢：把氢拿走，就是脱氢。
mnemonic_anchor.en: De- removes; hydrogen names what is removed: take hydrogen away.

morphology.text: di-（两个） + aster（星） → diaster（细胞分裂的双星相）。

etymology.text: 19世纪用 di-“两个”与希腊语 aster“星”构成，形容细胞分裂时染色体分成两组、在两极呈星状的阶段。

senses.meaning_en: a stage or figure of mitosis showing two star-shaped groups of chromosomes
senses.english_definition: A diaster is a stage or figure in cell division in which the separated chromosomes form two star-shaped groups toward opposite poles of the cell.
senses.collocation_zh: 双星相阶段；双星相图像
senses.sentence_en: The historical illustration shows a diaster, with two star-shaped groups of chromosomes.
senses.sentence_zh: 这幅历史插图展示了双星相，其中可见两组呈星状排列的染色体。

etymology_story.zh: 这是早期细胞学中的术语，由 di-（二）与源自希腊语 astēr“星”的 aster 构成。名称来自分裂过程中两组染色体形成的双星状外观，如今主要见于历史性或专门的细胞学描述。
etymology_story.en: This term from early cytology combines di- ('two') with aster, from Greek astēr, meaning 'star'. It describes the appearance of two star-shaped chromosome groups during division and is now chiefly encountered in historical or specialized cytological descriptions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 di-（二）+ aster（星状体或星状结构）；复数为 diasters。没有广泛通用的现代派生词；相关术语包括 aster（星状体）、monaster（单星相）和 amphiaster（双星体），但它们不是 diaster 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Analyzable structure: di- ('two') + aster ('a star-shaped structure'); plural: diasters. There are no widely used modern derivatives. Related terms include aster, monaster ('a single-star figure'), and amphiaster ('a double-aster structure'), but these are not direct derivatives of diaster.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: double-star figure（双星状图像）是描述性近义表达；anaphase（后期）是相关的现代分裂时期名称，强调染色体分离；amphiaster（双星体）强调两个星状体及其间的纺锤结构，所指并不完全相同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Double-star figure is a descriptive near-equivalent. Anaphase is a related modern stage name emphasizing chromosome separation. Amphiaster emphasizes the two asters and the spindle between them, so its referent is not identical.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: di- 是二，aster 是星：细胞分裂时出现“两颗星”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Di- means two and aster means star: picture two chromosome stars during division.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由化学命名中的 di-（二）与 ether（醚）组合而成。ether 经拉丁语追溯到希腊语 aithēr，原指明亮的上层天空，后来成为一类化合物的名称。
etymology_story.en: The word combines the chemical prefix di- ('two') with ether. Ether comes through Latin from Greek aithēr, originally referring to the bright upper sky, and later became the name of a class of chemical compounds.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：di-（二）+ ether（醚）；复数为 diethers。没有广泛通用的直接派生词；相关系列包括 monoether（单醚）、triether（三醚）和 polyether（聚醚）。diether 表示两个醚基，不等于 diethyl ether（二乙醚，只有一个醚基）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: di- ('two') + ether; plural: diethers. There are no widely used direct derivatives. Related formations include monoether, triether, and polyether. Diether counts two ether groups; it does not mean diethyl ether, which contains only one ether group.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: compound with two ether groups（含两个醚基的化合物）是准确释义；ether（醚）是更宽泛的类别名称；cyclic diether（环状二醚）则限定为两个醚基位于环状结构中的二醚。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Compound with two ether groups is an exact paraphrase. Ether names the broader chemical class. Cyclic diether is narrower, specifying a diether whose ether groups occur within a ring structure.

etymology_story.zh: diuron 是二十世纪形成的人工化学通用名称，所指化合物为 3-(3,4-二氯苯基)-1,1-二甲基脲。它属于根据化学结构创造的名称，不宜把每个字母片段都解释成具有独立意义的普通英语词缀。
etymology_story.en: Diuron is a coined twentieth-century chemical common name for 3-(3,4-dichlorophenyl)-1,1-dimethylurea. It belongs to structure-based chemical naming, and its individual letter sequences should not all be treated as ordinary English affixes with independent meanings.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中应整体识别为化学名称 diuron，没有可靠的普通“词根＋词缀”切分；通常作不可数名词。没有广泛通用的直接派生词；DCMU 是同一化合物的常用缩写，monuron（灭草隆）和 linuron（利谷隆）是相关但不同的除草剂。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, diuron is best treated as a whole chemical name rather than divided into ordinary roots and affixes; it is normally uncountable. It has no widely used direct derivatives. DCMU is a common abbreviation for the same compound; monuron and linuron name related but different herbicides.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: DCMU 与 diuron 指同一化合物；dichlorophenyldimethylurea（二氯苯基二甲基脲）是常见的结构性名称表达，精确命名时需标明取代位置；urea herbicide（脲类除草剂）是包含敌草隆的上位类别。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: DCMU refers to the same compound as diuron. Dichlorophenyldimethylurea is a common structural name, although a fully precise name specifies the substitution positions. Urea herbicide is a broader class that includes diuron.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把敌草隆与“二氯苯环＋二甲基脲”结构相连：它让杂草的光合作用受阻。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link diuron to a dichlorophenyl ring plus dimethylurea: a weed killer that blocks photosynthesis.

usage_note: 少见、正式的不及物动词；本课取谈话或写作离题义，常见搭配 divagate from the subject。

senses.meaning_zh: 离题；偏离主题或路线；游荡，漫游
senses.meaning_en: to wander away from a subject or course
senses.english_definition: If someone divagates, they move away from the subject they are discussing or, in literary use, wander away from a particular course.
senses.collocation_en: divagate from the subject; divagate into speculation
senses.collocation_zh: 偏离主题；离题而转入推测
senses.sentence_en: The essay occasionally divagates from its main subject into personal reminiscence.
senses.sentence_zh: 这篇文章偶尔会偏离主题，转而叙述个人往事。

etymology_story.zh: 该词源于拉丁语 divagari“到处游荡”，其中 di- 表示分开、向各处，vagari 表示游荡。英语保留了空间上的漫游义，并用它比喻言谈或思绪偏离主题。
etymology_story.en: The word derives from Latin divagari, 'to wander about', combining di-, expressing separation or movement in different directions, with vagari, 'to wander'. English retains the spatial meaning and also uses it figuratively for speech or thought that strays from its subject.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 di-（分开、向别处，此处不是“二”）+ vag-（游走）+ -ate（动词后缀）。屈折形式：divagates、divagated、divagating；主要派生词：divagation（离题；漫游）。相关词包括 vagary（奇想；反复无常的变化）和 vagrant（流浪者；流浪的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Analyzable structure: di- ('apart' or 'away', not 'two' here) + vag- ('wander') + -ate (a verb-forming suffix). Inflections: divagates, divagated, divagating. The principal derivative is divagation. Related words include vagary, an unpredictable notion or change, and vagrant, a wandering person or the adjective describing one.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: digress（离题）最直接地表示暂时偏离讨论主题；ramble（漫谈；漫游）强调言谈松散或行走无明确方向；wander（游荡；走神）适用范围最广。divagate 较罕见，带正式或文学色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Digress most directly means to leave a discussion's main subject temporarily. Ramble suggests loosely organized speech or movement without a clear direction. Wander is the broadest term. Divagate is uncommon and has a formal or literary tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: vag- 是游走，di- 是向别处：话题也会走岔路。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Vag- wanders and di- sends it away: a discussion takes a side road.

senses.english_definition: Dolma is a dish made by filling vegetables or wrapping leaves around a filling such as rice or minced meat.

etymology_story.zh: 英语在19世纪借入这一源自土耳其语的名称；土耳其语 dolma 与 dolmak“变满、被填满”有关，名称强调食物填有馅料。它不仅可以指葡萄叶包饭，也可指填馅的辣椒、茄子等。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed this name of Turkish origin in the nineteenth century; Turkish dolma is related to dolmak, meaning 'to become full' or 'to be filled,' and names food containing a stuffing. Its meaning includes stuffed peppers and aubergines as well as stuffed grape leaves.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整体借入词，不宜拆作英语词根与词缀。来源语构形为 dol-“变满、被填满”＋名词化后缀 -ma；英语复数可用 dolmas，作为菜名也可不标复数。相关借词 dolmades 来自希腊语复数，英语中通常指葡萄叶包馅食物。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, dolma is a whole-word borrowing rather than an English root-and-affix formation. Its Turkish structure is dol-, 'become full or be filled,' plus the nominalizing suffix -ma; the English plural can be dolmas, while the dish name can also remain uninflected. The related borrowing dolmades comes from a Greek plural and usually denotes stuffed grape leaves in English.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: stuffed vegetables“填馅蔬菜”是较宽泛的描述；stuffed grape leaves“葡萄叶包馅食物”只指其中一种；dolmades 在英语中通常也指葡萄叶包馅食物，不能覆盖 dolma 的全部范围。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Stuffed vegetables is a broader descriptive expression; stuffed grape leaves names one particular form; dolmades also usually means stuffed grape leaves in English and does not cover every kind of dolma.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“填满”：叶子包馅、蔬菜填馅，都可以是 dolma。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'filled': a leaf wrapped around stuffing or a vegetable filled with it can be dolma.

usage_note: 动物分类用语，海胆纲成员，包括海胆、沙钱等；不等于所有棘皮动物。

etymology_story.zh: 该词的历史基础是希腊语 ekhinos“刺猬；海胆”，并与新拉丁语类群名 Echinoidea 相联系。刺猬和海胆共享的多刺外形解释了这一名称的来源，英语随后用它指海胆纲动物及其相关事物。
etymology_story.en: The word ultimately rests on Greek ekhinos, 'hedgehog; sea urchin,' and is associated with the New Latin class name Echinoidea. The shared spiny appearance of hedgehogs and sea urchins explains the name, which English uses for these animals and things relating to them.

morphology_enriched.zh: 科技词汇构形为 echin-／echino-“棘；海胆”＋-oid“形似……的；某类成员”，拼写中共享连接元音 o，并非叠写为两个 o。直接相关形式有复数 echinoids、类群名 Echinoidea，以及同义形容词 echinoidean；echinoderm“棘皮动物”共享词根，但不是 echinoid 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: The scientific formation combines echin-/echino-, 'spine; sea urchin,' with -oid, 'resembling; a member of a group,' with a single shared o in the spelling. Closely related forms include the plural echinoids, the class name Echinoidea, and the synonymous adjective echinoidean; echinoderm shares the root but is not derived from echinoid.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sea urchin“海胆”是最接近的日常说法，但在与沙钱等并列时常指典型的多刺海胆；sand dollar“沙钱”是海胆纲中的一个类群，并非全部海胆纲动物的同义词；echinoidean 可作为形容词 echinoid 的近义替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sea urchin is the closest everyday expression, but often denotes the familiar spiny forms when contrasted with sand dollars; sand dollar names a subgroup rather than all echinoids; echinoidean is a close equivalent of the adjective echinoid.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: echin- 联想“刺”：海中的“刺猬”就是典型海胆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link echin- with spines: the sea's 'hedgehog' is a typical sea urchin.

senses.meaning_en: Of or relating to a transition zone between ecological communities
senses.english_definition: An ecotonal area lies where two ecological communities meet and gradually give way to each other.

etymology_story.zh: ecotonal 由生态学术语 ecotone 派生；ecotone 由 eco-“生态、环境”与源自希腊语 tonos“张力”的成分组成。名称把相邻群落相互影响的过渡地带理解为一种具有生态“张力”的区域。
etymology_story.en: Ecotonal derives from the ecological term ecotone, formed from eco-, referring to ecology or environment, and an element based on Greek tonos, 'tension.' The name presents the transition between interacting communities as a zone of ecological 'tension.'

morphology_enriched.zh: 直接构形：ecotone“生态交错带”去词尾不发音的 e，再加形容词后缀 -al，成为 ecoton-al。核心词族为 ecotone、复数 ecotones 和 ecotonal；ecology、ecological、ecologist 共享生态学相关构词成分，但不是 ecotonal 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: The immediate formation is ecotone, 'ecological transition zone,' minus its final silent e, plus the adjective suffix -al: ecoton-al. The core family comprises ecotone, the plural ecotones, and ecotonal; ecology, ecological, and ecologist share ecological word-building material but are not direct derivatives of ecotonal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: transitional“过渡的”适用范围最广；interfacial“界面的”强调两个区域的接触面；edge-related“与边缘有关的”强调边缘位置或效应。ecotonal 专指生态群落之间的过渡关系。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Transitional has the broadest application; interfacial emphasizes the surface or boundary where regions meet; edge-related emphasizes an edge location or its effects. Ecotonal specifically concerns transitions between ecological communities.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 生态＋张力：想象森林与草地交接处相互拉扯的过渡带。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ecology plus tension: picture the transition where forest and grassland meet and pull against each other.

senses.meaning_zh: 用电铸法复制；制成电铸印版
senses.meaning_en: To reproduce an object or printing surface by electrodeposition
senses.english_definition: If you electrotype an object or a printing surface, you make a metal copy of it by depositing metal electrically onto a mould.
senses.chinese_definition: 如果你对物体或印刷表面进行电铸复制，就是在模具上通过电沉积制成它的金属复制品。

etymology_story.zh: 该词形成于19世纪，由 electro-“电”与 type“印刷字模、印版”等义结合而成，与电沉积复制技术的发展相伴。它既可指复制出的金属印版或其他物件，也可作动词表示实施这一复制工艺。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in the nineteenth century from electro-, 'electric,' and type in its printing-related senses, alongside the development of electrodeposition as a copying technique. It denotes a resulting metal printing plate or other copy and also functions as a verb for carrying out the process.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构形：electro-“电”＋type“印版、复制形式”。核心词族包括 electrotypes、electrotyped、electrotyping，以及 electrotyper“电铸工；电铸设备”、electrotypist“电铸工”、electrotypy“电铸复制术”和 electrotypic“电铸的”。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern formation is electro-, 'electric,' plus type, referring to a printing form or copy. The core family includes electrotypes, electrotyped, electrotyping, electrotyper, 'an operator or apparatus,' electrotypist, 'an operator,' electrotypy, 'the process,' and electrotypic, 'relating to the process.'

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: electroform“电铸品；电铸制造”是较宽泛的相关术语，常强调通过电沉积形成金属物件；replica“复制品”不限定制作方法；stereotype“铅铸印版”在历史印刷语境中指另一种复制印版，其制作方法通常是向模具中浇铸金属。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Electroform is a broader related term, often emphasizing the creation of a metal object by electrodeposition; replica specifies a copy without identifying its method of manufacture; stereotype, in historical printing, denotes a duplicate plate typically made by casting metal into a mould.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: electro“电”＋type“印版”：用电沉积“长出”金属复制品。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Electro means electricity and type suggests a printing form: electricity 'grows' a metal copy.

senses.meaning_en: A landing place or waterfront area used for boarding vessels or loading and unloading goods
senses.english_definition: An embarcadero is a place beside the water where people board boats or goods are loaded and unloaded.
senses.chinese_definition: embarcadero 指水边供人们登船或装卸货物的地方。

etymology_story.zh: 英语在19世纪从西班牙语借入 embarcadero，源于 embarcar“登船；装船”。该词最初强调登船或装卸的地点，后来也用于滨水区域的名称；旧金山的 The Embarcadero 是专名用法。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed embarcadero from Spanish in the nineteenth century, from embarcar, 'to board a vessel; to load aboard.' The word names a boarding or loading place and also appears in waterfront place names, including San Francisco's The Embarcadero.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中按整体借入词处理，复数为 embarcaderos。西班牙语中可分析为 embarca-，来自 embarcar“登船、装船”，加场所后缀 -dero；进一步可联系 en-、barca“船”和动词词尾 -ar，其中 n 在 b 前变为 m。embark 与它在词源上相关，但不是它的英语派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats it as a whole-word borrowing, with the plural embarcaderos. In Spanish, it can be analyzed as embarca-, from embarcar, 'board or load a vessel,' plus the place-forming suffix -dero; its deeper structure involves en-, barca, 'boat,' and the verb ending -ar, with n becoming m before b. Embark is etymologically related but is not an English derivative of embarcadero.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: wharf“码头”通常强调沿岸供船舶停靠和装卸的平台；pier“突堤、栈桥”强调伸入水中的结构；landing“登岸处、登船处”强调上下船的地点，结构可以很简易。embarcadero 常带西班牙语地区或相关地名的地域色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Wharf usually emphasizes a waterside platform for mooring and cargo handling; pier emphasizes a structure projecting into the water; landing emphasizes a boarding or disembarking place, which may be quite simple. Embarcadero often carries a regional association with Spanish-speaking places or their place names.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 联系 embark“登船”：embarcadero 就是登船、装船的地方。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect it with embark: an embarcadero is a place for getting people or goods aboard.

etymology.text: 19世纪借自法语 enjambement，来自动词 enjamber“跨过”，与 jambe“腿”相关。可以想象句子的意思迈过诗行的边界。

usage_note: 诗学术语，句法和意思不停在诗行末尾，而延续到下一行；不要求一定押韵。

senses.meaning_zh: 跨行续句：诗句的语法结构或意思越过行末，在下一行继续。
senses.meaning_en: The continuation of a phrase or sentence beyond the end of a line of poetry.
senses.english_definition: Enjambement occurs when a phrase or sentence in a poem continues into the next line without a full grammatical break.
senses.collocation_en: the use of enjambement; enjambement between lines
senses.collocation_zh: 跨行续句的运用；诗行之间的跨行续句
senses.sentence_en: The poet uses enjambement to carry the reader quickly into the next line.
senses.sentence_zh: 诗人运用跨行续句，让读者顺势快速读入下一行。

etymology_story.zh: 19世纪借自法语 enjambement，来自动词 enjamber，意为“跨过、迈过”，其中 jambe 意为“腿”。诗学意义把句意越过诗行边界比作抬腿跨越。
etymology_story.en: Borrowed in the nineteenth century from French enjambement, derived from enjamber, meaning “to step over,” which contains jambe, “leg.” Its poetic meaning pictures a sentence stepping over a line boundary.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整体借入的名词，不宜按英语前后缀硬拆；历史法语构形为 enjamber（跨过）的词干 enjamb- + -ement（名词后缀）。常见相关形式：enjambment（异体拼写）、enjamb（使诗句跨行延续）、enjambed（跨行延续的）、enjambing（跨行延续；现在分词）；复数 enjambements。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, this is a borrowed noun rather than a transparent English prefix-and-suffix formation; historically, French enjamb- comes from enjamber, “to step over,” with the noun suffix -ement. Related forms include enjambment, the alternative spelling; enjamb, the verb; enjambed; and enjambing. The plural is enjambements.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: enjambment（跨行续句）是同义异体拼写；run-on line（跨行延续的诗行）指采用这种手法的具体诗行，而 enjambement 指这种现象或手法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Enjambment is an alternative spelling with the same meaning. A run-on line is a particular line that uses the technique, whereas enjambement names the technique or phenomenon.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 句意“迈腿”跨过行末：行结束，意思继续。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The sentence steps over the line ending: the line stops, but the meaning continues.

senses.collocation_zh: 担任顾问的葡萄酒酿造学专家；受过专业训练的葡萄酒酿造学专家
senses.sentence_en: The enologist monitored the fermentation and tested the wine's acidity.
senses.sentence_zh: 这位葡萄酒酿造学专家监测了发酵过程，并检测了葡萄酒的酸度。

etymology_story.zh: 由 enology（葡萄酒酿造学）对应派生，eno- 源自希腊语 oinos，意为“葡萄酒”，-logist 表示某门学科的研究者。词义一直围绕葡萄酒及酿造过程的科学研究。
etymology_story.en: Formed in relation to enology, the science of wine, with eno- ultimately from Greek oinos, “wine,” and -logist identifying a specialist. Its meaning centers on the scientific study of wine and its production.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构形：eno-（葡萄酒）+ -logist（学科专家）；也可理解为 enology 的学科名后缀 -logy 换为专家后缀 -logist。主要词族：enology（葡萄酒酿造学）、enological（葡萄酒酿造学的）、enologically（从葡萄酒酿造学角度）；对应的 oe 拼写形式为 oenologist、oenology、oenological、oenologically。复数 enologists。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: eno-, “wine,” + -logist, “specialist”; alternatively, view it as replacing the discipline ending -logy in enology with -logist. The principal family includes enology, enological, and enologically, together with the corresponding oe spellings oenologist, oenology, oenological, and oenologically. The plural is enologists.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: wine scientist（葡萄酒科学家）强调科研身份；winemaking expert（酿酒专家）范围较宽，也可指凭实践经验获得专长的人；winemaker（葡萄酒酿造师）强调实际酿造职责，不一定具有科学研究背景。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Wine scientist emphasizes scientific work. Winemaking expert is broader and can describe expertise gained through practice. Winemaker emphasizes responsibility for producing wine and does not necessarily imply a scientific research background.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: eno- 指葡萄酒，-logist 指专家：研究葡萄酒科学的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Eno- means wine, and -logist means specialist: a specialist in wine science.

pronunciation.note: 采用 Collins 所列法语借词读音；/ɑ̃/ 为鼻化元音，词尾 t 不发音。

forms: 复数 entrechats；词尾 t 不发音。
family: 法语 entrechat 为英语借入的芭蕾术语。

morphology.text: entrechat 作为独立词素记；意大利语历史构形 in-（进入） + trecci(a)（辫子） + -ata → intrecciata（交织的），与这个舞步名称的法语来源相连。

etymology.text: 18世纪借自法语 entrechat；更早关联意大利语 intrecciata“交织的”。想象双腿在跳起时像编辫子一样交叉。

usage_note: 芭蕾术语，跳起后双腿迅速交叉或击打。词尾 t 不读，保留法语借词特色。

senses.meaning_zh: 空中交叉击腿跳：芭蕾舞中跃起后双腿快速交叉击合的动作。
senses.meaning_en: A ballet jump in which the dancer rapidly crosses and beats the legs together in the air.
senses.english_definition: An entrechat is a ballet jump during which a dancer quickly crosses and beats the legs together before landing.
senses.collocation_en: perform an entrechat; a series of entrechats
senses.collocation_zh: 完成一次空中交叉击腿跳；一连串空中交叉击腿跳
senses.sentence_en: She performed an entrechat and landed softly in fifth position.
senses.sentence_zh: 她完成了一次空中交叉击腿跳，随后轻轻落地，双脚呈第五位。

etymology_story.zh: 18世纪借自法语 entrechat，通常追溯至意大利语 intrecciata，意为“交织、编结”，与 treccia（辫子）相关。舞步名称用编辫子的交错形象描述空中快速交叉的双腿。
etymology_story.en: Borrowed in the eighteenth century from French entrechat, generally traced to Italian intrecciata, meaning “interlaced,” and related to treccia, “braid.” The name evokes legs crossing rapidly in the air like interwoven strands.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为完整的法语借词使用，没有可自由分析的英语词根和词缀；不可拆成英语 entre + chat。复数为 entrechats；常见术语组合有 entrechat quatre、entrechat six，数字按芭蕾舞惯例计算腿部动作，并非简单等于双腿击合次数。没有常用的英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, this is a complete French loanword without productive English roots or affixes; it should not be divided into English entre + chat. The plural is entrechats. Technical combinations include entrechat quatre and entrechat six, whose numbers count leg movements according to ballet convention rather than simply counting contacts. There is no common English derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: beaten jump（击腿跳）是较宽泛的类别，entrechat 是其中一种具体动作；batterie（击腿动作的统称）指跳跃中击腿的动作技巧或组合，不专指某一次 entrechat。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Beaten jump is a broader category that includes the entrechat. Batterie is a collective term for beating movements or combinations in jumps, rather than an exact synonym for an individual entrechat.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把双腿想成辫子的两股：跃起，在空中快速交织。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the legs as strands of a braid: jump, then weave them together in the air.

forms: 通常不可数；指不同变动事件时可用复数 eustasies；另有拼写 eustacy。
family: eustatic 全球海平面变动的；eustatically 为其副词。

morphology.text: eustasy 作为独立词素整体记；相关派生 eu- + stat-（稳定、位置） + -ic → eustatic（全球海平面变动的）。

etymology.text: 英语 eustasy 是 eustatic 的名词化形式；后者承接地质学家提出的德语 eustatisch，使用了希腊语来源成分。记忆重点是全球海水面整体升降。

usage_note: 地质学名词，指全球海平面整体变化，区别于一地的潮汐涨落或局部地面升降。

senses.meaning_zh: 全球性海平面变化，尤指海水总量或海盆容量变化引起的升降。
senses.meaning_en: Worldwide sea-level change, especially from changes in ocean-water volume or ocean-basin capacity.
senses.english_definition: Eustasy is a change in sea level on a global scale, caused by changes in the amount of ocean water or the capacity of ocean basins.
senses.collocation_zh: 冰川作用引起的全球海平面变化；全球海平面变化的变动
senses.sentence_en: The study separates the effects of eustasy from those of local land uplift.
senses.sentence_zh: 这项研究将全球海平面变化的影响与局部陆地抬升的影响区分开来。

etymology_story.zh: 由形容词 eustatic 对应形成名词；eustatic 承接19世纪末地质学家爱德华·修斯使用的德语 eustatisch，其构词成分最终来自希腊语 eu-（良好）和表示站立、位置的词根。地质学中的专门含义是全球尺度的海平面变化，并不表示海平面保持稳定。
etymology_story.en: The noun was formed in relation to eustatic, which follows German eustatisch, used by geologist Eduard Suess in the late nineteenth century and ultimately built from Greek eu-, “well,” and a root associated with standing or position. Its geological meaning concerns sea-level change on a global scale rather than a sea level that remains stable.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜整体识记 eustasy，并与 eustatic（全球海平面变化的）、eustatically（以全球海平面变化的方式）建立联系，不宜把它解释为表示“良好”的 eu- 加上一个独立英语词 stasy。常见复合词族包括 glacioeustasy／glacio-eustasy（冰川性全球海平面变化）和 glacioeustatic／glacio-eustatic（冰川性全球海平面变化的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, learn eustasy as a technical whole and connect it with eustatic and eustatically; it is not transparently formed from eu- plus an independent English word stasy. Common technical compounds include glacioeustasy or glacio-eustasy and the corresponding adjective glacioeustatic or glacio-eustatic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: eustatic sea-level change（全球性海平面变化）是直接对应的完整表达；global mean sea-level change（全球平均海平面变化）强调全球平均值的变化，在现代研究中使用，但具体定义和测量基准仍须结合语境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Eustatic sea-level change is the direct expanded equivalent. Global mean sea-level change emphasizes change in the worldwide average and is used in modern research, although its precise definition and reference framework depend on context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“全球海面这一层”：看整体海平面升降，而非某处陆地升降。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of the ocean surface worldwide: track global sea-level change separately from local land movement.

morphology.text: farcy 作为独立词素整体记；历史同根 farc-（塞满） + -imen（名词后缀） → farcimen（香肠），与其拉丁语来源链相连。

etymology.text: 15世纪经古法语 farcin 借入，连到晚期拉丁语 farciminum；更早与 farcimen“香肠”、farcire“塞满”相连。名称的旧比喻关联皮下肿起的病变。

usage_note: 兽医学历史病名，指鼻疽的皮肤、淋巴管病变类型。学习此词只为阅读识别。

senses.meaning_zh: 皮肤型鼻疽；主要累及皮肤及淋巴管、形成结节和溃疡的鼻疽病型。
senses.meaning_en: The cutaneous form of glanders, affecting the skin and lymphatic vessels.
senses.english_definition: Farcy is a form of glanders in which nodules and ulcers develop in the skin and along lymphatic vessels, especially in horses.
senses.collocation_zh: 皮肤型鼻疽结节；皮肤型鼻疽病例
senses.sentence_en: The veterinary report described farcy buds along the horse's hind leg.
senses.sentence_zh: 兽医报告描述了沿这匹马后腿分布的皮肤型鼻疽结节。

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语经古法语 farcin 借入，最终与拉丁语 farcimen（香肠）及 farcire（填塞）相关。这个旧病名通常被解释为借用了病变部位肿胀、呈条索状的外观。
etymology_story.en: The word entered Middle English through Old French farcin and is ultimately related to Latin farcimen, “sausage,” and farcire, “to stuff.” The old disease name is generally explained as referring to the swollen, cordlike appearance of affected tissues.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 farcy 是不可再作有效拆分的整体名词，词尾 -y 不是这里可自由替换的现代派生后缀。相关形式有较少见的 farcied（患皮肤型鼻疽的）；farcy bud（皮肤型鼻疽结节）是名词组合，其中 farcy 作定语，不构成独立的常用形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, farcy is an indivisible noun; its final -y is not a freely replaceable modern derivational suffix here. A less common related form is farcied, meaning affected with farcy. Farcy bud is a noun compound in which farcy modifies another noun without establishing a separate common adjective sense.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cutaneous glanders（皮肤型鼻疽）是直接同义表达；glanders（鼻疽）指整个疾病，范围更广，还包括以鼻腔或肺部病变为主的病型。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cutaneous glanders is the direct synonym. Glanders names the disease more broadly and also includes forms characterized mainly by nasal or pulmonary involvement.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从旧词源的“塞得鼓起”联想到皮下结节：farcy 是皮肤型鼻疽。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the historical idea of being stuffed and swollen with skin nodules: farcy is cutaneous glanders.

morphology.text: 历史词干 fastigi-（高处、顶端） + -ate（形容词结尾） → fastigiate（枝条直立聚拢的）。

etymology.text: 17世纪借自中世纪拉丁语 fastigiatus“高耸的”，来自拉丁语 fastigium“高度、顶端”。想象枝条一起向上形成窄柱状树冠。

usage_note: 植物学形容词，指枝条直立且聚拢生长，常形成狭窄、向上的树形。

senses.meaning_zh: （树木或枝条）直立聚拢的，形成狭窄树冠的
senses.meaning_en: Having upright, closely grouped branches that form a narrow crown.
senses.english_definition: A fastigiate tree has branches that grow upwards close together, giving it a narrow shape. 指枝条紧密向上生长、树冠狭窄的树木。
senses.collocation_zh: 直立聚拢的枝条；窄冠栽培品种
senses.sentence_en: The gardener chose a fastigiate cultivar for the narrow space beside the driveway.
senses.sentence_zh: 园丁为车道旁的狭窄空间选用了一个窄冠栽培品种。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 fastigiatus，意为“形成尖顶的”，其基础词 fastigium 指“山墙顶、顶点或高度”。树木的直立枝条聚拢成高而窄的轮廓，由此形成其植物学意义。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin fastigiatus, meaning formed into a pointed top, from fastigium, a gable, summit, or height. Its botanical meaning reflects branches rising together into a tall, narrow outline.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中主要作为整体形容词使用；从历史构词看，可分析为 fastigi-（顶点、尖顶）+ -ate（形容词结尾）。相关形式有 fastigiated（同义形容词）、fastigiately（副词，罕用）和 fastigiation（直立聚拢的形态，罕用）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, fastigiate functions mainly as a whole adjective; historically, it can be analyzed as fastigi- meaning summit or pointed top, plus adjectival -ate. Related forms include fastigiated, an alternative adjective, fastigiately, a rare adverb, and fastigiation, a rare noun for this growth form.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: upright（直立的）只说明生长方向；columnar（柱状的）强调整体轮廓像柱子；fastigiate 则特别强调枝条向上生长并紧密聚拢。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Upright describes the direction of growth; columnar describes an overall pillar-like outline; fastigiate specifically emphasizes closely grouped, ascending branches.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: fastigi- 联想“顶点”：枝条一起向顶点靠拢，形成窄冠。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect fastigi- with a summit: branches gather upwards towards the top, forming a narrow crown.

etymology_story.zh: 直接借自拉丁语复数名词 fauces，意为“喉咙、咽喉”，也可引申为“狭窄的入口或通道”。英语在解剖学中保留其咽喉意义，在古典建筑研究中保留其入口通道意义。
etymology_story.en: Fauces was borrowed directly from the Latin plural noun fauces, meaning throat or jaws and, by extension, a narrow entrance or passage. English preserves the anatomical meaning and the architectural meaning used in descriptions of Roman houses.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是借入英语的拉丁语复数形式，应整体记忆，不宜按普通英语词尾拆分；英语中通常不另造单数形式。相关形容词为 faucal 和 faucial（咽峡的），可用词干 fauc- 加 -al 或 -ial 理解。
morphology_enriched.en: This is a borrowed Latin plural and should be learned as a whole rather than divided into ordinary English components; English normally uses no separate singular form. Related adjectives are faucal and faucial, meaning relating to the fauces, analyzable as fauc- plus -al or -ial.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: oropharyngeal isthmus（口咽峡）是解剖义的对应术语；throat（喉咙）是范围较广的日常用词；entrance passage（入口通道）可解释建筑义，但不限定古罗马住宅。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Oropharyngeal isthmus is an equivalent anatomical term; throat is a broader everyday word; entrance passage explains the architectural sense without specifying a Roman house.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“狭窄的入口”：口腔通向咽的入口，或住宅通向中庭的入口。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember a narrow gateway: from the mouth into the throat, or from a house entrance into its atrium.

usage_note: 正式、文学用词，强烈谴责极其恶劣、可耻的行为，不能只用来表示普通错误。

senses.meaning_zh: 罪大恶极的；极其卑劣可耻的
senses.meaning_en: Extremely wicked, criminal, or shameful.
senses.english_definition: If you describe an act or a person as flagitious, you strongly condemn them as extremely wicked or shameful. 用 flagitious 形容行为或人，表示强烈谴责其极端邪恶或卑劣可耻。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 flagitiosus，意为“可耻的、邪恶的”，来自 flagitium“可耻行为、恶行”。英语沿用其强烈的道德谴责意味，如今主要见于正式或文学性语境。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin flagitiosus, meaning shameful or wicked, from flagitium, a disgraceful act or outrage. English retains its forceful moral condemnation, chiefly in formal or literary contexts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词可按受限词干 flagiti-（恶行、耻辱）+ -ous（具有某种性质的）理解，拼写体现为 -ious；历史来源则是拉丁语整体词形 flagitiosus。直接派生词有 flagitiously（罪恶地、卑劣地）和 flagitiousness（罪恶、卑劣）。
morphology_enriched.en: For modern analysis, the word can be understood as the bound stem flagiti-, associated with disgraceful wrongdoing, plus adjectival -ous, appearing in the spelling -ious; historically, it comes from the complete Latin form flagitiosus. Direct derivatives are flagitiously and flagitiousness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: heinous（极其恶劣的）常修饰令人震惊的罪行；atrocious（残暴恶劣的）突出残酷或程度极坏；flagrant（公然恶劣的）强调错误明显、毫不掩饰，而 flagitious 直接强调道德上的邪恶可耻。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Heinous commonly describes shockingly serious crimes; atrocious emphasizes cruelty or extreme badness; flagrant emphasizes conspicuous, undisguised wrongdoing, while flagitious directly stresses moral wickedness and disgrace.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: flagiti- 的核心是“可耻恶行”：恶劣到值得强烈谴责，就是 flagitious。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor flagiti- to disgraceful wrongdoing: flagitious describes evil serious enough to invite strong condemnation.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 florescens，其词干为 florescent-，是 florescere“开始开花、繁盛起来”的现在分词；该动词与 flos“花”相关。英语保留了“正在开花”的意义，也偶见“繁荣兴盛”的比喻用法。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin florescens, with the stem florescent-, the present participle of florescere, meaning to begin flowering or to flourish, related to flos, flower. English retains the flowering sense and occasionally extends it figuratively to flourishing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 学习时可分析为 flor-（花）+ -escent（进入或呈现某种状态的）；历史上 -escent 对应拉丁语动词分词结构。直接词族包括 floresce（开花，罕用动词）和 florescence（开花、花期）；同根扩展词包括 floral（花的）、florist（花商）和 floriculture（花卉栽培）。
morphology_enriched.en: For learning purposes, analyze it as flor-, flower, plus -escent, entering or displaying a state; historically, -escent reflects a Latin verbal participial formation. Its direct family includes floresce, a rare verb meaning to flower, and florescence, flowering or the flowering period; the wider root family includes floral, florist, and floriculture.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: flowering（开花的）是通用表达；blooming（盛开的）常突出花朵已经开放的状态；flourishing（繁荣的、茁壮的）主要描述旺盛发展。florescent 较书面，常用于植物学语境，不能与表示“发荧光的” fluorescent 混淆。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Flowering is the general term; blooming often emphasizes the state of having open flowers; flourishing mainly describes vigorous growth or successful development. Florescent is more learned and often botanical; it must be distinguished from fluorescent, which concerns fluorescence.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: flor- 是“花”，-escent 是“进入某种状态”：正在进入开花状态。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Flor- means flower, and -escent suggests entering a state: becoming flower-covered or coming into bloom.

etymology_story.en: Freebee is a variant spelling of the informal noun freebie, formed from free with a playful noun ending. Its central meaning is something obtainable without payment, often in a promotional setting.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可按 free（免费的）+ 口语化结尾理解；常见拼写 freebie 中的 -bie 并非可自由套用的常规后缀，freebee 也不表示 free + bee“免费的蜜蜂”。本词复数为 freebees；常见拼写及其复数为 freebie、freebies。更广的 free 词族包括 freely（自由地、无拘束地）、freedom（自由）和 free-of-charge（免费的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Understand the formation as free plus an informal ending; -bie in the usual spelling freebie is not a freely productive standard suffix, and freebee does not mean free plus the insect bee. Its plural is freebees; the usual spelling and its plural are freebie and freebies. The wider free family includes freely, freedom, and free-of-charge.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: giveaway（赠品）常指宣传活动中发放的物品；complimentary item（免费赠送的物品）较正式，常见于商业服务；gift（礼物）强调赠予，不一定涉及促销。freebee/freebie 则是强调“白送、不收费”的口语表达。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Giveaway often means an item distributed for publicity; complimentary item is more formal and common in commercial services; gift emphasizes the act of giving and need not involve promotion. Freebee/freebie is informal and highlights receiving something without payment.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 free“免费”：拿到手却不用付钱，就是 freebee；常见拼写是 freebie。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to free: something you get without paying is a freebee, usually spelled freebie.

senses.sentence_zh: 这本地方植物指南以 garget 这一名称收录了美洲商陆。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古英语 garget、gargate 追溯至古法语 gargate，意为“喉咙”；其病名用法后来涉及动物喉部或腺体的肿胀，尤其是乳房炎。在美国地方用语中，它也成为美洲商陆的名称。
etymology_story.en: The word comes through Middle English garget and gargate from Old French gargate, meaning 'throat'; its disease senses developed to cover swellings of the throat or glands, especially inflammation of the udder. In regional American usage, it also became a name for pokeweed.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中按不可再分析的词干 garget 记忆，不宜硬拆为现代词根和词缀。派生词：garget + -y → gargety（患乳房炎的）；植物义作可数名词时复数为 gargets，病名通常不可数。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, garget is an unanalyzed stem rather than a transparent combination of productive roots and affixes. Its derivative is garget + -y → gargety, meaning affected with garget; the plant noun can have the plural gargets, while the disease noun is normally uncountable.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: mastitis（乳腺炎）是现代医学和兽医学术语，适用范围比旧称 garget 更广；udder inflammation（乳房炎症）是直白的描述性说法；pokeweed（美洲商陆）只对应植物义，是现代更通用的名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mastitis is the modern medical and veterinary term and applies more broadly than the old word garget; udder inflammation is a plain descriptive expression. Pokeweed corresponds only to the plant sense and is the more usual modern name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史线索：喉咙 → 腺体肿胀 → 牲畜乳房炎；植物义另记“美洲商陆”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the historical thread: throat → swollen glands → an inflamed udder; remember pokeweed as a separate plant sense.

etymology_story.zh: 该词以拉丁语 gingiva（牙龈）为基础，经新拉丁语 gingivalis 形成牙科形容词。它保留了原有的解剖学含义，专指牙龈组织。
etymology_story.en: The word is based on Latin gingiva, meaning 'gum', through the New Latin adjective gingivalis. It retains its anatomical meaning and refers specifically to gum tissue.

morphology_enriched.zh: gingiv-（牙龈）+ -al（……的）→ gingival。词族及相关构词：gingiva（牙龈，复数 gingivae）、gingivally（在牙龈处；与牙龈有关地）、gingivitis（牙龈炎）、gingivectomy（牙龈切除术）、gingivoplasty（牙龈成形术）、gingivostomatitis（龈口炎）、dentogingival（牙与牙龈的）。
morphology_enriched.en: gingiv- 'gum' + -al 'relating to' → gingival. The family and related formations include gingiva, plural gingivae; gingivally, at or in relation to the gums; gingivitis, gum inflammation; gingivectomy, surgical removal of gum tissue; gingivoplasty, surgical reshaping of gum tissue; gingivostomatitis, inflammation of the gums and mouth; and dentogingival, relating to the teeth and gums.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gum-related（与牙龈有关的）是通俗的对应表达；periodontal（牙周的）范围更广，包括牙龈及其他牙齿支持组织；oral（口腔的）范围最广，涉及整个口腔。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gum-related is the plain-language equivalent; periodontal includes the gums and other tissues supporting the teeth; oral is broader still and concerns the mouth as a whole.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: gingiv- 锁定“牙龈”，-al 表示“……的”：gingival 就是“牙龈的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor gingiv- to 'gums' and -al to 'relating to': gingival means relating to the gums.

senses.sentence_en: The gingko outside the library turns golden every autumn.
senses.sentence_zh: 图书馆外的那棵银杏每年秋天都会变成金黄色。

etymology_story.zh: gingko 是 ginkgo 的异体拼写；ginkgo 通常追溯至恩格尔贝特·肯普费尔对日语 ginkyō（銀杏，字面义为“银色的杏”）的早期罗马字记录。标准拼写中的字母组合一般被认为与当时的转写或书写差误有关。
etymology_story.en: Gingko is a variant of ginkgo, a name usually traced to Engelbert Kaempfer's early romanization of Japanese ginkyō, written 銀杏 and literally meaning 'silver apricot'. The unusual letter sequence in the standard spelling is generally attributed to an early transcription or writing error.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 gingko 是不可再拆的借词词干，不含可独立分析的英语前后缀；更常用的拼写是 ginkgo。复数有 gingkos、gingkoes，对应标准拼写 ginkgos、ginkgoes；相关构词包括 ginkgo + -phyte → ginkgophyte（银杏类植物）、ginkgolic acid（银杏酸）和 ginkgolide（银杏内酯）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, gingko is an unanalyzed borrowed stem with no independently identifiable English prefix or suffix; ginkgo is the more usual spelling. Plurals include gingkos and gingkoes, corresponding to ginkgos and ginkgoes; related formations include ginkgo + -phyte → ginkgophyte, a plant of the ginkgo group; ginkgolic acid; and ginkgolide, a compound found in ginkgo.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ginkgo 与 gingko 指同一种树，但 ginkgo 是更常用的标准拼写；maidenhair tree（银杏树）是传统英语俗名，得名于叶片与铁线蕨叶片的相似之处。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ginkgo names exactly the same tree and is the more usual standard spelling; maidenhair tree is a traditional common name referring to the resemblance between its leaves and those of maidenhair ferns.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一片扇形叶，一树秋日金黄；gingko 与 ginkgo 是同一种银杏。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a fan-shaped leaf turning gold: gingko and ginkgo name the same tree.

etymology_story.zh: 该词见于中古英语 gladsom，由 glad（高兴的）与表示“具有某种特点”的本族语后缀 -some 构成。它一直保留着欢乐、带来喜悦的含义，如今主要用于文学或带有古雅色彩的表达。
etymology_story.en: The word is recorded in Middle English as gladsom, combining glad with the native suffix -some, meaning 'characterized by'. It has retained its associations with happiness and the giving of joy, but now occurs mainly in literary or old-fashioned language.

morphology_enriched.zh: glad（高兴的）+ -some（具有……特点的）→ gladsome。直接派生词有 gladsomely（欢欣地）和 gladsomeness（欢欣）；同根词族包括 gladly（乐意地；高兴地）、gladness（喜悦）、gladden（使高兴，变化形式 gladdens、gladdened、gladdening）。
morphology_enriched.en: glad 'happy' + -some 'characterized by' → gladsome. Direct derivatives are gladsomely and gladsomeness; the wider glad family includes gladly, gladness, and gladden, with the forms gladdens, gladdened, and gladdening.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: joyful（喜悦的）强调明显或强烈的快乐；cheerful（愉快的）常指日常的开朗心情或明快气氛；heartening（令人振奋的）强调带来信心与希望。gladsome 带有更明显的文学或古雅色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Joyful emphasizes evident or strong happiness; cheerful often describes an everyday positive mood or bright atmosphere; heartening emphasizes renewed confidence or hope. Gladsome has a more distinctly literary or old-fashioned tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: glad + -some：带着喜悦，也把喜悦带给别人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Glad + -some: characterized by gladness, whether felt, expressed, or shared.

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语 hansel、handsel 与古英语 handselen 及古诺尔斯语 handsal 有关，核心意象是“交到手中的赠与或交付”。这种赠与被视为吉利的开端，词义因而扩展到首笔收入以及首次使用、启用。
etymology_story.en: Middle English hansel and handsel are related to Old English handselen and Old Norse handsal, with the central idea of a gift or delivery into someone's hand. Because such a gift marked a fortunate beginning, the word developed senses involving first receipts and the first use or inauguration of something.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 handsel 作为整体词干；历史上可联系 hand（手）与表示交付、赠与的成分，但不能按现代 hand + sell（出售）直接解释。名词复数及动词第三人称单数为 handsels；英式过去式和过去分词 handselled、现在分词 handselling；美式也用 handseled、handseling；异体拼写为 hansel。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats handsel as a single stem; historically it contains hand and an element associated with delivery or giving, but it should not be interpreted as modern hand + sell. The noun plural and third-person singular verb are handsels; British forms include handselled and handselling, while American forms also include handseled and handseling. Hansel is a spelling variant.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gift（礼物）不限定赠送时机，也不必有祈求好运的含义；first takings（首笔营业收入）对应收入义，但通常没有传统吉兆色彩；inaugurate（启用；开创）对应动词的开始义，更正式，也不要求赠礼。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gift does not specify an occasion or imply good luck; first takings matches the income sense without necessarily carrying a traditional lucky association; inaugurate matches the verb's beginning sense but is more formal and does not require a gift.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 新开始，礼到手：礼物讨吉利，首款开好头，再引申为首次启用。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A new beginning, a gift in hand: a lucky gift leads to first earnings and then to first use.

The name counts the corners of a polygon that consequently also has seven sides. [Etymology source](https://www.etymonline.com/word/heptagon)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词分析：hepta-（七）+ -gon（表示具有特定角数的多边形）→ heptagon。词族：heptagons（复数）；heptagonal（七边形的）；heptagonally（呈七边形地）。heptagonal 的重音移至第二音节，英式读音为 /hepˈtæɡənəl/。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: hepta- (seven) + -gon (a polygon with a specified number of angles) → heptagon. Word family: heptagons (plural), heptagonal (having seven sides), and heptagonally (in a seven-sided arrangement). In heptagonal, stress moves to the second syllable: UK /hepˈtæɡənəl/.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: septagon（七边形）是较少使用的同义词；seven-sided polygon（七边形）是透明易懂的描述性说法；polygon（多边形）是上位词，本身不限定边数。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Septagon is a less common synonym; seven-sided polygon is a transparent descriptive equivalent; polygon is the broader category and does not specify the number of sides.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hepta- 数“七”，-gon 数“角”：七个角围成七边形。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hepta- counts seven; -gon points to corners: seven corners make a heptagon.

etymology_story.zh: heteronym 由希腊语来源的 hetero-（不同）与 -onym（名称）构成，十九世纪末已用于词汇关系的描述。其文学义尤其与葡萄牙作家费尔南多·佩索阿相关，指具有各自人格和文风的虚构作者，而不仅是另一个署名。[词源来源](https://www.etymonline.com/word/heteronym)；[现代义项来源](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/heteronym)
etymology_story.en: Heteronym combines Greek-derived hetero-, meaning different, with -onym, meaning name, and was used for lexical relationships by the late nineteenth century. Its literary sense is especially associated with Fernando Pessoa and denotes an invented author with a distinct personality and style, rather than merely an alternative signature. [Etymology source](https://www.etymonline.com/word/heteronym); [Modern senses](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/heteronym)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词分析：hetero-（不同）+ -onym（名称；词）→ heteronym。词族：heteronyms（复数）；heteronymic、heteronymous（同形异音异义的；异名的）；heteronymy（异名现象；同形异音异义关系）。具体解释随语言学或文学语境变化。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: hetero- (different) + -onym (name or word) → heteronym. Word family: heteronyms (plural), heteronymic and heteronymous (relating to heteronyms), and heteronymy (the relationship or practice involving heteronyms). Their precise meanings depend on the linguistic or literary context.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: homograph（同形词）只要求拼写相同，不一定读音不同；heterophone（异音词）在同形词讨论中可强调读音不同；pseudonym（笔名）通常只是替代姓名，heteronym 的文学义还包含独立的人格和文风。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Homograph requires identical spelling but does not necessarily require different pronunciations; heterophone can emphasize the pronunciation difference when discussing homographs; pseudonym usually means an alternative name, whereas a literary heteronym also has a distinct personality and style.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hetero-＝不同，-onym＝名字或词：语言里“同形异读”，文学里“另一个作者人格”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hetero- means different and -onym means name: a different reading behind one spelling, or a different authorial self behind the writing.

etymology_story.zh: 美式 hoke 在二十世纪初的戏剧俚语中出现，与 hokum（做作的戏剧噱头）有词源联系，后来用于各种人为夸饰。[美式词源来源](https://www.etymonline.com/word/hoke) 北爱尔兰表示“挖掘、翻找”的 hoke 则另有来源，与苏格兰语及英语方言 howk 有关，不能与美式词源混为一谈。[方言来源](https://cms.nationalmuseumsni.org/sites/default/files/2022-10/Concise-Ulster-Dictionary-Letters-A-Z.pdf)
etymology_story.en: American hoke appeared in early twentieth-century theatrical slang, is historically connected with hokum, and later extended to artificial embellishment more generally. [American etymology](https://www.etymonline.com/word/hoke) The Northern Irish word meaning to dig or rummage has a separate history connected with Scots and dialectal English howk. [Regional source](https://cms.nationalmuseumsni.org/sites/default/files/2022-10/Concise-Ulster-Dictionary-Letters-A-Z.pdf)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代 hoke 可作为不再细分的词基；hoke + up → hoke up（刻意夸饰）。屈折形式：hokes、hoked、hoking，接 -ing 时去掉词尾 e；美式相关词族包括 hokey（做作的）、hokier、hokiest、hokiness（做作）；hokum 是历史相关词。方言词族另有 hoker（挖掘者；翻找者），与美式词族应分别处理。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern hoke can be treated as an unanalyzed base; hoke + up forms hoke up (embellish artificially). Inflections are hokes, hoked, and hoking, with final e dropped before -ing. The American family includes hokey, hokier, hokiest, and hokiness; hokum is historically related. The regional family separately includes hoker, meaning a digger or rummager.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: embellish（增饰）可以是中性或褒义，hoke up 通常含做作或虚假的贬义；overact（表演过火）专指表演，范围比 hoke up 窄；rummage（翻找）对应方言义，与美式“夸饰”义无关。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Embellish can be neutral or positive, whereas hoke up usually criticizes artificiality; overact specifically concerns excessive acting and has a narrower scope; rummage matches the regional searching sense and is unrelated to the American embellishment sense.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 美式：把 hokum 式的噱头加上去，就是 hoke up；方言：双手翻找，就是 have a hoke。两条词源分开记。
mnemonic_anchor.en: American: add hokum and you hoke it up. Regional: rummage with your hands and have a hoke. Keep the two histories separate.

etymology_story.zh: Holarctic 是十九世纪由 holo-（整个）与 arctic（北方的）构成的科学术语，形成 hol- + arctic 的拼写。它把古北界与新北界合并为一个生物地理单位，范围并不限于北极圈内。[词源与释义来源](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/holarctic)；[分布说明](https://torontobotanicalgarden.ca/blog/word-of-the-week/botanical-nerd-word-holarctic/)
etymology_story.en: Holarctic was formed in the nineteenth century from holo-, meaning whole, and arctic, meaning northern, with the spelling hol- + arctic. It combines the Palearctic and Nearctic into one biogeographic unit extending well beyond the Arctic Circle. [Etymology and definition](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/holarctic); [Distribution explained](https://torontobotanicalgarden.ca/blog/word-of-the-week/botanical-nerd-word-holarctic/)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词分析：holo-（整个）在元音前采用 hol- 的形式，hol- + Arctic（北方的）→ Holarctic。常作形容词，也名词化为 the Holarctic（全北界）；没有需要优先学习的常用派生词。Arctic、Nearctic（新北界的）和 Palearctic／Palaearctic（古北界的）是相关术语，并非 Holarctic 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: holo- (whole) appears as hol- before the vowel of Arctic, giving hol- + Arctic → Holarctic. It functions as an adjective and substantivally as the Holarctic; there are no common derivatives that need priority. Arctic, Nearctic, and Palearctic, also spelled Palaearctic, are related terms rather than derivatives of Holarctic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: northern（北方的）范围宽泛，不限定生物地理界；Palearctic（古北界的）指旧大陆的相应区域；Nearctic（新北界的）指北美洲的相应区域。后两者各自只是 Holarctic 的一部分，不能单独与之互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Northern is a broad geographical description without a fixed biogeographic boundary; Palearctic refers to the corresponding Old World region; Nearctic refers to the North American region. Each of the latter two is only part of the Holarctic and cannot individually replace it.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hol-＝整个：把古北界与新北界合起来，得到“全北界”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hol- means whole: join the Palearctic and Nearctic to picture the whole Holarctic.

senses.meaning_zh: 【语言学】独词句；表句词；以一个词表达完整句意的用语
senses.meaning_en: a single word used to express the meaning of a whole phrase or sentence
senses.english_definition: A holophrase is a single word that expresses a whole message, especially when a young child is learning to speak.
senses.collocation_en: use a holophrase; a child's holophrases
senses.collocation_zh: 使用独词句；儿童的独词句
senses.sentence_en: When the toddler says 'Up!' to mean 'Pick me up,' the word functions as a holophrase.
senses.sentence_zh: 幼儿说“Up!”来表达“抱我起来”时，这个词就起到了独词句的作用。

etymology_story.zh: holophrase 于十九世纪末见于英语，由 holo-（整个）与 phrase（表达；短语）构成，后者最终可追溯到希腊语 phrasis（表达）。这个术语把“完整表达”压缩到一个词中，尤其常用于儿童语言发展的讨论。[词源来源](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/holophrase)；[现代用法来源](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/holophrase)
etymology_story.en: Holophrase is recorded in late nineteenth-century English and combines holo-, meaning whole, with phrase, ultimately related to Greek phrasis, meaning expression. The term describes a complete message carried by one word and is especially used in discussions of children's language development. [Etymology source](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/holophrase); [Modern usage](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/holophrase)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词分析：holo-（整个）+ phrase（表达；短语）→ holophrase。词族：holophrases（复数）；holophrastic（独词句的；以一词表达完整句意的）；holophrastically（以独词句方式地）；holophrasis（用一词表达完整句意的现象或方式）。holophrastic 使用相关词干 phras-，不是简单在完整词后加 -ic。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: holo- (whole) + phrase (expression or phrase) → holophrase. Word family: holophrases (plural), holophrastic (expressing a whole message in one word), holophrastically (in that manner), and holophrasis (the practice or phenomenon). Holophrastic uses the related stem phras- rather than simply adding -ic to the full word.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: one-word sentence（独词句）是常用的解释性近义表达；one-word utterance（单词话语）只说明话语长度，不保证承载完整句意；interjection（感叹词）是语法类别，某个感叹词可以构成 holophrase，但两者并不等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: One-word sentence is a useful explanatory equivalent; one-word utterance describes length without necessarily implying a complete message; interjection is a grammatical category, and an interjection may function as a holophrase without the two terms being equivalent.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: holo-＝完整：一个词，装下整句话；如“抱！”表达“把我抱起来！”
mnemonic_anchor.en: Holo- means whole: one word carries the whole message, as 'Up!' carries 'Pick me up!'

senses.meaning_zh: 可被水分解的物质；发生水解的物质（罕见化学术语）
senses.meaning_en: A substance that undergoes decomposition by water; a rare chemical term.
senses.english_definition: A hydrolyte is a substance that is broken down through a chemical reaction with water.
senses.collocation_en: a hydrolyte; decomposition of a hydrolyte (illustrative combinations; this rare term has no established high-frequency collocations)
senses.collocation_zh: 一种可水解物质；可水解物质的分解（示例性搭配；该词罕见，没有公认的高频搭配）
senses.sentence_en: In this older terminology, a substance decomposed by water is called a hydrolyte.
senses.sentence_zh: 按这种较旧的术语用法，被水分解的物质称为可水解物质。

etymology_story.zh: 这是由希腊语来源的 hydro-（水）和表示可分解物质的 -lyte 构成的科学术语，后者与希腊语中表示“松开、分解”的词根有关。词义指向水所分解的物质，不能仅凭词形将其理解为水解产物。
etymology_story.en: This scientific formation combines Greek-derived hydro-, meaning water, with -lyte, an element associated with substances subject to decomposition and ultimately with the Greek root meaning loosen or dissolve. It denotes the substance decomposed by water, rather than necessarily the product of hydrolysis.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：hydro-（水）+ -lyte（可分解的物质）→ hydrolyte；复数为 hydrolytes。相关词族包括 hydrolysis（水解）、hydrolyse／hydrolyze（水解）、hydrolytic（水解的）、hydrolytically（通过水解）、hydrolysable／hydrolyzable（可水解的）和 hydrolysate（水解产物）；这些是相关构词，并非都直接由 hydrolyte 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: hydro- (water) + -lyte (a substance subject to decomposition) → hydrolyte; plural hydrolytes. Related family members include hydrolysis, hydrolyse/hydrolyze, hydrolytic, hydrolytically, hydrolysable/hydrolyzable, and hydrolysate; these are related formations, not all direct derivatives of hydrolyte.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hydrolysable substance（可水解物质）最接近原义，也更清楚；substrate（底物）指反应所作用的物质，范围更广；hydrolysate（水解产物）指水解后得到的物质，不能与 hydrolyte 混用。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hydrolysable substance is the closest and clearest equivalent; substrate is broader, referring to material acted on in a reaction; hydrolysate denotes the resulting product and is not interchangeable with hydrolyte.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hydro- 是水，-lyte 关联分解：记作“被水拆开的物质”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hydro- supplies the water; -lyte suggests breakdown: the substance that water breaks apart.

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自十九世纪早期建立的科学属名 Ichthyosaurus，由希腊语 ikhthys（鱼）和 sauros（蜥蜴）构成。名称以“鱼形蜥蜴”描绘这种海生爬行动物的外形，旧时普通用法的指称有时比严格的属名更宽。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from the scientific genus name Ichthyosaurus, established in the early nineteenth century from Greek ikhthys, meaning fish, and sauros, meaning lizard. The name describes a fish-shaped marine reptile, and older everyday usage sometimes extended beyond the strictly defined genus.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：ichthyo-（鱼）+ -saurus（蜥蜴，常用于古生物名称）→ ichthyosaurus；复数可用 ichthyosauruses 或 ichthyosauri。相关词有 ichthyosaur（鱼龙）、ichthyosaurian（鱼龙的；鱼龙类动物）和 Ichthyosauria（鱼龙类的分类名称）；严格的属名 Ichthyosaurus 首字母大写。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: ichthyo- (fish) + -saurus (lizard, frequent in prehistoric animal names) → ichthyosaurus; plurals include ichthyosauruses and ichthyosauri. Related forms include ichthyosaur, ichthyosaurian, and the taxonomic name Ichthyosauria; the formal genus name Ichthyosaurus is capitalized.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ichthyosaur（鱼龙）是现代常用名称，涵盖范围通常比鱼龙属更广；fish lizard（鱼形蜥蜴）是历史性描述名称；marine reptile（海生爬行动物）是更宽泛的类别，也包括其他类群。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ichthyosaur is the usual modern term and generally covers a broader group than the genus Ichthyosaurus; fish lizard is a historical descriptive name; marine reptile is a much broader category that includes other groups.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ichthyo- 鱼 + -saurus 蜥蜴：长着鱼形身体的古代海生爬行动物。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Fish + lizard: picture an ancient marine reptile with a fish-shaped body.

senses.meaning_zh: 把土地圈围成园地，尤指围成鹿苑或猎苑（古旧用法）

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古英语传入，源自盎格鲁法语 emparker，意思是“围入园地”。这里的 park 原指供圈养鹿或其他猎用动物的围地，因此产生了“圈地为苑”和“圈兽入苑”两种相关用法。
etymology_story.en: The word entered Middle English from Anglo-French emparker, meaning to enclose in a park. Park here referred to enclosed ground for deer or other game, producing the related senses of enclosing land as a park and confining animals within one.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 im-（表示进入、置入的前缀形式）+ park（园地）→ impark；这里的 im- 不表示否定。词形有 imparks、imparked、imparking；相关名词 imparking 指圈地为苑这一行为，另有变体 empark。
morphology_enriched.en: Synchronically, impark can be analyzed as im- (a form expressing entry or placement within) + park; im- is not negative here. Inflected forms are imparks, imparked, and imparking; the action noun imparking and the variant empark are also related.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: enclose（围起）只强调设置边界；fence in（用栅栏围住）强调具体围栏；empark 与 impark 同义，是另一种拼写形式。Impark 特别涉及将土地设为园苑或将动物圈入园苑。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Enclose emphasizes creating a boundary; fence in specifies a physical fence; empark is an alternative form with the same meaning. Impark specifically concerns making land into a park or confining animals within one.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: im- 进入 + park 园苑：土地围成苑，鹿群圈入苑。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Im- means into, and park supplies the enclosure: make a park or put deer into it.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古英语和法语传入，最终来自拉丁语 introitus（进入），与 introire（走入）有关。表示“进入”的词逐渐专指礼拜开始、神职人员入堂时所唱的圣咏。
etymology_story.en: The word passed through Middle English and French from Latin introitus, meaning entrance, related to introire, to go in. A word for entering thus became the name of the chant accompanying the opening entrance at worship.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 introit 当作完整借词，不宜强拆为能产的英语词根和后缀；复数为 introits。罕见形容词 introital 可表示“入堂咏的”，但也可与解剖学名词 introitus（入口）有关，须依语境区分；历史上的 intro-（向内）+ ire（走）属于拉丁语构词分析。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats introit as a whole borrowed base rather than a productive combination of English affixes; its plural is introits. The rare adjective introital can relate to an introit, but it can also relate to anatomical introitus, so context matters; intro- (inward) + ire (go) is a historical Latin analysis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: entrance chant（入堂圣咏）最接近其礼仪功能；entrance antiphon（入堂对经）可特指相应的对经文本或其唱诵；opening hymn（开场圣歌）范围更宽，不一定是礼仪规定的入堂咏。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Entrance chant closely matches its liturgical function; entrance antiphon can refer specifically to the corresponding antiphonal text or its singing; opening hymn is broader and need not be the prescribed introit.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“走入”记“入堂”：人入堂，歌开场。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect entrance with the opening chant: the clergy enter, and the introit begins.

etymology_story.zh: 该词借自古诺尔斯语 jarl，表示贵族或首领，与古英语 eorl、现代英语 earl（伯爵）同源。它在英语中主要保留为斯堪的纳维亚历史头衔，具体权力和地位随时代、地区而异。
etymology_story.en: The word was borrowed from Old Norse jarl, meaning a nobleman or chief, and is cognate with Old English eorl and modern English earl. English chiefly preserves it as a Scandinavian historical title whose authority and status varied across periods and regions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：jarl 是不可再作常规英语拆分的借词词根；复数为 jarls。jarl + -dom → jarldom，可指雅尔的身份、职位或领地；earl 是同源词，不是由 jarl 在现代英语中派生而来。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: jarl is a borrowed base without a regular internal English breakdown; its plural is jarls. Jarl + -dom forms jarldom, referring to a jarl's rank, office, or territory; earl is a cognate, not a modern English derivative of jarl.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: earl（伯爵）是同源且常用于翻译的头衔，但各地等级制度不能完全对应；chieftain（首领）突出领导群体的角色；nobleman（贵族）只说明贵族身份，不必拥有统治权。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Earl is a cognate title often used in translation, though the ranks do not correspond perfectly across societies; chieftain emphasizes leadership of a group; nobleman indicates aristocratic status without necessarily implying governing authority.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: jarl 与 earl 同源：把雅尔记作北欧历史中的贵族首领。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link jarl with its cousin earl: a noble leader in Scandinavian history.

etymology_story.zh: 该词出自十九世纪美国铁路用语：乡间支线的小火车有时需要停车，用桶提水给蒸汽机车补水，因此被称为 jerkwaters。这个名称后来转用于沿线偏僻小镇，并进一步产生“微不足道的”这一贬义。[词源依据：Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/jerkwater)。
etymology_story.en: The word arose in nineteenth-century American railroad usage for small rural trains whose crews sometimes hauled up water in buckets to refill their steam engines. It subsequently described remote towns along such lines and, more broadly, things dismissed as insignificant. [Etymological source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/jerkwater).

morphology_enriched.zh: jerk（猛拉、提起）+ water（水）→ jerkwater，属于复合词；形容词用法由历史上的名词用法发展而来。全词没有常用的派生形式；jerkwaters 是历史名词的复数，不是形容词的变化形式。
morphology_enriched.en: jerk ('pull sharply or haul up') + water → jerkwater, a compound whose adjective use developed from an earlier noun. The whole word has no common derivatives; jerkwaters is the plural of the historical noun, not an adjective inflection.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: backwater（闭塞落后的，通常用于名词修饰语）突出与外界发展脱节；insignificant（无足轻重的）只强调重要性低；two-bit（不入流的、廉价低劣的）着重贬低质量或地位。jerkwater 将偏僻、小规模和轻蔑评价结合起来。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Backwater, usually used as a noun modifier, emphasizes isolation from wider developments; insignificant concerns lack of importance; two-bit disparages quality or status. Jerkwater combines remoteness or small scale with a dismissive judgment.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 提水的小火车 → 偏远小站 → 偏僻、不起眼。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A train hauling up water → a remote little stop → remote and insignificant.

senses.meaning_zh: 冰砾阜；冰川融水沉积形成的层状沙砾丘
senses.meaning_en: Mounds or short irregular ridges of layered sand and gravel deposited by glacial meltwater.
senses.english_definition: Kames are hills or irregular mounds of sand and gravel deposited by water from melting glaciers.
senses.collocation_zh: 冰川作用形成的冰砾阜；冰砾阜与冰融洼地
senses.sentence_en: The retreating glacier left a landscape dotted with kames and kettles.
senses.sentence_zh: 冰川退缩后，留下了一片遍布冰砾阜和冰融洼地的地貌。

etymology_story.zh: 单数 kame 来自苏格兰语中表示“梳子”的 kame，可追溯至中古英语北部方言 camb，进一步源自古英语。这个词后来用于描述丘脊，并成为冰川地貌术语；kames 是其规则复数。[词源依据：Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/kame)。
etymology_story.en: The singular kame comes from Scots kame, meaning 'comb,' through northern Middle English camb from Old English. It came to describe ridged landforms and became a glacial landform term; kames is its regular plural. [Etymological source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/kame).

morphology_enriched.zh: kame（冰砾阜）+ -s（复数词尾，读 /z/）→ kames；这是屈折变化，不是派生。相关术语有 kame terrace（冰砾阜阶地）、kame moraine（冰砾阜冰碛）和 kame-and-kettle topography（冰砾阜与冰融洼地相间的地貌）；全词没有常用的派生动词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: kame ('a glacial sediment mound') + plural -s, pronounced /z/, → kames; this is inflection, not derivation. Related terms include kame terrace, kame moraine, and kame-and-kettle topography; there are no common derived verbs or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: mounds（土丘、堆丘）是形状上的宽泛近义词，不限定成因；eskers（蛇形丘）通常是冰下水道沉积形成的狭长曲折沙砾脊；moraines（冰碛、冰碛垄）主要由冰川直接搬运和堆积的物质构成。后两者是相关地貌术语，不能直接替换 kames。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mounds is a broad shape-based near-synonym without a specified origin; eskers are typically long, winding sediment ridges deposited in subglacial channels; moraines consist mainly of material transported and deposited directly by ice. The latter two are related landforms, not interchangeable synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 梳子的凸脊 → 地表的丘脊；冰融后留下沙砾丘。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A comb's raised profile suggests ridged ground; melting ice leaves sediment mounds.

etymology_story.zh: kibe 在十四世纪的中古英语中已有记录，其更早来源不确定。它保留了“溃烂的冻疮，尤指脚跟冻疮”这一旧义，现代日常英语通常使用 chilblain。[词源与释义依据：Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/kibe)。
etymology_story.en: Kibe is recorded in fourteenth-century Middle English, but its earlier origin is uncertain. It retains the old meaning of an ulcerated chilblain, especially on the heel, while everyday modern English generally uses chilblain. [Historical and definitional source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/kibe).

morphology_enriched.zh: kibe 是现代英语中不可再作有意义拆分的词基。kibe + -s → kibes（复数）；kibe 去末尾 e 后加 -ed → kibed（患有冻疮的，罕用形容词）；没有其他常用派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Kibe is a base with no meaningful internal breakdown in modern English. Add -s to form the plural kibes; remove final e and add -ed to form the rare adjective kibed ('affected with chilblains'); there are no other common derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chilblain（冻疮）是最接近且更常用的词，不一定涉及溃烂；pernio（冻疮）是相应的医学术语，常指这种病症；cold sore（唇疱疹）不是近义词，不应因含 cold 而混淆。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chilblain is the closest and more usual term, without necessarily implying ulceration; pernio is the medical term, often naming the condition collectively. Cold sore is not a synonym and should not be confused with kibe merely because it contains cold.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 固定画面：冷湿靴子里的脚跟，冻疮已经破溃；不强拆词根。

etymology_story.zh: 1959 年，新西兰出口商开始使用 kiwifruit，为此前称作 Chinese gooseberry 的中国原产水果重新命名。名称由 kiwi 和 fruit 组成；kiwi 原是毛利语鸟名，后来成为新西兰的象征。[历史依据：新西兰历史网站](https://nzhistory.govt.nz/chinese-gooseberry-becomes-kiwifruit)。
etymology_story.en: In 1959, a New Zealand exporter adopted kiwifruit as a new name for the Chinese-origin fruit previously called the Chinese gooseberry. The name combines fruit with kiwi, a Māori bird name that became an emblem of New Zealand. [Historical source: NZ History](https://nzhistory.govt.nz/chinese-gooseberry-becomes-kiwifruit).

morphology_enriched.zh: kiwi（几维鸟；引申代表新西兰）+ fruit（水果）→ kiwifruit，属于复合名词。可数用法的复数通常仍为 kiwifruit，也可用 kiwifruits；表示果肉或食材时可作不可数名词；缩略形式 kiwi 的复数是 kiwis；全词没有常用的加词缀派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: kiwi ('the bird, also an emblem of New Zealand') + fruit → kiwifruit, a compound noun. Its count plural is usually unchanged, although kiwifruits also occurs; it can be uncountable when referring to flesh or food material. The shortened form kiwi has the plural kiwis; the whole compound has no common affix-derived forms.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: kiwi 是常见简称，但也可指几维鸟或新西兰人；Chinese gooseberry（中国醋栗）是旧称，容易使人误以为它属于醋栗类；kiwifruit 的指称最明确。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Kiwi is the common shortened name but can also mean the bird or a New Zealander; Chinese gooseberry is the older name and misleadingly suggests a relationship to gooseberries. Kiwifruit identifies the fruit most explicitly.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: kiwi 是新西兰的标志，fruit 是水果：带着新西兰名称走向世界的猕猴桃。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Kiwi signals New Zealand and fruit names the food: the Chinese fruit marketed worldwide under a New Zealand name.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自德语 Knackwurst，其中 knack- 与 knacken（发出裂响、脆响）有关，Wurst 意为“香肠”。名称指咬破肠衣时的脆响；英语另有拼写 knockwurst。[词源依据：Duden](https://www.duden.de/rechtschreibung/Knackwurst)；[英语异体依据：Cambridge](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/knackwurst)。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed German Knackwurst, combining knack-, related to knacken ('crack or snap'), with Wurst ('sausage'). The name refers to the casing's snap when bitten; knockwurst is an alternative English spelling. [Etymological source: Duden](https://www.duden.de/rechtschreibung/Knackwurst); [English variant: Cambridge](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/knackwurst).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 knackwurst 作为整体借词使用，其德语内部结构为 knack-（脆响）+ Wurst（香肠），不是英语 knack（诀窍）+ wurst。英语复数为 knackwursts；异体拼写为 knockwurst，复数 knockwursts；全词没有常用的派生动词、形容词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats knackwurst as a borrowed lexical unit; its German structure is knack- ('snap') + Wurst ('sausage'), not English knack ('skill') + wurst. The English plural is knackwursts; the spelling variant knockwurst has plural knockwursts. There are no common derived verbs, adjectives, or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: knockwurst 是同一名称的异体拼写；frankfurter（法兰克福香肠）通常更细长；bratwurst（德式煎烤香肠）指另一类香肠，配方和制作方式各有变化。后两者是相关食品名称，不是可任意替换的同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Knockwurst is an alternative spelling of the same name; a frankfurter is generally longer and slimmer; bratwurst names a different sausage category with varied recipes and preparation methods. The latter two are related foods, not interchangeable synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: knack- 是咔嚓脆响，Wurst 是香肠：一口咬出脆响的香肠。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Knack- suggests a snap and Wurst means sausage: a sausage whose casing snaps when bitten.
